I called the restaurant and spoke with the manager who confirmed I was shorted one of my lamb chops and our wait was too long in between courses, he apologized and offered to make it up to us, even provided me with his cell phone number and said he'd follow up with me, he has yet to do that. text:
Zahav is an excellent Israeli restaurant - easily a 5 star review. I just wish it wasn't so hard to get reservations. 

I love trying different ethnic foods as the flavor profiles are so different from traditional North American cooking. Zahav is a perfect example of this. 

I always start with the Salatim - 5-6 different salads / dips and the standout hummus served with fresh laffa bread baked in a wood burning oven. This bread is incredible. The hummus is easily the best I ever had. What a way to start the meal. 

I would recommend getting a few of the small sharing dishes. My favorites are the fried cauliflower, kataifi nest cheese (kind of like fried cheese), roasted carrots and the tuna tartare. 

Next select 1-2 of the Al Hal'esh mains which are grilled over coals. The lamb kabob is ridiculously good as is the chicken sishlik, Branzino, eggplant and the hanger steak. 
It's the use of all the traditional Mediterranean and Israeli spices / ingredients that make Zahav dishes so good and unique. 

Prices are incredibly reasonable for one of the cities best restaurants. You can always order the taste of Zahav tasting menu witch includes the salatim, hummus, Laffe bread, two small dishes and a one main Al Hal'esh dish for just $48 a person. Everyone should order the tasting menu on the first visit to get familiar with the menu. I recommend each person select different dishes and share. 

Zahav is Philadelphia's best restaurant in my opinion. Amazing food, excellent service / atmosphere and at a fair price - the rare trifecta. 

Highly recommended (if you can get reservations).

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. It was crowded but still moved along. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. Would probably stop in again if nearby.
name: User

text: So we walk in and are essentially ignored by the hostess. We walk over to the bar and sit down at one of the many empty tables and wait staff keep walking by us but never stop at our table. I finally spoke with someone who was in charge  who told us we had to leave our table, go around the wall to check in with the hostess and then we could sit again. Didn't offer to help us himself so we got up and walked right out the door. No wonder there were so many empty tables.
name: Beth

text:
Great foodie addition to the neighborhood.  The food was by far one of the best we've had in St. Louis.  Finally, a sushi place without the oxersauced sushi rolls. The high quality fish is complemented with flavorful sauces without overpowering, which I absolutely appreciate.

Shrimp toast was creative and tasty enough.

Gyoza had a perfect twist and flavor profile than the typical.

Sake sashimi was beautifully flavored with ponzu sauce which was fantastic. I am not lying when I say I was using their big spoons to drink the sauce!! 

Hamachi with chili sauce had a sprinkle of sweetness.

We had 3 nigiris, but I can't remember exactly what we had.
Saba, salmon belly and another one (nodo/nobu something...)  that was out of this world!

While I commend their effort in flavoring their sushi rice (which many sushi restaurants forget) fell apart too easily with the nigiri.  

The price is on the high side, but that didn't deter us from ordering a ton of food.

Service was fantastically done by young, professional, hip and attentive cute folks.

I can't wait to try their lunch!
name: Jas

text: This is another occasion where a "Boise tradition" comes into play.  I've never been to McGrath's Fish House.  I've heard of it.  I've known folks who have been there.  I know folks who go there.  Much like several other "Boise traditions,"  this establishment is over rated in my book.  There's really nothing to see here.  Mediocre food and somewhat high prices (seafood is pricey granted).  The G.F. had the seafood fettuccine and I, scanning the menu and not being overly enthusiastic about the whole thing, ordered the Codfather.  Both were unimpressive.  My fish was undercooked.  The fettuccine?  Blah according to my G.F.  The only highlight was our very pleasant server with a great sense of humor.  Wish I could remember her name, young African American girl.  So, pass.  Pass.  Pass.  And not only that?  Don't bother wasting your money at McGrath's Fish House.
name: TheStranger

text: My coworker returned from lunch one day mentioning this new lunch spot down the street from our office that must of just opened. After looking at her food and the menu I figured let me go check this place out. Walking in the space is small, but adequate. I didn't receive a warm or any greeting for that matter mentioned in other reviews. I love how many options there are to choose from and all of the ingredients looked fresh. The workers sort of stared at us blankly as my friend and I decided what we wanted. I ended up with a chicken salad concoction which I greatly enjoyed. The pomegranate lemonade (free with check in) OMG delicious and refreshing! Sweet potato fries were straight up gross, soggy with oil and and I saw seasoning but didn't taste any. Should have gotten the pita chips, can't go wrong with those.
name: Adrienne

text: I had the trifecta, three different tales on eggs Benedict. It was delicious and I would recommend it to anyone, but it was a lot of food. Expect a wait here on the weekends, but it's worth it. Service was great too, kept the coffee full.
name: Bryan

text: Philadelphia is a great place for food and nightlife. There's a lot of things I miss about living in this unique and adventurous city, but there is nothing I miss more than going to champs diner for breakfast. This is a small and very cute diner located by Cecil B. Moore and Broad Street, right in the midst of Temple University. It's open until about 3pm every day. On the outside it looks like nothing special, but inside lies a homey atmosphere and great food. The wait was about 15-20 minutes on Sunday around brunch time, which is not too shabby for brunch in the city. I like this place because there's a dedicated place to sit and wait, and a lot of places in the city don't have that option. I ordered my western omelette (ham,peppers, onions, and tomatoes), and it comes with home fries with peppers and onions, and wheat toast with butter and jam. I also ordered the homemade pink lemonade. I absolutely loved everything. The food was delicious and everything I have dreamed about since moving away from the city. My boyfriend got the chicken and waffles, which is one of our favorites. The chicken is breaded beautifully and has a nice crunchy texture. The sauce that it comes with has a little kick to it and is too good! The waffle was soft and fluffy. You have the option of having whipped cream, strawberries, or other toppings on the waffle, but we chose to get it plain with powdered sugar. Overall,  I highly recommend this place for a quick bite. Try their specials, they are out of this world!
name: Melissa

text: Went with family on a Sunday and it was louder than I expected. The food was good and the service was easygoing. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Food was fresh and service was quick. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. A very pleasant experience. Nice little spot, decent portions too. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text: They have a wide selection of teas and are very friendly! The teas themselves are delicious and they also have smoothies and a selection of vegan and non vegan food. There also sell the tea by loose leaf- if you like tea or are wanting to try something new id definitely recommend!
name: Jalia

text: WOW, what an amazingly delicious and FUN restaurant! Came here on a Monday night on the recommendation of a friend and the wonderful Yelp reviews and we couldn't have picked a better place! All the servers were friendly and knowledgeable, and service was impeccable. Food was delicious: crab cakes, jambalaya pasta and jambalaya with dirty rice. And the muffins that they serve ahead of the meal are to die for - 5 different kinds and 2 of each, so TEN muffins for the 3 of us! Each one was better than the next. The highlight for me was in the middle of the meal, they give you a folded piece of paper that says "don't open until you hear music", and then all of a sudden, the music begins to play and the whole restaurant joins in singing and each waiter comes by to "toast" you. So fun. Very memorable dining experience. Wish we lived closer cause I can't wait to go back!
name: E

text: Quick cheap take out. Made the mistake of getting an appetizer and entree, was far too much food for one person. Not the best Chinese food in the world, but it's good for price time and proximity to campus
name: Megan

text: This is a 24 hour establishment located in the Grand Sierra Resort.  The server was extremely accommodating and seated me right away.   A great place for a full meal or a snack.   I was just a little bit hungry so decided to try the shrimp cocktail which is a pretty good deal for only $5!   Served in a large martini glass and on a small bed of lettuce, you get a pretty good amount of small shrimp for $5.  Cocktail sauce comes on top, and you can certainly ask for it on the side.  Definitely recommend the cafe as a "sit-down" alternative to the 24 hour bakery/cafe express, which is also good but more of a grab-n-go place.
name: Kalliope

text:
I've had a couple of my birthday dinners here. But, I have always gone here ever since I moved to Nevada as a kid. We mostly enjoyed how it is located within Summit and by all the stores we normally shopped from. The environment is nice, and their menu covers a wide array of food. There's pasta, burgers, pizza, tacos, etc. I can't forget about the liquor that they have, since the bar takes up almost half of this place. 

For appetizers, I always have to get the avocado egg rolls with the tasty dipping sauce it comes with. As for entrees, their jambalaya is to die for! It has the perfect amount of kick and portion is great, that I always have some to take home. I cannot leave a review without mentioning their famous pizookies. Those desserts are sooo delicious, and won't compare to pizookies in other restaurants. I always get the monkey bread one, but I do try out the trio sometimes. 

Ps. I've been an avid supporter of this restaurant. My BJ's rewards card has given me plenty of free meals and desserts the past few years. I advise you sign up free for the card and receive some deals you can't pass up. They also have online ordering, which is so convenient for people! I will continuously come here, I've never had an issue here.
name: Cheena

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. For a busy night they handled it okay. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Not bad for a quick meal. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text: Food is always good and you can't beat their the Taco Tuesday special!
name: Kitty

text: This is an adorable little cafe with a great menu!  I had the crab cake Benedict and my friend had the BBQ shrimp and grits.  Their grits are wonderful and creamy and the crab cake was delish!  They place the crab cakes and perfectly poached eggs on a croissant and topped it with a slightly spicy hollandaise.  It was perfect for me!  My friend said her shrimp and grits were amazing.  The service was friendly and the music they were playing was great.  Definite go!!!
name: Mary Beth

text: Excellent food & service.  In town for two nights. Tonight we shared small plates.  Tomorrow night will share entrees.
name: Kim

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Not a bad stop, just not one I'm rushing to repeat.
name: User

text: I finally tried chicken shawarma here and it was delicious! My wife and I recently moved to this area and this is walking distance for us which is great! Both of us are big fans of Mediterranean food and having this nearby is nice. We also got an order of Greek fries which were good but needed some spicy seasoning!
name: Ketan

text: The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. It was crowded but still moved along. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Pretty happy with it overall. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: I love this place, the restaurant side is amazing.  Service is always good, and the salad bar is a welcome blast from the past.  They offer a few specials including a 2 for $35 dinner special that include the endless salad bar and dessert and two entrees.  The gnocchi and meatballs are not to miss!  Located in a shopping strip mall, you may not expect the upscale, yet casual dining room, but it awaits you!  The warm bread rolls are a nice compliment to your soon to be delicious meal!  Manga!
name: Cory

text: First time at BLT... great experience! Sunday brunch was fantastic! They kept the mimosas flowing.... the food was great...the service was fast  and friendly considering they were super busy! One of the better places I've been for brunch in downtown St. Louis. They are a must try! S/O to Dan....Best Server-Bartender EVER!!!!!
name: Michelle

text: Excellent service. Kept my tea full and brought extra glass of ice without asking. Plenty of menu choices for everyone in our party. Menu prices may seem high for lunch, once the plate arrives you will understand why. Hearty portions. I had a full dinner with my leftovers.  A pleasant experience will return.
name: Julie

text:
45 minutes for one sandwich
Haven't seen employees work this slow in a long long time. 
Good to see city work ethics spilling over into parts of the county. 
I bet this location doesn't make it threw the year.
name: Echo

text: Actually really good!  I didn't like the veggie burger, it was too salty.  Everything else was really good!
name: Latoya

text: I had an awesome birthday dinner here!! Incredibly festive drinks, delicious food, and fun environment. Definitely a memorable experience and will come back very soon! Not very crowded on a Wednesday night, but nice to have the whole section for my goup.
name: Karen

text: Great food. Excellent service!!! Nick and Julie were awesome. Place was packed, but we were taken care of very well. Would give more stars if possible!
name: Darren

text: Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Food was good and came out fast. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text:
New place, still sorting the table assignments and wait staff 
The charred pizza crust was tasty but I'm kinda sorta deep dish guy so not the best when it comes to judging thin crust
On tap Beer selection was pretty good, I had my old standby Cronic Ale from Carlsbad's Pizza Port. Since this was first actual seating after being told a couple of nights before the wait would be 30-40 minutes, I would definitely recommend making a reservation as it fills up snowbirds and trendy hipster types
name: Charles

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine..
name: User

text: Great southern menu. Some of the best shrimp & grits I've had in years! Beef brisket sandwich is strong + great back deck with bar and cornhole.
name: Kurt

text:
Amazing find. Was rolling round outside the normal areas of New Orleans and found this great little place. 

Breakfast was great and the locals are friendly as well. Stole some of my spouses crawfish and spinach omelet and immediately wanted one myself. 

So going back tomorrow for my own

Go Saints Go
name: Scott

text: I've only been here once I think.  I got a roasted veggie wrap & a latte, & both were delicious!!  I'll definitely be back!
name: Christine

text: Edit: My wife and I came back this place because they always do it right. They entered our order wrong, but, before we ever even noticed it, the manager came by to correct the issue and comp our app. We told her that was completely unnecessary, but she was glad to take care of us. That's great customer service and the food was good as always.
name: Eric

text: Finally a great chettinad buffet in the philly suburbs! Very well run buffet with great authentic south indian items. Their speciality is non-veg chettinad though there are plenty of veg items as well. Never seen meaty crab soup (nandu mocha kottai soup being offered for buffet anywhere else. Hope they keep up the quality.
name: Whiterock

text: Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Will be back.
name: User

text:
Summary: Still needs to work out their timing, very slow for their opening weekend. Located in Chinatown with limited parking

Came here around 1 on a Saturday on what I think is their opening weekend. It was fairly packed a d we had to wait 10 min for a table for 2.

We then waited 1 hour for our mango shaved ice. It was very good and luckily we didn't have anywhere to be. Not worth a 1 hour wait, so hopefully they work out their timing.

Mango shaved ice ~14.00 Definitely share this! mango shaved ice that was very smooth but mango flavor is not that strong by itself. Surrounded by mangos and rice balls, topped with mango ice cream
name: Gabriella

text: My wife and I had a date here around a month or so ago.  The service was excellent.  We both enjoyed the ambiance and the drive out to the restaurant.  The food was absolutely spectacular.  Just a terrific experience all around.  We don't have the opportunity to get out together and have it be just the two of us very often so we really do appreciate it when everything goes off without a hitch.  Thanks Ginza!
name: Chris

text:
Had a very rare hankering for BBQ today.  Looked into Yelps reviews of some restaurants around town that could quell the spicy feeling in my ribs.  Found a newer place in town taking the place of an old standby joint called Shari's I believe. I might be wrong with from 25 years of being in the Old Pueblo I kind of remember that place.  
First thing you see when you enter in a young lady at the cash register and ordering area.  Menus are there as well as a black board with the days special.  Kind of pricey on the ribs so I went to my old standard a hamburger with Pepper Jack cheese, aoli sauce, tomato and breaded fried onions.  All stacked  high with some real delicious blend of tastes.  It came with the most delicious fries.  Hubby order the pulled pork sandwich with a BBQ Sauce.  It was a bit dry for my taste because he didn't want the BBQ on the bun itself.  So he opted for it on the side.  He enjoyed it.  It's very small eat in area a couple of booths and some stools for counter eating.  However, they do have a pretty large cozy outdoor venue to eat at.  It is still too hot so we opted for indoors.  I noticed other people ordered the ribs, brisket and looked like they were gobbling it up.  They have platters that offer pulled pork, ribs, chicken, bread and condiments.  Enjoyed getting away from my comfort zone and trying something a little different.
name: Cindy

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: Been here once before and got the Imeruli, bread with cheese in it to go. It was 10/10... went again for dinner last night. Got the kebabs, they were big portions. The Adjaruli, bread boat with the egg was great. Place is a nice spot. Their breads are the best, like a pastry almost. Go give it a whirl.
name: William

text: I was here for a temporary assignment with the Air Force just two weeks. My family and I decided since it's a staple in all our travels we'd go to fracker barrel it never lets us down...well except this time. After a 15-20 minute wait we were sat, waitress was ok but not personable. 45 minutes to get out food no salads no muffins no cornbread no soup...everything came out at once. Although the order was wrong and we had to send her back to fix it. The food was not as expected like the usual Cracker Barrel. The house salad had no cheese no onion no croutons my country fried steak had no gravy. The waitress never brought us silverware so I asked, she told me people have been complaining about the dirtiness would we mind plastic ware at least we know it's clean?!?! Really...Kids dumplings were not fully cooked and the waitress billed us wrong causing a problem at the register. I've been to 28 states and 32 Cracker Barrel's this is by far the worst...although this won't deter me from going to new and old ones alike I plead you if you read these reviews take my advice and pass.
name: Daniel

text: I have been coming here for years and  get salads often  and pay close to 11 dollars and last night and tonight my salad was so small it looked like a side salad. Very disappointed. They are making them smaller and they are not worth the money and the service is getting bad. They are losing a lot of their good help.....
name: Cheryl

text:
I really appreciate the gluten free options for BBQ. My husband is celiac and the dry rub was recommended and they noted in our order to change gloves. There were 2 sauces that we're not GF, but I can't recall which they were. We ordered the 1/2 rack and it was delicious!

I really appreciate the large dining space and separate bar area.
name: Kristina

text: This is the worst Wendy's ever.  Same as all of the others complained.  Waited 20 minutes.  Said hello, honked horn.  Only to be told to "wait a minute" with an attitude.   Critical Mistake.   I drove off.  Considering all of the complaints listed for this store and the way I was treated, I will call corporate.   They should know what a mess this franchise owner has made and pull the store from them. I grew up in this industry and I never told a paying customer to wait a minute. How RUDE.   These young kids have no idea what respect is and they will never garner it because of the way they hold themselves.  such a pity their mama and Daddy should've raised them better.
name: Dave

text:
I've been here wayyyyyy many times before and the food used to be great but now, you pay around $16+ for a dish and they literally give you just a tiny amount of it. (just good enough for  2 people). Went there with my group of friends, one dish isnt even enough for 3-4 people. food isnt worth it for the price. (Wish I took pictures of the food to show here.)There are tons of other best korean places to go too in Edmonton. Plus, the service can be good on some days but most of the time its shitty now. 

The only good thing Hanjan can offer is that its open pretty late compared to other Korean places.
name: Czaina

text: Somehow hadn't been to this location before, but it's right around the corner now, so I had to check it out. Definitely recommend the sugoyaki, which is a beef roll. It sounds weird because it is, but it's delicious. Get the long roll, though; the cuts in the hand roll are unwieldy. I can endorse the San Francisco and the dragon roll as well. I'm not entirely sure what's going on with the tempura upside down shrimp "nigiri," but it was quite tasty. We've actually been back at least twice more this past month--they're a little short-staffed right now, so it might take a minute, but it's worth the wait.
name: Patrick

text: I've had the pleasure of having a few lunch meetings at this location of Grimaldi's.  Every time I've been in, it's been a wonderful experience. The manager, Giovanna, has been such a delight every single time. She is so personable and enjoyable to be around. I highly recommend coming in!!
name: Tara

text: Bunches of things I miss about Tampa since moving away, and Brocato's is definitely one of them! By far the best Cuban I've ever had!!! The medium is still 2 meals... especially with the devil crab (which is a must). Make sure to get the Big devil crab opposed to the 2 smalls... it's filled to the max with the most delicious crab concoction. Chips and a drink are included with every meal. Always been pretty busy when I've gone so might wanna order ahead. Also, delivery is available through Uber Eats. We got there at 4:45 yesterday and grabbed a table outside since we had the pups with us. We finished our meals right as they were closing. They ended up calling us over the loud speaker to come back inside... we thought we were in trouble lol... or they wanted to pet the pups. They ended up giving us several extra devil crabs and potato balls! So incredibly nice and generous of them! All of the staff was really helpful and the gentleman by the door even situated my meal for me since I missed when they called my number. I still have my family and friends in Tampa so I visit pretty regularly. Brocato's will definitely be my Tampa staple from here on out... can't believe I let 2 years go by since my last phenomenal Cuban!
name: Erika

text:
M.L. Rose is one of my favorite go-to spots in Nashville for a reliably good burger, so I was excited to try their newest location.

We started with the bleu cheese fries, which were really, really good...and I'm usually not a big fan of bleu cheese. The manager on duty brought us a second order because she didn't think the original was up to their standard. I won't turn extra fries down!

I ordered my usual: the Five Alarm. The burger wasn't as spicy as I remember it being at the other two locations. I wasn't crazy about the raw jalapeños -- I prefer the standard pickles variety. But the burger itself was delicious.

I also tried a bite of the "ANM.L.-Style" burger, which was perfectly cooked and very flavorful, thanks in part to the grilled onions. I've never been to an In-n-Out (which inspired the name of this burger). But if it's half as good as M.L. Rose's, I'll be impressed.

I finished my meal with a helping of the always-great sweet potato waffle fries. They pair so well with the spicy Five Alarm burger.

I liked the atmosphere in this location. Being in a new building, the vibe is a bit more modern and upscale, but it still retains that classic M.L. Rose character from the other locations.

My biggest gripe: the flies. I've never seen so many flies inside an enclosed sit-down restaurant before. This definitely needs addressing. Otherwise, I was impressed with this new location.
name: John

text: The sound on all the TVs in the gym doesn't work.  Apparently it has never worked since opening day 4 months ago. When I notified the front desk they said it was the first they heard of this. This is certainly not true as a few other guests who have been here before told me that management is aware but has not address it.  Very surprising for a resort of this level to not have any real working monitors in the gym.  It's too bad the gym is very nice but this will not be as enjoyable for me for the next few days as I work out.
name: Michelle

text: If you're looking for a great place with excellent Mexican food, look no further! My fiancé and I decided to try this place out after he saw a bacon wrapped burrito on instagram and this place was tagged. Yes, you read that correctly- a bacon wrapped burrito. Upon arriving, we loved the location. Fishers is so welcoming and parking was extremely easy to find, and FREE. The service here is counter style so you order and are given a number. We both ordered the bacon wrapped burrito with chicken inside. There is a salsa bar where you are given cups to select your own salsas. The house salsa is very unique but has great taste! Our absolute favorite was the jalapeño ranch, it was incredible. After about 15 minutes of munching on chips a worker came over to our table carrying to trays with a one burrito split in half. He told us that the kitchen made a mistake on the meat inside our burritos but that we could have this one for free in the mean time. We were so understanding and would have just sat continuing to eat chips, but that was extremely nice of them! We ended up getting full on just that half and ending up being able to take our full burritos home. The halves of the burrito that we did try were so good! The bacon adds a flavor to the burrito that I have never had before. There is an equal ratio of all the ingredients inside so it's not too much of one thing. I love the avocado that is inside! Every worker that we encountered was extremely nice and working hard in the kitchen or keeping the space clean. There is a seating area, then there is also a bar top that allows you to watch the chefs working on your food right in front of you. This place is clean, great service, and excellent authentic Mexican food!i
name: Brianna

text: We were passing through and our hotel suggested this restaurant. When arriving minutes from our hotel we decided to sit outside, it was a beautiful night and the venue was very nice, fireplace, bar and very spacious. We were immediately taken to our table that was dirty with the previous guests. We gathered by the table as we waited for the servers to clean the table, something that should have been done before they took us to be seated. The menus was great, so much to chose from. Our waitress came up and introduced herself. Kalin was not friendly, no warm smile, not welcoming at all. She took our drink order and said there was a special menu. When she came back to the table with our drinks she didn't have the menu, so my friend asked for it and she said, "oh I have to see where it is." The four of us ordered. My friend told her no blue cheese with her Wedge salad because she did not like blue cheese. I ordered a steak salad, medium. My husband ordered the ribeye special, medium. He asked for sweet potato fries, she said no substitutes. Flat out no apologies just that she would try. Again no smiles, and very uncomfortable for all of us. Our food was brought back. The salad that was ordered had blue cheese on it.:( Her pot pie was not good, not much flavor and it was topped with something that looked like a croissant. My steak was rare as my husbands was also. His steak was made up of about 3/4 fat, I am not exaggerating. My steak was extremely tough.  Our salad plates were not cleared until we asked to take them. She came back and did ask how everything was, again just out of obligation not feeling like she really cared. I wanted to say something but my husband said to just leave it alone. He didn't think she would have done anything. I am in the business and I felt it was my duty to speak out, but honestly Kalin  was so unconnected I decided to leave a review. Fortunately for her she was left a 20% tip per the husbands.  I hope she reads this and changes the way she treats her guests. Maybe she just doesn't like what she does. We all agreed that we would not be going back.
name: Joanne

text: Went for Sunday brunch, relaxed and chill atmosphere. I got the chicken and biscuit breakfast and I LOVED it! Much better than chicken in waffles in my opinion but I'm obsessed with biscuits. Ask for a sample of the 1205 liquors - they are all so good! Hubby got the fish tacos and they were very tasty too. My cocktail was very refreshing for a nice summer day. A storm rolled in during our meal and the ambiance of the restaurant is super cool when it's dark out! Great date night location.
name: Marcy

text:
Been looking at trying this place out for some time now and glad that I finally did! 

The place is very cute! It has both inside and outside seating. We decided to sit outside because it was a warm evening. They had a live singer who was singing some jazz classics as well as some Christmas tunes- perfect for a December evening! 

For our starter, we had the hummus. It was delicious. The naan might have been the best I've ever had. 

My parents both got the fish and chips and they said it was delicious. (I used to live in England and they've both visited there, so that's saying something!) My mom said that the tartar sauce was one of the best that she's ever had. 

As for me, I had the Cocoa Cumin Pork Chops. It was so flavorful and delicious. I don't normally order pork chops when I go out, but decided to get something different and I'm glad I did! 

Our server was wonderful! Always refilled our water cups and was happy to answer any questions we had about the menu! 

Would definitely come back!
name: Ali

text:
Very mediocre and pretty expensive. The menu item was titled "Prime Coulette Steak" 
Description: "fingerling potatoes, pickled onion and house steak sauce" I ordered the steak medium like always in places like this. It was well done. 
It seems every time I'm at some wannabe nice place that serves the steak already cut it's just crap. The outside of the steak is dark like it had a good char but it actually seems artificial. Like they ordered it from some meal prep/delivery service. Then they slather it with some overwhelming sauce to hide the fact that it's not a prime cut and that it was probably seared at 6:00 this morning or, sprayed with something to give it the appearance of being seared at 800degrees. This was NOT prime cut and it was worse than Sizzler. I sent it back and it came back again nearly well done but almost cold ant super tough. What gives?
name: John

text: Hate to write a negative review about this place because my first 3 meals were quite good. However, decided to try their breakfast out and it was so bad that I couldn't not review it. For starters, they handed me a small plate that included eggs, bacon and French toast. Instead of giving me a separate plate for my French toast they set it on top of my bacon and eggs so I had to request a separate plate because I like syrup but not on my eggs or bacon. More importantly, their was something wrong with the bacon. I couldn't even swallow my first bite so I had to very unlady like spit it back on to the plate. It was inedible, it seemed cooked perfectly but the  meat tasted bad. I had never had bacon taste like that before and my meals were always tasty in previous visits. Also, they keep ketchup on the tables right next to the windows so the sun heats it up and hot ketchup is not appetizing. I do plan on giving it another try because this kind of thing can happen to any restaurant and they did apologize and take it off the bill and that goes a long way with me.
name: jessica

text: Ate here a few evenings ago. Just two of us at a high-top near the bar. Admittedly, the setting is really interesting. The bar is awesome, and the place has a nice vibe. We purchased the 6-beer sampler, which included the seasonal. The beers were generally fine, each more-or-less true to its style. Nothing notable, but all pretty well crafted. The food was just ok. More than anything, the food was served cold, and the server was completely indifferent to us-- to the point of rude. I get that this place is really busy; and perhaps the staff is overworked. But it's not as if we got a discount for that. We paid full price, and we would have liked competent, professional, and friendly service. We got none of that. As a caveat, let me say this: If you love the NoLa waterfront; if you enjoy the area where the French Quarter begins to transition into the French Market area, then you'll probably dig Crescent City Brewhouse. I personally think NoLa is kind of a dump; and this place didn't do anything to improve my impression. So again, if you really like NoLa and are fine to sub-par service, descent beer, and cold food, then you may really like Crescent City Brew.
name: Rob

text: I really enjoy UC and all it has to offer. For moms who work from home but also have kids to take care of and entertain, it's a great spot for mom & kid. My little guy gets to make new friends, play with toys we don't have at home, test his knowledge, and mom gets some stuff done for work! The staff is always kind & engages with the kids - which helps know our kids are safe and cared for even if mom occasionally has her head down at a laptop.

text: I won't go there for Korean food. They don't know what they are cooking.. we ordered 4dishes(Kimbap, beef soup, soy bean soup and bibimbap) and didn't finish any of them. Very disappointed. Don't expect to eat Korean food. No flavor in their dishes.

text: Been twice. Really good food. Last time I got the steak quesadilla and it was really good. Food comes out fast and they are super helpful when ordering.

text:
This is my absolute favorite Mexican restaurant in Tucson. Literally the best salsa that I've ever had. It's got a perfect kick to it and is the perfect consistency. Anything you get here will be amazing. The drinks are great, and I also love the tamales! My mouth is watering just writing this review haha. 

Also the atmosphere is so amazing, I love the overall feel of this place. Seriously check it out!

text: Fun, vibrant place. The decor is awesome. The food is very good, but somehow the service seemed off to me, which is why I gave 4 instead of five stars. The chips are amazing-best I've ever had. The big guacamole bowl is very good and perfect for a small group. The pitcher of margaritas only gives you an extra half glass of margarita...so you mind as we'll order individual ones. Margaritas are authentic and not too sweet. Our table had chicken tacos (person said best taco ever), shrimp ceviche, chicken enchiladas (delicious), and the veg tacos (good). The waitress seemed distracted-only negative comment.

text: Gave previous bad review because of service. Updating to five star because of Customer Service and quick response to feedback. Compliment to management for caring and responding. They not only reached out, apologized, working hard to make sure this does not happen again. We are definitely going back.

text: I love it!!! I could literally eat this everyday. There customer service is pretty great too! Thanks for suggesting the hot Cheetos to my burrito

text: I went to Rex for the first time for Brunch on Sunday 2/24 with a good friend of mine. I have been informed in the past that Rex actually has great burgers, but I was unaware of it being such a great brunch spot! My friend and I both ordered the fried chicken and waffles made with the typical egg Benedict sauce. So delicious. My only complaint was that the waiter did not remember to bring my friend his coffee or his appetizer. He said that it was busy, but the place seemed small to me. Other than that the hostess Paige was excellent :)

text: Very disappointing! Came here around 2pm to find out they didn't open til 5. Came back at 11 pm to find out some company rented out the entire place and we couldn't come in until 12:30! When we were here earlier there was nothing posted mentioning the party. You should have the bottom downstairs open! Too bad we didn't get to try anything.
name: Amber

text:
I've known about this food truck for years and I'm kicking myself for not trying it sooner. I had never actually physically seen it until today. It was in front of the Brandon Oriental Market on Pauls Drive between Brandon Blvd and Oakfield Drive. I feel like it's a hidden gem, even though they visit many parts of Brandon and the name is out there. I just haven't been to any of those other spots. 

Fresh Hawaiian food is their specialty. I was blown away by what I tasted today. I've never had Hawaiian food before but I could tell it was very authentic just by reading the reviews. What I love is that the food is unique and full of flavor. The side dishes are very solid. I think any fried rice (kimchi or coconut) that you choose will be a winner. I tried my husband's kimchi fried rice from his Hawaiian mixed plate and it was so wonderful. 

So, I dropped off my husband's food and took the rest to my mother's house. Mom loved the South Pacific wings! She commented every now and then when she got that little kick of heat, but it was sweet and spicy for the most part. I had to try one and it was very good. We shared some of my shrimp and coconut fried rice. My coconut fried rice soaked up the sweet chili sauce from the shrimp which made it even more tasty. The whole plate was amazing including the citrus ginger slaw. I could eat that slaw every day. I love that it has no mayo. The ginger and citrus flavors were very present. Loved all of it!! 

My husband called as we were finishing our meal. He wanted to know where I got it from. He was pretty impressed with the flavors. Just hearing that made me happy because it's very rare to hear him rave about any kind of food. It looks like we'll be visiting South Pacific Grill on a regular basis. I was told that they are there every Sunday. It will be our go-to spot for all things Hawaiian.
name: Karen

text:
Outstanding. 

Bacon oyster sandwich alone is beyond amazing. 

Toss in the rest of the menu and you won't find another place better in NOLA.
name: D

text: Had dinner for four last night....was not impressed. Shrimp soup sounded good but shrimp was rubbery and few! Lamb shanks, bland but large corn pieces were delicious. The appetizers were good. I left thinking it was over priced and bland. Maybe just a bad night but not real busy.
name: Donna

text:
Update to previous review. I was in the neighborhood and craved seafood so I figured I'd give El Pescador a second chance. THUD again.

I ordered shrimp (camaron) and octopus (pulpo) Al Mojo de Ajo. Now the foundation of al mojo de ajo is chopped garlic sautéed in butter after which the seafood is added. Various cooks dress the dish with chopped parsley, chopped cilantro, green onion or crumbled toasted dried chile de arbol; Rick Bayless even floated a recipe where chipotle en adobado were added but the core is chopped garlic sautéed in butter. Not at El Pescador -- their "Al Mojo de Ajo" was some weird cream-based sauce with the barest hint of garlic if any. It was like going to a place, ordering a burger, and being served ground turkey sloppy joe on white bread as "our interpretation of a burger".

Two stars not a tad more. And if you really have a craving for caldo de mariscos try Panderia La Paloma where their Caldo de Camarones (shrimp soup) completely smokes El Pescador.
name: Ed

text:
Good tacos, served quickly and with a smile.

A menu with pricing would be nice (tacos are $2 each, I learned).

Doubling up on tortillas also keeps them from falling apart, as these single-wrap ones did.

Carne asada was well-browned and delicious. Al pastor was just ok. Chorizo could've been spicier, but the salsa verde definitely made up for the lack.

I'll stop by again.

text: This is now my new favorite food stop in the area. Excellent service, wonderful view, good prices, good food. I love watching people sail and being right by the water. 10/10 recommend

text: I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Food was good and came out fast. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Not bad for a quick meal. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. text: I've been here a few times, and the last time was my final time. The chicken is okay, although the chicken fingers/tenders are better. I make a mean fried chicken. I have found the chicken here is void of any real seasoning. Anytime I have to add salt to my chicken, it's not seasoned well. The sides are also okay. The loaded potato salad was not very good and again void of salt and pepper. The hot sauce and corn bread muffins are good; but $2.00 for a muffin, that should come with your order, is outrageous.  I would like to see this place rethink the pricing and the taste of their food. On a more positive note, they have very good customer service.

text: Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Nothing about the space rlly stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. text: I can't get over how lovely this place is. The Turkish delights are all delicious. Every drink and tea we have tried has been tasty and unique. The Istanbul fog is my favorite. The owners are very friendly and every time we have gone so far we have gotten impeccable service. Can't recommend enough.

text:
I found this place on Yelp, it wasn't a place I had bookmarked so when I walked up I was surprised at how long the line was. For some reason I end up  picking places that everyone wants to go. The wait was pretty long, I think it was 45 minutes. The food was good but not good enough to stand in line for 45 minutes again. One plus though, is that they sell Bloody Marys so I they made me a Bloody Mary to go so I could have one while I waited.

When we finally made it inside the restaurant is very small but really cute. The servers are extremely nice, friendly and attentive. I decided to get the Cochon Eggs Benedict it's made with braised pork on a biscuit with 2 soft poached eggs, hollandaise & side of fries. My meal was delicious, full of flavor , tender pork but it could have been a little warmer but the flavor made up for the temperature. My friend decided to get the Cochon poy boy and wasn't impressed. It had the braised pork with a cole slaw on top of the pork but there was hardly any cole slaw on it, maybe like a tablespoon so it was a bit dry. Not the meat but the sandwich itself since there wasn't a sauce or much cole slaw. So she asked for something to add like aioli and they gave her jus. My meal was good  but she didn't enjoy hers. 

Over the experience was good but I wouldn't stand in a 45 min to hour line to dine here again.

text: Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. text: If you want a lot of food, I mean a lot of food, this is the place to go. The portions are gigantic; however, the restaurant does not skimp on quality. The chicken was moist and had great flavors. For breakfast, I ordered the chicken asparagus hash and subbed sweet potatoes for red potatoes. Delicious- the layering of flavors was outstanding. My dining companion had the meatloaf for dinner. It was a two dinner portion and a different hash style egg breakfast. We both took our breakfast leftovers home. text:
UPDATE FOR LUNCH: 

Based on my lunch experience I'd drop Ichichoro to a 4 Star instead of 4.5.  We came a little before 12:30 in the afternoon hoping to beat the lunch rush and avoid waiting since we only had 1 hour. Restaurant is 10 minutes drive from my workplace and we were able to eat  and come back to work before the hour was up. So service is pretty fast!  We were seated immediately and all tables except one 4 seater was taken when we arrived.
Been wanting to try their rice bowls since they first started featuring them but just never been able to make it for lunch, as the rice bowls are not part of their dinner service. 

My coworker and I both split the Cubano bao buns with the side of tostones/crispy fried green plaintain (11 dollars), along with the ropa vieja (Cuban style shredded"seasoned"  beef) rice bowl with veggies - 12 dollars. I put "seasoned" because the beef lacked the flavor that a true Cuban ropa vieja should have. It tasted like watery bland shredded meat. Best I could compare is when you make beef stew in the crockpot and you add too much water and the seasoning doesn't stick to the meat and you over cook it and it's overly shredded and holds on to that lightly flavored water. The rice was really over cooked and had some clumps. Food temperature was not warm for the rice or meat and I like items such as rice and meat to be warm when I consume. Seems like my bowls was just sitting out already made waiting to be picked up. One thing I did like was that the bowl had a huge portion of vegetables including pickled vegetables. Could use some more korean gochujang sauce to help add some flavor and more spice.  Highly disappointed though overall with the flavor and taste of the bowl. Would not get again. I regretted not getting their "Karage" fried chicken  rice bowl instead. I would not venture to try again and vow to stick to their ramen only.

So glad My coworker and I split two things instead of ordering our own entrees. I would have been more upset if I had a whole portion of  the rice bowl alone and nothing else. The Cubano bao buns along with tostones that came with buns saved the  meal from being a terrible meal. The tostones were perfectly crispy and honestly taste better than most authentic  mom n pop Spanish restaurants I go to. I can tell they are fried to ordered and made fresh. Not made before hand and fried then refried when ordered, like a lot of  places do.  I did miss the negi-mayu (creamy aioli sauce) that is served with tostones, fried yuca and sweet potatoe app during dinner.  The bao bun was the perfect rendition of a Asian fusion Cuban sandwich with  its thick cut of pork belly and deli style sliced ham. Wish these were served at dinner too! I tried the frozen Kirin (5 dollars) because I'll admit that the Instagram posts got me! I would say it's very instagrammable but would rather stick to regular poured Kirin. I  don't like the water down taste of the frozen Kirin on top. I like the full bodiness of the beer that's underneath the ice. Just think of when your soda or any drink gets frozen a little bit there is still some liquid that did not freeze. You drink the unfrozen portion that is sweeter and richer then the ice melts and what melts barely any sweetness or flavor.
name: Mishka

text: Ordered a bacon breakfast burrito in the drive thru.  The menu board shows a price of $4.99.  The intercom is faint and I can barely make out a voice.  Drive up to the window and the order taker says $7.00.  I tell him your menu board says $4.99 and we go back and forth with him insisting $7.00. I tell him I come in regular for the breakfast burrito and it's always $4.99 plus tax so the total should be roughly $5.50.  So he says well you pulled out a $20 and I say well that makes a lot of sense that you're charging me $7.00 because I'm paying with a $20, so if I pay with a $10 what will it be?  So he says $6.07.  Astounding!  I call him an idiot and I just drive off.  He was probably pocketing the extra $ he was charging.  But that's kinda par for this Viva's, the order takers are inconsistent in what they charge, some charge you the price listed on the menu board others charge an amount pulled out of their butt.  Sometimes you have a long wait, sometimes the intercom isn't working, sometimes the order you receive is wrong.  As others have said the customer service sucks.  The owners don't seem to care.  Makes you question if the kitchen is clean cause of the other inconsistencies.  I'm done with this place, won't be back!

Check this place out; support local business, and eat some really yummy food.
