text:
I really do like the food. Everything I've gotten has been delicious but the quality over the last year has been dwindling. The most troubling is that there always appears to only be one person preparing all of the orders every time I'm in there which may explain why the food hasn't been consistent and the wait times are long.

I still believe it's worth ordering from here. We love the chicken shawarma, hummus, baklava, Syrian fries, just to name a few.

I hope they are able to add more people consistently to their kitchen to improve these inefficiencies. It's one of my go-to's for a good comfort meal

text: Horrible food, beans are dry, terrible service, no hot sauce. Taco Bell, have visited hundreds of Taco Bells, this is in my list of 3 worst taco bells I've visited.  Food, service everything was horrible.

text:
My cousin and I came here for brunch on our last day in philly and loved it! We brought our dog and the owner was so nice, he sat us in a comfortable area and was very attentive and helpful even though it was extremely busy. 

The cafe was very cozy, staff was super nice and the food was delicious.
name: Rebecca

text:
YUMMY!! And piping hot food!! Lovey outdoor patio with soothing water fountain against the brick wall. 

Suggestion - While we enjoyed sitting outside on the patio, the chairs are not very comfortable.
name: Kimberly

text:
My boyfriend and I came in on a cold November night expecting a sushi restaurant.. well, it's not really just sushi, although there is some upstairs at their sushi bar, but Little did we know what a treat we were in for downstairs... 
  So we walk in, sit down at the small cozy bar just inside the front door, check out the menu, and realize this is much more than sushi but a Chinese restaurant at heart. But not just any Chinese restaurant. This is authentic traditional family owned delicious cuisine.  The owners were obviously working and we had impeccable service from them and their staff. We are foodies so we venture off from the usual well known Americanized dishes. Let me tell you... 
  The spicy white fish stew.  A Szechwan dish with white fish, Napa cabbage, green onion, chili, etc, and love. It was absolutely one of the best dishes I've ever had in a restaurant. ever.  Just enough spice to make you sweat but not harm your tastebuds or the flavor of the dish. Served with white rice and we also ordered the sautéed spinach with garlic to accompany it. Just amazing. Family style servings so it's great to share. So.. If you like seafood, spice, vegetables, stew, and great service then you need to come here and get that white fish stew. Worth every gd penny in my opinion.  I'm going to try the Kung Pao rabbit next...
name: Cat

text:

text: Had lunch there today.  Ordered a Ricotta pizza and my daughter got Kobe sliders. My pizza came out first and after the first bite I asked for peppers and Parmesan cheese.  It didn't have a lot of flavor.  I got the  peppers but was told they charge for the Parmesan cheese. What kind of pizza place does that?  I added salt and pepper and the pizza was much better.  Did without the parm-it was a matter of principle!  Then my daughter got her sliders and asked for ketchup.  They have six different kinds of sliders but they don't have any ketchup in their restaurant.  How do you serve burgers without ketchup?   I just don't understand the logic of not having basic stuff available for customers.   While the food was ok, we couldn't get past the other stuff. We won't go out of our way to come back.

text: Went here for brunch and the food was amazing! Good drinks, friendly staff, comfy booths and I will be back.

text:
Great addition to downtown Clearwater. The food can be a hit or miss at times, but to be honest which restaurant has the best dish every time?

Our favorite is the duck brussel sprouts. They are THE BOMB. The curry dish is also good with short rib.

But really if you get the Brussels Sprouts that's all you need to know about this place, the atmosphere is also quite nice and the remodel and back room we're done so well, kudos to the owners.

text: It's nice to have something new in Pottstown. We both liked the beer we ordered and our dinner was good. I had the fish taco special and my husband had the sausage sandwich. Both tasty. Really good fries.
name: Shelley

text:
My wife and I just ate here for the first time.  The service was welcoming and very helpful, the food was simply awesome.  We both had steak bowls with black beans, rice and various vegetables as well as my favorite, sweet plantains :) yum, yum.  The steak was flavorful and tender, the rice and beans were great and the vegetables were fresh.  The servings are plentiful and most definitely filling.   The inside and out are clean and quiet, very relaxing.   We were really pleased with our experience, food quality, food quantity and service.   The pricing is reasonable for the type, quantity and quality of food.   If you haven't tried this place yet, don't wait any longer, you will not be disappointed.

ENJOY
name: Bobby

text: In the restaurant, there was my family and another family, so it was not overwhelmingly busy at the time we arrived. We were given our drinks, but that was the only thing that came in a timely manner. text:
I really wanted to like Otaku, I really did. But there was so many disappointments I just couldn't be satisfied. 

Let me begin, I love the location, the design, and the service. I didn't get our servers name, but he was really cool and gave us a lot of help. Now too what I was dissatisfied with:

1. The Menu offering: For dietary reasons, I don't consume pork. While this usually isn't an issue, there were only two options that weren't pork, one of them was broth-less ramen, so no lol. Luckily, We were able to sub the only ramen with chicken broth with chicken instead of pork belly, but it's really frustrating when you have to little to no options - shout-out to the server. 

2. The Ramen itself was okay, I'm sure their pork broth may be better but their chicken broth was very underwhelming. Ramen is all about the broth, and it was a big turn off to not have that, especially given the price. They offer a pork miso broth, I don't see why it would be impossible to add some other chicken broth options to diversify the menu. 

3. To add some flavor, we asked for some hot sauce that they ended up charging us extra for, another frustration. When you're paying 14+ for ramen I don't think it's necessary to charge for some hot-sauce, especially when it's a clear broth that was one of your only options if you still wanted meat. but that may be a little biased of me. 


I really wish Otaku can broaden the menu and do more on the chicken side of ramen. It's so annoying that their menu is overwhelmingly pork heavy, and I've talked to other people who were frustrated about the same thing. Even if you want to focus on pork, I would recommend having one alternative that isn't vegetarian so just give the customers more options..

text:
Pastaria is fine. I'm originally from NY and was excited to try a good, Italian pasta restaurant since Nashville seems to only have the Nouveau Italian food. However, Pastaria just failed to deliver. Contrary to most complaints on Yelp, our service was quite good. We ordered the risotto balls and found that what they lacked in flavor, they tried to cover up with excess cheese. I suppose I was hoping for it to be more like an arancini. It was a fine dish, but a touch of acid or spice was lacking. 

We also ordered the citrus salad, which I quite enjoyed. I'd say this was the most successful dish.

We ordered broccoli and cauliflower sides. Both had great flavor, but the veggies were slightly over cooked. For $7 a piece, it was frustrating to bite into limp broccoli. 

We ordered the cacio e Pepe and the Toasted Linguine and clams. The Cacio e Pepe was the more successful of the two. It had good flavor and was appropriately peppery. However, while good, I was a bit confused as the sauce was more Alfredo like instead of olive oil based which a typical cacio e Pepe is normally. For the linguine, the pasta was cooked correctly but that's about it. The sauce was missing flavor and the clams tasted like they were frozen. I ate a 1/4 of it. This is a skip. 

Finally, we finished our meal with the not tiramisu. This was delicious and by far my favorite. 

Takeaways: as a pasta place, the pasta was the most disappointing. I'd go back for salad and dessert.
name: Maggie

Big smiles greeted me when I went to check on my order, but both staff I addressed had confused looks when I told them our number and showed them our buzzer thing. One was completely cold (lasgna-like dish) and the other was mostly just a corn-bread waffle with a teeny bit of jackfruit and avo in the middle.

Soon after we returned to both our respective homes, my sister and I were texting each other about our upset stomachs. YIKES. Don't want to get graphic. My sister and I both contact the restaurant outside of review sites, and we both did not receive a reply. YIKES again. This was my sister's go-to place. Not sure how I feel about trying again.

text:
Such a disappointing and embarrassing experience. I chose Cooper's Hawk to welcome new members into our family and I am disgusted with the entire experience. Typically CH is relatively consistent, so rather than risk the unknown at a different restaurant, I made a reservation for 5 at 6:45pm. Our reservation being on time was the only thing saving this review with 1 star. 

Once seated we waited 15 minutes for a server to bring water to the table. Five glasses of water  not on a tray, but rather held against her chest; armpit to armpit. She physically pushed my shoulder aside to set  all 5 glasses of water on the table and asked me to pass them around. Another 15 minutes go by, I had to physically get up, walk into the adjacent dining room to locate her and ask that she come to the table to take our drink order. Ten minutes later she brought our wine samples and a beer for my grandfather. Another 10 minutes went by before she asked if we would like wine. Again she brought 5 glasses (wine), pushed my shoulder aside and set all 5 glasses along with the wine carafe in front of me. She then poured the wine and asked that I pass around the glasses. I should note here that we were sitting at a round table for 6, only occupying 5 of the seats. Each time she stepped in between myself and another of my guests when pushing my shoulder. Two orders of bread later and still no orders taken for appetizers or dinner. At this point we were 50 minutes in after being seated.
 
She finally returned and we ordered appetizers for the table. We were told that it would be best to place our dinner orders at the same time, but that orders would not be rushed, so we obliged. One of my guests ordered gnocchi with squash and vegetables; remember this in a few sentences.

15 minutes later appetizers arrived. Again, no tray and carried with her thumbs and fingers gripping the plates. I actually asked her if it would be better for me to move to the empty seat to my right. "No. Just pass this over." Nice.  We dished out appetizers and 5 minutes into eating 2 busboys converged onto our table with our meals. We had barely started eating appetizers, our table was full of empty wine tasting glasses, water glasses, wine glasses, appetizer plates, two empty bread boards, silverware, etc, as nothing had been clearedm

I told the busboys we were not ready for dinner, our server - who was at the table next to us - turned toward our table and the busboys and instructed them "to take the food back". Great. Now our dinner was going to sit under heat lamps for who knows how long.

We actually cleared our own table by stacking all the plates and waited for her to return. Again, 10 minutes later she showed up with busboys in tow, carrying the hot plates with napkins, and barking out "Who had the Salmon? Who had the Grouper?" Etc. When my  89 year old grandfather claimed his meal, the busboy lowered the plate over my grandfather's head, draping the napkin in his face! I pulled the napkin away and told him to put the plate down. 

Remember the gnocchi I mentioned above? The vegetable gnocchi? It was served with chicken. Which, if one wanted the vegetable gnocchi WITH chicken it had to be requested and there was an additional charge for the protein. Not cool when your guest is protein intolerant. My guest was too embarrassed to say anything at the time, given the epic fail that service had been up to that point. Meals that came with mashed potatoes had sat under the heat lamps and created a thick, pudding like skin on the outside. Potato crusted Scallops were dried out and cold. I could go on, but you definitely get then picture by now.

I excused myself immediately after dinner arrived, telling my guests I needed to use the restroom. Instead I went to the hostess and asked to speak to manager. I explained to the manager that I did not wish to address my complaints at the table in front of my guests, nor did I want her to address our server while we were still seated for the meal. I expressed my disgust with the entire evening thus far, expressed my embarrassment, disappointment and the unacceptable manner in which the server physically pushed me. I remained calm and shared that I also work in a customer service based industry. Her response? "Are you drinking wine? I can comp your bottle if you are." Well, our wine was already part of our dinner, given I am (was) a CH Wine Club member. "I am happy to make an adjustment to your check."

That adjustment was for the appetizers. Less than 10% of my total bill. 

Cancelling my CH Wine Club experience and will not be returning. For what I spent I should have made a reservation at Harry & Izzy's. Service there is always impeccable.

text:
Bern's is an institution and deservedly so. It's one of those restaurants you save for special occasions like birthdays, graduations, anniversaries, holidays and any other reason you can find to go. Dining at Bern's is as much about the experience as it is about the food. 

To start, you should block off an entire evening for a visit to Bern's. You need time to soak in the atmosphere, ambiance and vibe of the place. The dining space is broken into various rooms, each with it's own feel. While we've jokingly referred to the decor as "Victorian-era brothel", it does work. The combination of leather, oil paintings and dim lighting produce a very old-world effect. You should also plan to dress for dinner. This is not the type of place to show up in jeans or a golf shirt. 

The service is flawless. We been told that the training to become a waiter can take years and is not taken lightly. This is reflected in the service which has never disappointed us. The staff always seems to know exactly what you want/need before you do. It's a nice change from what we've experienced in some larger, chain restaurants. 

Since you're probably going for the food, let me offer a few tips. First, don't over-order. Most entree's include French Onion Soup au Gratin, salad, Steak House onion rings, loaded baked potato and vegetable. There are lots of great appetizer choices, but just be advised there is lots of food to come. Secondly, when ordering steak, try to combine orders rather then order individual steaks. For example rather than ordering two 6 oz Filet Mignon's, order a single 12 oz steak. This larger portion of beef is cooked and sliced table side. Believe us, there is an awesome improvement in the taste of the meat. 

Finally, be sure to ask your waiter to reserve a table in the Henry Waugh Dessert Room upstairs for your post-dinner drinks and sweets. Not only is this another amazing experience, you also get a tour of the kitchen and wine cellar on your way upstairs. 

In case we've been vague, Bern's is and always will be one of our favorite steak houses of all time. Maybe we'll see y'all there next time.

we heard such great things about Malvern Buttery and wanted to check it out for a quick brunch the other day!

3. there's apparently a rear garage that offers free parking as well

we walked in and loved how bright, open and airy the space is - we were a little confused at first about the ordering process, but there's a sign that recommends how to go about it.

1. grab a seat - most of the seating areas are communal
2. order a coffee / tea from the staff member standing near the cashier 
3. take a wooden tray (they can be found to the left of the cashier area) and start picking out some food!
4. when you sit down with your meal, there should be a notepad with Malvern Buttery's logo at the top - write down the items that you ordered (scout's honor!) and put it to the side
5. enjoy your meal!
6. pay at the end by bringing your written list of items to the cashier and bus your area

they are magicians when it comes to baking a flaky pastry! we had a savory leek tart topped with a sunny side egg, a delicious farro-based grain salad that was lightly dressed in a buttermilk ranch dressing, and a cinnamon croissant for a sweet ending to our meal.

text:
Started in 2004 by the same team that developed McAlister's Deli, Newk's Eatery is a relative newcomer to the Indiana market after the growing fast casual chain started in Mississippi. 

Newk's takes its name as sort of an homage to the fact that many of its recipes are from the founding Newcomb family's cookbook and the restaurant's menu includes a wide variety of sandwiches, pizzas, salads, soups, mac n' cheese, a kids' menu and a special 600-calorie menu. 

The pizzas all come in one size, right about 10", and run in the $8-9 range for the most part. The crust is thinner and the dough hand-rolled. There's not a create-your-own option, so you are limited to finding one of their specialty pies that fits your palate - with everything from a basic pepperoni to a more experimental spicy shrimp you should be able to do so. The sandwiches also have a set menu with quite a bit of diversity within that menu. 

While the lack of create-your-own options may seem bothersome, judging by the crowd that was present on this Friday afternoon visit people are clearly able to find something that makes them happy.

Newk's Eatery is located in a strip center just across County Line Road on the Northside of Greenwood and within a couple minutes of Indy right about Emerson and County Line. They have a couple of easily accessible spots with appropriate curb cuts. The front glass doors are easily workable - you go up to the counter to order, they give you a number, you fetch your own drink, you place the number in a holder on your table, and your food is delivered to you. 

In terms of wheelchairs, there's a handful of booth options and mostly tables. The floor design is mostly open concept. Tables are roomy enough to accommodate even larger chairs. I had little difficulty accessing the fountain iced tea, though the lids were WAY too high. 

The young man working the cash register was friendly and answered the questions that I had since this was my first visit. The crew was friendly, though I did get a feeling of being rushed and I couldn't help but be a tad bothered by the fact that when I went to get my iced tea refill an employee moved the chair back into place where I had cleared my spot. Maybe a friendly "Were you leaving?" before assuming would have been appropriate. 

The pizza was good, but not great. They add thinly sliced Roma tomatoes to the top, a unique choice that I didn't particularly care for and, in fact, I removed them. I found the toppings a bit easy to fall off the dough, though overall I enjoyed it and would easily order it again. My entire bill came in at just over $11.00 for the pizza and a drink. I noticed their sandwich prices seem to be in the same price range. So, you can likely plan on spending around the $10-15 range per person. 

The atmosphere is pleasant. Despite being quite busy, the noise was bearable. I sat too close to the kitchen, a choice I regretted as it seemed like social hour was the rule. However, there's nothing wrong with being happy at work and I would note they served people quickly, cleared tables quickly, and were never less than friendly. 

Newk's Eatery isn't a place I'd go out of my way to experience, though I wouldn't hesitate to visit again when in the area. This particular corner is populated with restaurant options and I'd imagine Newk's will be a popular option with good service, good food, and fair prices. A notch above area fast food options and a solid entry into the fast casual arena, I look forward to Newk's Eatery's growth in the Indy area and hopefully an expansion closer to my Northeastside home.

text:
I'm not a real big fan of pulled pork, but  if other places made it this juicy and flavorful, I'd probably be a bigger fan of it. The Cubano, featuring said pulled pork, ham, Swiss cheese, dijon mustard and housemade pickles all tucked between flatbread, given a nice big fat smooch by the grill, had the waterfall in my jowls going full bore. I took my first bite and juice from the pulled pork squirted down my shirt; so wear an old shirt or tuck the napkin in your collar so yours doesn't suffer the same fate. 

Now, if you are sodium-sensitive, this sandwich may not be for you, but if your favorite atomic number is 11, the Cubano will make you very happy.

My wife's burger had so much stuff she had to knife-n-fork it. She did ask me at one point if grilled onions were sweet. So between the salty bacon and bleu cheese, there is obviously flavor contrast as well as gooiness from the fried egg on top.

Fries came with both sandwiches and were hot and fresh. No real service issues on this visit. We'll definitely be back to the Dutch to try some of the other stuff on the menu that had me intrigued...

My husband ordered the chorizo burrito. It was a nice portion for the price. We both agreed that it was a little too salty. 

A friend ordered their Sunday special which is a homemade quesadilla. You can pick your choice of meat. It comes with a corn tortilla instead of flour. I thought it was flavorless. Both of the other dishes had no flavor either, other than salt.. yet this one had no flavor at all. 

The service was great. I ended our dinner with a fried ice cream. Probably one of the best I have ever had. Their salsa is also some of the best salsa I have had in a long time. 

Overall... I will give this place another try. I'll just be more mindful on what I order in the future and ask questions.

text: I ordered 2 sandwich's yesterday.  A hot dog and a turkey sandwich.  It is hard to ruin a hot so the problem was with the turkey sandwich.  This is a sandwich I order often.  The hot dog was actually heavier than the turkey.  3 star has in the past had great fresh turkey sandwich's but I have no clue what happened yesterday.  I had to take the turkey off of one side and put it on the other side just so I could taste the turkey it was that sparse.  Guess I need to find a new place for fresh turkey sandwiches.   I would have called but I understand the owner does not take complaints well at all.

I ordered the biscuits and gravy which was very good. It's nice to see country gravy that actually has sausage in it! Would definitely come again.

text: nice little spot, decent portions too. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. text: This rating is for service. The food that made it to our table was fine. In fact, the menu is full of great choices and the food was attractive and decent. However, despite the fact that we told our waitress we had a movie to go to and a time frame (1 hour) our dinner took 45 minutes to reach the table at a time (5:30) when there were only two other parties in the restaurant.  They obviously forgot to get the order to the kitchen and only did so when we inquired why the service was so slow. In addition, one meal was never delivered to the table. The restaurant staff response to these mistakes was not appropriate for the poor level of service.  With numerous other quality Thai restaurants in the area, I would be hard-pressed to return.
name: Jeff

text:
I went to the Fat Tomatoe and I hadn't eaten all day. I say that because I ordered an app that had (2) Shrimp with a cream sauce on it...the one shrimp tasted fine, but the 2nd on had a strong fish taste, but the sauce did seem to cover the taste a little.  After I ate it, I almost immediately experienced stomach cramping and became sicker to the point of needing to go to the ladies room.  I was vomiting and in there so long, my husband came to see if I was ok.  I told him that I thought that one shrimp was bad and I just wanted to go home.  I also told him to please let the owner know that I believed the shrimp may be bad.  
I finally got back to the table, and my husband did tell the owner about the shrimp.  She came to me and said she went back and checked out the shrimp, and it wasn't their shrimp.  She said it must have been something I ate before I arrived at their place.  I told her...I hadn't eaten all day.  And that I was sure it had to be the shrimp. She basically said it wasn't possible, never offered to remove the cost off our bill or offer a comp to try to make it right.  Mind you, I wouldn't have ordered anything else because I was really sick.  But not charging for the bad shrimp should have been a given.  I didn't need the $, but at least it would have showed they were trying.  I felt unheard and not believed.  I own a business...I would Never treat a client like that.  I have NEVER been back to the FAT Tomatoe.  I Never complain or have gotten sick like that before and we go out a Lot... Im sure most of you will go and have a fine meal... I just can't after being treated in such a back handed way!!!
name: Kathy

text:
Until today (6-17-18), I would make an extra effort to dine at McKenzie. However:

text:
Decided to try out Yard House while taking care of some Christmas errands at the mall with my husband. Used the call ahead feature which they stressed is not a reservation. It was PACKED and we had to wait about 10 minutes or so upon arriving. We found a seat at the bar and didn't need to flag down a bartender, she was prompt, attentive and friendly. I ordered the Black Orchid, (sooo good!!! - kind of like a cosmo - raspberry vodka, blue curacao, watermelon pucker, and cranberry juice) My guy got a Yards Brawler, good as usual. 
We were seated at a huge booth. It would easily sit 8.
Our server and all of the service was excellent, attentive, we didn't need to ask for anything. Plates were cleared quickly. We had to wait a bit to get both our starter and entrees, however, we cut them slack as it was a very full house. Like another reviewer said, "it felt chaotic but organized at the same time." That is exactly how it felt.
We started off with the Poke Nachos which included raw ahi, avacado, green onions, and lots of other good stuff. It was delicious, my husband raved about it several times. He's pretty fussy with food and not that easy to impress.
I got the grilled cheese - tomato bisque. It was a combo of cheddar, bleu cheese, swiss, and fontina. I thoroughly enjoyed every bite!
Husband got the fried chicken sandwich. He loved it!
We did not think it was too loud like another reviewer. At all. It didn't even cross my mind. It wasn't like being at a wedding or anything. There was music playing, very cool, mostly eighties hits mixed with Christmas songs. We were able to converse across our table without any issues. No ear problems after leaving. Lol!
Prices were as expected. I'm not sure why another reviewer thought it was overpriced. My drink was $11, not sure of Brawler pint cost, nachos $13.95 (and well worth it with a decent amount of the raw ahi), grilled cheese was $11.75, fried chicken sandwich was $12.95. 
We bought gift cards for our sons, and we plan to return. 
Excellent all around!
name: Patty

text: This place was really good. I make breakfast bowls at home but they do not look like the ones made here. The ones here made me feel self conscious about my own cooking. That's good though because it means they're doing a top notch job here. My self consciousness is my own problem that I have to work through, you know? That's not this establishment's issue. I'm reading a few books that are helping me and have been meditating so that superior cooking doesn't bother me like it did before. I will come back here and eat a meal and it enjoy it for what it is, and that's a meal that's better than any of you could make at home. Deal with it.
name: Real Friends

text:
We got take out.  The restaurant was pretty empty and the food was prepared quickly. The food was decent.  Not the best burgers I have had but enough! They had tater tots which is my go to starch.  They were decent, although I prefer crispier tots.  One of the burgers had cheese on it, yet the description did not state cheese on the burger.  Given cheese was not desired, it was an unwelcome addition to the burger.  
Overall, it was an ok burger, but I prefer Shake Shack. It's cheaper.

text:
Waffle, Fried Chicken, and Bacon. Great combination!!  How was the bacon was done. It hide between the waffle. The bacon are all pan seared to crispy then mixed between layer of waffle. It becomes waffle bacon. Amazing concept. 

I have the trip RyRy Triple Threat waffle chicken and the Korean wings. The triple threat comes with three different RyRy signature chicken. The original, southern, and Korean chicken. These chicken pieces from the chicken breast and make in three different flavor. I like all of them with variety in one order. It also come with choices of syrup. I got the sriracha syrup with some spiciness in the taste. Great combination. 

The Korean wing I have it non breaded. You can have the option to breaded the wings. The Korean sauce on the wings is great. It has tiny ginger in the sauce and make it sophisticated. All orders need to be waited. Table is limited if you decide to eat there.
name: Boon

text: Aldo's on buck road = awful. Our sever Lauren took our order; soup,bread, and drinks came out rather quickly then Lauren was MIA for 30 minutes. I once went to Ulele just for dessert and ordered my husband and I separate orders of it. Yes, we did finish it but there was just way too much. The decor and ambiance are really nice. I would say it is a great spot for a date or celebration. I will warn that the prices are rather high, but it is a good spot for a special occasion. I have hear from others that the quality of the food has varied and there are different experiences each time they went. I will have to see next time I go.

text: It's Cracker Barrel. You know what to expect. Go during the week Monday thru Friday, never on a weekend. You walk in and the entrance smells good. Seasonal clothes and items in front. Navigate to the rear and left to find the restaurant. We've never had bad service at any. Coffee hot, if you want Hot Tea like my wife, then tell your server Hot Boiling Water. That way no surprises and service will flow 'cause they do get busy. Huge portions, fair prices and a very good product. My only complaint is most restaurant windows that we have been to 'Face East' with the rising sun. So we never like to sit East and by the windows. We met the Manager Mr. G Clemons at store 026 and he was very friendly and a credit to the restaurant chain. We will be back before we head home to North FLA. by first of week September 2019.

text:
A great new restaurant with attentive service. Their chips and dip are SO GOOD i feel like we should have been charged extra for the amount my table ate. 

I was satisfied with the flavor of what I ate, although the portion sizes are a little small. I would have liked to eat a bit more. Nevertheless, in terms of quality, service, and management, this restaurant is worth your time.
name: Kirk

text:
I'm not vegan...I'm not vegetarian...in fact, if I could exist completely on cheese and steak, I'd probably do it. That said, sometimes my guilt gets the best of me and I'll consider a salad. I can say wholeheartedly if you want a fantastic salad, you can get it at HGC, but the topper is that you can get wraps, salmon, pizza and pesto that are just as amazing...and that's just to name a few! 

Being from California I am a complete snob about what my food looks like, and I will judge you if your avocados are anything but optimal, but HGC gets top marks. I've only ever had food delivered (the hype is true: free delivery) but HGC is gorgeous every time. The Avocado Star salad is as delicious as it is beautiful. I also love the Roasted Beet salad, no selfish bits of goat cheese here, I'm talking mounds of it. They don't nickel & dime over requests like extra dressing either. Homemade guac is good and comes with yummy pita. I've tried the King Kale juice, which wasn't a favorite, but I'm game to try others. Portions were more than enough for everything, delivery was quick and simple, and it's honestly just good, clean food.
name: Ashley

text: Still the best. The nachos are outrageously good! And the lychee martini is still a stunner. Still highly recommend!

text:
I've had this placed bookmarked for a while. At first I was super excited to try it out, showed up on a Saturday night and nothing was as expected. Food wise the portions were very small, four tacos for $10.00 is pretty hefty when it comes to street food. The food felt rather dry, over-cooked, and simply no where near its value. The steak here has a weird taste to it, not sure what type of meat they use for their steak but it was not satisfying one bit. I was also not impressed with their menu and level of customization. 

I rarely leave negative Yelp reviews, unfortunately this had to be one of them. I will however state that the workers here were very professional, nice, respectful, and quality people. text: This is an incredible breakfast place.  Completely unique menu and everything I have tried has been exceptional.  Friendly service and usually a very unique decorated interior.  Keep up the good work!
name: Martin

text:
This place is probably one of the closest bars to my mother-in-law's house and so it was perfect for a quick meal / drink while baby spent quality time with grandma. 

Atmosphere: 
Dive-y but noticeably very clean. Normally when I think dive I picture sticky floor and spilled drinks but this place was very tidy. Regular 4 person tables and a pretty long bar with fixed seating. 
Crowd was townies and fairly tame -- didn't seem like a place where people are going too nuts. Good chill vibe.  

Order: 
Nonna's platter (an amazing sampler of half size lasagna, ravioli, mini braciole, and big meatball) -- $11.95. We snagged the last one they had on stock around 8PM. 
A santa saison

Pros: 
Delicious food! It's always bonus points with me when a bar serves really good food, especially because I can't drink much without some eats. When I hear bar food I think more like greasy chicken fingers and fries. While they have that and other bar staples like baskets of wings and burgers, they have very legit food (hot food, cheesesteaks) and you can totally get a full meal out of their menu. They have a rotating menu of specials throughout the week and luck be with me, I was here on Italian platter night. Other specials included pasta fagiole soup and eggplant parm platter with pasta (10.95). The platter we got was big enough for 2 and we took home leftovers. YUM YUM YUM!! I would totally come here just to eat. 
Bartender was super nice and gave us extra serving utensils to split the platter. 
Parking to the right of the restaurant. 

Cons: 
Small space -- while there are tables for 4, this would not be the most comfortable for large groups. 
Because it's small, the smoke can be a little stifling but I personally don't care.
name: Anita

text:
Never had any problems with bamboo (at Whitaker Ave) before. But now more issues with them happened everytime me and my friends came here. The young girl taking orders really had attitude problems. She never cracked a smile or had warm welcome towards customers.

How much they can save to fill up a full cup? It is technically only milk and tea. Back then, i either ordered the less ice or no ice, it was always full but recently the quantity has changed. text: I can't believe I haven't done a review for this place.  I love the Cheesecake Factory...especially the cheesecake!  We were at the Galleria doing our last bit of Christmas shopping and I really wanted to eat here.  It's not hubby's favorite place, but he indulged me and so we had an early lunch.  We beat the crowd and were seated right away in a nice booth.  We ordered and then we waited and waited and then waited some more.  We had both ordered breakfast dishes and thought maybe that was throwing them off.  Then I thought...hey wait... it should not matter what we ordered, it wasn't busy and it was just eggs, breakfast potatoes and English muffins!  I could fix that in about 15 minutes...hubby became frustrated, but I refused to let this ruin our day.  I kept chatting happily, silently praying our food would arrive soon.  It did indeed show up eventually and thank goodness it was delicious.  My eggs were so fluffy and moist and the potatoes were crunchy, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.  I have no idea why it took so long to get our food, but I got cheesecake so I'll let it pass!  I love this place and think it's the most beautiful restaurant I've ever seen.  To me, it's like be transported to Europe.  The decor is so gorgeous with all the soft colors.  I took the cheesecake home and ate it the next day.  I always get the 30th Anniversary.  It has chocolate cake and white chocolate mouse.  It's smooth creamy and decadent with crispy chocolate curls on the side that gives it just the right amount of crunch. The yummy food saved the day!
name: Sara

text: This place has the worst service and the food isn't that great. The hamburgers are just hamburgers nothing special. We ordered the truffle fries they were cold with a ridiculous small amount of cheese not at all what we expected from this place not to mention I never got my fries that came with my hamburger. text: I've been coming here after work for years now. It was a great place to grab a beer on happy hour talk to friends and maybe grab a bite too eat. The food has taken a steep nose dive. I'm fairly sure they cook everything in a microwave. The last time I was there a customer returned his food because he was dissatisfied. I watched the new manager take the wings to the kitchen area and in sight eat the food. That was enough for me. I over heard this same manager talk to the bartender, that has been there for years now, as if it was her first day on the job. By far one of the most unprofessional "managers" I have meet to date. All my friends and I wanted was a comfortable and clean place to enjoy our night. Over the last six to eight weeks it has been extremely uncomfortable to be there. They brought the neon lights for the out side inside. I like a dive bar as much as the next person but this is EXTREMELY tacky. There are dozens of bars and restaurants in this area. Stopping and getting a six pack and a wawa hoagie and eating by the dumpster is a better night than this hole. One star is only because zero is not an option.

There was an elderly couple in front of us who also needed to be sitted and were never greeted. So there are now 4 of us waiting to be acknowledged. When FINALLY get acknowledged at which time the hostess says she has to clean the tables and will seat us. Now another part of 4 comes in after us and walked right in and began to speak with people they know. Because they knew people that were already seated and who was in the middle of their meal the 4 people were seated in front of us. How do you let that happen when you acknowledged we were next.  We asked for the manager who was rude and didn't acknowledge he was wrong. He proceeded to tell my mother OH WELL. After she just asked why was it ok that the other people were seated first

text:
Went back for lunch with a co-worker and what a better experience. 

Started with the shrimp hush puppies and all Incan say is Woozah!!  The sauce is delightful and the texture and flavor of the puppies is awesome. Definitely get them!

The mussels were served in a great sauce and had bread for dipping. Perfect amount for lunch portion. 

Salmon had a wonderful sear and was cooked perfectly. Again great portion for lunch. Cost was a bit steep for lunch but lucky it was being expensed!

Overall great experience!
name: Anne

text:
I personally love this place. Being that I exercise a lot, this place is perfect for the lazy takeout of your dreams. They also drive around in a food truck sometimes

The food is the essence of copious, and not to the point of where the tastiness subsides. You have a choice of 1-10 on spiciness. I usually go 8, and the taste isn't compromised. If you're masochistic, go for 10.

And this place is super duper cheap. The double whammy of my stomach says: bring this place closer to Boise (rather than Eagle...)
name: Jordan

text: Food was ok but not amazing. The waitress asked us if we would like more chips for our dip then on my bill they charged me for them. Extra anything dressing or condiments they charge you so beware. For being a supposedly nicer restaurant why do they give you only one fork??? She made us keep the same one through appetizers and salads and our main course, Won't be back I was not impressed.
name: L

text:
Tried this coffee shop after seeing it had great reviews and an interesting atmosphere.
Upon arriving, we weren't greeted until I looked the server directly in the eye.

We ordered our food which was 2 spiced ice coffees and the waffles and monte cristo burrito.
Around $32.

We were instructed to find a seat and our order will be brought to us.

Coffees came out a few mins later and our food followed a little while later, only is wasn't our food. We were brought someone else's order. 
The server apologized and said she'll see what happened to our order. 10-15 mins later(maybe more) out food was brought out. The waffle my husband got was a bit over done, meaning is wasn't fluffy, but a bit on the crispy side  and the bacon it came with was crunchy. Which isn't a big deal. But the burrito I ordered looked appealing but didn't come with the sauce it was supposed to come with. I asked a gentleman that worked there if I could have some ketchup and he responded saying they don't have ketchup and he named off some hot sauces and sriracha . I chose sriracha because I remember being told that it wasn't really spicy. Not sure if they tweaked it but it was very hot. Also, no one came to check on us or asked how we liked the food. 

The two star I gave was for the multi theme they have which was interesting *biker, nautical , steampunk and minimalist* and the coffee was great.
name: Rue

text: Really nice atmosphere and beer choices. Monday night is 2-4-1 beers which is a deal! I split the Belgian fries with a friend and got the yum sauce, it was just okay and I probably wouldn't eat here again. I definitely want to try the shot ski!
name: Allison

text: Was a little iffy at first... seemed like an average fast food joint... WRONG!! This place is very good. We had the charbroiled oysters which my 7 year old daughter loved. They were fantastic. The thin catfish and fried shrimp were cooked really well. The misses got the strawberry fields salad and loved it. Kids enjoyed their burger and tenders and especially the ice cream !!! Please check this place out. Not only good food but the service is really good as well !!!!!
name: Dwayne

text:
Sorry, this place is going to be a hard pass for me. I've never had an $8 sandwich this skimpy before. I ordered the Pizza sandwich, and when you closed the roll, you couldn't even see the filling, and this was the 'bigs'. It looked like what amounted to 2 pieces of capicola, a few rounds of pepperoni and what appeared to be a slice and a half of cheese. That was topped with roughly half a crumbled up meatball. 

What saved this review from being 1 star was the marinara sauce, which had a good flavor, but when the bread makes up the majority of your sandwich, it'll be a long time before I go back.

I'd recommend going to a Subway before I'd suggest Potbelly. And I'm not a fan of Subway. I even deleted the Potbelly app from my phone.
name: Bruiser

text: It looked better online than it did in person. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The wait felt longer than it should have. Probably not coming back. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Not bad for a quick meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Sad to leave 2 stars. I went there for dinner with three other people, and everything we ordered was just too salty. Too much salt. It left me so thirsty for the next few hours. Service was good, but unfortunately the seasoning ruined it all. No one can blame you if you opt for logans, long horn , Texas Roadhouse or any other steakhouse for better quality and experience :( it was a special occasion, and as an organizer I was even sorry for the guest that I chose this place :(

text: Philly's BEST cheese steak you can get! And on South St., which is always a fun night! Order wit whiz, onions, mushrooms
name: DJ

text: Really good sashimi and sushi and super affordable for happy hour especially. There is a cucumber roll that's super refreshing and delicious. Salmon sashimi is good quality.
name: Ivona

text: Fun decor but service is slow (at the bar and not busy) food is covered in sauce. It might be the 80's way but I would have rather had a microwave meal
name: Ty

text:
I stopped in for breakfast. I had the French toast with fresh strawberries and bananas. It was delicious. It did come with whipped cream and other toppings so let your waitress know which ones you want or if you want some on the side. 
Plenty of coffee servers walking around to refill coffee whenever needed. Price was reasonable. I will go back
name: Stephen

text:
Stumbled upon this place when my friend and I were looking for a place to grab a quick lunch. This place blew our minds. We came back for dinner the same night, that's how good it was. Mango guacamole with pepitas is out of this world fantastic. I loved the chips that were served, it was a combo of corn, malanga and plantain chips. My friend gorged on 3 portions of Mexican styled corn . I don't like corn, but even  could not stay away and ate 2 pieces. A spice fest in my mouth. I've also ordered fried plantains , which melt in your mouth. Tons of juxtaposed flavors. 
Margarita menu is a whole other story. We have tried every kind on the menu and all were phenomenal. French and strawberry/basil margaritas were my personal favorites. Not cloyingly sweet, tasted very realistic and not heavy. 
If you're visiting , this place is not to be missed!!!
name: Al

text: We stopped by this place on a road trip glad we did. Their sandwiches were great, good size. Buffalo chicken, and chicken cordon bleu. Yummy !!! Staff was great and fast service.
name: Marta

text: My first disappointing burrito. The servings were smaller than what I've been used to throughout the years I've been going to Chipotle Nationwide. Rice and chicken were served tablespoon size. And the chips weren't cooked all the way. Some chips were soft, didn't have that crunch to the chip. All for a $10.99 price tag?
name: Daniel

text:
We ordered two Large pizzas. Pepperoni and plain. The pizza was good. Not great, not bad though.
The large pizza is more like a medium size. I will say the service was really good, pizzas were ready right on time for pick up.Thats all I got to say about this.
name: S

text: People!!!!! This place is incredible. The food is fresh and flavorful. The staff is extremely knowledgeable and proud of their environment. Drinks are made stiff and food is portioned above expectation. To top it off... every bite from start to finish is a rush of savory flavor!!!! If someone gives this place a bad review they are absolutely insane!!!! Don't miss out on this GEM!!!
name: Patrick

text: Make sure if you want to get in on the weekends to make reservations. Because me and my friends didn't they only had patio seating but thank goodness it was a nice day and they had patio heats. We all got something different and the portion was a lot. We probably could of shares two entrees and still be stuffed. Service and food was great!
name: Lyna

text:
The food here was great. The service was attentive.  The atmosphere lively.  And the beer list on point. What else can you ask for?

The menu ran the gauntlet from fish fry to being able to bring your friend who's on a diet here.  I had the fish tacos, and I'd definitely recommend them and get them again.

I don't remember what anyone else got, but no one complained.  It was our first time here and we were definitely talking about going back.
name: Tom

text: They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was fresh and service was quick. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which prob says everything.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Food was good and came out fast. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. They were out of one thing I originally wanted..
name: User

text:
The only reason I'm giving 30 Main one star is because Yelp won't let me give them zero.  I have never in my life sent food back, asked for money off the bill, or done any of the things people typically do when they are unsatisfied with their experience.  That being said, the fact that I thought my experience at 30 Main deserved zero stars says a lot....

We walk into a weird scene.... blinding neon green light, DJ equipment shoved in the corner, and a lifetime movie playing on the TVs. The place doesn't seem to know if it wants to be a high end bar, a high school dance club, or retirement home. We awkwardly stood by the hostess desk for 15 minutes before anyone greeted us. I requested a booth and was guaranteed one.We're told we cant get a booth even though there are 4 empty ones, which were still empty when we left. We are finally sat in the front at a table with a chair on one side and a dirty white couch on the other.  My girlfriend sat across from me on the couch, which was so low it was hard for her to reach the table. It looked like she was sitting on the floor (see pictures). We asked to switched tables.

They were out of my first 2 beer choices, which didn't help their already limited beer selections. I didn't see soup on the menu so I asked if they had any. The waitress told me "Oh yea we do, it just isn't on the menu".  Riiiiight. We also saw a guy eating tacos but there was not a single taco option on the menu.  Speaking of the menu...FYI to whoever typed it: you didn't accidentally select a Christmas theme in Microsoft Word, when the squiggly red or green lines show up under a word it means that something is misspelled or there's a grammatical error (see attached photos). I got soup and my girlfriend got some tuna over white rice thing.  It took 40 minutes for our shitty apps to come out. It was then another hour until we got our entrees. 2 different times I saw tables who came in significantly later than us not only get their food first, but get the same exact food that we ordered. We were told "our food was coming out in a minute" for an hour and given a free beer.
We ordered scallops and shrimp over risotto and lobster ravioli...but I'm convinced it was expired baby food. The "risotto" on my plate was exactly the same as the "white rice" that was in the tuna appetizer.  It was so undercooked it crunched as I chewed.  Call it risotto or white rice or whatever the hell you want, but I'm calling it finger nail clippings because that's what I thought I was eating.  The shrimp and scallops were no better. There were a few that were so charred that I couldn't even tell whether it was a scallop or shrimp.  When I could tell the difference, it was because the shrimp tasted like burnt woodchips and the scallops (burnt on the outside but uncooked mush on the inside) were like little blobs of jizz...yes, jizz - - as in semen, cum, etc....the lobster raviolis were essentially flavorless pierogis thrown in cold sauce. The table next to us also had a bad experience.  Rightfully so, they complained about their ice cold "Best of the Mainline" muscles and the waitress took all of their apps off the bill. When I got my check and noticed nothing was taken off I almost lost it.  How she justifies discounting someone elses check right in front of my face, but not mine when my experience was far worse is bananaland. Now I was noticeably frustrated. Idk if the guy working was a "manager" or what but he kept looking at me out of the corner of his eye and was asking every other table how their meal was except mine like a coward. My girlfriend didn't want Valentine's Day to be ruined and urged me to just keep my mouth shut. I paid, left a good tip and left. Ironically enough, on my way out I heard the waitress begging another customer "not to give them a negative review on Yelp". They should be grateful all I'm doing is yelping them and not calling the cops and filing an attempted murder charge against them for the poison they served me. Pretty shitty spending almost $200 on a meal and drinks and still having to stop at McDonalds on the way home...which tasted like heaven in comparison. 

I get things happen and people make mistakes. The bad experience isn't what upset me the most.  It was the fact that nobody gave a shit. Nobody tried to make it right. Nobody even acknowledged that they messed up. Nobody cared whether I walked out of there satisfied or not. Is that how you run a business? It wasn't even the least bit busy!! If it was super busy and the staff was hustling around and my food took forever and sucked I wouldn't ever complain...bc at least they were trying and gave a shit. Now I know why 30 Main was the only place I was able to get Valentine's Day reservations at anytime I wanted....the day before Valentine's Day. 

Moral of the story, if my entire family was dying of AIDS and the only way to save them was if I ate 30 Main again, I'd let them all wither away and die without thinking twice.
name: Will

text: Came here for brunch and ordered the cinna-roll stuffed toast. It was nasty. I can't place what was disgusting about it, but I could barely eat half. My mother was dining with me and agreed that it was not good. I will not be back for brunch, but I have heard good things about lunch/dinner so perhaps will give this place another chance.
name: Marissa

text: We wanted this place to be great.  It was recommended by our BNB hosts.  Unfortunately, our hopes were dashed beginning with drinks.  One in our party had to send their drink back for a remake. Dinner delivered, tepid is best we can say for temp on three dishes.  Sent back and returned barely warmer than before.  A disappointment = three meals out of four.  So sorry to give this review but unfortunately it is the honest truth.
name: Laurie

text: The music was louder than it needed to be. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Worth checking out. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. No big complaints, just a nice meal.
name: User

text: Another great family lunch at Nilsa's. My husband is officially addicted to the Chuleta which was amazing again and we tried the Pastel and the chicken bites and both dishes were delicious. Plus they offer a Military discount!
name: Maria

text: Delicious meal and excellent, attentive service provided by Bree! She made our evening wonderful!!   She was so kind and knowledgeable of the food.  Be sure to try the carne seca ,  tamale stuffed chicken, and Carlotta's salad.  Yummo!  Having  a delicious, flavorful meal is great, but when you get excellent service on top of a great meal it makes for an enjoyable dining experience.  We will be back!!
name: Kimberly

text: This place is probably the best place to hit up for a fun time without worrying about bumping into a rowdy cracked out tourist. The band was great. The bartenders were very attentive and even came outside the bar area to check on you. Great place. Classiest place on bourbon street in my opinion.
name: Michael

text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. Anyway, the food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Honestly, really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Anyway, the wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Idk, they were out of one thing i originally wanted..
name: User

text: Stopped in for a great BBQ lunch after an early fall bike ride in Eagle State Park.   Food was served gast and hot, just like it should be.    I'll be back.
name: Bruce

text: It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Also, the ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but i still finished most of it. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. so yeah kind of mixed on it.
name: User

text: The whole meal felt kind of uneven. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Wouldn't really choose this place again. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. It looked better online than it did in person. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text:
This place would have gotten a 5 star review, except the fact that my friend and I got sick after eating here :(

I loved the concept of it, and how many great and healthy options they had. I had the kale Caesar salad with chicken and the serving size was huge. My friend built her own salad with Caesar dressing and really enjoyed hers too. The prices were on point as well. I thought I got a ton of food for right at around 10 bucks. 

The restaurant itself is SO cute. It has a bright and contemporary feel, and there were plenty of comfy seating options. 

I'm super disappointed that it didn't sit well with either of us, because I would have frequented this place often.
name: Maria

text: This place reminds you of Chinatown in downtown Philly. The food is in my opinion the best Chinese food in the area. The prices are good and the place is very clean. Give it a try!
name: Rodger

text:
I was happy to see the restaurant obtained new heaters . It was warm so the deck was full, however, they add an updated look to the front. I am anxious to come on a cold night without 3 layers of clothes.

 I ordered the Chicken Picatta this time and it was very good. My server was outstanding, as always,  and the patrons of this establishment  are friendly.
name: Dee

text: Oh my.  The service was amazing.  And a full meal with soup, salad, an egg roll and the entree at lunch for less than $9. Who could want for anything more???
name: Lisa

text: My friend found a cockroach egg in here boba... if that doesn't tell you about the quality of the restaurant I don't know what will ‍
name: Carolina

text:
We had a reservation for 4 at 8 PM. We showed up on time and were seated promptly. At 8:20, As no one had come to our table since being seated, I had to go and find someone to see if we could place a drink order. It took another 15 minutes for the drinks to arrive. We ordered our food, including soup/salad and our entrees when they brought our drinks. First course arrived timely but then waited 35 minutes for our entrees. 

Now for the food. One order the seafood paella, one fish and chips, one salmon, and one clams pomodoro. On the pomodoro, there were a total of just 6 little necks on a  $20+ plate of pasts and the chef completely murdered them! The pomodoro sauce was over spiced and beyond that had absolutely no flavor other than raw tomato. The seafood paella was equally disappointing with an astonishingly small portion of seafood, completely tasteless sauce and dry yet uncrispy rice. The fish and chip? Save your money and go to long John silvers. Their batter has better flavor and you at least get a reasonable portion for under $30. Regarding the salmon, it was billed by the waiter as being a summer dish with sizzling salmon and cold accompaniments. Unfortunately, the salmon, while cooked well was barely like warm and so was everything else on the plate. As well, the pickled veg served with it had no flavor other than vinegar.
name: Shane

text: This is one of those places where I can see other people loving it more than I did. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Nice little spot, decent portions too. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food was fresh and service was quick.
name: User

text: This is probably my favorite seafood restaurant so far.  Family friendly , love it !!
name: Laura

text:
Horrible Pad Thai. Served with Raw noodles. Had to return it to the kitchen twice and still the same. 
The chicken Pho soup had old and rubbery chicken. Do not recommend this place.
name: Tanya

text: Ordered a chicken greko salad to go and it came with barley any chicken and the chicken did get was all skin. Really disappointed in how low quality the meal was.
name: Lola

text: We really want to like this place...but it was just lackluster. We would eat there again if others wanted to go but it would definitely not be somewhere we would seek out. The service was good - our waitress was very sweet and personable. The food was...okay. I added gin to my drink and I'm not convinced it made it in the glass. My husband felt the same about his Moscow mule. The food just lacked anything special honestly. I ordered honey dusted fried chicken and I'm still not convinced it was the correct flavor. It tasted like regular fried chicken. My husband said the blackened catfish was fish - nothing special and nothing "blackened" about it. The sides were okay but kind of bland, and my husband didn't get the correct side but ate it anyways. Biscuits and compote was good and probably the shining moment. Overall it wasn't bad really, but this isn't something we will add to our typical dinner restaurant list.
name: Tawni

text: Everything here is always delicious. Lamb ribs are amazing but a somewhat small serving. Get the burrata and focaccia and thank me later. Drinks are always yummy too.
name: Rachel

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: The restaurant was very cute inside. Great service. The food was really good as well. We had the crab fried rice and the beef fried rice and they were both good
name: Robbyn

text: Great food. Walking distance from our Airbnb. Found this gem on yelp. Food was delicious. Wait staff were extremely friendly. Definite place to try for brunch.
name: Christina

text:
As first time patrons my family and I received the worst service we had ever received.  We were seated quickly ( in about 15minutes). 

Once seated after waiting about 15 minutes our waitress said she'd be right with us however she never did.  After waiting another 30 minutes we flagged down another waitress to submit our order. 

After waiting yet another 30 minutes with no food in sight we asked to speak with the manager. 15 minutes later the manager came with our food. Frustrated with the service we declined the food and expressed our extremely disappointed with the service
name: G

text:
So close to USF and yet tucked away in small strip plaza this place is a verifiable gem
Excellent service from the start. Small place but warm and welcoming
The recommendations from our server were right on. Spinach spanakopita
Lamb was fall of the bone tender and delicious 
The highlight however was fresh sea bass. Owner, Maten, was a great host
name: H

text: Visited from Cincinnati and decided to check this spot out look and feel are amazing, staff very caring and nice, food is top notch (kudos to the chef) would definitely recommend and will be back again!!!
name: Steven

text:
great a lot for your money.nice and welcoming.
This was our first visit and upon our arrival at 10:30 am we had to wait bout 8 minutes for seating. This restaurant always seems to be busy from what we observed throughout the day. The staff was very friendly although a little hurried since the place was packed, although they were attentive to ensure our meal was good and refilled our water glasses without being asked.
name: J

text: Okay spot with relatively cheap eats. Margaritas are average. Waiters seem confused, don't know why. What concerned me was very shifty workers buzzing in and out; one guy particularly taking workers around the corner to the back alley. Maybe I am just being over observant but it happened enough for me to express it here. Hopeful it's nothing, otherwise average AmeriMexican food in a busy spot.
name: Christina

text: You would think being the only game in town that sits on the corner of Ursinus campus that they would have great food, I mean like a classic college town pizza joint that is an institution! Well not here...Overpriced, typical pizza shop with nothing that sets them apart, well unless you count price increases for smaller amounts. Cheesesteaks I have had are fatty, typical Sysco foods. Customer service in here is deplorable as well. At one point I accumulated enough points for a free small pizza, when I went in to order it I asked the guy at the counter where the machine went that recorded our visits as I had a free small due to me. His response "it's out being cleaned" he knew damn well they got rid of it. I let it go and waited till the following day and again went back to get my free pie, well this time I was told they got rid of the machine we would enter our phone numbers into and was abruptly told i had no free small pizza coming to me. So basically they lost a customer for life over a $6 pizza, need I say more about how they understand customer service. I will say this however to end on a good note...They have a killer bacon cheeseburger!
name: Michael

text:
My only complaint was that they took a long time to bring out our food. However, we were a large party with virtually zero wait time, so, really, CAN I complain?

Party Fowl was our introduction to Tennessean hospitality. Friendly and attentive staff. For my meal I ordered the "Brick-Tattooed" chicken, a chicken breast (surprisingly juicy) with sage and goat cheese. It came with a side of sauteed veggies and that was probably my healthiest meal to date in Nashville.

I also treated myself to a drinky drink: The Fowl Language, their take on an Old Fashioned. It was so smooth, had it asked me out on a date, I'd have said yes.

For kicks I also ordered a side of Piggy Chips. They were pretty good, if a tad on the salty side.

Overall, I was pleased with our first stop of our stay here.
name: Cynthia

text: My dad recommended this place because he loved the shrimp and grits and they were AMAZING. My boyfriend got the seafood stew and it was good but it came out way too hot it burnt his mouth and he couldn't start eating it until 30 minutes into the meal. Highly recommend getting the smaller plate because it was a lot of food. The char broiled oysters were SO GOOD. One of the best we have had.
name: Taylor

text:
Ordered the Horchata latte and it was delicious.
There's always parking which is nice and the great thing about El mariachi is why you're sipping your coffee , walk around the different stores and ch do little Mexican market and get yourself some meat from the butcher or some Mexican fresh bread or some Hispanic produceProduce.
name: Bianca

text: Green Papaya is an excellent addition to the neighborhood.  We were happy to see that many of our favorite dishes from Sam's made it onto the menu (Roti Canai, Chow Kueh Teow...etc.).  The flavors are excellent, and they didn't assume that we would want the mild version of the dishes just because we are American.  We would happily give Green Papaya 5-stars if the servings were larger.
name: Clifford

text:
A surprisingly good pizza place tucked away in center city. All the pizzas here are roman-style (basically really thin and crunchy crust). One pie per person is usually sufficient. 

I tried both the spicy soppressata and spicy sausage. Neither was actually spicy, but both were delicious! The spicy sausage pizza approximates a classic fennel sausage pizza in appearance and taste, but the spicy soppressata had a nice twist by throwing on some honey, which gave some sweetness to balance the saltiness of the salami.

In general, found it hard to get good pizza in philly, but this is definitely one place to try out
name: Matt

text: People are being a little dramatic in these comments honestly. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. I had a better visit than I expected to. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: Delightful and enjoyable! The outside seating is protected by an awning and beautiful view of inter-coastal water way. Our waitress was so much fun and very knowledgeable and took the time to explain different menu items. We started with a pitcher of Mojitas made tableside - a tad too sweet, I would ask if more limes could be added or less simple syrup. But definitely the way to order drinks for 3 adults. Appetizers, "salted cod fried balls" - were surprisingly (?) really salty, and chicken croquettes, good but I think we will continue to try other appetizers, in the future. Of course, a must have, tableside prepared house salad, Columbia 1905 Salad, with green olives, thin julienne slices of ham and swiss cheese. Very good. Huge proportion of the daily special coconut mahi mahi with rice. The fish was awesome, but the rice I thought was a bit overcooked. Cannelloni de Langosta  "7 Portes", two rolled pasta filled with lobster, scallops, shrimp in a lobster bisque sauce. So good! The Original Cuban Sandwich had many delightful flavors, essence of an "Italian Submarine" yet it own flavor. Pasta and Sandwich were too big to finish, with appetizers and salads - tasted just as good the next day.  This will become a favorite to have a meal at.  My friend recommends the White Sangria, something to try next time.
name: Renee

text:
Soggy N oily Fries

4$ for 3 nuggets

Look at the Chicken sandwich done in a hurry

Never going back !

45$ worth of waste
name: Vaibhav

text: This is the best burger in the city or Tampa in my opinion. If you go here and get the kicker you will fall in love.
name: Ian

text: Great food. Taco options are amazing, very big filled tacos. Having one taco was very filling. The guacamole of the month was absolutely amazing and great fresh taste of guacamole. The queso blanco is very great, had to order a second round! Drink deals were perfect for groups and tons of different flavors and options for all.
name: Alexandria Nadine

text:
SEE REVIEW ON 25TH AVE LOCATION:
First ordered a chicken Caesar salad through Uber eats from the 25th ave location. If you've ever had a Caesar salad from any restaurant, ever in your entire life existence, you'd obviously know that black olives, feta cheese, jalapeños, beets, other miscellaneous vegetables, and Greek dressing are definitely not at all ingredients anywhere close to a standard Caesar salad. Once I realized my order was completely incorrect, I decided to reorder the same, regular Caesar salad through Jet's delivery service from this Jet's location instead of Uber eats. Boy, was that a mistake and an absolute waste of twice as much money. That decision was completely unrecognizable because my second salad delivered from this Jet's location delivery was a standard Caesar, but still included black olives, tomatoes, and the wrong dressing. Definitely not worth getting charged/waiting for the wrong food delivered once, and absolutely not twice. text: Not terribly impressed. We had the enchiladas.  The corn tortillas where like corn flavored rubber. Too thick!   The stuffing was just chicken, nothing else. The red sauce was spicey but tasteless.  Needed salt.  Nice ambiance and staff though. Outside seating looks nice!  Convenient location.

text: Such a unique and delicious taste. Everything on the menu is worth trying. I especially recommend the pulled turkey!
name: Amanda

text:
Ok so Im only giving 4 stars because the coffee at Union coffee bar was horrible. No coffee that morning so I was looking forward to a nice fresh cup there and liked the whole coffee bar idea. But I prefer to add my own stuff to my coffee so it would be nice if they left stuff out i stead of having to ask for everything. Also, the creamer I think was bad too because after I added that it got clumpy. Next time Ill be sure to have coffee before I go there. 

I also tried Zukku sushi... this was fresh and delicious. And I love that you can customize your order. I got the sushi burrito with salmon and some other stuff. The only complaint I have is the seaweed was really difficult to bite into and chew. I literally had to take it apart and ended eating  with chopsticks. So def will go for the regular sushi rolls next time or maybe try the poke bowl. 

Ill definitely be back. Another bonus is that it is right on the riverfront so you can take a nice walk along the water too.

text:
Why 4 stars?

Good country food, service is always decent, facility is mostly clean and the selection of old candies and goodies is great.

Pricing is pretty decent compared to others and as a chain, this would be one of the tops. 

Breakfast is pancakes or Uncle Hershel's for me and way to many options for lunch and dinner. This is not only a road trip stop anymore, but a weekly visit for some country cooked food!

text:

text: Great cheesesteak albeit not much space to sit. Definitely go! HIDDEN GEM IN PHILLY.

text: Food was fresh and service was quick. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. text: The people here are super friendly, last time they gave us dessert on the house which was really nice of them. The arepas are delicious I had the pabellon which I'd highly recommend! Also there is a USF student discount which is awesome.

text: Decent food or it would have been if it wasn't for all the salt. So. Much. Salt. For the price I expected the cook/chef to have tasted the food!

text:
I have to say this location gives you the New Orleans feel. The French Quarter vibe is an awesome experience.  Obviously the oysters are great and a must have, but the Boom Boom Shrimp are delicious. 

There is an Acme Oyster House in Harrah's Casino area, but from my experience, any chain restaurant in a casino tends to be subpar. (Las Vegas is in driving distance for me.) So I would go to the French Quarter location.

text: One of the few (maybe only? ) exclusively vegan/vegetarian places in town. While I'm not vegan myself, I went with a friend who was. Everything I had was outstanding - everything was locally sourced and fresh. The staff was kind, caring and attentive - they were all knowledgeable about the menu and wiling to answer any questions at length. Food was very reasonably priced as well! Very cute place. text: I really wanted to like this place a little more. I went during Essence Fest so the wait was 2 hours. It was to be expected and they set up a bar and a DJ outside to entertain us. You can also see where you are on the waitlist via the Yelp waitlist feature. While waiting, I tried the Bow Wow and it was STRONG but doesn't taste that great. It's basically light and dark rum with fruit punch. If you want to get tipsy, one will do the trick. I had the grilled pork chop dinner with Mac and cheese and green beans. The meat was seasoned to perfection but the green beans appeared to have come out of the can. They use a spaghetti like noodle for the Mac and cheese which I found a little interesting but it was flavorful. All in all, not a terrible visit. I'm willing to come back again during a less busy time.

The calamari came with a sweet sauce and was good and tasted fresh made as opposed to frozen, and the pizza was delicious, about a 12 incher and thin crust, very good. Not an every day lunch spot for me, but great when you want to splurge and feel good about it.
