text:
It's been a while since I've reviewed Fujiyama but when you have an excellent meal it's worth yelping about it.  Fujiyama is my favorite sushi restaurant and I feel their quality of fish far surpasses that of the other sushi joints in town.  When you eat sashimi (raw fish only, no rice) you can truly taste the difference.  The other sushi restaurants have to mask the poorer quality of fish with sauces and other toppings, but not Fujiyama, their fish quality stands on its own.  I wont even go elsewhere for my sashimi craving, it's not worth the money.  Today's fish was no exception.  It wouldnt have been much fresher had it been caught and eaten right at the ocean. It was extra fresh today, each variety of fish at its freshest tasting, tender, melt in your mouth deliciousness.
While I used to complain about the customer service, they have greatly improved and I only get excellent service. My needs are anticipated before I have to ask, and my drink, although it's only water, is refilled before my glass is empty.  Today, they went beyond and I was able to substitute one fish for another on my platter and the server was extra attentive and helpful.  For inkand sushi, you can do no better!
name: Cristen

text: No fish no Black Eyed Peas no cornbread the jerk chicken a leg and a chop thigh whatever they have on the menu will not be the same when you go in person buyer beware my turkey wing platter the wings were kind of dry I'm one and done on this spot

text:
Tucked away, it may be easy to miss this location if you're not super sure where you're going. It used to be a donut shop, and the feel of that still lingers - not many restaurants where you can order your food and check your lottery tickets.

It was very quiet for a Saturday night at 6 (meaning, it was just us) so we were able to ask questions and chat with the owner who made our order. Really really friendly. Makes you really want to root for them to succeed.

We ordered quite a few things to go (#YOLO): papusa, empanadas, arepas and cake! The mixed papusa had a bit of everything (meat, cheese, beans) and came with small containers of slaw and a thin salsa. Very traditional, though I think it was too overwhelming with so many fillings - I typically just like it with meat. It was hefty in weight for sure. The empanadas were my favourite!! A sweet-ish dough that was crispy and not too thick (greasy though) and filled with super flavourful shredded beef. I would eat a couple of these as a meal and be quite satisfied. The arepas were ok - again, very greasy to the touch. For fillings we chose the BBQ pork with cheese and the chicharronada (pork skin). The BBQ pork was thick cut and plentiful, but we found it dry and lacking a sauce or something to give it flavour. The chicharron wasn't quite what we expected - it was again, plentiful, but there was *too* much of it and the texture became very tiring quickly (soft & very chewy). The arepas came with a green salsa and a creamy sauce which we definitely used to cut the meat taste. Finally, the three milk cake and the pineapple flan were good but wasn't life changing. I prefer the tres leches cake from other places in town much more.

I would definitely come back for those empanadas because OMG they were delicious. I'd try different arepas too. They have cachapas on the menu which I'm curious to try as well. So, if I'm in the mood for a drive, I'd go there again.
name: Lily

text:
Came here yesterday to give this location a try since it used to be really good at this location and my carrollwood location is always a waste of money. Well seems to be that it was also a mistake. Our family chicken dinner was black charcoled burnt. It was absolutely disgusting. 
Our 2 nugget dinners were overcooked and fried were old and cold. Should of just took my $30 and went to grocery store. The girl cashier was also very short on politeness with what else do you want questions. And is that all then just pull to the window. It blows my mind how the manager allows her to talk to customers this way. Not to mention she told us they were out of all sauces and gave me 2 guava bbq only. Not even the one we wanted. Disappointing as this brand was good when it first opened.

text:
My parents stayed here twice recently for multiple nights and I was able to check it out during their stay.  Their rooms were very nice and well taken care of.  The hotel was very clean and sparkly and decorated nicely.  The pool was also nice, though a tad cold for the winter season.  The continental breakfast was apparently wonderful, although sadly, I did not get to partake.

The only thing my parents complained about was the thin walls, which seems to be a problem of hotels everywhere.  In this day and age, why hasn't someone figured out how to make them soundproof!?! 

Overall, this Best Western is a very nice hotel that I will recommend to my out of town guests.

text:
We went to Pad Thai Friday August 31st. 
We arrived early (4:30) because we knew the line gets long. We were seated right away. It took a little bit to get out drinks, but we ordered 3 menu items. Nothing difficult or special. About 45 minutes in we got a salad and our chicken satay. We waisted about 30 more minutes and by this time we're both really annoyed that other tables that arrived after us were eating and/or done and getting ready to leave! We told the waitress that we were leaving and she got the manager. The manager apologized and said I take care of then left and when she returned she said I put your ticket next! So who knows when we would have gotten our food. We've ate here for 12 years and never had a problem at the old location. Our first visit to the new location was definitely disastrous. We assumed our meal was going to be comped but no. We ended up being there almost 2 hours. By the time we got the rest of our food we really didn't want to eat and didn't enjoy it.  
It was a very sad experience overall.

text: We loved this place in the past, but it has taken a turn.  We had their "new" chicken salad sandwich today which had old discolored iceberg lettuce on it...ugh.  Limited chicken salad also on it, for a $14 sandwich.  Ironically their "old" chicken salad sandwich was FABULOUS and I went specifically to get it many times. Service tonight was ok, but they also had a very loud (and not great) band outside.  Hoping that Farmer's Daughter will go back to the way it has been in years past.

text: Had the best salmon burger of my LIFE here today! And my fiance had the bacon and blue, which is usually what I would've ordered, and it was RIDICULOUS!!!! The only thing I would've changed would be adding a few more jalepenos to my salmon burger. It was perfectly dressed, perfectly cooked, the vegetables and meat were super fresh. I could've asked for a better burger!!! Their sign is hard to read (other than BURGERS) from the road, but don't let that fool you. These guys are LEGIT. So glad we found them on Yelp, driving from Orlando to Cape Coral.

text: Terrific new Italian restaurant just West of the main section of downtown Collingswood. The waitstaff is very well trained and made lots of recommendations and knew the menu. text: Unfortunately, for the past (and only) two visits to this joint, I have been disappointed.  I say unfortunately and disappointed because I have been told numerous times before that they sell good social food here, and the atmosphere is relatively hip for the area.  I have ordered a variety of tacos, mainly, which have been bland, out of cultural touch, and sloppily prepared.  Typically, I can deal with the blandness or oddity so long as the food is either healthy, good, unique, or any combination of the three; of which, this food is none.  With that being said, it is a cute physical place, worked by a younger crew (service can be sporadic/unorganized), and stationed in what is or will be a prime location in town.  I would recommend Station Taproom, as a much more satisfying alternative in the immediate area.

text:

We love to recommend this place but our last visit was mediocre and this one was terrible... won't recommend  again.

text:
My husband and I drove up to Santa Barbara for the day for my birthday. I remember coming here several years ago and loving it. However, this time fell flat, very flat. I looked at the menu beforehand to see what I could eat considering I have many more dietary restrictions this time around and saw they had what I thought to be a charcuterie board. Perfect, meat and cheese. No bread, no pasta. I'll order that. 
We had our dog with us so we sat outside. I'm giving two stars simply for the fact that the outdoor seating is adorable and was grateful we could partake in lunch with our dog. Very well done. Unfortunately, the service is counter service only until 4. So I sit with our dog and tell my husband I want the meat and cheese board. He goes in and comes back out saying it is either a meat board or a cheese board. What?!!! They weren't kidding either. So instead of the beautiful charcuterie I was envisioning on the two hour ride from Los Angeles, I got some slices of salami, prosciutto, and mortadella. It was pretty awful. Didn't even want to eat it. Fed a little to my dog. Birthday lunch was pretty much ruined. 
If I wanted both meat and cheese they would have charged me 16 for each. I've spent less for beautiful charcuterie boards that come with crudités and jams and toasted bread and nuts along with meat and cheese. 
My husband's pasta came as a HUGE portion. It was lunch so I was shocked how heaping his bowl was. Penne with bolognese. Tasted very acidic when I took a bite. Very underwhelming. 
It's sad when a place you used to think of fondly misses the mark so badly. 
Feel like I wasted a birthday lunch on this place.
name: Chanel

text:
If you're looking for healthy food or something light- Fuel should be on your radar! Their menu is all under 500 calories and $10. 

I used to come here pretty frequently a few years ago. I stopped coming and haven't been for awhile but just recently I have seen them on social media and that they made an app for your phone to receive discounts and I thought their marketing was rad and definitely worth another shot. When I came in I realized that they updated their menu as well. 

Everything here is awesome and they offer options for vegans, vegetarians, gluten free and those with no dietary restrictions. They have tofu, chicken and other options and I really like the diversity of their menu. They have appetizers, salads, bowls, sandwiches, wraps and even juices and smoothies. The calories are shown and don't include bread but you can easily ask for those calories because they have them available as well. 

The parking unfortunately isn't the best because it's Passyunk so it's street parking but the most I've ever parked is like 2 blocks away. They also have a check-in offer to get 10% off after 3 check ins and sometimes you can find them on Groupon!
name: Ariona

text: Food was hot and fresh.  Tastes fantastic.  Portions were very generous.  The service was great.  The Owner/Chef checked in on us.  Would highly recommend!
name: Lisa

text:
I finally made it here after hearing great remarks about this place. The food was absolutely delicious, but I can't go back and look at the menu to tell you the exact name of everything....because they change their menu daily!!  That is what is so awesome about the place.  We went Memorial Day weekend so the theme was more "grill out" or "picnic" with items like hot dogs or hamburgers. We started out with a soft shell crab and some strawberry cold soup (sorry I can't give more of a description as it is not on the menu today).  Both were delicious.

My daughter had the seafood boil, my wife had the whole "branzino" fish, and I had the grilled sirloin.  All of it was absolutely delicious, including the bread.  The only negative I have is that the red wine was very warm.  It seamed warmer than room temperature as if it is close to a light or warm kitchen.  That part was displeasing.  I know you can chill a bottle but just getting a glass gets you really warm wine.  I guess I am a wine snob that likes it from 55 degrees to less than room temperature.  Our server wasn't the best either and we had to wait for him on long periods of time....but I will still give this place a 5 stars for Margot's food.

text: The food came out fast, which was good because we were starving. The staff seemed tired but still polite. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait.
name: User

text: I love this place, great snack options, even better fresh food, can't go wrong, from breakfast to a midnight snack
name: Allison

text:
It's sad that it has taken me this long to try Ichicoro. The restaurant is located in Seminole Heights in what appears to be an old warehouse. The parking lot is small but we didn't have an issue on a Sunday afternoon. I also like that you can join the line via the NoWait App so you don't have to worry about waiting forever, which is good because the restaurant is very tiny.

I really like the atmosphere of this place, it's trendy but cozy at the same time and I enjoyed the stump stool chairs. The menus are dry erase boards, so you mark what you want to eat with a dry erase marker which is a cool idea. We started off with the Karaage which was super crispy and was complimented perfectly by the spicy garlic mayo. Now for the ramen, I went with the Mushroom Ramen which was amazing. It was loaded with different kinds of mushrooms and truffle butter, I also liked the option of adding whatever extras you wanted. I could barely finish, it was so filling, but I couldn't leave a drop of that delicious broth in the bowl.

Service was very friendly and we were in and out in about 30 minutes (but didn't feel rushed at all). I'll definitely be back!
name: Annah

text: Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. The music was louder than it needed to be. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Would probably stop in again if nearby. The food was good and the service was easygoing.

text: Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. The wait felt longer than it should have. text:
On opening night the service staff was on its game, we were impressed! Food was very good, elevated pub food with an Italian accent. We didn't really understand the name or the concept though -- draft beer, bourbon flights, bar food, sports bar. 
  We wanted to sample a lot and so we ranged across the menu and were impressed, no misfires. We got a pizza to taste and take home for later (nice crust, crisp with good chew). App: Fabio's meatballs on polenta (creaminess of polenta balanced out the hearty meatball and spicy marinara). App: croquettes with beer cheese, grainy mustard, and a really delicious lemon chutney. Side: creamed spinach (hot from the broiler, minimal cream). Pasta: Mac and cheese with smoked brisket (orecchiette, not baked but a loose sauce so not heavy, with tiny cubes of the tenderest brisket and a lovely smokiness. We were prevailed upon to try dessert: three scoops of gelato (more like ice cream), good flavor on both the salted caramel and the double chocolate). Setting aside the pizza: bill with tip came to $80 including two glasses of wine, and that's more food than we'd normally order. Pretty good! Be warned: very loud! Had a hard time hearing someone sitting directly across the table!
name: Peter

text:

text:
Waiters are friendly and happy here. They also keep the coffee and water flowing and ask if there's anything else you need; outstanding service. 

I'm definitely a carnivore but the Two Chics has me wanting more veggies; veggie fritters, oh yeah! I must say I now have a new love for vegetables. 
The butter is very dangerous here too, it's favored with fresh strawberries or blueberries. I'm a butter lover already and whipped with flavors like this, it's easy to get in trouble. 

I ordered their chicken fried steak with over medium eggs and veggie fritters. Eggs were cooked to perfection and my chicken fried was too. The gravy is the bomb! I come from gravy capital (Texas) and the Two Chics do it right! Portions are pretty hearty here but I just couldn't leave without trying the Simply Sinful melt sandwich; gooey marshmallow cream, peanut butter, Nutella and bananas, that's all. After all this and to my surprise, I was able to comfortably and happily exit the premises after this without rolling out assistance.

This is definitely one of my favorite breakfast spots now. I want to try their butternut squash cereal next time I go, it just sounds so comforting.

text:
After a night at Laurel, needed a good brunch and came here.  The wait was not terrible. The guy you put your name in with has a list and says the wait is 30-40 minutes but it's more like 20-25.  

Initially we put in our name then went to get coffee at Honeys which was good then we had to put in our name again since we missed him calling for us lol.  

I was on crutches due to a minor snowboarding injury last weekend and they were quick to seat us and take my crutches to set aside since it's small tight spot.  

We started with a coffee which was good La Colombe which I love and yellow lentil soup.  My buddy got the sweet potato bisque.   

After taking forever for us to decide what we wanted since so many items on the menu sounded so good I went with the eggs Benedict with bacon.  While it was good I wish I went with something else different like the huevos rancheros.  My buddy got the lamb pita and his girl got the open faced Mediterranean burrito both of which were better than the regular eggs benny lol.  

At least I got the yellow lentil soup which was piping hot and very delicious! And two pieces of bread to dip with.  

Staff is friendly and rotate throughout keeping your water filled, topping off your coffee and taking away your plates when your done to help with the quick turnover.  

This place does seem slightly more expensive than other brunch areas like others have noted but it is worth the wait and time to try and I am going to have to go back to try something else!

text:
My fiancé and I go here about once a week so I felt it was about time I write a review. I've had their tacos before which I like but I usually get their bowls with chicken, a tiny bit of brown rice, pico, guacamole, salsa and cilantro. In my opinion, I like their bowls better than Chipotle, but I've never been a Chipotle fan anyway. The only thing I will say is that their chicken is hit or miss-sometimes it's good but sometimes it's a bit too chewy for me. They're burritos are also way better than Chipotle's. They actually don't even compare because they're on an entirely different level. 

Now for the real reason I wrote this review: their nachos. I tried them for the first time the other day and they were SO GOOD. I'm very picky when it comes to nachos and usually don't like nachos at many places, so for me to feel this compelled to write a review about nachos is a big deal. 

I got mine with queso, Mexican rice, black beans, queso, cheese, guacamole and cilantro. My fiancé got his with queso, Mexican rice, ground beef, cheese, salsa and cilantro. I don't really know what it is that makes these nachos so good-I really don't. I've ordered nachos like this at other places, but they haven't been as good, so I suppose it's just their flavors/freshness of the ingredients.

I've also never had any issues at this location in terms of service or cleanliness. They can be a bit slow at times, but other than that everything has been great.

I ended up having to send it back and wait another 10-15 minutes for the new dish to come out. The flavor wasn't bad and the sweet potato latke that came with it was ok. It was nice that three different staff members came up to our table, including our waiter, apologizing for the dish being undercooked. They ended up giving our entire party of 4 free dessert as well. I would have liked to see them remove the entree from our bill, but free dessert was a very nice gesture. I probably would eat here again, but I'm in no rush to return any time soon.

My meal was NOT comped despite what management states!  Free dessert lol


This is absolutely pathetic that Harvest feels the need to lie about what occurred during our visit to make themselves look better. I am taken back that they are publicly arguing with a customer on Yelp. My intentions was never to have this situation taken so far and out of control. We paid with cash as well as a $10 off gift card. We know how much the total was, and I'm appalled that they are blaming the customer for lying and not owning up to their mistakes. Don't call your customers out publicly and expect them to message you privately. The sad part about this whole incident is that I really enjoyed going here.... What a shame!

text:
Let me start off by saying that Langhorne PA is the place of long forgotten restaurant chains. We stayed for a weekend and I could have eaten myself into a food coma trying all of the restaurants that used to exist in my area growing up during my youth. Thankfully my wife was there to be my food governor. 

The Ground Round was a popular restaurant growing up in my neck of the woods, always packed, with floors littered with peanut shells and one night a week was all you can wings. In the 80s it made a national book as one of the hot spots to meet and socialize (odd, right?). 

This wasn't the GR of old, more in line with today's fare of Applebees, Chili's, etc... and that is not bad!

Since it was in walking distance from the hotel I had a corona, the Mrs. a glass of wine and the baby a chocolate milk. 

dinner consisted of salads for each adult, steak dinners and the 3 year old had what just about every 3 year old has: chicken nuggets/tenders and fries. 

Pros:
-The servers were friendly, super aware of the child and took the initiative to bring her food out first without prompting. The brought her crayons and were super engaging.
-The food was good, not too expensive and cooked to our specs.
-The eating area of the restaurant was clean and appealing and had TVs on as a nice distraction for the little one.

Cons:
-The A/C was too cold and we changed our seat 3 times but everywhere we tried there was always a vent over us.
-The restrooms could have used a bit more TLC. The floors were sticky like a 70s movie theatre.
-My wife did not enjoy the wine (wine is not their strong suit).

Overall, it's a nice place with good food that won't break the bank.
name: Rich

text:
Mad Beach Craft Brewing is a cute little brewery/restaurant located on the second floor of the John's Pass shopping area. The beer (and cider!) selections were fantastic, and while I wasn't absolutely in-love with my pretzel and cheese, the menu was varied enough that I'd still be excited to try something else next time. Plus, the ambiance is fantastic and there are SO many games!

NOTE: If you're into coupons, there's a coupon in the Welcome Guide-Map for Tampa Bay and Gulf Beaches hand-out for the 2018 season that you can find around the area in markets and hotels. It's for a Free Tots Fondue, Select draft beer, Sangria, or wine by the glass with purchase of $15 or more. 

ACCESSIBILITY NOTE: Mad Beach Craft Brewing is located on the second story of the John's Pass shopping area. There are a couple different elevators located throughout John's Pass, but Mad Beach Craft Brewing is lucky enough to be located right in front of one. There are also stairs next to it. 

PROS:
-Lovely interior. It's roomy, spacious, and well-decorated. The ceiling lights make an amazing statement with the high ceilings and huge layout. Tons of huge tables with lots of chairs that make this place a good fit for huge parties. There are some booths for smaller parties as well. 
-Enough toys to entertain you for years. If you love lots of social games when you drink, you're going to love Mad Beach. There's SO much to do. There's an air hockey table, multiple bags stations, giant bean bags that are right next to a giant projector TV, a jukebox, tons of Super NES game consoles pre-loaded with games, multiple pool tables, large Jenga blocks, and more. There's a ton of stuff to do while you drink here. 
-Fantastic beer selection - especially if you love cider. When we went, they had a coconut, pineapple, and strawbeery cider. While the pineapple was gone, we got to try the other two and went home with crowlers of both of them. Fantastic, unique taste that doesn't taste like anything you'd try at the store. You can find those "core, familiar beers", but it seems like Mad Beach is also experimenting with unique and different beer tastes, and I like that. 
-This place does serve pretzels. I'm a stickler for good soft pretzels. However, they're listed under the "Beer Cheese" as the menu item. And it's definitely clear that the beer cheese is the focus of the dish. The pretzels are okay - but more like bread than pretzels. The beer cheese is the stand-out of the two, and it has a unique thickness and silkiness that I've never tried anywhere else. Similar to the consistency of Velveeta - only with a taste that's nothing like Velveeta. It was a good experience to try. 
-Staff here has a sense of humor and seem to enjoy their jobs as well. Every few minutes, we were hearing a squeaky toy - and confused as to where it was coming from. We finally realized that it was being used as the "food is served!" bell from the kitchen area. Once we realized that, we noticed that the chefs were squeaking it in different manners and laughing about the way they were doing it every time the waitresses showed up to pick up the food. It's really nice to see people enjoying their jobs. 

CONS:
-If you were coming for the pretzels, the pretzels don't taste much like pretzels. More like bread. Depends on whether you were coming for the beer cheese or the pretzels.
-As this location is located in John's Pass, you'll need to pay for parking. It's likely not going to be too much of a walk once you find a spot, but if you aren't enjoying anything else in the area, it'll add to the frustration factor of getting here. 
-We came during a weekday. After we had finished our meal, we were pretty excited to play around with some of the game offerings, but there were tons of children running around while parents ate at the tables nearby. I know that it's not the restaurant's responsibility or fault that children are impeding on the enjoyment of some of the items, but none of us felt comfortable sticking around to play Jenga or walking around to play the Pool table for fear of stepping or tripping over a kid.

text: Although their is food is fresh and great, this location is not the greatest. I get takeout when I do go there and usually have to ask for something That was supposed to go with the meal. Like dressing on my salad, I asked for the dressing because there was none. I got a reply with attitude, that it was on the salad. I asked for an extra dressing anyways and thank goodness because when I got home there was absolutely no dressing on the salad.
name: Sherri

text:
We picked up dinner here one night--there's a ton of construction on the surrounding streets and we had a bit of difficulty navigating to the restaurant.  Once we were there, the service at the restaurant was perfect--super friendly and thoughtful.  The person who put our order together double checked each item and thoughtfully provided the needed accoutrement.  They have a self-serve sauce bar which is really well stocked and organized.  This was an easy way to make sure that each person got their po' boys dressed the way that we preferred. 

The food was good!  The sandwiches were stuffed with shrimp.  I didn't love the potato salad--I thought it was a bit dry.  However, the French fries were perfect!  Overall, a solid choice for lunch or dinner.
name: M

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The wings had a good kick to them but the texture was inconsistent. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Not bad for a quick meal. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text:
Pluses = Good food and Atmosphere pleasant.

Deltas = Bus staff wanted to remove plates while we were still eating. To make it clear the bus staff did not offer a take away box for the food remaining on our plates only the statement "I will take your plate." One might ask were we dallying with our meal, this I assure you was not the case. 
Inattentive waitress despite time of day and activity of restaurant. 
One other delta to add was as we returned to our car we noted the male host had exited the front entrance. Immediately after exiting he stood only one to two steps from the entrance steps and began smoking. Was this just a poor representative of a quality establishment?
name: Katie

text:
Quite possibly one of the worst experiences I've ever had at a restaurant. 

I'd been here before a couple of times, and received friendly service each time, so I did not expect to be met with the incredibly demeaning service my boyfriend abc I received last night. 

When we asked for a menu with toppings for the build your own pizza (which was plainly listed on the menu) the server responded back in a nasally tone with an exasperated sigh, "we don't have a list of ingredients, what kind are you looking for? It's your basic ingredient list." My boyfriend and I were both taken aback, not only with the server's rudeness and unwillingness to serve us, but because the last time we were there, we were gladly offered a list of ingredients, which is how we knew the restaurant has one. 

The server continued his snotty and off-putting attempt at conversation, "I do know we are out of pepperoni, and that pissed me off." After he left, my boyfriend and I looked at each other awkwardly. We felt uncomfortable and unwelcome. The waiter came back and obnoxiously informed us, "we do have bacon!"

After that, we decided to leave. If that was the first 15 minutes, we could not imagine what we'd have to tolerate for the rest of the night. The experience was so upsetting that I doubt I'll be back at Basso anytime soon. It's important to treat all people with respect, and servers shouldn't need to be reminded of such.
name: Yoli

text:
This place is so cute - totally midtown hipster vibe of Reno.  Met some family there last week so my sister could try their 'impossible' burger - it's so dang good!

The reason I give this place 3 stars is a couple quick things - 1. The price - they charge $15 for a vegan burger - compared to others around town, that is a few dollars more.  And the side dishes are a joke - the fruit was basically just honeydew melon that tasted like a carrot (very hard) and the shoe string fries were practically raw.  The drinks (alcoholic) are a minimum $6 per, pretty reasonable for a midtown type restaurant. Oooh, and the appetizer (we got deviled eggs) are extremely small portioned and pricey as heck. I was so surprised. 2. The reservation/seating policy - this place is small, once the dining area fills up, instead of telling you a wait time or anything, they ask for reservations only... so we sat at the bar, no biggie... just didn't know this policy, and it is pretty unorthodox. 3. They seem insanely under staffed. Sitting at the bar, a group of 4 - one waitress and the whole place was packed. The waitress was pregnant too, poor lady! She should be pampered! Poor lovely, seemed so overwhelmed, forgetting drinks for us, and just seemed like she had had it. 

So, it was A-OK. I've been there a few times.  And I'll probably go back.
name: Sallie

text:
I came here with an associate, as we were curious about the various Mexican restaurants that Italian Market has to offer! We found this place randomly and decided that the next time we went to south philly, we'd come here. 
So we came here during brunch hours, and they have the brunch menu! I got the ham omelette which is perfectly doused in light cheese sauce, seasoned rice, and beans. It was fantastic and not way too heavy, but very filling. My associate had an al pastor taco and beef taco combo, all of which were fantastic and flavorful! Tender meat, juicy. Service was excellent! The guy helped us get to know the menu very well and made sure we knew what we were getting. Even explained the al pastor tacos being a little on the fatty side, just in case we were not into that I guess. That's always nice to know the details of the food we get. I would definitely come back here!
name: Jeannie

text: They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. No big complaints, just a nice meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. It was crowded but still moved along. Will be back. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: Service was amazing. Super attentive waitress & good food. Also a good selection of mocktails. The burlesque show was spectacular. Can't wait to come back.
name: Susan

text:
So we used to order from here all the time then they started going down hill- missing items, taking super long, food quality declining- final straw was an error on an order that they wouldn't correct without me having to pay an additional fee (ordered a la cart - they gave me a combo) when I called and told them I would return the item and would pick up correct item / they told me I would have to pay the difference? I ordered correctly - and was willing to go go and pick up - said forget it / stopped going there for over two years! Bring us to today....husband ordered from there / guess what - they forgot a quart of something - when my husband called - they asked him four times to count the containers??? Really??? When he went back I told him just get the money back you don't know what they have done to our food? He packed everything up - so they could count containers - they wouldn't give his money back 
It was fried rice - maybe $7? You lost a customer over that!??? Shame on you!! Too many gigs in town to treat us like we were trying to rip you off for rice 

So now we won't be back
name: Jody

text: I was thrilled to hear a proper southwestern breakfast taco joint was hitting East Nash (brought to us from the Butcher and The Bee chef, I believe). Having lived in Texas twice, totaling around 7 years, I came to know the joy that is a breakfast taco. My wife and I gave this place a try this past week (opening week) with high hopes but we were let down in many areas. Yes there was an incredibly long wait (took a little over an hour to get 7 tacos) but we expected that on opening week and with it being in east nash. Tacos that tasted and looked as if they had been sitting under a heat lamp for 30mins and being filled about halfway (I'm not lookin for a 'merican sized taco here but not a laughable, pathetic looking portion either), decor that seemed more suitable for a cafe you would find in IKEA (although we loved the diner vibes present in this place), and feeling the stress of the kitchen were some of the most notable things. I do believe these guys are still finding their footing and flow. While we were disappointed with the food, we found the servers to be total pros (we even chatted with the bartender about some of these observations and she was very chill and open minded hearing all the feedback) and potential for the vibe and overall workflow of this place to hopefully settle in. They had a guy working on building a deck for outdoor seating while we were there, which is awesome. We didn't try the margaritas but they looked pretty tasty. I'm giving this place 3 stars because it does have loads of potential and it has great Nashville food people backing it. We will try going back in a month or two and see what has changed.
name: Matt

text: It's a Vietnamese restaurant with yummy phó! I like this location do to its location to my work. The staff are friendly and prompt. It's not the most upscale restaurant, but most good Vietnamese places aren't. It's just a good and quiet location to enjoy some good rice noodle soup and spring rolls. I need to sample the drinks next time. We'll see how those stack up. I love a good boba!
name: Bob

text: Brunch never disappoints. Expect a wait during peak times, but the staff is usually very friendly & engaging, despite having their hands full, often literally. If you like Bloody Mary's then you should definitely try P&P's, not only is it delicious, but it is also accompanied by a quasi-petit aperitif & canapé to hold you over until your food arrives!

text: I am sitting in Daawat having a scrumptious meal. My new favorite Indian buffet. I have been to many, hands down the best in town.
name: Dan

text:
OMG.  Horrible. Mobile order for drive thru. They shut the drive thru down. Went inside. Waited, waited, waited. Manager in the phone talking with a friend while attempting to make fries

I hope the owner goes broke.  The lack of oversight is amazing
name: brett

text:
Drop the kids off came here for a late valentines dinner. The wife and I really get to go out alone. So we are shooting the works. Drinks, steaks, lobster and crab (Oscar). 

Wife bought some gift cards from Costco so we could try this steak house. $100 for the price of $75. Its always a great deal while trying a new place. 

First I must warn you, that if you do not like country music, you should not come here. The whole two hours we were here, it was like a country western Radio station without the adverts. Decor is also full of cowboy memorabilia, cowboy boots, hats, saddles, ropes And electric guitars all over the walls. Plus a deer head....

We ordered a ruby tini and an ultimate Margarita (substitute the 1800 for Patron) for drinks. For dinner we ordered the 20 ounce prime rib (medium rare) and the bacon wrapped filet, Oscar style, with an ad on lobster tail. We don't normally go so decadent, however it's a Valentine's Day celebration, even if late. 

We are allowed to choose two sides and I chose the mushrooms and asparagus, my wife chose the garlic mashed potatoes with white gravy and the roasted tomatoes with Parmesan. For dessert we ordered the fresh apple cobbler (Togo)

The steaks were cooked perfectly. The Filet with crab/asparagus was perfect. Had a nice Smokey flavor. Probably from the bacon wrapped around it. We did have an issue with the 20 ounce prime rib, as you can see in the pictures it was about half fat. I remove the fat and I showed it to the waiter. He did acknowledge the he noticed a lot of fat. He said he brought it to the managers attention, and she took $10 off our dinner. I Told him I didn't think that was good enough as half of the steak was fat. The manager never came by our table. She took another five dollars off, but come on, the chef should be trained in recognizing this and adjusting the cut. Also, since there Was so much fat, Why not just comp the steak? The mushrooms were great, all of the sides were great. 

We probably won't try this place again. The quality control was lacking. The service was great. The price is just too high considering you pay $30 for about 10 oz of meat. Maybe they need a little work on keeping customers by fixing problems on their end. I am not a picky customer, but I do expect High-quality  for a $30 twenty oz prime rib.
name: Tommy

text: Absolutely the worst pizza delivery in STL. We placed an order at 11:30 pm and kept having to repeatedly call for an update because our pizza never showed. At 12:50 we were told it was on the way. At 1:15 we called because the restaurant was .5 miles away. They told us our order had been cancelled. We waited 2 hours for a pizza that was never coming! Absolutely ridiculous. When I asked for a refund on my card they hung up on me and said "have a good night". Robert Nelson was the manager on duty.
name: Tailor

text: This place is an absolute dump. Crazies inside. Crazies outside. One normal person in the whole place. I looked up a sports bar near 30th Street Station to watch football before my train. Only true statement is sports because there was football on the TVs. Maybe it's cool at night but stay far far away while the sun is up
name: George

text: The waiter was friendly and gave us a complimentary appetizer (so sweet) but the sushi just wasn't fantastic. My sweet potato tempura roll had barely any sweet potato. The salmon roll fell apart and the shrimp tempura roll was mostly cucumber. Everything is pretty cheaply priced so I guess you get what you pay for but there are certainly better sushi joints in the city.
name: Christina

text: This is our 2nd visit to Mario's during our vacation and both days they were scheduled to be open and they were not.  They are scheduled 5-9pm and we arrived at 5:30pm and the doors were locked.  No note on the door, no notice, nothing.  The last time we will visit Mario's.

text: There food is out of this world I've been goin there since I was a lil girl my mother is really good friends with the two owener they are brothers my mom also grow up with them..

text: I will agree with one of the posters who said this is definitely not the best location in the chain. I've had a wonderful experience at the CPK on City Avenue but the Plymouth Mall location should be avoided at all costs (unless you're not in a rush and don't care how long it takes to get your food -- if you even get it. I was already frustrated by poor service the last few times I went here but last night's took the cake and I won't be back. I came with a party that included my sister-in-law and her three young children (one a newborn!). We were in a bit of a rush. The one child got her food promptly. Our entries never came. After almost an hour wait (and the server repeatedly saying "it will be right out") we flagged the waiter and asked what was going on. He was very snooty and short with us and said he couldn't help what was going on in the kitchen. Eventually we all had to leave without getting our food. We flagged down a manager and told her to cancel the order. She comped the kids meal but all in all did not seem very concerned about our experience. I'm going to stay away from this CPK...
name: Michele

text: We've ordered online many times and loved it, we thought we'd try visiting there to eat. Big mistake. Every order has something wrong. A Caesar salad in a tiny cup (and I mean tiny, like the size of a small sides cup) with no dressing for $9? No rolls on the meals, had to ask three times. And another salad with just cold fatty meat, at least that one was the appropriate size for a salad. Very unappetizing.
name: Kris

text: 2 stars? Hear.. ahem.. read me out.  Came here for my girlfriends birthday and I was not too impressed.  I've driven by this place multiple times and it looked like a cool spot. Now, that part does not disappoint. When you walk inside, it has that modern industrial feel to it. Cool decor, cool phrases on the wall and an overall modern look. I went for lunch around 3 pm and the place was empty. Now it was a Tuesday and not happy hour yet, so you'd think service would be fast? Nope. The waitress who was also the hostess , while friendly, did not know many of the menu items or any of the beers I mentioned. Also the food took so long to come out, and again, we were the only ones there at the time. Also , when the food came out it lacked a lot of flavor. I ordered the crab ravioli, which sounded delicious, but was bland and very small in portion. $16 plate I definitely expected a little more to it. The best part of the meal was the deviled eggs appetizer we had. It had some good flavor to it. The last thing that really through me off was when I asked for a Kentucky mule and they brought it out without the whiskey. That sealed the deal for me. The place is nice & the waitress nice, but service and food is lacking.
name: Noel

text:
Wasn't impressed with the food. 
Chilaquiles were dry and way too spicy. 
I place my order over the phone and the to go boxes are typical of Mexican restaurants. 
Small portions. 
Only thing good was the homemade tortillas.

I ordered 4 quesadillas, an order of chilaquiles with steak at whatever extra cost I needed to pay to get it and 4 steak gorditas.  I spent over $50 for my food which I don't care if it's as delicious as it's reviewed to be. 

Quesadillas are made with homemade tortillas, which are what makes this 2 stars.  The salsa they use is extra watered down making the quesadillas extra soggy. 
Quesadillas were probably the best out of my order. 

Chilaquiles were DRY and OVERLY spicy. 
The owner seems to think chilaquiles means extremely spicy to the point you're pretty done eating after 3 spoonfuls.  Quality and delicious are obviously below spicy in his list of things that are important when making food.  The steak I paid $9 for was chopped into pieces on top of my chilaquiles, which I'm sure was done to give me less of what I paid for.  The steak was seasoned well and that too contributes to two stars I'm giving. 

The Gorditas are basically two of the homemade tortillas, one on bottom and one on top, filled with steak and beans. No crema and hardly any cheese.
The sauce, again, made the gorditas nice and soggy as you can tell by some of the pictures the owner has posted.
The masa the shell is supposed to be made of was cooked on the stove top I'm assuming because it was just seared as you can tell in one of the pictures the owner posted. You should be deep frying the masa, not pan searing. 

Overall, it's a typical Mexican restaurant in Reno. 
I would stick with Mexican food trucks for sure.
name: The Gallant

text: The service was fast and the food was really good the drinks were very sweet but good none the less! And they give you beads with the check which was a great touch!
name: Samantha

text: The best, most authentic poboys in Nola. These guys have been a family business for years, and they know what they are doing. The biscuits (no matter what you get on them) are fantastic too. Super inexpensive menu. Usually a line, but worth it. A hole in the wall, but many gems are.
name: Allison

text: We went to the regular Sunday brunch buffet today. Those shrimp are still amazing, and the food choices were even better than the last two times we visited. Today, we also sampled pasta al forno, hand-carved roast beef, caprese chicken (with a great pesto sauce), crab-stuffed flounder, roasted vegetables and a few breakfast items. We didn't like climbing the long staircase to get to the restrooms, but the downstairs restrooms were closed. The service put The Stone Barn over the top for us today. Our servers were pleasant, efficient and delightful! The price for the regular brunch is $25/person, which we felt was reasonable for what we got.
name: Mary

text:
I was charged for drink at lunch and I never ordered one, nor was i apologized to for the discrepancy.   I felt uncomfortable after I pointed out the discrepancy. The individual who I identify as the proprietor was waving her arms around over at the register when speaking around her staff.  This is in direct eye view of everyone in the restaurant.  Lunch was not bad tasting, but the whole exchange at the end turned my stomach.  I checked receipt from the last time I had lunch there, again I I was charged for a drink i did not order.  I think this may be a systemic problem and that really puts me at unease from ever going there again.  If this keeps up, I'm sure another restaurant is not far behind in her spot.  
I don't wish to eat where the proprietor is pinching pennies to this extent.   Not a pleasant lunch!  Watch your receipts.
name: Craig

text: Been going here off and on for a long while. They are much improved over this time period. It goes without saying that one gets out what one is willing to put in. If a server is dealing with an uppity asshole then they will end up paying the price somehow.
name: Thomas

text:
We order "cheap Chinese" take out food from here about once a month when we are pressed for time or it's too late to start cooking dinner.   The food is passable but inconsistent in that depending who is cooking will affect how spicy the food is.   

Generally the food is pretty sleepy but we have tried so many places within a 3 mile radius and have found nothing better except the place in Media but it is also expensive and not a quick event.

Typically we order from an abbreviated list of the fried dumplings, Kung pao chicken, the General Tso's chicken, chicken with broccoli, moo shoo pork, house fried rice, roast pork lo mein and egg foo young.

Don't order delivery.   They underestimate the time significantly.

The youthful voice on the phone gets the order right every time but has a rude edge.
name: P

text: I came here after a night out with friends. We couldn't find the place at first because all we saw was the club. We ended up going inside, hoping for the best. All the way in the back of the club is the entrance to the restaurant. It's a tiiiiny place with just a few tables. We ordered vegetarian burgers with a fried egg and the mac and cheese bites at the window. The guy that took our order was not super nice. Looked like he didn't want to be there, not sure. The food was yummy though! Great fried drunk food for sure.
name: Sandra

text: It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Pretty happy with it overall. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text:
Excellent food and service!! Everyone that I've brought here has been satisfied. I have gone out of my way to come here when I craved pizza even though I live more than 20 minutes away. The prices are reasonable and the owners are wonderful to talk to. There is not a single pizza place in Florida that beats Magdalenas Pizzeria. 

I will continue to come here as long as I can. I highly recommend coming here if you are in the area or just craving pizza. You will not be disappointed.
name: G

text: After seeing so many posts from others and reviews.. finally decided to stop in and check out the hype. I ordered a classic burger and the special burger fry fries..there was a little wait on the food so I sat down in the dining area. It was large and clean. The food took about 15 minutes which I wasn't expecting to take so long. I even noticed others who had ordered after me got their food first. Guess the special fries take a little longer. I'll admit the appearance of the food was great. And it was fresh and tasty but the burger wasn't all that I was expecting and something about the taste of the fries threw me off a little bit. Also the prices are very high. BUT in the future I would love to try another burger, regular fries and a shake:)
name: Jenna

text: I am giving two stars, one for decent decor, and the other for our nice server who was attentive and had a great smile. That means nothing for the food. From the reviews, I was thinking I had a 50/50 chance of getting a fresh lobster roll, but sadly, not my day. I ordered a Connecticut style, which is supposed to be poached and drenched in butter. Not today, as it was drier than a bone, and tasteless to boot. I also upgraded from the homemade chips and apple slaw to a side of lobster mac and cheese for $4. It was a small cup serving with one piece of lobster on the top. I  know my lobster, having grown up in a restaurant up North, and ate so much fresh live Maine lobster, I didn't eat it for 3 years after I after I moved away. My friend opted for the Parmesan Truffle fries upgrade for $3.50 extra, and they were overcooked to the point of dry inside, very little Parmesan sprinkle, and Truffle taste nonexistent. I did see some good reviews for lobster rolls, but not worth my $28 including tax and tip to roll that dice again. Shame on this lobster establishment.
name: Lita

text: Food was great. The bearded hipster waiter that had to explain everything up to how to use a napkin was booth inauthentic and annoying, though.
name: Jenny

text: This place is adorable. Sitting at the bar. Great service and wonderful drinks. A perfect stop!

text: I wanted to like this more than I actually did. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Maybe better dine-in than delivery, hard to tell. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.

text: I ordered a Chicken Cheesesteak Stromboli & Two Slices of Pizza and the delivery was unbelievably fast. Realized that the food came fast because the Stromboli was not cooked thoroughly. The dough was extremely moist so I attempted to heat the Stromboli in the oven to finish cooking. After the top was finally browning we decided to cut it & realized that the chicken was also not cooked through. I called to inform the Employees who stated that he never had that problem before and did not attempt to apologize, resolve the complaint or have the Stromboli returned for inspection. I will never order from this place again

text: I cannot begin to express what an amazing supper club this place is.  The new owners of this space have done an a fantastic job in preserving the history of the building but elevating the experience to a venue where you don't want to leave.  The service is impeccable.  You are not rushed, we spent close to three hours at our table.  The food is outstanding!  The cocktails well crafted! The beer and wine list extensive.  Entertainment was amazing.  It's rare when you find a place where all points are hit.  Just one word of caution, do not go there for intimate conversation.  Go when you want to taste a gourmet Chef driven affordable priced menu, listen to amazing entertainment, enjoy craft cocktails and feel like your in another era!

text: This is a must if visiting St Pete. Amazing clam chowder great atmosphere and wonderful staff. So glad we stopped and will come again!

It looked better online than it did in person. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. For a busy night they handled it okay. Idk, i got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. not sure I'd order the same thing again. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..

text:

The salad had good flavor too. But the focaccia bread on the sandwich was amazing! Next time I go back, I want a sandwich. 

Price: prices are decent. Not cheap but not super expensive. I've posted the menu so you can decide if it's expensive or not.

Location: there's outside seating which is nice now that we have warm weather. Inside seating feels air conditioned which will be perfect for summer. 

Overall: recommend for a quick lunch.

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kinda a mixed bag. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Food was fresh and service was quick. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Would absolutely visit again. Food took a while and didnt really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: This was by far the worst dinner service we have had in a very long time. It took our waiter over thirty minutes just to get our drink orders. Now, I understand that it was a busy Saturday night but it was another 30 minutes before our dinner order was taken. 15 minutes after our dinner order was taken two loaves of hot French bread( very tasty ) were delivered to our table of 7. We had to ask for bread plates..which arrived substantially later. Ok...so it's been about one and a half hours since we have been seated...the two tiny loaves of bread are long since gone and our waiter promised more...which eventually showed up ...and we finally get our appetizers: soup or salad. My tomato basil soup was a bit heavy but the ceaser salad ( of which I shared from my date) was very good. We finish our appetizer course and begin waiting for our entrees...and waiting...and waiting...and finally forty minutes after we finished our salad, we get our entrees. My two sister in laws ordered their steaks medium and medium well respectively...they both had to be sent back because they were way too bloody.  My steak on the other hand was supposed to be medium rare and was not pink at all in the middle. It's a steak restaurant for goodness sake...and they can't cook their steaks made to order? text:
Dim sum in Tucson...at a sushi place?! Sure, why not? A surprising find in Tucson that satisfies the cravings of someone who grew up eating dim sum at variousChinese restaurants. This place has a lot of solid dishes and a few not-so-perfect traditional dim sum dishes.

What is dim sum? Think of it as a Chinese version of tapas. Various dishes are steamed and served in small metal or wooden baskets or plates. People in Hong Kong love to eat dim sum and drink tea as their version of brunch. 

Traditional dishes include pork spareribs, chicken feet, turnip cake, ha gow (shrimp in a translucent wrapper), and shu mai (pork and shrimp in a wonton wrapper), plus various dishes that are pushed around in a cart for customers to pick to their delight.

Although Sushi Lounge does not have a cart full of dim sum being pushed around and requires placing an order from a menu, there is a large amount of dishes to choose from. 

Chicken feet were flavorful and tasted authentic. Not a lot of people enjoy the cartilage and lack of actual meat on the chicken feet, so choose wisely or be bold and try this dish out. It's marinated chicken feet with black beans and tastes sweet.

The turnip cake had a bitter taste to it which is normal for radish; however, overripe or radish going bad may also have produced such bitterness (also slightly burnt food may create this as well). It was a decent dish.

The ha gow (shrimp) was served with 4 per dish. Great shrimp filling with flavor, but the wrapper was a bit thick compared to the filling inside. Decent, but could use some work.

The shu mai was seasoned perfectly with pork and wrapped in a wonton wrapper. Definitely one of the better dishes.

Egg tarts were deliciously filled with custard and a semi-flaky crust that could have been more flaky.

Other dishes not mentioned specifically were decent at best but probably will not be ordered again, including shrimp cheung fun, barbecue pork, and trip.

FYI-this place fills up pretty quickly around 11am so be sure to come early.
name: Cindy

text:
This restaurant is a new addition to Eagle's dining scene.  Franck Bacquet is a well known chef in the area.   Some of his restaurant associations are L'Coq Rouge, Angell's, and L'Coq D'or.   

The restaurant's decor is mostly French bistro style---earth tones, accompanied by posters and old photos of Montmartre and other well known destinations.  The most notable feature is a large chandelier, fit for a baronial hall!  It's a great focal point near the kitchen and wine cellar area.

The menu is handwritten and illustrated by Franck.  It's divided into appetizers, seafood, meat, a lunch menu, and a patio menu.   The food has some classic French components, like the escargot grand-mere, rack of lamb(which they were out of tonight), and tarte flambe(an Alsatian specialty.)  The rest of the menu has Italian flavors---veal piccata, ravioli with truffles, caprese tower.

We were dining with another couple and we chose to share entrees, remembering the generous portions that Franck served at other establishments.   I chose escargot grand-mere, my husband had coquilles au gratin and our friends shared ravioli with truffle.  The escargot were served in the traditional garlic butter in a porcelain dish and were as I remembered.  It's nice not to have to struggle with shells and clamps like the old way of serving snails.  I mopped up the sauce with the rest of the bread in the basket! My husband was not as happy with his dish as he was expecting a more creamier version of coquilles st. Jacques.   The ravioli with truffle looked beautiful and our friends seemed to enjoy them.

My husband and I chose Pork Gorgonzola---pork medallions in a gorgonzola cream sauce with a carmelized pear, fingerling potatoes,brussels sprouts, and roasted root vegetables as well as roasted endive(a treat!)   Our friends had Boeuf Forestier--rib eye with mushroom bacon sauce with root vegetables done medium rare.  It was a very thick steak, nicely cooked and very flavorful and tender.   The pork medallions were pounded thin, sauteed and cooked in a nicely flavored creamy sauce.

We all ordered dessert---raspberry layer cake, tuxedo cake, and creme brulee.  All delicious and enjoyed by all!  Fresh brewed coffee made it complete.

As this restaurant is new, there was no wine list.  The server listed the wines by the glass.  I noticed other people ordering bottles, so I guess one has to ask, or peruse the many bottles of good vintage that is on the shelves near the back of the restaurant.

It's great to see a new restaurant in town.  There is also a patio area and live music is featured every evening.  There were many folks out there this evening enjoying the nice weather, a good meal, and some mellow sounds of a female vocalist and keyboard player.  We wish the Bacquets much success in this new endeavor!
name: Mary

text:
The place has to be really bad for me to give 1 star.  If I could, I'd give it zero, it's that bad!

First a little background.  My wife is Taiwanese and I've been married to her for 43 years.  I've spent much time in Taiwan and I know what Taiwanese food is...this is NOT that.  The menu is laced with American/Chinese food that you can get at any typical American Chinese Restaurant. 

I ordered Chicken Curry (which is not Taiwanese food) as it was the only thing that I normally like.  It was the WORST tasting food I've ever received at a restaurant.  It had chucks of green pepper, onion, and chicken that tasted like it was boiled, not stir-fryed.  I think they just added the ingredients to a pot of water, boiled it and added some curry powder and called it Curry Chicken.  It was supposed to be spicy...nope, not spicy at all.

Usually if I have a bad experience at a restaurant, most of the time I give it another shot...not this time.  I have no desire to patronize this establishment ever again.  

Just remember, I warned you.

text:
My first time up in Zionsville, I had a good experience dining at the salty cowboy. I'll start with the food. I have pretty high standards for tacos, and the tacos here did not disappoint. The Pescado taco had perfectly crispy fish and a nice crema sauce over the top, and the Cancun Oink was a nice cross between BBQ and Mexican. The pulled pork on this one was moist and fresh. All three were truly delicious. If you are a fan of corn tortillas, this place makes them homemade does them very well. We also had tableside guacamole, and while this was good, it was lacking a little flavor. I would've like to see some seasonings added to it rather than just produce ingredients. 

For drinks, I ordered one of their spicy margaritas, and it was okay. I've had better, I've had worse. The price was reasonable though so I couldn't be too mad. Our service was also just slightly above average; my justification being that while she was very friendly, they were a couple instances of being absent when needed. 

Overall, I will come back to Salty Cowboy when I am in the Zionsville area. I live downtown and wouldn't go out of my way to get it, but I really enjoyed the fish and pulled pork tacos, and I would also be interested in trying their quesadillas, which I almost ordered in this first time trying the restaurant.

text:
I hate to write poor reviews, but three strikes and you're out. Aka the number of times that my meal at TBBC was messed up.

Came here for a Friday lunch with my sister with high hopes. She had been here previously and said that everything was delicious. The crowd on a Friday was surprisingly busy, and we opted to seat ourselves outside.

After taking some time to look at the menu, we ordered-- myself the tatanka (bison burger) and beer, and my sister the lobster roll.

Then... We waited. After about five minutes (and seeing folks who ordered beers after I did receive them), I flagged down a server to ask where my brew was. A couple minutes later, our server finally brought it, apologizing for the long wait. Strike #1.

Then... When the food finally came out, I noticed that my burger had no jalapenos on it, even though I had explicitly ordered them. When I brought it up to the server, he asked if I was sure that they weren't on the burger before saying that he would bring me some on the side. Strike #2.

Finally, while I was waiting for the jalapenos, I decided to take a look at my patty. I had ordered it medium rare, but cutting into it I saw a decidedly well-done and not at all juicy core. Strike #3.

When our server returned with the jalapenos, I brought up the problem with the burger. To the server's credit, he did have the kitchen re-make it. Only problem was, when the new burger came out it was still not cooked to specification. At best, it was medium to well-done. I know I said three strikes, but you could almost count this as strike #4...

However, by that point I was hungry and tired of the back and forth game, and since the burger at least wasn't cooked to the crisp, I opted to eat it. The verdict: pretty decent, but still decidedly not what I ordered.

So, overall, the final burger I got was ok. The beer was good. But the three (or four) mistakes in a single meal, oh boy. Our server did ask if we wanted the overcooked burger to go (which is a big no, considering I didn't want to eat it there means I definitely do not want to eat it at home), but really what I would have appreciated was a comp for something or at least a couple of different options presented to me for ways to make up for all the issues.
name: Angela

text:
Skillets Pancake House was not quite my first choice for a relatively late breakfast on this holiday morning but, in fact, my first two choices were both closed for the holiday. As I was driving around contemplating my options, I remembered that a new Square Donuts had gone in on this corner and I thought "Maybe I'll just have donuts." 

But then, I remembered spying this new place right around the corner and decided I'd go for something resembling an actual meal. Located in the large strip center on the Southwest corner of 96th & Allisonville Road, Skillets Pancake House is pretty much what you'd expect from a locally owned, indie breakfast/brunch type of joint. It offers mostly a breakfast menu, though there's a decent enough list of lunch options mostly in the way of a wide array of sandwiches. 

This strip center has multiple accessible parking spots. They're typically side-by-side spots with excellent curb cuts. The restaurant actually has two almost directly in front, though both were taken and I parked a little bit further down the building. There's a single-sided, double glass door entryway. My guess is it was already designed this way as the little lobby area appears to have little functional purpose (but is actually decorated). 

As you enter, there's a small hosting area and a dining area that includes wooden booths, quite a few tables, and a lunch counter type setting toward the back that was rather charming. I sat at one of the tables. It was a 4-top and definitely fine for a wheelchair. 

My server, whose name I never caught, was rock solid throughout. She brought out a glass of water. I opted for an order of buttermilk pancakes and a side of hash browns along with my usual unsweetened iced tea. The bill was a bit over $10 and definitely worth it. 

The clientele seemed rather diverse. This area is right on the Indy/Fishers line and in a strip center known for its diversity with multicultural restaurants, groceries, music, etc. It's definitely more of a blue collar joint, but it was clean and super comfortable. I definitely felt like this could be a place where you'd get known by the staff. 

The food? I won't say it was the best I've ever had, but it was very good across the board. The serving sizes were generous - the three pancakes were largely, almost too large, and served with butter and powdered sugar. They had syrup in smaller containers, but actually gave two of them. The hash browns were rock solid - just a hint of crispy and, again, in a solid serving size. I enjoyed both items and would easily order them again. My iced tea was refilled - she seemed a little surprised I wanted one considering I was near the end of my meal, but didn't flinch when I said "Yes" and didn't seem to mind when I lingered to read a bit. 

In terms of wheelchair access, most of the tables can easily be made accessible. The lunch counter would not be, while the booths would also be a challenge. However, there's quite a few options here and the aisles are decently roomy. 

Overall, I was quite happy here. While I'm not quite willing to go the 5-star review, I can easily call it a 4-star experience with really good food, fair prices, and top notch service. While this may have been an unintended visit, I have no doubt I will return in the future.
name: Richard

text:
If you're looking for a small, homey, quaint breakfast/brunch spot.. Cafe Audrey is your place! It's located in one of Fort Ben's historic brick buildings, just across from Jockamo's Pizza, off of 56th street.

I have been to Cafe Audrey quite a few times now and have yet to be disappointed. One thing I love is their bottomless coffee bar! They usually have 4 different choses.. decaf, a specialty, medium roast & then dark roast. Along with it, they have a variety of tea that you can have as well if you're not a coffee drinker. This especially comes in handy when there's a wait time.. you can go over to the coffee bar, pick out one of their many mugs, get your drink and then enjoy it while you wait for your table.

They serve breakfast and lunch all day so there are many options to choose from depending on what you're in the mood for. My favorite and go to meal is Florence's omelet w/fruit and their cinnamon toast. De-lic-ious! I haven't tried anything off of their lunch menu yet because I am just addicted to their breakfast but I have heard good things and maybe one of these days I'll step out of my bfast zone and try one of their lunch options.

Service is quick and the food is always fresh! Waitstaff is also very friendly and welcoming. They are very knowledgeable of the menu and are certain to make recommendations if you're in a rut.

text: I came here for brunch at 12:30 on a Sunday with a few friends. The games are awesome and I like the flag ordering system on the table to help flag down wait staff. However, even though we placed our order quickly it took a reallllly long time to get our food even though it was mainly easy breakfast items and it was not prime time for brunch. Our food ended up being good but we were really hungry by the time we got it. We ordered Hemingway and Bee's Knees cocktails which were both good and worth their cost. Also be aware everyone is charged a $5 library fee which reduces by $1 each time you order an item. I will definitely be back sometime but I'm put off by how inaccurate the wait time is. They need to take reservations for a little smaller of parties. We had a table of 8 ahead of us and they also weren't seating at the bar to prepare for a party they had booked later in the day.

text:
Unfortunately we decided to start our new year off with a common family outing to Edison's. Typically one of our "go to" places for a lot of fun, good food , and excellent service. This time Edison's went 0 for 3. I am extremely shocked by the events that took place. First, I was told it would be 1/2 hour to get a bowling lane. No big deal, New Years Day they should be busy. It was closer to an hour. That's fine. Secondly, we get in our lane to bowl and the lane is malfunctioning before we can even get started. The gentleman that was working said the lane had been giving him multiple problems for days. After multiple problems, they decide they will switch us lanes. No problem. We wait 10 minutes and all the sudden they tell us just bowl because the gave the other lane away. There where 5 open lanes they could of gave but they insisted we stay in the malfunctioning one. Fine. We order food.... I am told the only thing we are out of is spring rolls....  no problem again. We order our food and it comes out in a timely fashion. I get to looking at it and on a 4 appetizer tray, two things are substituted. I asked the waitress and she said " we where very busy last night and we had to sub some items out". Would of been nice of her to tell me when she brought the food out. Not for me to have to inquire about it. Then when I wanted to switch to something else and  I was inconveniencing her and to push the other items on a plate so she can take them back. (Like I was trying to get free food). Really???  The manger that I see every time I am there ,which is quite often , came out and was very nice and offered to buy my dinner. A nice gesture. I assured him that I wasn't looking for a free meal , I was just very disappointed in what had transpired this evening. The bowling alley never did work. The girl at the counter said "I am gonna need a receipt before I can help you at all". I had the shoes in my hands for all four of us and the lane number with our names on it. This was done in malice because I was unhappy that our lane was messed up and on top of all of it they knew it and still put us on this lane. I understand that everyone had a rough night every once in a while but to mess up on all three aspects of our New Year's Day is extremely disheartening. I hope this isn't a sign of things to come for this place. I know for a fact this place prides itself on their customer service separating them from other places and they really missed the mark this time. 
Ps. I always tell them when they do a good or great job so I am not just complaining to complain. I want them to improve so we can continue to enjoy this place. Thanks for taking the time to read this long but very accurate review/rant.
name: Ryan

text: We ordered beef crispy tacos, veggie burrito, fish burrito, and chicken torta to go.  It's possible that the food were soggy after 20 minutes, but the taste was just so so in addition to the soggy texture.

text: This place has very good food and a nice vibe with the live entertainment while you're dining. The lemon pepper scallops are a must have. I do not agree with the policy of not seating groups of four at a table meant for six when there wasn't anybody waiting. text: I'm visiting from New York City and was highly recommended this bar from a friend. I love beer bars that has a huge selection from micro to macro breweries.  This rating is purely for the service. The bartender asked for our IDs and ignored us for 5 minutes. Keep in mind, it's a slow day on a Monday so the bar was not crowded at all. After, when I finally got her attention, she asked for my order and I said a pint of Dale's.  Then, she pulled out a pint glass, put it under the tap without pouring anything, and walked away. I saw her walk to the other side of the bar, rest for a bit, ask another customer for their drink order, and continue to make their order. She clearly did not want to serve me and my friend. This was the rudest experience I had in NOLA. I love my beer bars but this is one I'll definitely have to considered coming back. This is so disappointing since I heard such great things about this bar.
name: Jodie

text:
Hey Sam's Place, welcome to Nipper's Corner.  We are very happy you are here!  A welcome addition to a busy corner in the neighborhood.  Corner Pub vibe but with a different menu and a bigger interior.  

The wings were really good.  Very meaty.  My friend had a half slab of ribs and loved them.  Fries were fantastic.  My burger was very nice.  Next time, I will skip some of the lettuce and mustard, but it was very good.  

Nice beer selection.  Lots of nice items on the menu that I cannot wait to try.  And a very fun vibe for a dreary rainy Sunday afternoon.  Lots of TV screens showing stuff, lots of people in a good mood.  Lots of laughter.  The place is well designed and comfortable.  

Really personable service with our waiter, Bryce.  We are so lucky in this little corner of Brentwood/Nashville to have so many wonderful choices now.  This Sam's Place will hold its own in this busy area.  I think the weekday happy hours and midweek specials will really be popular.  

I am a fan and look forward to returning.

text:
Came here multiple times! Their hummus is smooth and warm! Their pita is also served warm! Very comfort food esp on a cold winter night!

Word of advice though: Their menu is always changing, sometimes by the season I believe. So it can work for you or makes you sad when your favorite isn't there
