text:
LONG wait for a table at lunch but hey, let's see what all the fuss is about.

Our friend recommended stopping by for an afternoon feeding session, and while we waited we sipped some wine (Sauvignon blanc) out front and petted some pooches on the canine-friendly outdoor area.

We did finally get a lovely table inside and our server was extraordinarily good. We told him we are vegans and he knew exactly where to steer us-----well, there was really only one good option------two veggie clubs with no cheese and, *drumroll* no bread. That's right, the bread they serve has whey in it, a milk product. So our "sandwiches" came wrapped in iceberg lettuce. Amazingly they tasted pretty good, especially with the veggies we ordered on the side, of course with no butter.

Great looking wooden bar inside----a little lower than you normally see them which allowed people to sit even more comfortably; and there were plenty of them enjoying the food and drink and good looking clientele. 

This would have been 5 stars all the way except, PLEASE make it easier for vegans to eat something other than a fake sandwich wrapped in lettuce. On the plus side, thank you for your crew of educated servers who knew the ingredients and helped us get our order going as well as possible.
name: Grape

text: The fried chicken is LEGIT. The staff is very busy, but also very warm, genuine, and kind. A great experience! A+

text:
Food exceptional! 
Service even better than exceptional!
Liza was extremely kind and attentive you have a gem of a restaurant. Keep up the good work

text:
Was brought here by a co-worker.
We were sat right away on a Wednesday night, but it filled up quick.
The service was really poor.
Slow to take orders, and after we ate, we waited 20 minutes for our check.  That was annoying.  But aside from that...the food.

The horchata was good!
You don't get chips and salsa when you sit down, you have to pay for it.  Not cool.

We ordered and chips and salsa, because...obviously.

The salsa was really just pico de gallo and was okay.
I ordered lengua tacos, so bonus points for having lengua!
They were actually quite good, cubed not shredded.  I prefer cubbed anyway.

You had to order beans and rice as an extra side...what the heck?
Just include them in the taco plate.
Then, the ice was like rice pilaf, not spanish rice.  Also weird.

So yea...I eat a lot of Mexican food and have never expericned Mexican quite like this, not in Mexico, L.A, or anywhere else in California.

But maybe this is Mexican in Canda...who knows.
I wouldn't go back, but the lengua was good. Just awful service.
name: Luke

text:

My friends food was also pretty underwhelming. The menu really needs some works, but the drinks were good.

Probably one of the best crust's I have had on a pizza. Good price too for a XXL 18 inch pizza. Only negative is the pizza hardly had any sauce, but I will definitely order there again

text: This is a nice hidden away neighborhood place. Service is always quick and friendly and very accommodating. The food is generally great and imaginative. As you might expect the imagination sometimes misses the mark a little. It's never a big miss but it can put you off a little. I always try the new items just to explore new tastes and have only been disappointed once. I mentioned it to the server and he fell all over himself trying to make it right. We finally convinced him that the meal was fine and we only mentioned the seasoning in case the chef wanted to tweak the recipe. In any case he still tried to comp the dish in spite of the fact that I had  cleaned the whole plate. Give this little place a try.

text:
I only have three words for you.  Get.  The.  Milkshake.

But when you have 6 adults and instead of any sort of alcohol, they opt for what is usually only on a kids' menu, you know it's something to investigate. And okay, maybe I was a bit spoiled because you can get the milkshake or the cream soda (also something to try!) and I got one of each - no judgment - but definitely this is one of the specialties. 

I had the farm burger, which by itself is large, and you can add toppings for $0.50-$2, but really, you don't need to.  They seem to be already topped with the right combination of stuff so that they enhance the burger, not overpower it.  The fries are...fries.  As one of my absolute favorite sides, I was "eh" on them, but oh man, you dip them in that milkshake - no judgement - and it's pretty darn worth it. 

They do have tater tots, but those are harder to dip, so I skipped them for this go around, but maybe next time!

text:
While my family and I visited Philadelphia, we wanted to enrich ourselves with the taste of as a local would. After much research of which were the best Philly Cheesesteak locations, we decided to stay away from the tourist traps of Genos and Pats. Although these two locations were recommend for the rivalry experience, we choose taste over an atmosphere experience. So we went to Dalessandro's, Jim's Steaks, Woodrow's Sandwiches, and Tony Lukes. 

We started by going to Dalessandro's Steaks on our arrival on a Saturday night around 8. The place was packed and the line was out the door. This looked good.

You walk into the building finding that most people have already ordered and the line is just people waiting for their order. You shimmy your way through the people to get up to someone who takes your order and name. You pay when you pick up, CASH ONLY, the cost was about $9 a sandwich. Then you wait for your name to be called.

Not having anywhere to eat, we returned to our car which was parked across the street and down a little bit in a gravel parking lot for the park.

Expecting this food to be the best I've ever eaten, I was ready. My mouth watering and waiting to accept nothing but goodness......and then.......disappointment. Wow, was not expecting that.

The bread was soft and good. We order provolone, with onions. We could not really taste the cheese at all, which was a disappointment. The meat however was packed into the sandwich, but was very greasy and soaked the bottom of the bread in greasy drippings. I ended up pulling the onions off because they did not add the right flavor or texture for some reason. I'm not sure if it was just a bad onion or someone else. I do wish we got one provolone and one whiz. My little one got a cheese burger which he really enjoyed which is a positive for what a picky eater he is. It was gone even before I could try a bite to review. I left feeling that if this was the best Philly had to offer, maybe I did not like Cheesesteaks. My wife, a Cheesesteak connoisseur, commented that she preferred Jersey Mike's cheesesteak over Dalessandro's. Since I planned this Cheesesteak trip for her, I felt defeated. 

Our next stop was Jim's Steaks. When we walked in at lunch time on a Monday and it 5 people were inside, I became worried again that I may have made a mistake. We ordered one with provolone with peppers and one with whiz and onions. We also ordered an Italian Hoagie for my little one.

We found there was additional seating upstairs, which only had 1 table left. I felt a little better at this point about my selection, then I took a bite.....Wow, what a difference, redemption. The bread was amazing for both the cheesesteak and the hoagie. The steak was cooked to perfection, no fat, and no grease. The bread stayed nice and dry besides the generous helping of cheese. They apply cheese on the bottom and onto of the sandwich making sure it was fully of cheesey goodness. The peppers were good, having a sweet taste. 

The whiz and onions, definitely the way to go. Wow, I could not get enough of it. Knowing we still had another stop and another Cheesesteak to go, I found it really hard to not go back for a full sandwich (my family of 4 split the 3 sandwiches). The Italian hoagie, was just as flavorful for someone who does not like Cheesesteak, like my little one. However, I must note, that even my picky little one liked the Cheesesteak whiz with. The sandwiches here cost $8, $9 with cheese, CASH ONLY.

Woodrow's Sandwiches was a little bit different. Here they make their own whiz, which is made with truffle oil. The cost is $12, so it is a bit more expensive. The sandwich itself was packed full of flavor. The truffle oil whiz definitely brought another flavor element to the table, which elevated the sandwich. The steak however was greasy and left the bread soaked at the bottom of grease. The staff was very friendly and helpful, even recommending other locations to try Cheesesteaks on our tour.

Tony Luke's - The bread was decent, but not as good as the other three locations. We ordered a cheesesteak with whiz and onions. The steak was not as tender as the other 3 locations and was in much larger pieces instead of your typical diced cut. The meat was also very greasy, dripping all over while eating it. The onions were barley cooked, leaving a heavy onion taste and the whiz was nothing too special. The cost was $10. 

If you are trying to decide where to go, I would go to Jim's Steaks followed by Woodrow's. I would stay way from Dalessandro's and try a different location all together after Jim's and Woodrow's. Tony's was ok, better than Dalessandro's, but still worlds apart from Jim's and Woodrow's. 

In my opinion, if your looking for the best local Cheesesteak, I would go with Jims. If your looking for the best Cheesesteak that has a unique flavor, I would go with Woodrow's. If you want to try two good but differnt styles of Cheesesteak, stick with Jim's and Woodrows.
name: Brett

If you can't honor your word, you will never get my business again.  Deplorable business model.
name: Danielle

text: MyGirlfriend and I love to visit this place every single time we go to New Orleans the Hot Dogs are great! So many different combinations and toppings, they also have vegan options. It's a twist on a traditional hot dog! They have an excellent bar and a great variety of beers on tap. Timing is everything when it comes to enjoying your meal here. If you come during a rush period don't expect excellent or expedient service, but your food will be on point! Make sure to place your order at the bar when your ready to dig in!
name: Kerry

text: I LOVE this place the food is amazing and I have never had a complaint before. Tonight was the WORST service I have received in a long time. I think our waitress forgot we were even there or the fact that she was working. Katie didn't even bring us our drinks until two appetizers were almost ready, that's how long it took us to get our drinks. Two hours later and several mistakes made on a 4 person table with a very simple meal. I think Katie might need to be retrained or shadowed by management.
name: Sara

text: I can't say too much about the service etc. I was only there once but this is a grab and go place so I wouldn't expect a whole lot! I had the burger and it was well made and fresh, didn't taste like a frozen patty thawed (which honestly is the case for most burgers at places like this and why I usually never order them). The rest of their menu looked good as well. If you are looking for a grab and go place with food that does the job and is freshly made, Petra will get the job done!
name: Noosh

text: I'm lucky enough to work across the street from 9 Roses, so whenever I forget to bring my lunch, or want inexpensive takeout for dinner, I can always pop in here. I'm one of those people who always orders the same things - pho chicken, chicken spring rolls, and chicken vermicelli. It's always so fresh and delicious, with lots of vegetables as others have noted. The curry chicken is also great. Depending on how busy it is, as one reviewer recently noted, wait times for takeout can be long, but typically for me it's only 15 minutes or so. A very welcome addition to the French Quarter lunch options!
name: Courtney

text: I just visited this establishment for my sisters birthday and the service was excellent! Everyone was very friendly and accommodating. The place was jam packed and on a wait yet they treated us like we were the only people in here. Our server Eni was excellent and the manager Alvi came to check on us a few times and was very personal! The food was absolutely amazing and I was stuffed in 15 minutes and the chocolate lava cake was amazing! Money well spent!!
name: Erica

text: The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: This place is around the corner of our beach house on Sunset Beach. They had live music (one guy) the night we were there and I started off thinking it was going to be lame but was actually pretty good. Their menu was varied and having just returned from New Orleans it had a NOLA vibe to the food items. I had the Shrimp n Grits that was really good and my husband had one of their hamburgers.  They had a little mix up on the service that night but recognized the issue and apologized comping some Beignets in the process. We will definitely return.
name: Lisa

text: This is by far the best BBQ in Nawlins. The food and drinks were amazing. This place is awesome. Expect long lines but worth the wait. If you are able to get a seat at the bar, please go for it. You will be able to skip the line. If you are a whisky connoisseur you will enjoy the many whisky they have. I had a Japanese whisky which was great. Next time I'm in New Orleans i will be coming here.
name: Tiffani

text: Gross as hell. Tasted like ass and lard. Please don't eat here. It's a tourist trash.
name: Brittany

text: I went here a week ago for my friend's birthday and I was floored. The atmosphere. The booze. The quality of the food. The music. Everything was amazing. To say the least. I'll be going back around the end of May with a special friend of mine, so we can hang out there and have a great time. With booze.
name: Kaitlyn

text:
Aah peace in my soul.  A little bit generic atmosphere, a little bit irreverent music, and delicious etouffee!  Delicious.

So I walk up to the counter and proudly announce that I came all the way from Ithaca (NY) to dine here.  I received precisely the correct response: "Meh..."  These folk speak my language.

If you get chance, hit up any of the Yats in Indy-you just might dig it.  I sure did!
name: Don

text: I love coming to Wingstop. Never disappointed in the food or the service. One tip... if you don't want to wait order & pay  online. The food is  always made fresh to order.
name: Alison

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It was crowded but still moved along. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. There were a couple things I liked and a couple things I probably wouldn't get again. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait.
name: User

text: I go to the Oaks location almost weekly and in the past several months I've seen a decline in the quality of food, specifically in my once favorite wings. The wings use to be crispy and always had the perfect amount of sauce so you got the best of both worlds with sauce and the taste of chicken. Now when you order wings expect a once crispy breading on your wings to be a wet mess and a puddle of extra sauce on the bottom of your basket so overwhelming it's hard to taste the chicken. I hope you guys listen to this and go back to the back you use to do your wings, without skipping corners.
name: Nick

text: Went before the P!nk concert tonight for the first time and it was awesome.  One of us is Vegan and the other two aren't.  The food, atmosphere and and service and drinks were great!  Plenty of flavorful choices for all.  Will definitely return.
name: Jessica

text: I love this place for their broast chicken. Reminds me of KFC back in Singapore. Since KFC in St Louis is not halal, St Louis Gyro Broast is the next best thing.
name: Muhd

text: What a deceptive place...food looks pretty promising on photos. But somehow they mis-execute the delivery of standard late night food badly. Meat is dry. Noodles bland.
name: Ryo

text:
I rarely give 1 star to any restaurant but... if you stoop this low, i have to let people know (please read below... i will start with all the bad and then the one good)

This place was open not too long ago and i had a decent amount of expectation since i love soup dumplings and Chinese food. I did not have the same expectation as the ones not the city but still, some expectations. The first time i went, it was ok. The soups dumpling was kinda whatever but the other dishes like beef chow fun made me think it was just a bad day. I tried a lot of everything as well like beef pancake, mapo tofu, and shumai. Again, everything but the beef chow fun was bland and meh.

The second time i went, the soup dumplings were lukewarm and very very fatty... the food again mediocre except for beef chow fun. 

The third time... this is when it got it's 1 star rep from me. My party was seated and we already ordered. They then came and asked us to move for a bigger party... the bigger party didn't even show up even after we were on the way out... that irked me...

Ok, so the service was whatever. The food got even worse compared to my pervious 2 visits. The beef pancakes which was ok turn bad; the dough was soggy and floppy. The soup dumplings continued to be lukewarm and made from leftover junk, and Kung pow chicken was more like Kung pow breading (literally... no chicken in any bites that i took)

Here is the biggest kicker. If you divert your attention to the pictures i posted, the glassware: gross. My tea cup had hardened sesame seeds stuck on the inside and the glasses were improperly washed. 

If the food is subpar; that's ok... I'm sure you can take criticism and make it better with practice. If the cleanliness is something that needs to be address; it just shows that you don't care. 

I mentioned i would put 1 good thing. Bok Choy. At least they got the one thing right

TL;DR: THIS PLACE IS NOT CLEAN. I probably avoid this place until maybe way later than ill try for the sake of my love for dim sum and also in the respect for it being in my hometown. 

SMH....
name: Jae

text: The only good thing about this restaurant was the taste if the gumbo.  It came out lukewarm and without the bread.  I did not have any chicken in the chicken and sausage gumbo.  I did tell the waiter about it and i did not have me pay for it.  Problem resolved and the waiter was very nice.  I came with a party of 8 and all but 2 said the food was not warm enough.
name: Emma

text:
It's been nearly 7 months since my very bad experience at the Belleville Pizza World, but I thought I would provide an update.  I saw the message from Lisa below my review.  I called yesterday to speak with her, but was informed that she no longer worked there.  I spoke with Bruce, one of the new managers, and he informed me that all of the former staff no longer worked there and that the business was under new ownership and new management.  I said I was willing to give them a second chance after everything I heard.

Tonight, I placed an order for our family favorite - the Appondonza.  Flat out - this is the best pizza in town!!!  My family and I loved every bit of it and I was very pleased with the professionalism and courtesy of Bruce and his team.  I even met the new owner who thanked me for my loyal patronage.  I told them it was great to be back and I was happy to put the "blip on the radar" from the past behind us.

Thank you to all for making things right and continuing to make great pizza!

Jeff
name: Jeff

text: I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Pretty happy with it overall. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: We ordered sultani kabob platter it was an okay platter . Portion Size was good and we loved there beef kabob but not so much chicken . We will come back to try other dishes. There beef sambosa was the best .
name: Jamshed

text: Just finished my meal and it was absolutely fantastic. The menu had a massive variety of rolls that all tasted great, and it was super quick. You could keep reading or you could just go and check it out. I have to say this is probably the best sushi I've had in town.
name: Gabriel

text:
Love the farm to table aspect of this place, the waiter was kind and informative, and the ambiance of the restaurant was comfortable and classic.  

Drink: Crimson & Clover. This was refreshing and very well done! Dinner: Bronze Scallops.  Presentation was nice, but overall the dish was very salty. Appetizer: Shishito Peppers. A good dish, you got a spicy pepper every few bites.
name: Kathleen

text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. It just never really recovered once things started off weird. Maybe other people have better luck here. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. It looked better online than it did in person. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh.
name: User

text: Service is great! These guys are at our office on Wednesdays! Love it. They are really helpful. And the Gringo is my favorite burger. I Won't shy away from the burger just yet.
name: Chantelle

text: I wanted to try THT as I read that they were closing at the end of this month. I've walked past this place many times with my dog as it's right off the Monon Trail and 54th street. It's a beautiful and quaint little house but since I had the dog, I didn't go in. They have a convenient side window to order from. The girl that helped me was very nice and read me all the flavors since I couldn't see them. I ended up with a double scoop cup of cheesecake and black cherry. Although it was delicious, I didn't necessarily think it was the most smooth or most creamy ice cream. There are quite a few craft ice cream vendors in Indianapolis that could easily compete with THT. I will say that it was around $6 for this cup so a bit pricier than I had hoped.
name: Megan

text: I'm here to support the review I wrote on my husband's Yelp account. 'Cause I'm petty like that mhmm. I really wish this will get the manager/owner's attention. I understand it's a restaurant, I understand it's late, I understand everyone wants to go home because it's 19 mins to closing time. But I can't understand how it's okay to be nasty. I was just calling to ask if I could place an order, if not it's ok too. Just don't yell at a customer and then proceed to hang up. If you could do something about your rude waitress and improve on the service, I'd love to give you guys a try. If the one at the phone is disrespectful, I wouldn't expect the ones at the table to be any better.
name: Michelle

text:
If you're a soup lover, do yourself a favor and check out some of their offerings.  I'm taken with their tomato basil, especially when I pair it with their kids' grilled cheese.  The grilled cheese is one of their options for the little ones, but I've never had a problem ordering it.  And then there's the mushroom soup.  Mmmmmmm. It's earthy and rich, and it should be eaten with the complimentary bread. Oh, and slather the complimentary bread with the complimentary butter first. You're welcome. 

There are so many other items that I love here - ALL of the salads, especially the pecan cranberry wild field salad.  It's got sweet and salty flavors, and it's delicious. The chicken salad is a winner too - so perfect on one of their flaky, buttery croissants.

Their breads and pastries are fresh and I've never had something from their bakery that I wasn't completely satisfied with. 

My only complaints are that the restaurant is tiny and somewhat cramped, and the parking lot is usually full.  There's street parking, thank goodness, so I just park and hoof it. It's a gorgeous area and on a pretty day I enjoy the walk.
name: Patricia

text: Yikes. I am actually at this restaurant right now. Had a reservation at 7pm. Didn't get bread until hmm about 7:45. Waiting on my second drink I asked for about 30min a go... which I had to practically wave down our server to ask. A table sat after us has already eaten and left about 10 min ago. We got our salads a hour after we sat down. Upon arrival the hostess merely pointed at our table and said to go sit there leaving us without menus. Cool cool cool. Maybe the food is good. Still don't know. Maybe we just had a terrible server. But this is absolutely unacceptable. Super glad we chose this place for my brothers 18th birthday. The time is 8:35 pm. Update: meal was brought around 8:45. It was just ok.
name: Alissa

text:
This restaurant is located in a weird area, near other bars and restaurants. It definitely isn't easy to find parking, so we uber & just walked around. 

The décor is very whimsical and unique, cool vibes

The staffs were fast & friendly. They kept us entertained and provided excellent service.

Our group decided to join their happy. Enough variety of drinks selections:
Sangria, House Margs, Drafts. from light to dark craft brews, one Flying Fish (Somerdale, NJ) and one Full Pint (North Versailles, PA). Love the Margarita

Drinks are super strong which equals amazing. 

We got the chorizo sliders - Great, nice flavor
The chicken quesadilla, and chicken empanadas - Mediocre 
The usual squids ceviche - Love it but small portion

Would like to come back & try salsa lessons
name: KN

text:
Food was just ok, a little too much salt in the tamales and they charge extra for pico de Gallo in a small container.
Not worth the price of the food in my opinion. $38.+ dinner for 2 and nothing but water to drink
name: Danny

text: Got the spicy basil with beef rice cames with a tom yum soup. You can adjust the spiciness of the dish. Great food and awesome service!
name: Sarah

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. The staff seemed tired but still polite. I left full, which at least counts for something. Food was fresh and service was quick. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text:
Highly impressed with this restaurant experience, because that's what it is - you're not dining, you're having an experience. We were lucky to grab Sunday brunch reservations for 11:30 AM.  Any later, and even with a dedicated parking lot in the back, I can imagine time wasted looking for space in this compact Fishtown location.

Staff here are ON POINT. Everyone from the hostess to our server to the folks delivering our plates knew what they were doing and did it well. We ended up with a table for four in the back - happy because we were warm, we could hear each other talk, and it was a great spot for people-watching. Next time, for something different, though, I'd request in advance for counter seating so I can watch all the kitchen action!

We arrived early, so enjoyed a few minutes in their little marketplace. They scored a $35 set of copper measuring cups out of us - LOL.  As soon as we were seated, we began to order. Dishes arrived on time and in an orderly fashion - from the hummus with their pillowy soft pitas (allot about one pita per couple) and a chocolate & almond financier pastry to start off the morning with our coffees and rosehip tinted chai teas. 

"Man'oushe" (pronounced like "minutiae") are like tiny little flatbread pizzas. We ordered both the beef and gravlax version. Sublime, especially with their house brand hot sauce. The beet salad with grapefruit and falafels were a hit, as was the mezze plate sampler.

Beautifully done every step of the way. The kudos are well deserved from any angle.
name: Allie

text:
Sadly not what they used to be.   Apparently a new chef and based on how the manager acted , probably a new owner as well.  
The dishes are dramatically different from the past and not for the better
name: D

text: Service was friendly had the Detroit all meat. Sausage had a nice spice to it and was good.
name: Melody

text: Our favorite place. Staff and food sure do beat the chains. Large drink and food menu, much better than the applebees and Ruby Tuesday. Love their salads
name: Donald

text: I ordered the pulled pork plate, brisket sandwich and a half rack of ribs for my girlfriend and I... wow!!!!! This bbq is amazing.... the meat is tender and not over smoked , you can actually taste the flavor of the meat.... the ribs are outstanding !!!! I have not had bbq if this quality in Arizona before ... the sides are really good too... the Carolina bbq sauce is homemade and pairs lovely with the pulled pork .... I highly recommend this place , the bbq is fantastic ... thanks red desert for bringing great bbq to the desert !!!!!!
name: Eric

text: Bar "comfy" -- everything about this spot vibes cozy and welcoming, including their wine on tap and housemade beer! I've been several times and always have a great experience. The food menu is interesting and well done. They even have hard seltzer on tap!
name: Selena

text: Ike's is probably my favorite place in IV. They have a lot of vegetarian and vegan options which is great and the bread is so good. They also give caramel covered apple lollipops too which is super cute.
name: Christina

text: First time in here and tried the pizza and cannolis. Pizza was amazing and the service was quick. Everything felt as if they truly cared about the quality of the food and the service. Will definitely be back! Thank you!
name: Johanna

text: The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text:
I've been for brunch and dinner! We have yet to be disappointed.  Their brunch is our go to in Brentwood--crabcake benedict or chicken and waffles!! The 2 for 1 mimosas aren't a bad touch either :)
Dinner wise the fried catfish, shrimp poboy, or jambalaya have been favorites of ours. Service has also always been awesome!
name: Meagan

text:
This pizza is different and depending on your taste is very good. Yes it does have a mustard taste to it which some people may not like however I thought it was very good. No sauce on most of there slices or if there is I didn't taste it but the Kale pizza was very, very different and to grab one slice is okay. I would not eat more then one kale slice but again that is a good thing not to binge on unhealthy pizza.

The mushroom was quite good with I want to say bermuda onions on it and again alot of flavor. Your either gonna love there pizza or hate it botttom line. Will update review once I try more of there selection but I believe there thing is all vegan slices just an FYI if your looking for more of a meat fulled slice.
name: Mike

text:
So I'm super sad to not be able to leave a great review here. I had been so excited to come try Liberty Common as all the Instagram pics I saw were amazing & it just looked like the best new brunch spot in Nashville.  So finally today my hubs & I got to try it & to be honest it was a let down.
Don't get me wrong- the aesthetics were exactly what I had hoped for and expected... the place without a doubt is darling. Details are perfect. The music, vibe, decor- all an A+.  But the service was very average. Host seemed like she didn't want to be there. And the guy taking our order took forever to actually take our order (even though it wasn't busy at all and they seemed to have a lot of staff). And the coffee... oh my gosh so terrible and it wasn't even hot!  Not a good start to brunch.  Hubs had the chicken & waffles (which from their Instagram seemed to be a popular choice) and they were just meh. Nothing special at all. And they only had Tabasco as far as hot sauce goes, so definitely lacking there.  The burger was decent though.  Not the best burger, but probably was the best thing out of all that we had. Super bummed to say we won't be back. Wanted this to be a new brunch fave so am so disappointed it was sub par on too many levels.
name: Karla

text:
Went down to Neptune Grill over the weekend for the Gulfport Grand Prix and it had good seating outside (has inside seating as well) right across the street from the water so great view! 
Great menu selection and specials on different days. 
I had the Seafood Mediterranean that included shrimp, scallops, and grouper! Great portion size and lots of meat, just lacked flavor and could have seasoned more.
name: Nicholas

text: For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. It was crowded but still moved along. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Definitely coming back. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. It looked better online than it did in person. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Service was nice, kitchen was just moving kind of slow. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The music was louder than it needed to be. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Would probably stop in again if nearby. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text: Amazing ! Fast and tasty ! Great service. Would come again and again with all the choices !
name: Deborah

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. The music was louder than it needed to be. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: Amazing food and great live music! Very pleased. It was our first time here, but we would definitely come back the next time we are in town. The staff was very friendly and gave us great recommendations on the food. Nice atmosphere. The best catfish! So light and fluffy. The Mac and Cheese with house hot chicken was amazing too!!! Huge portions. A really great place to visit.
name: Heather

text: Are server was the worst. 1 hour and half later and we are still waiting on our sushi to show up. This is the worst dinner experience I have ever had in my life. I actually thought about leaving a $20 on the table and going to jack n the box. Seriously if I could give negative stars I would.
name: Michael

text: Pretty good fresh food here. I like that it's a little different than all of the other places around this area. Perfect for lunch!
name: Elise

text:
Great Full Gardens has been a reno staple for years. The new location at the Legends continues to impress. 

The same great food, service, and atmosphere as the other locations. 

If you are looking for a tasty meal that is healthy and delicious then come on down! 

Meals are easy to order for take out. There is even a specific pickup counter to make carry out even easier. 

The portion sizes are perfect! I feel that most places either serve too much or too little. Great Full Gardens serves the perfect amount. You feel satiated but not stuffed. 
 
I highly recommend trying the chili oil with your meals, but beware, it is spicy. A little goes a long way.
name: Rebecca

text: Went back a second time after a mid week afternoon. This time on a Saturday afternoon. Still a disappointment. Very high prices for drinks, food is just so so and not reasonable. No wonder the place was not busy at all on a beautiful day. Had high hopes for this place because it is nearby and on the water. Won't go back any time soon.
name: Jim

text: Ordered takeout because I didn't feel like cooking and it held up okay. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold.
name: User

text:
I really like this spot a lot. Came here twice on dates. Once on a Friday night in the winter and another time on a Tuesday night in the summer so we opted for outdoor seating. I remember it being crowded and pretty loud on the Friday night, weeknights are more chill. Service is good but both times they took forever to bring the bill at the end.

Most importantly though, the menu here is incredible. So many choices, not enough room in my stomach. The margaritas are on point too. Spicy mango for the win. My friend got a pickled watermelon margarita.. not sure what that is but creative. I got some calamari/chorizo tacos this past time and it was out of this world. Don't come here for traditional Mexican dishes.. come here to get something with a twist. Will definitely be coming back more and trying more menu items.
name: Nate

text: World of Beer? Must be flat Earthers because the selection is fairly limited. Medieval Fiefdom of Beer, more fitting. First and last visit.
name: Alijandro

text: This place is fun! Overall I like it, especially the vibe. The patio is an awesome space with games, seats around a heater for the colder days, lots of seating areas so you won't be searching for an area for your group. The inside is smaller, and there's probably 10 seats at the trolley bar. Drinks on draft and cans were about $5-6 each, service to the tables was pretty slow so we opted to just get up and get drinks from the bar (which we honestly preferred but the waitress seemed like she wanted to take our order..). The bar was pretty empty on a Wednesday - one or 2 other groups at the whole place besides mine. My biggest gripe is that their website says they're open til 3 and they did last call at 10, which sucked. We picked there because they claimed late night, but that wasn't true. So overall a good spot, slow service, few staff, decent prices
name: Elizabeth

text: Best gumbo in New Orleans! Service was on spot. Try the catfish bites-omg they are sooo good! Drinks were great too. Will definitely return:)
name: Jenny

text: I'm very picky when it comes to Mexican food but my oh my this place is very authentic. My husband & i brought my mother-in-law to try this place. The horchata has a coconut taste which i love coconut. I ordered 3 of them! We ordered the empanadas, the chips and salsa, and the rajas con queso as an appetizer. For our entrees we ordered the enchiladas, the chilaquiles and huevos rancheros. Everything was fresh! Very highly recommended!
name: Anna

text:
Totally worth it. 8 bucks for a fast, flavorful plate? Yes, please! Not too casual: hits the spot, and if you're in the mood for sauce and more flavor, than there's a spot just for that. The owner was explaining the menu options and what style of food it was. That was some genuinely delicious Cajun food. It's always different each day, and all of the food is amazing.  You leave the place stuffed to the gills and content knowing that you got a lot of bang for your buck. Totally recommend the chili cheese etouffee, drunken chicken, sausage and beans, and the gumbo! If you go here, you won't regret it, that's for sure! 

Service: 5 stars
Food: 5 stars 
Cost: 5 stars
Speed: 5 stars
Hospitality: 5 stars


(AKA:You have to go here;)
name: Aiden

text: I've been wanting to try Smyrna Cafe and decided to try it tonight. I got there and it closes at 3 on Monday's but as I was walking back to my car the owner opened the door and welcomed me and my daughter in. He turned the grill and fryer back on and quickly got us our food. I've never had a restaurant open back up for a customer. But OMG the food was sooo good, we'll definitely be back.
name: Misty

text: A bit disappointed unfortunately.  Let's start with what was good: filet mignons grilled over an open fire in front of us was actually really good and makes up for all the negatives, very large dessert bar, drink included in price, good service from our waitress.  What was disappointing: buffet small overall, food mostly just average with exception of the petit mignon, mashed potatoes were made from packaged powder, and very small and lackluster salad bar.  Also, I was disappointed we were seated in a back corner room with no decor.  It looked like a cafeteria that employees would break in and just didn't have a good atmosphere to it.  There was a lot of open tables and booths in other areas but we got seated here instead so not sure why.  Probably won't be coming back.
name: Lisa

text: Probably one of the worst restaurants downtown. Went to the bar to get some bites before the titans game. Ordered oysters came out small and seemed warm. Enough cocktail sauce and horseradish for about three of them had to ask for more. Steak biscuits we ordered came out raw. Wife ordered crab cakes and salad. Salad was wilted and all stems. Honestly it all seemed like freezer food. Bathroom had paper towels all over floor cause urinal was stopped up. It would have been acceptable for a downtown restaurant if I didn't have $100 bill at the end. The only positive was the young waitress that took care of us. Ended up having to hit Jimmy John's on the way home. Needless to say I do not recommend this place to anybody
name: Bret

text: Quick, cheap, and authentic! The three things that you want when it comes to good tacos. They have really quick service, so you can stop by and grab a bite and eat them right away. They have a small building aside from the bridling for larger groups and patio seating too. You can get tacos for $1.25 and if you're vegetarian you can customize by telling them what you want.
name: Ting

text: Great breakfast place!   Go early or else plan on waiting a few before a table is ready.  Tucson has figured out that this place is 'da Bomb' on the weekend!  Tried many items on the menu and NONE have ever been disappointing.  All have been Excellent!  Try their trainwreck (spicy) with an egg over easy... it's out of this world!  It appears we now know where Bobby Flay moonlights during the breakfast hours... in the Baja Cafe Kitchen!
name: Mike

text:
The lights, the lights, the lights!!! Visiting here is a MUST for me around the holidays! They have a fountain/ light/music show that will have you memorized! After the fountain show, there is still so much to see. The palm trees, the perfectly positioned poinsettia's, the huge tree ornaments, the waterfalls, the smiles and love seen on families faces, the gift shops, the smell of hot cinnabon's and warmed candied almonds, the perfect position of the lights hanging from the ceilings, the nativity scene, and SO much more! Then outside of the hotel there's sled riding, s'mores stations, and a magical reindeer/christmas/ice display! 

For all of my fellow Christmas lovers, bring your scrooge's here, and you'll be sure to win them over! Tis' The Season To Be Jolly!

Parking: Ugh! The worst part! Lol - If you choose to visit, make sure you bring your patience and your walking shoes with you, because parking around the holidays is a bear! We were able to find parking at the mall, and then strolled on over to the hotel.
name: Asia

text: One of our favorites. We came here twice on our trip. Really good and casual place for a bite to eat on a budget. The happy hour is a really good deal: $1.75 for domestic drafts and $2 off for any other draft.  The food is very tasty and a good portion size for a very  reasonable price. There's a lot of options on the menu so you can find something for everyone. I recommend any of the bowls. They  played really good music so it had a good vibe. They also gave us free key chain/bottle openers which was cool.
name: Jessica

text:
U called this is "Medium rare"?

Worst service ever......

The waitress are so rude, they don't deserve any tips or any customer to come in for $24-40+ dinner meal.

Anyone know RB training for any required????
name: Kelvin

text: I've been to Swezey's nearly a dozen times now for lunch. The service has been great, and the food is always delicious. I don't live in Pleasant View but I visit often. Swezey's is always an option when I go out for a meal in Pleasant View.
name: James

text: Such amazing food! Came here for dinner and the food was incredibly delicious. Really fast service and good prices too. I'll have to come back for the lunch buffet!
name: Tasha

text: Found this place before the Texas vs Georgia football game.  It was packed. Unbelievable bar selection. Clean bathrooms
name: Bob

text:
We went for brunch. The waiter (Graham) was excellent. they have $15 bottomless mimosas and I didn't see the bottom of one mimosa before another one was on my table. Also, the mimosa pours were very impressive (like 80-90% bubbly and just a little juice). 

I had the chicken and waffles. I really enjoyed them. Pretty basic dish, nothing overly fancy. I would order again. 

My husband has the crab cake Benedict and he really liked that. His only complaint was that here was a little too much spinach. 

The breakfast potatoes were tasty, but it was a small portion imo and they weren't hot because...

I dinged them a star because our food sat in the window way to long. I saw the food sitting. Our waiter was busy and when he saw the food he was obviously upset that no one notified him or ran the food. I only know because I was specifically watching him as he went to get the food since I knew it had been sitting a while. However, before he turned to our table he had a big smile on and he walked it over to us (I appreciated his ability to shed his annoyance/anger before approaching our table). Although the food was a little on the cold side, it was still really tasty, so we didn't complain. 

We brought our 1 year old son with us. There were at least 4 other babies there during our time there. All of staff seemed really friendly despite the fact that there were so many kids throughout the relatively small restaurant Haha
name: Sarah

text:
The prices are excellent and fair. The steamed seafood was nice and tender. None of that fishy smell with steamed food that turns into dried gum. 
Price was great, food was excellent, needs to improve on quality in cleanliness and service.
Definitely needs to improve on never allowing servers to return dirty plates to the table; never bring back the same plate to the table that was just used by the customer. If a plate that had leftover shells was emptied it should never be brought back to be reused unless washed and cleaned. You simply should not ever throw shells away and bring the same dirty plate to the table to be reused. If you do that at home that's your choice but not at a restaurant and never with customers who pay you to get cleanliness, quality food and service in return. Always bring back a clean dish even if it's to throw away shells. Giving a customer anything dirty to be reused could be turned into a sanitary and health issue that could affect your license.
name: Heri

text: My absolute favorite ice cream shop in reno. They have such unique flavors and take suggestions from patrons. My favorite right now is the smoke chocolate. Delicious! After a romp in the park with my LOs, we like to stop here before heading home for nap time.  I love their rotating flavors, and sometimes you can find a past flavor in the pre-packed pints. I always grab a pint to go if they have something I like. Peddlers deli is housed in the same unit, they open during week and is delicious for a lunch and dessert!
name: Dianna

text: Food took forever but ended up being better than I expected. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. It was crowded but still moved along. We shared dumplings first and those were prob the best thing on the table. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The staff seemed tired but still polite. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Not sure though.
name: User

text: My friend liked it more than I did. The music was louder than it needed to be. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: You never know until you try a new restaurant. Salsa was was watery tomato sauce. Tv is on the NFL Network. Two tacos with two bites of meat $9.50. Interior is a hodgepodge of styles.  NEXT !
name: Eddie

text: OK, went to the Daiquiri shak Saturday night and I had a great time, The band (Stormbringer) was awesome, the drinks were awesome and so many flavors to choose from, the food was very good. I had the quesadillas and the were delicious and a large portion for only $8.95, my wife had the mussels and said there were also very good. We had no trouble finding parking, there are a few pool tables and televisions with sports tuned in. Our waitress was new and only 20 years old. I saw some past reviews the were harsh on the waitstaff. we had no trouble once we established a relationship with our waitress. maybe you folks were just bad customers...lol. My only knock was he lack of seating for such a popular band. I wish there was a 4.5 star rating.

text: Always busy! But the wait is never that long. We have been loyal Lincoln Square patrons for years. Tried this place out on a whim and now we rotate between places. Great food, prices, and service!

text:
Speisekarte ist übersichtlich. Es gibt 5-6 Appetizer, und ungefähr gleich viele Hauptgänge und auch ähnlich viele Beilagen.

Personal ist fix und sehr freundlich.

Essen war sehr gut, meine Fries die als Beilage kamen waren aber zu stark gesalzen.

text: What a disappointment this place was. After placing my order, the wrong food was bought out, the bartender kindly took the wrong item off of our bill, at that the owner came out and laid into him.  Also, one of my items was not served at all, I asked them to remove it from our bill because we were leaving, the bartender goes in the back and brings out the food.  At that, I asked to talk to Eddie the owner.  He came out and acted like a real ass.  He told me I already gave you free food.  I didn't want his free food, I wanted the food I ordered and it to be served in a timely manner, not when I was leaving.   The man sitting next to us, said I really can't believe he just treated you like that.  On top of all of this the food was subpar!  Don't waste your money or take the chance of being treated like I was. Stay away from this place!!

text: My husband and I visited The Habit for an eat supper. We were given a friendly greeting when we walked in. The cashier/order taker efficient and friendly she answered my questions about how the burgers are dressed.  You can see into the kitchen area. The burgers are well seasoned, the onion rings are you standard restaurant onion rings, but an order is went for 2.
name: Mercedes

text: It's always delicious, and the ambience is very nice. I give 4 stars bc the line is so long and I think it's a bit pricy. I'll go back and enjoy again without a doubt.
name: Ilana

text:
I'm not a regular at this place but whenever I go for late shows at AMC, I make a pit stop here for a quick drink and a bite. This place is always crowded and I mean it in a good way. It's lively with tons of TV screens and fairly quick food service. 

This time I tried a German beer named Weihenstephan hefeweissbier and I must say I loved it. I'm not a beer girl and that's why this special mention. The beer had a subtle banana flavor at the end, which is very refreshing. The wings are okay but the Herman style seasonings are spot-on. I also loved the garlic teriyaki sauce. Yum!

text: Hidden gem in an alley. Very friendly workers and very clean as well. Definitely recommend you come and try the delicious food!
name: Emily

text: I've been a few times and all I can say is it's the best. The food is great the service is exquisite. Definitely worth the price.
name: Retro

text: The soup was better than the sandwich, which I wasn't expecting. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Food was good and came out fast.
name: User

text: This restaurant is not just average hotel restaurant. Servers are great and service is fast enough. And food is great. We ordered several different dishes from salad to lobster pasta. Everything was great.
name: Penny

text: The photos made it look a little better than it actually was. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. For a busy night they handled it okay. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Tried the shrimp fried and scampi style, both were decent, but the battered portion of the shrimp didn't have any flavor and was disappointing. Also tried the blackened mahi tacos. There were two tacos and the fish was a large portion of the taco. The filet of fish actually overwhelmed the taco itself. The downside: the mahi tacos saturated the actual taco itself and fell apart. This resorted in having to eat the taco with a fork instead, and tossing the breaded portion all together. The atmosphere of the restaurant was that of a wanna be fishers market, but came off more like a captain Ds. The most redeeming portion of the restaurant was the "Florida" croquettes which were crab cakes. They were a good price for a good portion and contained mostly crab meat and less filler.
name: Danielle

text: I give this place a five star because I was blown away, I was expecting mediocre Mexican food & drinks! We ate here before we left for the airport on Sunday afternoon, I was pleasantly surprised the food was so tasty! I sent compliments to the chef & our specialty drinks were fabulous, the female bartender was very cool and made us feel very welcomed! We really enjoyed our last meal here so it was a good end to a Funtastic 4th of July trip!
name: Bev

text:
When it comes to picking a hotel to stay, for me, it comes down to location, then price.  For those reasons, the wife and I chose the Fairfield Inn and Suites in the Gulch for a Monday to Friday stay.  We'd stayed at other Fairfield Inns across the country, but this one seemed a bit more contemporary in its design and offered nicer amenities such as the rooftop cocktail bar with an excellent view of the Nashville skyline and live music in the lobby on Wednesdays during the hours that its complimentary breakfast is served than other properties in the chain. 

The hotel was strategically located in the seemingly rapidly developing Gulch section of town.  We were within short walking distance to many excellent restaurants and two excellent craft breweries (which made me happy), but found many of the sites of interest like the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum and the Ryman to also be within reasonable walking distance of the hotel.  A caveat...the wife and I like to walk, so our estimation of a "reasonable" walk may differ from yours.  As for price, the Fairfield Inn wasn't necessarily inexpensive, but compared to other hotels of equal quality in downtown Nashville, it was on the less expensive end of the spectrum and offered solid value.  Services like housekeeping went unnoticed (in a good way) in that we never saw housekeeping, but our room was always cleaned and reset every afternoon when we returned to our room after a day of sightseeing.

In the end, Fairfield Inn and Suites will be at the top of my places to stay the next time we're in Nashville.
name: Gregg

text: Honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Food was good and came out fast. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly.
name: User

text: They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Glad we tried it. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. Food was fresh and service was quick. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent.
name: User

text:
If you're Vietnamese, just order only chicken to-go. Don't try noddle soup. It's tasteless & too much MSG. Chicken is alright. Not bad.
Luckily I didn't have to drive 2 1/2h to eat "mehhh" chicken noddle soup. My sister drove to there, from VA, and brought home 2 carry-outs. 

Next time, just buy ready-to-eat Pho in packages. Then go to your local Chinese restaurant to get a steamed chicken. It's way more better.
name: Kenny

text: The square pizza was very very good, crisp on the outside, good sauce and burrata & basil, what else does one need?  Big enough to split.  Oh the salad...the Italian was so BIG, 2 of us couldn't finish it. Best of all was Tiffany!  She needs a raise and a promotion.  She was delightful, knowledgeable, and made the whole experience fun & rewarding.  I hope she's there when I return.
name: Victoria

text: Traveled from Delco PA.to NE Phila.to purchase some goodies from Polka Delli for the Christmas Holidays    What I returned with,was bags of delicious food,a smile on my face from meeting beautiful people, and a firm handshake from the owner.Merry Christmas and Happy New Year!! STOLAT !
name: Frank

text:
Just the most outstanding soups dumplings you'll find around. Not to mention this place is an icon for us - been coming for years. 
Still remember the night the owner and his family were gracious enough to talk "food" and let us taste some homemade pickled jalapeños.   
He won our hearts over!!!
Thank you staying true to your food and consistency. 
We'll be back over and over again!!!!
name: Crissie

text:
I was invited to lunch at Zeppelin. If you haven't ventured here yet, you're in for a treat. The atmosphere is dynamite. The room is only open to those who are 21+. This means no kids, babies. This doesn't mean they don't like them, they're just not allowed inside. The front door openly states the room is for 21+, only. There will be a family oriented, related spot on the other side of this location but for now this is how things are run. 

The service is great. I happened to know the bartender, Annalisa Suarez, who knows so much about craft cocktails as well as their fantastic beer selection. They offer taps, and cans but I didn't see any bottles. Their selection of spirits is amazing. If I could post up at the bar and enjoy the various bourbons they have, I'd stay for at least 8 hours. 

The food is delicious. My friend Matt had their Reuben on Pumpernickel while I enjoyed a half order of pulled pork sliders. The down side to the order, they're only served as is. If you want a side, that's additional. I wasn't disappointed. I just didn't know how things were over there. The food arrived in a timely manner with a smile from the kitchen. Both my plate and Matt's plate were satisfying. We'll go back in the days ahead but for now will revel in the greatness that we enjoyed. 

The location is new and offers ample parking. They also have a private room for events so if you're looking for a great spot in South Reno for your next company function or just a lunchtime get together, check out Zeppelin.
name: Chris

text: I haven't been to McAlister's in probably almost 2 decades.  Since I moved out of my home town of Memphis in 2004.  Lunch was totally up to me today, due to all my coworkers having plans or already left for lunch, so I decided to check things nearby.  I knew there was a McAlister's nearby, so decided, let's do it.  I'll just put in an online order and pick it up.  NO GO.  I tried to place the order, but it would never let me "add to order." So I did it the old fashion way and called.  Drove in, place was busy, picked up paid, drove back to work.  I got a pick 2, broccoli cheddar soup, and french dip sandwich ($1.25) upcharge.   Unpacked my lunch.  The soup and au ju were plastic wrapped to insure there was no spillage on the way to my destination.  I open the soup.  It's almost 3/4 of the way full.  Looked a little light, but was very delicious.  I open the dip and the sandwich, dip my sandwich in the sauce and take a bite.  HEAVEN.  So delicious.  Followed it up with the "Sweet Tea" which is not really that sweet, mostly I believe is because I'm in the midwest, and not the South.  I'll definitely be back.
name: Ken

text: Lots of flavor - concept is comparable with Chipotle but for noodles, in terms of ingredients' freshness, speediness, & customizability. I love & crave the sauce in their sauce bowl. I have always ordered that with sweet potato noodles, all the veggies/toppings, & either tofu or duck. Never fail to hit that mini spice bar on the way out as well. Unfortunately, it can be hard to get them to answer the phone for take-out sometimes, it's extremely rare that they ever have duck in stock (I've gone countless times since moving to SoHo almost a year ago & can count on 1 hand the number of times they've had duck stocked... Thankfully, they had it for my most recent visit :) It had been SO long!!!) Also, as many other reviewers seem to note & value, the portion sizes have always been generous.. but one time a couple weeks ago let me down a LOT on that part. (I'm not greedy about portions because I grew up in the food business & I know America is conditioned to want these massive servings, which people don't seem to know or care can sacrifice quality, but they should still be consistent..) But on this visit, I got it planning to share with my co-worker who I'd told about this place & when we opened it, there was about a quarter of the amount of noodles I usually get... (swear I'm not being dramatic. It was so strange.) Since I understand sometimes you have to do this, I called them to inquire about whether it was intentional or not & I didn't get a clear answer - something about it depending on who made my bowl & some advice about asking for extra noodles for a charge next time? I was so disappointed cuz they should still be at least measuring for *consistent* serving sizes regardless of what those sizes are, but this has only happened once so I'm definitely giving them another chance with that.) It's always clean inside, staff is always nice (even when not knowledgeable,) & I really do like the place.. just wish there was more consistency & clarity in a few experiences. I realize my focus is on the duck, take-out calls, & a single instance of portion problems, which might just be exactly where moments of weakness are for them.
name: Trina

text: While the food is pretty good for a fast food spot, the new management is very condescending to those who support the business.  Big turn off, but if they can turn around their disdain for the customers, this will be a happening food spot, a go to, since they are open much later than other restaurants in the area (open until 3am).
name: Jody

text: Our Uber driver suggested that we go to Frenchman Street for the NOLA musical experience, if we wanted to avoid the craziness of Bourbon Street. We're so glad we heeded his advice. We had a very nice, tasty dinner at Three Muses, and enjoyed a great combo providing fun, lively music. We had a great time at this restaurant, and would definitely recommend it.
name: Penny

text: Unique place. Had multiple little gift shops to wonder thru while you wait. Get the breakfast! Great experience.
name: Diana

text: This is a family favorite.  They have vegan burgers that you can substitute. Also, if you want a healthier option, try side salad, veggies, or fruit on the side (instead of fries,) whole wheat rolls and/or lettuce wrapped patty. My husband and boys love bottomless fries. The mountain high mud pie is huge and delicious.
name: Erin

text:
My husband and I were really disappointed with our take-out order. We ordered the meatloaf platter, fried chicken platter and philly sandwich. The platters were so overly salted that we couldn't eat them. Mashed potatoes with gravy and sautéed vegetables as our sides. The potatoes and gravy was really were we just couldn't do it. The gravy was so salty that it was inedible. The veggies in one of the to-go containers were burnt on one side and flipped to the other.
The Philly was alright. Nothing to special. For the money we spent, I probably won't be going back. Which is too bad. The restaurant is in a super convenient spot- right on the way home.
name: Katie

text: One of my favorite places in the city. Great for people watching or grabbing a bit! Highly recommended...
name: Drew

text: The first few bites were promising and then it kind of leveled out. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. Kind of landed in the middle for me. Ordered a few things and liked most of it. The leftovers held up okay the next day..
name: User

text: Consistency prevails here.   Always a good meal.    Staff is very friendly and attentive.
name: F

text: So much fun.  With friends or with kids.  We went with our 3 and 7 year old.  They both loved the food and wanted to keep playing rounds of golf forever.
name: Megan

text: What a fun night out.  Real dining experience, excellent service, a fabulous wine list, and best seafood I've had in long time (try the sole).
name: Patricia

text: Such a cool spot to grab a beer or two and check out a lightning game. The food is very tasty- and for the tiny kitchen - literally behind the bar they make the most of it- big fan of the grilled cheese. But the real star is the beer selection. Recently they had the Goose Island Bourbon County Vanilla on tap. Sure it's pricey but nearly impossible to find on draft and well worth the $$- like finding a bottle of Pappy you get what you pay for. They bartenders are very attentive and good for convo. Highly recommended place if you don't want the crowded chaos of the other sports bar a few blocks away :)
name: David

text: They're idiots here, too. Definitely don't place a Grub Hub order. You at least won't get it per the time window that Grub Hub states, and you may not get it all! I had to hassle with Grub Hub for a refund. I did not get my order. I suppose I should be reviewing Grub Hub too, for their lack of reliability in drivers that obviously don't want to work!
name: Harlan

text: My organization held a private event at FSC. Working with the events team was a dream. Our attendees gave me rave reviews and compliments, which I owe entirely to the team at FSC. They expertly handled all of the details, including several last-minute requests. The space was gorgeous--it was perfectly setup for our technology needs and to have a cocktail hour--and we even had a private bartender. There were tickets for drinks to help manage costs, as well. Booking the space, ordering the food, getting the invoice, all were incredibly smooth. The food was absolutely delicious and perfectly timed to coordinate with our needs! Thank you so much Ling and team!
name: Josh

text: Wonderful Sunday Jazz Brunch at Commander's Palace.  So much food and so amazing.  I had the Commander's Palace salad and it was the best salad I've ever had.  The ingredients were chopped up so perfectly that you got each ingredient in every bite!  I had the steak and eggs with the most amazing grits!   Steak was cooked to perfection.  I ordered it rare.  I don't care for eggs, so I didn't eat that, but the dish had a lot of flavor and it wasn't spicy.  I ordered the strawberry shortcake for dessert but was way too full to even take a bite!  My daughter had some and said it was really good.  Fun brunch with Jazz music and lovely atmosphere.
name: Erin

text: This is a great little neighborhood restaurant. Really good food and a nice variety of menu items. I didn't give 5 stars because of the loud, hip-hop music that is broadcasted in the restaurant. I have nothing against hip-hop music, but it is better suited to a club or bar! I have friends complain about the same exoerience recently. I noticed the music change and volume go lower when the owner showed up. A word to the owner, I hope you find the staff responsible for this loud environment causing disgruntled customers and diminished enjoyment of your restaurant and food.
name: Cathy

text:
This location is dirty and when crowded, the line/ordering is a little disorganized. The ice cream tastes good and the quality is the same at all Baskin Robbins though. 

If you visit on the 31st, it's $1.50 per scoop (limited time).
