text:
After flying into Indianapolis we were starving.  I wanted Chinese food, but coming from California where there are TONS of great Chinese food restaurants we were a little apprehensive.  Well thanks to my fellow yelpers and GPS we found Naisa.  A great spot in the Fountain Square area.

The restaurant is clean and has a calm vibe.  There were two servers ours was Darvin he was nice and friendly, and gave us a recommendation for another place for burgers (Kumas Corner-review coming soon).  We started with hot tea.  They had a selection, not just house.  So I opted for the Jasmine.  We then had wonton soup.  It was excellent, a nice clean broth with excellent chicken wontons. No filmy oil on top, just great flavor.  We then ordered combination chow mien.  Now that was completely different than what I am used to.  The noodle was a thin noodle, not an egg noodle.  It was yummy, although reminiscent of an Italian noodle.  It was flavorful with cilantro and other thinly sliced veggies.  Not your run of the meal chow mien, but delicious.  We also ordered the tangerine shrimp.  It was good a little too tangy for me, but my husband enjoyed it.  

We will be back again.

We were surprised the inside bar had plenty of available seats. After a few minutes, the bartender greeted us and then gave us several menus.  I was starving so I ordered calamari but the bartender warned me against the selection. I then opted for the soft shell crab appetizer. It took a while for the app to come out, but it was okay. I found it to be extremely greasy but the sauce was good. 
Moving onto dinner: we both ordered filets. I ordered mine medium and my friend medium rare. Well let's just say neither of the steaks were cooked correctly. Both steaks were cooked well-done and were room temperature. The plate was not hot nor were the mashed potatoes. Had I not been starving, I would have said something but honestly- you just get the sense at this place they don't care.  On two occasions I watched the bartender stand in plane view - counting his tips. Never once did he even ask about the dinner. 

I think it is important to point out a few things. I was born and raised in Florida. So, I don't make the "trip" to Clearwater often. I have been going to Island Way Grill for 18 years (or longer). I think the restaurant may be a great spot for individuals who are in the area on vacation and wish to spend a lot of money on very unremarkable food.
name: Whitney

text:
If you're craving falafel, this is indubitably the place to go. It's so crispy on the outside, but light and fluffy on the inside. The flavor is spot-on, and the entire experience is so addictive. Sometimes I just want a whole meal of falafels (which I can get with their bag'o'balls!). Mostly, I get their falafel salad. It's pretty pricey for a salad ($9), but the amount of fresh veggies and falafel they include is well worth the price in my opinion. The dish is packed full of kale, beets, cucumbers, carrots, dill, tehina, and crunchy sunflower seeds. Plenty filling, and doesn't make me too guilty! I also like the shawarma spiced french fries, which are paired with a spiced ketchup.
Their tehina shakes are also pretty good. Rich and nutty (almost like a peanut butter shake), they come in a few different flavors. My favorite so far is the coffee one! It is a bit heavy though, and I can never finish one on my own.
Basically, this place is bomb. Definitely stop by.
name: Sanika

text:
Pop down finally to check out the brunch here, and worked out that it was worth their big fifth anniversary bash! We didn't have a reservation at the staff was very kind to squeeze us in at the bar, even though it was jampacked and tons of reservations.  Last time we made the mistake of trying to bring some kids, and they don't except children for the brunch.

The brunch was sponsored by Moet, and there was tons of balloons and Champagne flowing!

I really like the brunch menu, it's a really good mix of lots of hangover favorites... And then some really nice Benedict's, and some healthy things.

My friend went with "the cure", which is basically a super huge poutine with all the fixings and some poached eggs on top... Definitely "the cure" if you know what I mean!

And with the avocado and tomato Benedict, it was really nicely done and I did like their take on the classic hollandaise sauce. Also pop a bottle of bubbly! Definitely will be back for the brunch here.
name: Chris

text: Very, very good pizza. I think it's considered NY style. I'm not an expert. But it is delicious. So far I've tried a cheese pizza (10/10) as well as a meatball sub (also 10/10). Garlic knots I'll give a 7/10, almost too much flavor for me personally. But still good. My new favorite spot in Lutz
name: Josh

text:
Came here for dinner and enjoyed the meal. I ordered the Pad Thai, which was good and a decent sized serving. My date order a chef special (shrimp and scallops). It was good, but wouldn't say it really stood out. The desert (lemon cake and homemade coconut ice cream) was REALLY good. The flavors where delicious and the ice cream was thick and creamy. We both said the dessert was the best part of the meal. 

Decor was nice and the restaurant was clean with good service. Currently it is BYOB, but the server indicated they will have a alcoholic drink menu shorlty. Overall a nice meal and experience! Prices were average, perhaps a bit high. However, I would recommend Nui Nui for a nice meal and/or date night.
name: Matthew

text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. For a busy night they handled it okay. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. I can see why people like it, even if I wasn't fully sold. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. For a busy night they handled it okay. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. It was decent, just a little uneven. No big complaints, just a nice meal. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text:
We ordered kalbi and cold noodles tonight as the warm weather was perfect for this combo. 
The cold noodles were from the freezer bc it barely pulled apart and was too soggy. I know this bc I've prepared the $1.99 frozen cold noodles before. Also the broth was just plain nasty. Drained in chicken stock from the cube barely dissolved with tons of MSG. 
The kalbi was cooked from the kitchen as it was a single serving. It was served luke warm and very dry. When I addressed the clumps of cold noodles found in the bowl to the server and that I can not eat it anymore, she stirred the chopsticks around the bowl a few times and said, "Okay, I won't charge you any tax on the total." I paid for the meal and left in disgust. 
When I got home, I drank tons of water as the MSG left a bad taste in my mouth and stomach. $52 dollars of grief is what I ended up with.
name: Mary

text: Love love love this place.  The food is very delicious and the employees are spectacular. I would recommend everyone try them.  I'm a regular and hooked on the PHO and boba tea.

text: Spent way too many days here, but the drinks and music were awesome. Some of the people play across the street at night, but one guy gave his MAGA hat to my gf. Nice!

text:
A Saturday night in Northern Liberties always has me in the area of the Piazza. I was finally able to stop by Urban Village for some good food. Their specialty is definitely their pizza. I had the Sofia (fennel sausage with pesto). The sausage they use on this pizza is delicious! The only complaint I would have is that the pizza was more dough than toppings. I don't know if it was just the pie I ordered or if all of them are like this, but the crust was taking up more than I had hoped. 

Service is great here. Even if it's a Saturday night which I thought would be busy, the waitress came by right away with water, gave me a few minutes to decide what I wanted to eat/drink, and hen followed up after the food was served.

text: Really cool place, even if you're going for a drink or two. Their food is really good as well and they have a couple unique items with cool spins on your typical Vietnamese dishes/Banh Mi.

My girlfriend mistakenly dropped her drink and the staff was kind enough to ask her for another even though it was her mistake. Good service goes a long way and will definitely return!

text: One of my favorite places to eat, the cheesesteaks, the wings and the BLT club are my favorites. I love place.

text: I dine at this steakhouse fairly often. Every time I go there I ask myself why. The service and atmosphere are excellent. They have wide verity of beers. They always offer warm buns with cinnamon butter. All the amenities are perfect but food is just mediocre. I would expect a good quality, nicely broiled steak from a restaurant that calls itself a steakhouse. They never cook it right. Steak tastes mushy. It has no flavor. It feels like a cheap cut of meat cooked on griddle. There are hardly any grill marks or seasoning on it. Their burgers are just like any other burger anywhere else. Nothing special. They have some seafood but I never ventured in any of the seafood. Sandwiches are simply sliced bread with the usuals. I always go there for the steak but for me it doesn't cut it. But service and atmosphere are pretty good.

text:
Kung Fu Hoagies are a staple at the Saturday Clark Park Farmers Market! They're so delicious, and the portions are so filling! 

All of the bánh mì hoagies are served on a baguette with traditional bánh mì ingredients (carrots, cucumbers, daikon, jalapeño, cilantro) and vegan mayonnaise.

I've tried the BÁNH MÌ XÍU MI (homemade tofu meatballs with red sauce) and the BÁNH MÌ THIT BÒ (vegetarian beef protein with homemade BBQ sauce). Both are great! 

I can't wait to go back and try the vegetarian pork hoagie, as well as the noodles and sides!

text: The food was good and the service was easygoing. Food was fresh and service was quick. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. So I had pizza with meatballs. It was very good, though the sauce to cheese ratio was low on sauce for my taste. My friend and I enjoyed the atmosphere on the patio.

text: True story: I didn't go to Ruth's for five years because a server was rude to me. Five years. I don't know what I was trying to prove, but I can tell you that was stupid, because this food is fantastic. I came back today for lunch with a friend and we had a wonderful experience. My friend is on some pretty serious dietary restrictions, and they answered all of her questions, going back to check with the kitchen on several items. She really enjoyed her salmon/avocado salad. I asked the server to help me decide between the chicken salad and crab cake sandwich and she didn't hesitate to say chicken salad. She was right. I don't know what's in this stuff, but it is amazing--not too mayonnaise-y--and I loved the swiss and butter lettuce that came on the sandwich. I got the side of greens with the house vinaigrette, and it was heaven. LOVE that they use eco-friendly to-go containers and don't offer straws. Ambiance is super warm and charming. And the server was a DELIGHT, so it will absolutely not be another five years before I return

text: I go here a lot.  Love the outdoor seating options and beer selection.  The pours are a little weak for cocktails, otherwise I'd give it a five.  Food is good, it's Edleys.  Get here before 4pm or the brisket might be out for the day already.  Smoked turkey is awesome and under rated.
name: Scott

text: Chicken tikka masala is great but DON'T ORDER DELIVERY unless your willing to wait 2 hours. Other reviews I see have said the same thing. This place is 5 minutes from my house and the first time I ordered delivery it took 2 hours until I received my food. The driver blamed it on traffic.  From then on I ordered take out, however, I was unable to drive last night so I ordered delivery. The lady on the phone said it would take 45 minutes. Once again, I didn't receive my order until 2 Hours later. The same driver, again, blamed traffic and then had the nerve to ask me to tip generously. Very unprofessional and should have at least given me a discount for the 2 hour wait.
name: Jen

text: I've tried this restaurant a few times for lunch and dinner. The service and ambience is good. The lunch special is a steal for money and comes with a soup, main and rice. The hot and sour soup is really good and spicy. Wonton soup was a little bland and needed a decent helping of salt. The egg rolls are good and comes with a nice dipping sauce. Love the dan dan noodles. The noodles are good and the sauce is yum. The garlic chicken is also very good. Very mild in spice level and the sauce has a subtle hint of garlic. One dish I was really disappointed with was the fried dumplings. The dough is super thick and the dough to meat ratio is way off!! I couldn't taste the meat at all. This is the worst dumplings I've ever had and hence the 3 star. The only good part about it was the dipping sauce which was good. It's such a shame. I hope they change their dumplings. Apart from that rest of the dishes I tried there was good.

text: I love to love Buena Onda. I stumbled upon this one day just literally walking by & had to stop in. Everything is delicious & reasonably priced. My personal fav is the chicken quesadilla (no beans) which is pictured here. They have taco deals throughout the week & a nice happy hour. The salsa here is to die for & you def have to try their frozen margaritas. I couldn't give 5 stars though, simply because sometimes the service is really slow.

text: Great local spot to take friends and family. Big menu so lots of options.  Many tv's to watch the big game or kid shows to entertain the younger crowd.   Full bar for adults.   Tenderloin is very good.

The waitress was very pleasant and accommodating. I definitely recommend this restaurant!

text: Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. For a busy night they handled it okay. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Glad we tried it. The food was good and the service was easygoing.

This is the first time I review Vincent's but not my first time there.  If you're looking for amazing Italian food and want to be treated well, this is your place.

text: The food and cocktails are very good: large portions, incredible presentation. The service is bad. The dirty dishes piled up with each course and nobody was clearing. We had to ask repeatedly for simple things like butter, beverages or utensils. We were in a side room that had clearly not been touched since the last restaurant that was in this space. It is distractingly bad - veneers are peeling off, a wall of shadow box shelving has lightbulbs out, nothing in them but old candles and some silverware. It is embarrassing. I will not go back.

Only negative in the experience was with the staff at the front bar who handle the "moonshine tasting" - - this group was unfriendly and not particularly welcoming and seemed dedicated to making this "tasting" a stressful rather than pleasurable experience (to the point that I bailed before it really began).  Otherwise, this is a gorgeous and well-appointed place with great food, beer and cocktails and I would definitely visit again.

text: Arrived mid-morning on a Tuesday, and the place was far from being busy. Was seated at a booth adjacent to the kitchen access. Our order took which seemed like forever to come to our table. We watched our food sitting on a shelf under heat lamps for at least 15 minutes. Our waitress was rarely to be seen, and another food runner finally brought our meal, and ran off without asking if we needed anything. I had to wait again for condiments when our waitress finally made an appearance. No apologies for the long wait, she was just cluless. Also, they charge $2.79 for coffee,and $2.79 for a refill. No manager in sight, just an inept staff minding the store.

text: Our first time at this locations. We decided to divide and conquer. My husband had the half chicken with canary beans and green beans. Neither one of us was impressed by the flavor of the chicken. We've had better at boston market. Both beans weren't bad. I had the Wow Lomito (steak sandwich) with plantains, and i added a side of cilantro rice. This sirloin on this sandwich was seasoned perfectly, i just wished they weren't so cheap with the portion on the sandwich. They barely even put enough of the mayo on the sandwich for me to say it wasn't dry. Even my husband said he would order the steak next time. The plantains were cooked perfectly and the cilantro rice was pretty good. We shared the herbal limeade. It's quite refreshing and wakes you up, but really too sweet to be a drink and should be sold as a shot at a juice bar. Between us both we still could not drink the whole thing. But don't get me wrong the flavor is there. You can get it with no ice take it home and sip on it all day.

I'm sure you could get anything on this menu and you'd be pleased.

text:
My girlfriend and I decided to dine here for the first time as a date night. Prior to making the reservation, I was skeptical due to the negative reviews I read online. However, my mind was completely changed after visiting Davio's at the King of Prussia Town Center. Here were my main take aways:
1) The scenery: the restaurant itself occupies a large space that gives a nice open, cozy feeling. We immediately felt welcome and were excited to be seated. Although there were online complaints about it being too loud within the restaurant, I thought the noise level was fair. Granted, closer to the bar there was a lot more noise, but that is too be expected as my girlfriend and I had no trouble holding a conversation.

2) The service: Our waiter, Dave, was one of the best servers I have had the pleasure to encounter. Not only was his knowledge of the menu in depth, but he was comfortable in communicating with our preferences to try off-menu drinks or even a new type of food. He was extremely friendly, warm, and patient. As a bonus, the manager found out it was our first time at the restaurant and payed for our dessert. When we couldn't decide on which dessert to get, Dave just brought us both! Although the skeptic in me thinks we were probably given less popular desserts or something they needed to get rid off, it was still an enjoyable experience and we both appreciated the gesture.

3) The food: My girlfriend got the caprese ravioli and I got the braised beef short ribs as well as calamari. In my opinion, every dish was up to par and totally worth the price in both quality and quantity. My only regret is not being able to try more of the entrees, but that is an endeavor for a near future time.

Cons: The only negative comment I can make is when one of staff kept coming to refill our water. He was way to aggressive in pouring into our glasses. When we received our menus, he rushed to fill our drinks, overfilled my water, and had it overflow onto my menu. He repeated it a second time, only it was worse and he ended up soaking half of the table as well as my expensive sunglasses and almost my phone. What made it worse was the he seemed to pay no mind to his unprofessional behavior and didn't even offer acknowledgment of his mistake nor an apology.

Overall, our first experience at Davio's was unique, satisfying, and an afternoon to remember. We look forward to coming back for more.
name: Jimmy

text: I had prize-winning ribs, which were indeed very tasty, falling-off-the-bone tender, and very nicely flavored - neither too spicy nor too bland, neither too sweet nor too acid.   The crowd was very compatible with us - we did not feel like the oldest people in the room (nor the youngest), the waitress was homey and cute in her own way, and even the specially brewed beer was quite to our taste.  The Eggplant Bruschetta starter was toasted crisply and flavored fully, Linda enjoyed her somewhat spicy crab cakes, and we saved enough for lunch (or possibly dinner) today, leaving room for dessert, which turned out to be a blueberry cobbler that tasted a little like bread pudding.  All in all a very good birthday dinner.
name: Frank L

text:
I'll give an updated review once I give TF's menu another try but first stab was so-so.

The good: 1)This site clearly puts a premium on customer service - we were greeted upon hitting the front door and helped patiently with our order as we were first timers.  Staff asked if all was OK while we were eating and helped with refills.  2)Churros were warm and worked excellent as a palette cleanser.  3)I can see from the specials the time to go is Tues or Thurs to get the bill down so we'll take advantage of that next time. 4)Chicken tacos I ordered were just OK...wouldn't take them over Chipotle for sure.  However, I was eye-balling the philly steak flautas my daughter ordered...I probably should have gone that route and she said they were the bomb.  Noted.

The not so good: 1)Parking at this location is awful.  Went right at opening time (11a/Fri) but actually had to drive around until a spot opened despite what seems like a vast parking area.  I guess everyone is parking to eat @ First Watch?  Big hassle.  2)Not wild about that "tip" line when I pay with credit card before I've actually been served.  Not a major thing...I'm willing to tip but it's always awkward as I want to see how my service is at the table before I actually do my tipping, y'know?  3)Was looking forward to the sauce bar as I love the spicy stuff but this was probably the biggest let-down.  Something like 15 sauces and I tried just about every one and ALL disappointed.  I ended up eating my taco dry.  Next time I'll bring my packets from taco bell I guess.  My advice to Tijuana Flats is to forget about these manufactured sauces with the dumb names and work on some good hot, medium, mild in-house sauces as clearly more doesn't necessarily mean better.

This is turning into a short novel so I'll end it here.  Updated review will be forthcoming if/when we hit this spot again.
name: Dan

text:
The decor of this place is really pretty! Only downside is my friends and I went for Happy Hour and it was SUPER crowded in the bar, which meant waiting for a table was super squished (since the aisle is really only about the width of one person). We didn't make a reservation, but luckily we got the last table outside. 

Our server was Martin and he was really nice and super helpful! I ordered the iced coffee and blackened fajita tacos. I loved the paper straw that was in my drink! The coffee was strong but good!! Martin told us that the food was on a special Happy Hour price, so I could essentially get two tacos for the price of one (thank God I got two, because I devoured the first taco in minutes since it was sooo delicious). Usually I don't like spicy food, and the peppers made it spicy, but they were sweet, as well as caramelized onions, it was absolutely phenomenal. I also tried a bit of my friend's coconut rice and I fell in LOVE. Sooo good!!!! 

One thing I will say is that the price on the menu said iced coffee was $4, however, I was charged $5. I didn't want to make a fuss over a $1, but just something to note.

text:
In the past 3 weeks, I've visited Bevi Seafood 3 times & you were closed during business hours without notice. The 1st time was a Friday at 4pm. The doors were locked without a sign on the door. The 2nd time was a Saturday at 3pm. AGAIN, the doors were locked without a sign. I called this time. Someone answered the phone & rudely stated, "We are out of everything, so we are closed." I politely said, "Okay" and left. I am someone who gives businesses multiple chances, particularly local "mom & pop" shops. So, I gave you a 3rd try yesterday at 5:10pm. AGAIN, the doors were locked with no sign stating why you randomly closed during business hours. I called because at this point I wanted to make sure the owners knew this was happening, probably more times than I experienced. Someone picked up the phone & rapidly hung up. I called again & the phone was off the hook. 

We eat seafood on a regular basis, live nearby & will no longer be visiting your establishment. I will be sure to rate your service on Yelp, TripAdvisor, OpenTable & any other social media I can find with your name on it. I will not be recommending your business to anyone. There are too many seafood restaurants in the area with the same or better options who value their customers.
name: Ali

text:

text: I hate to do this, but to save anyone from making the mistake and going to this place for a meal, I will. We are in Nashville and there was to be entertainment at DB Whiskey Row so we thought it would be awesome to grab dinner and watch the performer. Big mistake. Right off the jump, the performer was going to be on the second floor. No biggie. We go up there and wait patiently for a table. While waiting we ordered two beers and two diet sodas from the bar. The female bartender was rude as hell, and, not exaggerating put one fourth of soda in the glass. Left the rest empty. Ok, we overlooked that and her attitude and found an empty table. The previous group had warned us the table was super wobbly and spins. Jesus, they weren't kidding. Nobody could dare place a hand on the table because it always shifted and drinks were spilling. When we asked the waitress she said, yeahhhh all the tables are like this. What? How about someone put a lil pride into this establishment? Oh and the floors, I am all for the "honky tonk" but shoes shouldn't literally stick to the floor! The food was disgusting. When we left our plates were nearly untouched. Here's the kicker, the bill included a TECH FEE of 3%. Waitress had no idea what it went for and we paid cash so there was no CC fees. The TECH FEE clearly isn't being used for cleaning supplies. Dierks, if your putting your name on something, you damn well better make sure it's not a flop!

text: This was an awful experience. I like the concept of fresh seafood steamed and dumped on the table. I spent many years in the South and Frogmore Stew was one of the best things about it. This, however, is not that. We ordered the seafood by the pound which seems to their main thing. The food is cooked in excessively oily stuff.  The seafood was tasteless (I guess it's all been frozen?).  The seafood and the corn/potatoes sides were way overcooked so the shrimp was tough and the potatoes were mush. The corn was so waterlogged that it was inedible.  The clams fared better but in not sure why. The food came in plastic bags.  It was double bagged so that was two 2-gallon plastic bags per each pound of shrimp/clams.  So much plastic waste! And not a great serving experience to just have all these bags plunked down on the table.  Price was high but wouldn't have seemed unreasonable if the food had been good.  This place clearly only exists because of tourists. I can't imagine them getting repeat business.

text:
THIS. Let me tell you, genius idea here. Tastings of quality wines that you rarely get a chance to try because the bottles are so expensive. I mean, come on. Any wine lovers dream!

It seems a little weird to have to put money on a card, but then when you see the system, it makes more sense. We opted for one card for our group of 7 because we weren't local so we didn't want to waste all those cards. We put $10 each on the card and grabbed a glass to taste. The wine coolers with the tasting pours is in the hallway and got a little cramped as we all huddled around deciding what we wanted to try first. There were a few good rosés like Whispering Angel, we tried a couple interesting red blends, and I got to try a few Italian whites I liked. The fun part of all of it was trying different sips for only a few dollars each. There were a couple more expensive bottles that were pricier for tastings too.

They also have wine by the glass and a bottle list if that's more your style. The space was cozy, situated in a converted home. There were a few patio seats outside too. I definitely wish I could revisit this place more often. Consider opening one in Rochester, perhaps?

The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Not bad for a quick meal. text:
I am seriously disappointed with this place. If you are going there after a touch week to relax, put your breaks on because you will not have that glass of wine you have been waiting for. No alcohol. 

OK, I thought, I am going to have a nice meal and it won't matter. Here comes the cucumber salad which is NO DRESSING and cut up cucumbers with romaine lettuce. I thought- alright, this is an Indian restaurant catering to Americans, so I will stick around for an appetizer. 

Chicken pakora comes in and tastes like McNuggets, at which point I left.

text: No wait at 7am on Monday morning!  The Monte Cristo sandwich on Brioche French Toast bread, are you kidding me, this is awesome!  Hubby had half for breakfast and the other for lunch! I had the Simple Breakfast. Two eggs (cooked just right over medium) wheat toast and VERY tasty pork sausage. Roasted potatoes were a little too crunchy for me, but very flavorful. Loose leaf tea was French pressed to perfection. Would have given 5 stars but restroom needed attention. Not sure if the one stall in particular had not been cleaned the night before or if someone blew it up first thing this morning. Hard to overlook. Otherwise I would highly recommend the food, service and atmosphere. Will come back next time I am in town.

text:

name: Craig

text: Best fried red snapper I've ever tasted. It was fantastic. I highly recommend the snapper for people who maybe avoid eating fish for fear fishy taste. This fish is flat delicious!
name: Michael

text:
This survey is for the drive they line at the McDonald's located at 3318 Kirkwood Hwy, Wilm., DE ONLY!  Otherwise I like McDonald's. 

Speed of check out is glacially slow day after day. Often times the employees at the windows are talking and laughing with each other, even with their backs to the windows, surprised to find me waiting in my car at the window. A typical, "Oh, I didn't see you!" is a typical response. Wow. You took my order and then you are surprised I would drive forward to the window?  3x this happened. 

Inaccuracy of my order is a huge problem for this location. How hard is it?!  This includes not only the food, but not including napkins and a straw in the bag. This is the only work they do!  Take orders. Fill orders. Take money. Hand you your order. Simple. Not really I guess. 

Temperature of food is an issue so often. Cold food is typical, especially during off hours. I guess my burger and fries sat an hour after the last customer drive through. Not fresh. Dry. Cold. 

Nothing is worse at a McDonalds than driving away in your car only to find an inaccurate order of cold, dry food after waiting an eternity, no straw or napkins. (Try drinking a soda with no straw while driving and stopping and starting at lights. Not pretty. With. I kid it just spills.)

Customers cannot turn around and drive back once they are in the highway having ordered "fast" food. It becomes an issue of choosing to be late to work or going back. That's a no-brainer. 

Because of my frequent problems with this store, I have spoken to 3 different managers at this location. 2 of the 3 were at least empathetic. The most recent interaction with a manager "Shay" was so upsetting I called McDonald's customer service line. 

During that visit to McDonald's at this location, Shay blamed the problems with a change of shift. The previous manager blamed the problems on a new employee. The one before was apologetic. 

This branch needs a lesson in customer service. It is not the customer's fault if food is cold or dry due to off-hours. It is not the customer's fault there is a shift change or a new employee. It is not the customer's fault the order is wrong or napkins or a straw are not included. 

I felt the customer service phone call to their call center was not received helpfully. 

Although this McDonalds is on my way to work; it is the only one in my way to work, in the future I will go to Wendy's, Burger King, or even Wawa. I am just fed up.
name: Judy

text:
I have lived in Tucson for quite some time and occasionally drive down Oracle Road and Miracle Mile and pass Club 21. I had never been to the establishment until this evening and it was a result of a birthday party for my dad.

Upon his suggestion we met at Club 21 for Mexican food. He had arrived before we did and had a table waiting for us. When we arrived, we were promptly greeted by a warm smile and directed to our waiting party. 

Our waitress was attentive and absolutely knew the menu and when I asked her several questions, she was knowledgeable and kind. When she returned with our drinks she kindly offered to refill our chips and salsa. Throughout our time at Club 21, she came back to check on our table which was also a huge plus. 

The food? Absolutely delicious. We ordered a variety of food as we were celebrating a birthday with family such as the Chile relleno, cheese enchilada with tostada, vegetarian burritos, and tacos. Everything was delicious and our wait was what would be expected for a busy Friday night. 

I wholeheartedly recommend Club 21- the food was outstanding as well as the service.
name: Robyn

text:
Gangster Vegan Organics offers heart healthy food and drinks, its kinda pricey but makes since for organic food.

I was in the neighborhood and decided to use my handy yelp to find a nearby store that offers smoothies or healthy juices. That's when I discovered Gangster Vegan Organics.

The store is pretty small and it has a reggae and carribean vibe. It offers pressed juices, salads, vegan desserts, vegan burgers and much more. The menu is creative and the food items are named after iconic rappers and songs. Some of the items are the Notorious tuna cesar salad and the flava in ya ear juice. I decided to get the De la Soul pressed juice.

The De la Soul juice consisted of oranges, lemons, carrots, ginger and of course love! I love that the bottle was in a glass which 100% made it free from chemicals and it makes a great recyclable water bottle! I paid about 7.00 but it was worth it. My juice was delicious and refreshing. It was sweet with a hint of kick from the ginger.

Overall, If I was local, I would definitely visit this place often just for the juice!
name: Jenaya

text: Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Will be back. Food was good and came out fast. Would probably stop in again if nearby.

text: Had lunch here and it was nothing special. We were excited at first, the menu had a lot of variety and seemed interesting. I had the Turkey Chicken Avocado sandwich and it was pretty disappointing. The turkey and chicken were your basic deli slices of processed meat, and the croissant seemed like a Costco bulk purchase. The fries were pretty greasy and not crisp. My friends ordered the sweet potato chips with their sandwich and they were definitely worth the extra 50 cents. The best part of the meal was the corn dog nuggets appetizer - sweet and crunchy wrap around a bite (or two) sized dog. The atmosphere was nice, very open room with your choice of regular or tall tables. They have a nice sized patio in the back too.

text:
Looks can deceive when it comes to this Zionsville gem! You may think twice about coming here, but don't be deterred. It's definitely worth the chance. 

Since we moved from our apartment in College Park (86th and Michigan Rd) to Whitestown (near Zionsville), we've yet to find a local, default Asian restaurant where I can get my sushi, and my hubby can get his gyoza and orange chicken. Well... we have found it at Happy Kitchen! Everything from the decor, the service, and of course, the food is amazing!

We came in during lunch, so we ordered off the lunch special menu. I ordered my typical eel and avocado roll and a spicy tuna roll. The tuna was fresh and infused with the right amount of spice. The eel avocado roll was also very fresh with an acceptable meat:veg ratio. I hate it when some places skimp on my eel! Two rolls for $8.50. The husband ordered one roll and a kitchen item (General Tso Chicken) for $9.50. Great deal! We also had some lovely, hot Jasmine tea to make the experience complete. 

The menu is extensive, so I would suggest taking a look at the menu, on their website, and take a look. Oh, and they have GF soy sauce for my gluten-free folks! Enjoy!
name: Raechel

text:
I met out of towners here for NYE dinner at about 5:30.  They had a nice crowd but not overly packed. 

It's a casual place with a New Orleans style vibe. Lots of HBCU and Mardi Gras flags up . 

They have a daily $3drink special and on Sunday it's Bloody Mary. I tasted my sisters and it was pretty good . Spicy though . 

Perhaps it was the holiday so staff didn't show up but service was SLOW.  It took 30 minutes to get our orders after waiting 15 for her to come back to take it. She also never cleared dishes and for a table of four the table can get messy.  She was very polite and did update us but i think she needed more help . 


I ordered mahi mahi tacos .  After waiting 30 min they came with cheese so she had to send them back . Frustrating !  Ok so the mahi mahi was blackened and good but the overall dish was terrible. Probably the worst fish tacos I've had. My mistake for ordering  this in a Cajun establishment.  The tortilla was hard and dry and it was over stuffed with cabbage then just a teaspoon of salsa . No flavor. I just ate the mahi out of it .  Came with red beans and rice ( not good) and slaw ( decent) . 

Others at the table had the fisherman platter and crab cakes and i believe shrimp and everyone devoured their food so the moral of the story here is stick to Cajun if you go here. This is obviously what they do best. 

I'm unfortunately allergic to shellfish so I'm not sure i will be back
name: Kimberly

text: I checked Bubbakoos out for a quick to-go lunch this week after seeing it open about a week ago. After having great experiences at Andale, a similar chipotle style restaurant, I figured I'd give Bubbakoos a shot m. The menu was a bit all over the place so I decided to ask the staff for some advice (as I usually do at new places) but unfortunately they were disinterested and unhelpful so I was left to figure it out myself. I ended up making a brown rice and chicken burrito bowl. Everything appeared to be pretty fresh but was severely lacking in flavor. I tried to spice it up a bit with the Bubbakoos habanero hot sauce but it ended up just being repackaged Frank's. Personally, I don't think this place adds much value to the Grant Ave lunch options but I guess in a pinch I might give it another try!

text:
Came here for a cute little date night on Tuesday. This spot was featured in Craig LaBan's best burger list, so we had to come give it a try. I was definitely impressed. 

The aesthetic is cute. I'm sad it was a rainy night - I want to come back when the weather is nice because they have cutie outdoor space. The bar area looks pretty cramped, however, we sat in the dining room. I think there may be an upstairs too. 

They have a HH menu available at the bar. We got the pretzel appetizer. WOW! So good. And I got the burger with their house loaded fries. V good. You know we went in for dessert as well. The snickers bar was amazing. House made!!!! 

The drink selection is wild. They have an avocado margarita!!! I was intrigued, but stuck with the Malbec. I'll be back to try more items off this menu. I think I want to bring my parents!!! Worth the trip from the city!
name: Stephanie

text:
I was asked to give a review of one of the dishes on their new breakfast menu. So here goes...

As with most of the items on their menu, it was good. However, I have a few gripes. First, they use WAY too much rice. The dish I had consisted of one egg, a tiny bit of meat which I believe was BBQ pork rib and ham pieces, a ton of green and white onion, very little seasoning and about two large handfulls of white rice. As a breakfast item, there needs to be more protein. White rice should not make up 75% of the plate.

If I could make a suggestion, I would only use about 1/3 the rice, add another egg or two and more meat. As far as flavor goes, the massive amount of bland white rice killed the dish.

Granted, this is a new venture for L&L, and I am by no means trying to steer people away from trying them out. I wish them all the best. I just wanted to share my thoughts.
name: Terry

text: I think of this place as Chipotle but for Indian food. Plenty of options with different curries with a rice or salad base or can do half. I'd recommend a curry with either brown or white rice. The naan is very good too. Plenty of seating and parking and veggie options. Salad bar has lots of different chutneys or varying degrees of spice to try - would definitely recommend trying them all!

text: I've been here twice now and both times were superb. First of all, the service is great, every staff member has been very nice. I've tried 3 different cocktails and they were all consistently delicious!! And of course the food is outstanding. I was here yesterday but already want to go back :)

text:

text:
First, the food was very good.  One of our party was confused with the menu and ordered a philly  which came as a wrap.  The waitress offered to bring her a bun so she could fix it herself.  She declined and picked at it until an olde waitress with light colored hair came along and said "if you're done picking at that, I'll take your plate.  Surprised, she just pushed her plate away, and the waitress grabbed it and dumped the contents in the garbage.  When we finished, I went to the register to pay,  (mistake, the same waitress was there)  I asked about the philly, and she rudely showed me the menu, pointed 3 or 4 times to the word WRAPS.  I said ok and tried to pay.  She grabbed a cloth and said i'll be right back, and never returned.  I will go to my local Breakfast Station, But NEVER back to the New Port Richey location again.

Gloria
Zephyrhills, Fl

text:
It's burgers and hotdogs. We're not really reinventing the wheel here. I've had people RAVE about Portillos but maybe it's because they know something I don't know... Or maybe they're from the Midwest and it's nostalgic. I thought the restaurant was cute, large, and convenient. They have a massive parking lot and a drive thru. They specialize in hotdogs, roast beef sandwiches (that can be "dipped") and burgers. The meats are the same cheap portions and cuts you get from fast food restaurants.  

The prices were good and I was served relatively quickly. The flavor was ok. I would go again because it was cheap and good but I don't think I'll go around raving about it and I can certainly live without it. 

The staff is made up of teenagers who could use a little burst of enthusiasm but they got the job done.
name: Bridgette

text:
Update: Dear Crafty Soul, you really broke my heart today. For months after I discovered ya'll in my initial review I ordered solely from you because I love your food. I took a bit of a break recently and had a craving for some soul food today and went to what I thought was a reliable source for some. The crab cakes were full of shells and inedible. The potato salad had way too much vinegar in them and the while extremely tender the meat way under seasoned. I am highly disappointed. 

Original:
Ordered food for the first time through UberEats and it was very good. Had the Whiting platter with Shrimp Mac and cheese and collard greens. Everything was seasoned well but not over seasoned and for $11 the price was very reasonable for the portions provided.
name: Marchella

text:
I used to work in this area and always passed this place up without wondering what it was. I kept thinking it was Boucherie and not a separate place associated with it. I found this place by reading an Eater New Orleans article, "Where to Eat New Orleans' Best Chicken Wings."

I came here with a friend for a Monday lunch and catch up. There was a good bit of tables outside, but we opted to sit inside. The inside is a lot smaller than it looks from the outside, so plan to sit outside if you have a large group of people. There were menus at the counter and an eager worker to take our order. She was really nice and helped us decide on what we wanted to order. After we ordered, we got our own water cups and picked a spot. After maybe 10 minutes or so, the food comes to our table! Which I thought was pretty fast for the amount of food we had ordered. We ordered 3 different kinds of wings, a meat pie, a spicy pork boudin link, and beef fat fries. Everything was pretty good, but the meat pie really stood out to me. I thought it would be just a regular beef filled meat pie like you would find at Cajun seafood places, but it wasn't. There was a lot of flavor and some heat, which I enjoyed. It was just a tad bit on the salty side. The wings were pretty good, but nothing too amazing in my opinion. 

Overall, nice place to bring a group to eat some good wings on a beautiful day outside. I will return one day to try some different wings and food on the menu.
name: Anthony

text: I have been wanting to come here for several months and finally ended up coming here for my birthday. We chose to do the "Create Your Own 4-Course Tasting" and this was so much fun.  I ended up choosing a salad for my first course, the gnocco frito as my second course, followed by the salmon as my main finished with the cheesecake as the dessert. Even though the portions are smaller for the tasting, it was still a lot of food and the portions were still extremely generous! My significant other ended up getting the burrata, tagliolini, steak and the goat cheese pana cotta. The service was really good and I felt attended to and listened to and the price of the tasting is extremely reasonable! I can't wait to come back again and try more.

text: We had an event with about 100 people and Ilya and The Stone Soup Company team brought the goods with paninis, empanadas, rice + beans and a couple types of salad. Professional catering experience serving our plant based needs. Love your passion for food and life!

text: Cool, fun environment & bar. We really enjoyed our time there. Drinks were good as was the food. Tuna tacos salad, guacamole & chips hit the spot! Our server was friendly & helpful! We bought some nice swim shirts too, check em out.

text: This was a great surprise for us! We came in with no expectations, just looking for something to eat after a busy day of traveling here. We picked this place based on other reviews and showed up with no reservations on a Friday night. We were told it would be a thirty minute wait so we went to the bar and decided to try out their bourbon choices. Wow, we were overwhelmed with the huge selection of choices. If you like whiskey, or even if you don't, this is a great place to try something new. Thankfully the bartender was able to help us find something to fit our taste. We had just gotten our drinks and we told our table was ready. Matt was our server and he walked us through the menu choices and gave his recommendations. We loved our food, it was quick, fresh, cooked to our specifications and tasted fabulous! The fries were homemade style, seasoned and deep fried perfectly. We loved our meal and left feeling like we had been treated to great experience. If you are looking for a variety of drinks, great food, wonderful service, I would highly recommend this place.

text: One of the coolest place I've ever been in my 66 years! Don't pass on the opportunity to go to this truly historic venue!

text: Absolutely horrible. The waiter was pleasant, the hostess kind, seated at 5:25pm left at 6:37 pm. During this time frame six other tables were seated and served multiple dishes. Check it out!

text:
I saw another review from an "Elite" member saying they were hoping for Nashville's noodle scene after visiting this place. It's authentic but not sure it helps the noodle scene. 

It's next to Vandy and the authenticity is there but not sure the students want that. I went on a Monday night at 8pm and there was only one more table sat besides me. 

The broth was great. I got the tomato sirloin with a little spice. The sirloin was fatty and not flavored outside the broth. The noodles were good. Vegetables were fresh. If I came back I'd try a different protein.
name: Wyn

text:
I had a fabulous lunch at Carne today.  It's been my experience that lunches can be quite ordinary but today's meal was spectacular!  The service was wonderful; the food delicious and the servings quite generous......and the dessert, well, there wasn't a crumb left on the plate!
We were very pleased and will certainly be back again.

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. For the price I expected more than this. Also, food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. The whole meal felt kind of uneven.
name: User

text: I would have given two stars but because our server was nice as well as the floor managers I gave 3 stars for trying to improve my experience otherwise the food overall was disappointing.  Worst halibut I've ever had.  Thin and pan fried in too much oil and overcooked. It resembled tilapia and maybe it's the quality of the local fish.  Rice pilaf was bland and mushy with celery and mushrooms. The corn salad was ok, it had the most flavor. Bread and clam chowder was good. This must be a place that you have to order specific items on the menu. I didn't eat mine so they comped our food which shows they care about their restaurant. If there are items on your menu that aren't great it's probably best to remove them.  Less menu items and focusing on making them spectacular is the best way to go.
name: Adriana

text:
Location / atmosphere- We stopped here at around 9 pm on a Saturday night. We waited around 30 minutes, which was not too bad considering the midtown courtyard was so crowded. There are tons of places to sit and things to do outside while you wait, so that was no biggie.  We sat outside on the patio, and really enjoyed it. There was nice people / dog watching in the court yard. 

Service - Jeremy was our waiter. He did a great job. Seemed very busy and was running around a lot, but really knew the menu front to back and was very nice. The hostess greeting and taking us to table was also welcoming. 

Food - The menu has about everything you could want on it, bar food wise. From burgers to pizza to salads to calzones to many different sandwiches. I got the meatball sub, since I was interested to try the sauce with so many Italian options on the menu. It was not bad at all, but it was definitely not the best food I've ever had. The sauce did not have a ton of taste to it on either my sub or another's calzone. That said, I did eat the whole thing, and could not complain too much. Would've liked a little more fries, but the prices are not too bad for the areas. 

Overall - great location, atmosphere, and service, but the food left room to be desired. We will probably go back, since they have so many options on menu to try.
name: Daniel

text:
This is a dreamy place. This is the place where you go when you're on a good date, or the place you take your child to for a special treat, or the place you visit by yourself to just get away, breathe, and treat yourself to something nice. 

One time, one rainy day, I just planted myself here and ate three croissants. Because ... they have great croissants. It was also $1 croissant day, so I only spent $3 (plus whatever it cost for a cup of black coffee)!

I was here once with my husband and we only ordered desserts and tea. It was perfect, because their desserts are wonderful and the tea is sublime. 

They have an outdoor seating area that is great for just sitting and relaxing. 

The parking is kind of atrocious, though. The parking is very limited, so you might have to park a little ways away and walk, but it's totally worth it to dine here.

text: I've had fantastic rib-eye (bone in) here before, and over my lifetime I've eaten butt loads of steak. At tonight's birthday celebration (mine) with the little woman, I had the. Best. Steak. text: Ended up here pretty late, maybe around 9:30, because everything else nearby had a wait. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..

text:
Meal and service were marvelous!

Will definitely be back when in Tucson!!

text: For the price I expected a little more care. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. text:
The Café Patachou on River Crossing Boulevard just off 86th Street on the Indianapolis northside is one of six located in central Indiana. It provides ample convenient parking in a lot right outside the Café door.

The public dining area here is one medium-sized rectangular space with seating for approximately 100 diners at tables and chairs and a few counter stools. The room is clean and well lighted. The east wall comprises floor to ceiling windows providing a view of the parking lot. There are no TVs. Recorded background music plays at a comfortable level conducive to conversation.

On a visit for breakfast just earlier this week I was greeted promptly in a welcoming manner. My server was identified on the receipt as Schaeffer, and she was charmingly cordial and quite attentive throughout without ever being intrusive.

The Café Patachou menu includes omelettes and other egg dishes, fruit and yogurt, toast and grain selections, a variety of specials, sandwiches, salads, soups, and more. There is also a dessert menu, a children's menu, and a choice of cocktails and other beverages. What there is not is any option for biscuits and gravy nor for eggs benedict; odd omissions, I think, for a breakfast/brunch/lunch eatery. The food prices are all quite reasonable, but the cocktail prices are slightly high for the market.

I first ordered a Bloody Mary and it was brought out immediately. I appreciated that it was not overly garnished which seems unfortunately to be a growing trend right now. From the specialties I then ordered the Cuban Breakfast--a fried egg over seasoned black beans and rice with white cheddar, avocado and sour cream, and spinach-jalapeño pesto. The food was presented within five minutes of me ordering.

The fried egg was a fried egg. What can I say. The beans and rice were somewhat bland until I mixed in the spinach-jalapeño pesto (why else was it there) and then they were deliciously tangy.

A random side note is that the Cafe Patachou website currently describes this location as being "in the...area at the intersection of River Crossing Boulevard and 86th street...in between Borders and Champps." In fact there is not a Champps anywhere in sight and there has not been a Borders bookstore anywhere in North America in almost a decade.
name: John

text:
After being forgotten at Le Peep, we went looking for soemwhere to get a quick breakfast. Friday was busy, but it was "date morning"! No kids!!! Everywhere we tried had a long wait or no low carb options. We decided to skip breakfast and just get coffee and found Hot Spot Cafe! We did even know they were here!

From the moment we walked in, the waitress was smiling and helping us. The coffee came fast and was great. The menu was amazing with so many different items that all looked incredible! I loved that gluten free options were available for toast, crepes, French toast, pancakes, and more! The kitchen was happy to swap out fruit with tomatoes and make all of the little changes that I asked for. They were great. 

When the food arrived, it was incredible. Honestly, I haven't had steak that tasted that amazing in a long time! We will be back!!! I am excited to try new things from the menu! 

I highly recommend trying this hidden gem.
name: Crystal

text:
