text: I love this place - our food was delicious, drinks divine, and hospitality was warm.  We had Sunday brunch here, and my favorite was the horchata, followed by the watermelon frozen margaritas!  But the food is delicious as well - the guacamole was some of the best I've had, ceviche fresh and clean, queso divine.  I'll definitely be back with our next trip back to New Orleans!
name: Marylee

text: Food was good but the service we received was not great. We noticed that all the older white customers received great service, with servers/bartenders making conversation and being super friendly with them (we're a younger Hispanic couple). We were ignored most of the time. We had to ask to order each time we wanted something instead of the server coming to us and offering. And about 45 minutes of being there the bartender came by and took the happy hour menu away. So we got the hint to leave. There were many other small details that implied we were not as welcome as some of the other "better off folk" but I won't get into every little thing. So basically, if you're younger and non-white, don't waste your time going here. You won't be treated well.
name: Christine

text: Great little spot in Broad Ripple. My wife and I enjoyed our lunch at this spot. Can't wait to try one of their plate combos. The restuarant was clean and warm on a cold day. Don't be afraid to ask the owner questions about the different menu items. Can't wait to go back and try dessert.
name: Jon

text: Delicious! A first timer... ordered Cheddar Cheese Burger combo. Great Food, Great Price & Great Service! I will definitely be back soon to try other tasty dishes on the menu.
name: Sophia

text:
First time going to this place not too far from my work so walked. Good thing because if you drive not sure where you would park. The inside is nice, plentiful seating and it was a nice day out so with fans on, it was pleasant in the restaurant.  Hopefully they have AC for the hot summer. The woman taking the orders and the chef were pleasant and informative.  Now the menu online is way outdated for pricing although the food seems the same so have included the big boards they have to order from.  They said they were getting paper menus you can take with you soon, they have been ordered.

Now the weird thing is hoagies don't always seem to be available.  When I called the other day they said they had beef and tuna (no turkey) and when I took a chance and went at 11:45 am, the woman initially said they didn't have them at all yet (maybe waiting for ingredients but not a fan of that, when I go to a place and order I want to be able to get what I want) but then the chef said they did so I got exactly what I wanted a small turkey hoagie and small fries which came out to around $7 which is a good deal.  They have a dine in special, any sandwich/fries/drink for $6.  Can't beat that.  My only gripe is they only had american cheese which I am not a big fan of for hoagies.

The hoagie ingredients and bread were fresh (although looks like they gave me wheat bread I assumed would get white) and a decent amount of meat.  So for $4.80 or so well worth it and good enough for me, the large is $8.50.  I did like their steak fries too.

I will go back and try their burger and tenderloin steak sandwich (that should be interesting doesn't sound like cheesesteak but actual steak sandwich) and maybe wings but they have quite a menu.  I know I know, it is a soul food restaurant and I'm getting non-soul food but they Ajay have a good amount of favorable soul food reviews and several good places in Trenton have closed down recently (Latino Americano Pizza and Thomasenas) and need to find a good food place for good simple "American" classics.
name: Chris

text: The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Food was fresh and service was quick. Would return. The service was off and the meal kinda followed that energy. Food was good and came out fast. Nice little spot, decent portions too.
name: User

text: My new hangout!  I enjoy every aspect of Benton Park Cafe!  The food and fun is awesome!!
name: D

text: We used to drive to Bellevue or Green Hills but are so happy to have such great Greek closer to Sylvan Park! The food is fresh and full of flavor and the customer service could not be better! We will definitely be regulars here.
name: Amanda

text:
What a wonderful little find! Apparently, Hattie B's is a Nashville tradition and destination for locals, vacationers and my fellow Gastromaniacs!

After an arduous morning shopping, we found Hattie B's. Actually it was on the bucket list of a close friend who gastronomic prowess I truly respect. We pulled up and there was a line around the building!! Well, a wait in the middle of the day, in the middle of the week and in the middle of February is always a good sign. And so we waited. 50 minutes and 10 degrees of body temperature lost later, we made it inside. So the decor was nothing special but frankly they were set up to quickly, efficiently and comfortably handle a large crowd. We ordered and each chose chicken.

Now this was interesting, southern, mild, medium, hot and insane - we got a taste of both hot and medium, MommaK going for the small medium and me, small - hot. Seems our pal went for both! One pitcher and several napkins later, we were licking our fingers and getting ready for a well earned food coma!

I must say that the food rocked! The sides (for both of us - Mac and cheese with bacon) were also awesome. We really enjoyed! 

Do not go for the ambience, go for fried chicken the way only Nashville could do it! It was worth the wait!
name: Peter

text: They are ALWAYS out of Crazy Bread. Had to wait 12 minutes in the drive through. The service here is absolute s**t. Wish I had an alternative closer. Do NOT recommend.
name: Adam

text: Is it dramatic to say this is the best place ever? Because it is. This place really puts rockledge on the map. The red headed waitress is the best. There's rarely a wait. I've never had a bad meal here. Decently priced. The only con is that they don't delivery but I'm kinda glad they don't because I would order too much.
name: Sam

text: We were early for our reservation, but were happily seated right away.  We were originally seated near the front bar upstairs, but too noisy,  They gladly moved us to the rear bar with a view of the river.  Service was a little slow for some reason, but food was great.  We took an order of Bananas Foster to go and were shocked at the serving size.  It could have easily served 4 people.  We didn't complain.
name: Douglas

text:
"That you liked Pina Coladas, and getting caught in the rain. And the feel of the ocean, and the taste of champagne"

A little background on me...Im a 38 year old single father of a 10 year old pregnancy scare.

This review is going to be slightly different. I really like Amigo Joes. Its cost effective, fast, good and their staff is really nice. 4 out of 5. Id give it 5 stars but that would be biased.

Amigo Joes queso is awesome. It makes me feel like a man again. Plus their chips have a way of making me forget that there is no future. Ive peaked both mentally and physically and the next few decades will be a study in heart disease and short, fruitless relationships with 3-5 mentally unstable women.

Just so they remain anonymous, ill use initials and aliases. Guest one (G.C.) will be referred to as "Cheech" and Guest two (A.A.R.O.N.J.O.H.N.S.O.N.) will be "Chong".

Aside from me dumping a heaping teaspoon of sour cream on my belly somehow in between the buttons of my shirt, my meal was great.

Both Cheech & Chong are 1%ers used to very high end establishments where the food is served on naked himalayan women. Amigo joes is not that.  Its here for us 99%ers that dont know or even care what gluten is. They have sombreros. Nuff said.

Cheech had never been there before and looked terrified. He ordered chicken fajitas and remarked that it was good, even though he only ate 10% of the meal. He didnt touch the queso, which is a major deduction in regards to stars. He gets uneasy around us flyover fattys so ill cut him some slack...I give him 2 out of 5 stars.

Chong is a walking black hole of cherubic social awkardness. His approach to queso is to dip the chip, then let the excess cheese drip onto his basket of chips...then eat them. Only a serial killer would do that. His main conversation starter was "look at that mural. why is the mariachi band in the ocean?" Clearly the wall mural was depicting a medly of Mexican images that make you feel like youre on the beach on the other side of the wall. He ate at least 50% of his tacos...I give him 0.5 out of 5 stars.

All in all it was a delightful meal.
name: Andy

text:
What a great dining venue for all special occasions.  We enjoyed the historical and cultural atmosphere of this restaurant.  The food was so amazing, not only was the presentation very impressive, everything we had melted in our mouths like butter.  

French bread, lobster croquet, seafood casserole, ribs tapas, chicken and yellow rice, seafood paella and calamari ---- they were all outstanding! 

Can't wait to travel back to Florida so we can go back to Columbia Restaurant!
name: Giang

text: I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. Not bad for a quick meal. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy.
name: User

text: I just ate here a with a coworker and the service was great. I think they must train all of their servers in the South. Because they're always extremely pleasant and overly friendly and familiar. Like your favorite Auntie.  It's hard to mess up eggs and pancakes, so the food is always good but what I really enjoy is the "down-home" service.
name: John

text:
Had dinner here a few nights ago . First time there . Place had a cool vibe and we liked the southern themed menu . We ordered the fried green tomatoes and pimento cheese for starters . The green tomatoes were ok. The breading was too crumbly and didn't adhere to the tomato properly. Pimento cheese dip was ok as well. I'd say it was more cheese dip than pimento cheese but was still ok. 

For dinner I had the fried chicken with collard greens and a side of grits , my wife had the cod tacos and a Cesar salad . The chicken was well seasoned and fried perfectly no complaints at all other than I wanted another piece lol. 
Collard greens were a bit of a let down . I'm from the south and am particular about my greens and there were def. "northern" greens ‍. Grits were just meh,for the same reason as the greens. 

Wife loved the cod tacos and salad . Service was great and the place was clean . We were promptly seated at our designated reservation time. Nothing was bad tbh it just didn't have enough soul in it in my opinion. Wife wants to try their brunch menu so maybe we'll give it another go.
name: Philly

text: So I know that Frankie's Fellini Cafe is a local BYOB favorite which is why it pains my soul to write this review especially since the staff, waiters, and hostess are so incredibly nice and inviting to the point that they make you feel like family and you want to make them a part of your family as well. With that said we got the Penne Fellini and Stuffed Chicken Breast all which lacked any flavor. Unfortunately I don't see myself going back to this place.

text: Worth a 30 minute wait.  Great place to meet people. No one in line near me had been before. Chicken was spicy aka "hot" and moist but not greasy. Tried three sides and all were ok but pimento mac and cheese was the best.

text: Came in today to grab a quick bite to eat. Staff is super friendly and helped get my food to me quickly. Glad we stopped in :)

text: Decent Chinese food. Fast, cheap, and satisfies the craving for the most part. I've eaten here 4 times and I've learned to stay away from the fried entrees because there just never any meat I them, just breading. The best dish I've had was the garlic chicken. Huge portion and really good.

text: This is probably the best pizza I've ever had. Like actually. I came with my husband and we had a great time. The restaurant has great vibes, great music, and very great service. Highly recommend!:)

text: Food was delish. I recommend the gumbo.  The roux base was perfect and all the flavors blended well.  My husband had the bbq chicken and he said it's the way bbq chicken is supposed to be.  Loved this place.   The service was fast and good.  Not rushed but our waitress Sam was there whenever we needed her

text: Absolutely one of the best sushi places in Indy! A very inviting and comfortable interior with plenty of cozy seating and excellent servers. You can even see some of your food being prepared at the counter! Difficult to find parking on weekend nights but definitely worth the hassle.

text: I've heard a lot of good things about this place, so I finally got around to trying it out myself. I got the fried avocado and Korean BBQ cauliflower tacos. One word: AMAZING. I am really picky with tacos because I love authentic Mexican tacos. It's hard to find quality ones unless you are at an actual Mexican restaurant (or in Texas), but I was SO impressed! Both tacos were so tasty. I am big on the cauliflower kick and how versatile they are. The Korean BBQ cauliflower gave me BBQ chicken vibes with honey flavoring and a little spiciness. I think IF I had to pick my favorite out of the two, it would win. BUT, you cannot go wrong with avocado. I will definitely be back and I think everyone should give it a try! I'll have to try the frozen margs next time!!

text:
Great attentive service from Brandi!
Backed up by some of the best Prime Rib in the area! Outstanding sides and atmosphere.

text: We were in Tampa for the night because we were cruising out of this port. We decided on Columbia restaurant for dinner and we were not disappointed! The building is beautiful with many historic attributes. The service was phenomenal and the food was very fresh and authentic. Everything was spectacular and I have no complaints! The Jesse Gonzalez (shrimp stuffed with crab meat) was excellent!

text: Honestly I think my dog likes this place more than my husband and I, but it's pup friendly and the food is pretty good! The best part is the margs (which are super strong) and the fact that you can rent a paddle boat and bring your pup for the ride. Definitely recommend for a date or just for a fun afternoon in forest park.

text: We decided to try this restaurant because a realtor recommended it to us. Well...by the looks from outside, I was pleasantly surprised when we entered this restaurant and the decor was pretty neat! The wait staff was very friendly and welcoming!  My husband ordered a breakfast burrito and he loved it! I ordered traditional breakfast and everything tasted freshly made and my daughter ordered lunch, chicken fried chicken and mash potatoes and the Gravy was very creamy and tasty and the breading was delicious and crispy but not oily, we all tasted it because she was raving over it. The veggies were also delicious and they had some seasoning that made them even tastier! Needless to say we are definitely are coming back! The coffee was also delicious and our waitress was very attentive and always refilling our coffees! We ordered pancakes and they were good and they serve desserts but we were too full for desserts, so we will have to keep that in mind next time we come back.

The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. text:
Place is located in a small strip mall surrounded by more shops. Upon entering they have marinating food for purchase as well as many Indian sweets. For a new business, I didn't receive a very warm welcome. I think they could work on their customer service skills, even though I was just picking up an order. 

When I opened my food I was delighted to see a lot of naan. The quantity of one order varies from restaurant to restaurant so I always order two just to be safe. This place doesn't skimp on naan. I ordered two garlic, however, I received one garlic and one regular. I was surprised to see quite a large container of Shahi Paneer but when I opened it, it was mostly just sauce with barely any paneer; luckily I have lots of naan. I asked for mild spice but the food had quite a kick. I would be afraid to order the spicy option! Unlike most places, they leave the spices in the sauce (think chai latte spices) which are unpleasant to chew on when enjoying your food. 

Overall, I won't rush back to this place considering there are many better options around the city.
name: Randi

text:
Never miss out when in the Boise area! Full espresso bar, fresh specialties & killer jams!
Omelettes, eggs, benedicts, cakes, crepes - everything is yumm!
name: Jim

text: This place was absolutely amazing.  The scenic view was incredible, the food was delicious and the service spectacular.  My girlfriend took me here for my birthday for a nice dinner and our server Wanda did an amazing job making our experience perfect.  We would definitely recommend and return.
name: Rob

text: Impressed!  Great place to dine when attending a show at TPAC but plan ahead by making reservations.  Interesting menu and attentive service.  Large portions, tasty cocktails--yum!  Wish I had room for dessert...But the icing on the cake is the atmosphere! I love the vintage vibe and the live entertainment in the ballroom downstairs.  Will definitely be back.
name: Tiffany

text:
I was so excited to see a Puerto Rican place open nearby that I could not wait to try it. I know good Rican food...and unfortunately this was not it. I wanted to give it 2.5 stars because the place seemed clean and the servers were friendly, but not halves on yelp, so 3 it is. 

This place has been open only about 2 weeks so I expect and hope that it will get better. The wait was pretty long for our food, but again I expected that with it being a new place and them getting into their groove. I ordered the stuffed chicken breast (stuffed with sweet plantains and cheese) with rice and beans. The chicken was good, but could have used some more seasoning. It was however the best part of the meal.  The rice was bland and too al dente, the beans needed a lot of seasoning too. My fiancée had the mofongo with churrasco (skirt steak). They didn't ask how we wanted the steak cooked so it came out almost well done and with -again - barely enough flavor. It was also a very small piece of meat (maybe 3 x 5), but I guess for $13.99 it's not too bad.  The mofongo was just okay - definitely could have benefited from more seasoning and garlic and DEFINITELY needed a sauce with it. Overall - I was not happy with the food at all and it was not worth the wait. I wouldn't rush back anytime soon. Maybe we will try it again in a few months - if it's still there.
name: Liliana

text:
We decided to try Nada as out of towners passing through on a Monday around 530p. Even sitting at the bar the place was busy but we got a spot to watch the drink making action.

We had the mex'orean fried chicken, pork belly taco, mu shu taco, avocado taco, cucumber salad, chile-mango cocktail, and the sangria roja. The texture of the fried chicken was quite memorable and I enjoyed the flavor of the sauce and the fact that the sauce was served on the side so it didnt arrive soggy but perfectly crispy. The tacos and cocktails were good but were missing something but I'm not quite sure what. The cocktails come from a tap whoch means they're mostly premade so if allergies or customizing is important to you, I'm not sure how much of an option that it. 

The interior was beautiful, noise level was fine, and service wasnt bad although the bar staff were visibly rushed and likely under staffed when its full. Overall I enjoyed our dinner but I would probably try another place if I ever make it back to the area.
name: Heather

text: When you want a more personalized pizza and want it decently fast, MOD Pizza is the place to go. It is following the popular trend restaurants are taking where you walk down the line and have the associates add what you want as you go.  The options available are nice and they have a nice variety of toppings. For my pizza I got the traditional red sauce - which is a standard sauce.  The flavor of it did not blow me away, but considering the set up of the restaurant, makes sense.  They cook the pizza in a wood-fire oven which gives the bottom a nice crust. The cheesy bread is also very good.  You also don't have to pay an exorbitant amount for it. Going for MOD Pizza when you want fast, fairly good pizza, this is the place to go.
name: Paige

Seating is a bit limited might have to share a table like my family did.  I recommend the southern greens as one of your sides.
name: Logan

text: I live right up the street from here, and thought I should give it a try. I love saint charles. I have lived here my whole life. This is one of those "troubled spots" in saint charles that whatever establishment goes up seems to have trouble staying. So when I saw this restaurant I was hesitant to try it. BUT, I love new places, and food so I figured, why not. Now, I did order out, which as we all know means things aren't going to be the best, but it was my only choice given I have three kids and do not want to spend a week night in a restaurant. Needless to say, my standards and expectations were already set lower. So, I had my wife go and pick up 30 wings, and two caesar salads for the family. They gave us four sauces(we ordered 7, not including the ranch), and no dressing for the salads. Not ok, so I call them, ask for all the sauces we were charged for, and that I would be up in a few minutes. When I arrived, no one was at the front podium, and I had to wait at the bar for a staff member to even acknowledge my presence(which they did not, I actually had to call a bartender over to me), as I was waiting for the new person to retrieve my sauces I waited and spoke to another customer. They  had gotten her order wrong as well. Another employee handed me my sauces, I opened them, and realized they were still missing several. I hail another employee, and they said, "ok, I'm sorry, I'm new and don't know much, let me grab my manager." Here comes a man, not more than 22 years old saying he didn't know the other sauces were on there. You absolutely did, because I had you pull up my receipt prior to me being there. Long LONG story short, this place is not going to make it either. Go elsewhere, people. You'd have better service and quality going to KFC. Better yet, mcdonalds has better quality chicken nuggets and service. This place isn't going to last long. But hey! Get drunk on over priced cheap vodka and you just might think this place is it. Go elsewhere.
name: Raquel

text: Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Probably not coming back. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..

text: Overall, one of my favorite restaurants right now. I wish I could eat everything on the menu. Their fried rice is the best I've ever had and their sushi is to die for. Wonton soup is a must, as well as their Crab Rangoon. Very tasty food, and if you go, you have to ask for Kory. He's one of the best waiters I've ever had! Very friendly and very efficient. He always has a smile on his face. The only downside is that some of the other waitresses like to stare and make it obvious that they're talking about you. It makes the experience a bit uncomfortable but otherwise, this place is amazing. Best Japanese food around!

We were excited to see they are now open for breakfast. Parking can get bad, so we recommend arriving early. Excellent views, right on the water.

text:
I am overjoyed because my husband has decided that we should go out to brunch once a month.  Boundary was the choice this time.  Where I loved going to Boundary for dinner, I was really disappointed in their brunch.  Brunch is served from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.  My suggestion is to make reservations if you can.  We had reservations at 10:15 a.m. and the place was pretty well filled up.  Parking can also be a problem.

I did not look at it but apparently they have a extensive make your own  Bloody Mary bar.  The girl sitting next to me came back with her drink and it looked like she had an entire meal on top of it.  Anyway, he ordered the French toast with a side of bacon, and I ordered Joan's classic eggs benedict.  He said his French toast was very sweet because of honey on it and would have preferred powdered sugar sprinkled on it.  He raved about the bacon and how thick it was.

Now onto my Joan's classic eggs benedict the operative word being classic.  On the menu it said it was "Canadian bacon, English muffin, poached eggs and hollandaise sauce."  I really do not think that that day there was Canadian bacon with it.  It seemed like it was thinly sliced ham with a strong smoke flavor to it which changed the entire dish.  I really wanted grits but changed my mind when I found out they were cheese grits so I went with the potato hash.  My potato hash was a few new potatoes that had been cooked and smashed a little with a fork.  What a disappointment they were.  Well, really I was disappointed in my entire meal.

Would I come back here?  Not for brunch. There are too many different places out there that serve brunch. I'll see you in the funny pages.
name: Joan

text:
This Roy Roger's site is located within a New Jersey rest area food court. There are various menu readily available for customers to retrieve on their own. text:
Four of us walked in on a Saturday night and were asked to wait while they set up our table. It felt like it was 80 degrees in the restaurant, but seemed relatively packed so we powered through. Anything to convince ourselves Doylestown will eventually have one decent restaurant that isn't so expensive you have to refi your mortgage. After about 5 minutes and a little confusion we sat down. 10 mins later we were told the specials- but no menus were provided. 20 mins in - we had menus. Let's do this!

The wait staff was hilarious, which is great if it's Amateur Night at the Apollo, not so much when it's 7:30 and you just want some din din.

We ordered some apps- hummus, babaganoush (which the waiter responded with "ew!" when we ordered it) some other dips, grilled octopus and fried calamari.

The apps come. First off, they only gave us 4-5 pita pieces for $20 worth of dips. Secondly, every dip taste like paste. No salt. No lemon. No Garlic, all I tasted was Elmer's. The grilled octopus was decent, however, the fried calamari was so overcooked I tried to pick one up with a fork and it disintegrated into a crushed Frito, which reminded me of the turkey in National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation. 

Our entrees come out. My husband ordered a lamb gyro- out came a falafel for him. The wait staff tried to correct it, but we were already ready to eat. I also ordered a falafel gyro and well again- tasted like paste. The tomatoes in the wrap were cherry tomatoes. In the height of jersey tomato season if you choose to put cherry tomatoes in a dish- I cannot trust you. The fries were really good, but we only got ~7. We order dessert as one final save. Baklava and some pudding Baklava things. 

The baklava was the worst I've ever had and I've had a lot. The pudding thing- again paste. I kept taking bites praying in my head and trying to convince myself it wasn't as bad as it was, but it was bad. Real bad. 

The bill comes and it was $130 (no drinks- BYOB)- and I was shocked. This is food truck style fast food and again Doylestown expects us to pay 4 times what it's worth. 

As we were packing up yo go, defeated by yet another overpriced bad tasting restaurant in Doylestown, the waiter says jokingly "you're still here?" 

Yes, unfortunately.
name: Elle

text:
I've been here three times already and enjoyed every experience. Each visit had a few hits and misses, but overall this is one of my top sushi spots. Location can be sort of ducked off as it's connected to a big building and parking can be a pain so keep that in mind. 

I'll mainly focus on my visit tonight. I made a reservation for my birthday for 4, but we ended up having 5. I called and they gladly changed it and confirmed my reservation. They were very busy upon arrival. The whole restaurant was packed and if you didn't have a reservation, I'm not sure there was any open table besides maybe the bar. Our server bought out water for everyone already since one of the guest arrived first. We all got there within the next 5 minutes and ordered drinks and our food. 

Now to what we ordered, we got the snow crab salad, ika fries, spicy edamame, baked salmon. For rolls we chose spicy tuna roll, crunchy roll, rock and roll, black and gold and lastly tiger tail roll. I enjoyed the spicy edamame and baked salmon was the BEST. I wish the ika fries were fried crispier and didn't taste so much like a potato chip. Snow crab salad is average. All the rolls were good, but our fave was the black and gold! It's very rich so sharing was a good idea. I don't think I'd be able to take on a whole roll. Our server was a bit MIA. We were checked on once and that's it. Never got any water refills, no new side plates even though we were offered some after eating apps. No big deal.. I heard our server had a large party. I get when it's busy and things can get a bit overwhelming. After we waited for a while, we got the attention of a manager who helped clear our table and bought out a birthday dessert for me. Very thoughtful and tasty! It comes with vanilla mochi, some fresh fruit for garnish, chocolate writing "happy birthday" and pocky sticks. I've tried other things on the menu before and they've all been good. 

Overall, I've been well taken care of on both my birthday visits. The food is good, atmosphere is a bit upscale but still remains casual. I like how there's many unique menu items you can try. It may seem a bit pricier, but hey if I'm paying for good food why not? I'll be back and maybe tsunami may be my birthday tradition!

text:
Run, don't walk, to this outstanding St Louis restaurant.   If you go early you can  get a spot at the bar-- otherwise make a reservation.   The menu is small.  The seating is limited.   It's worth the wait to get a spot.   

I went with a friend early on a Saturday eve and we had a fantastic time.  Great service (thanks Adam!) and delightful food.   After ordering our drinks we were presented with scallion cakes-think small crispy pancakes- accompanied by a savory dipping sauce.   We then had spring rolls, perfectly crisp, and carpaccio with tiny shallot rings and capers.   Tart and mineral.   

For the second course we both decided on the heirloom tomato and white peach salad with fresh herbs.  Usually I'm hesitant to order tomatoes in a restaurant as they are often refrigerated and mealy.   Not the case here.   These were a lovely balance of sweet acidity.   

Main courses:   Short ribs with fingerlings and swordfish with vibrant olives and cherry tomatoes.  My friend loved the beef-- savory with a sauce served tableside, and my fish was a just right portion.   My only tiny complaint might be that several of the mains seemed to come with the fingerling side.   They were well prepared, just a wee bit boring in comparison to the rest of the meal.  

Lastly, dessert.    The creme brûlée was to die for-- and certainly a shareable portion size.   I had a zingy Chilean coffee cocktail which was a lively combination of spice heat and sweet.   I am going to have to hunt down the liquor used in the drink-- Adam wrote it down for me.   I'm envisioning a fantastic Bloody Mary as a possible use for it.  

But I digress.   Please.  Go.   The owner, Zoe Robinson, is a well known local restauranteur-- and here fine dining know-how is evident.  The moody black interior is dramatic, set off by large scale abstract black and white artwork.  This was an exceptional experience and while I'd kinda like to keep this one to myself... I can't.  I'll be back again very soon!
name: Carrie

text:
Visiting in Nashville and wanted to try a good hot dog.  This place was on a couple of "must eat" hot dog lists and I picked Cori's based on their online menu.  So I order two, one with mustard, chili, and onions: the second with mustard and sauerkraut.  The hot dogs are 4/1 skinless all beef and the taste reminded me of jumbo Fischer's Meats which I have eaten before.  To me, the first thing that makes a good hot dog is that it should be delicious on it's own with just a roll and no condiments.  This was not one of those dogs as it had a mostly mushy mild beef taste. Could not taste the spices, no garlic, onion or anything else.  Just bland.  The mustard is Heinz yellow (not deli) and the chili tasted like it was from an institutional supplier. 
Two good things were the New England style buns baked fresh and toasted. (Wish they were butter toasted).  Secondly, the french fries are hand cut, unpeeled and then cooked once.  Good taste and nice mix of crispy and limp.
If Cori's changed their hot dog to a better quality one, it would then be "the"  five star place for hot dogs in Nashville but for now I can do no more than two stars.

text:
What a great first experience! I came here Monday night 11/12 to celebrate mine and my sister's birthday with family. Things started slow, but due to the weather, we might have been the only table they had all night. I work in the industry myself so I am patient and understanding. However, things quickly got back in gear. 
The vibe is warm and welcoming when you walk in and they have several tv's playing music videos or other channels on the wall. There is a huge bar along the side wall, however they haven't been granted their liquor license just yet (get your act together, St. Louis Hills!!) We chose to sit at a table as opposed to the large floor seating area with cushions, but it sure did look cozy! The woman working that night was kind enough to offer suggestions for sharing, but since my sister is a vegetarian we had to go a different route. *The only issues I had with the menu was that there were two.. half of ours had prices scratched out and changed and the others didn't, and the menu with photos had items that were not on the main menu. This made things confusing, but I understand getting menus printed over and over to fix every detail isn't feasible, and they will have the whole thing straightened out soon enough. There also weren't a lot of vegetarian options for my sister, but again, I understand a new restaurant needs time to figure itself out and find its groove..* We ended up starting with an order of sambosa and falafel. Both were delicious! For the main course we ordered the Afghani mantu (dumplings), chicken tikka masala, and mixed grill (for which we subbed an extra beef skewer, as they were currently out of lamb skewer). Everything was SOO GOOD!!!! The kind gentleman that sat us also offered us desserts for our birthday, which were a type of rice flour pudding with walnuts. Also delicious!!!! The finishing touch was that they played happy birthday for us on the tv at the end  Thank you all for putting the personal touches on for our birthdays! I am so excited for leftovers, and can't wait for my next visit!! Hope to become a regular

text: So, this is unfortunately long.  But I strive to be honest and helpful in my reviews.  The Omni is perfectly located in the heart of downtown Nashville and strives to be a business/conference destination.  To this end they achieve their goal.  To add to their appeal their facility backs up to the Country Music Hall of Fame, and contains an amazing foodie Restuarant (Kitchen Notes), a respectable upscale steakhouse (Bob's Steak and Chop House), shopping, a Spa, a well stocked modern work out facility, as well as an abundance of conference facilities.  Their lobby is modern, efficient and luxurious.  Their staff helpful and polite.  So why not 5 stars?  Well it came down to the little things, and mostly the room.  The bed was lump and lacked support.  When we asked if there was something that could be done, they politely and efficiently brought us a thick piece of plywood to put under the mattress, which surprisingly helped.  Its still a poor mattress nonetheless.  The pillows are a disaster for me personally, others might find unsupportive overly soft pillows that require stacking 3 of them to make 1 normal pillow a minor thing.  Again, some of this is personal preference obviously.  The shower water temperature control was a total mystery.  While water pressure was terrific, unlike many places I have stayed, trying to control the incredibly touchy water temperature required dancing in and out of the water stream to avoid getting alternatively scalded or frozen.  It was miserable.  Perhaps this is just my misfortune and the other rooms dont share this problem.  The rooms while mostly modern in appearance are a little tired, with plugs on the night stand not functioning and the room lighting at night just too dim.  I realize it may appear that I am being picky and that its uncommon to have a perfect stay, but if you want 5 stars, you have to do better.  All in all, its location and other amenities make the small stuff much less noticeable.  Enjoy your time in Nashville.
name: Raleigh

text:
I'm an easy person to please when it comes to pizza, trust me. So when the office decided on pizza for lunch today, I thought it would be a safe choice! Unknowingly, my coworkers and I called into what would be the worst experience in memory.

Pizza: The pizza is nothing special and the employees were light handed with toppings. The crust came out chewy (not a bad thing) but for some reason felt thick and quite heavy. After a while, it was akin to chewing rubber or gum. Flavor was acceptable, but even 30 minutes later, I don't remember much of it. Pretty unremarkable.

Service: This is where Persona lost me and definitely lost any chance keeping my office's business. We called in at 11:55  ordering 2 pizzas (one with split toppings), and 3 salads. Upon trying to order, the person on the other line had no idea how to log a pizza with topping on only half the pie. That's fine, maybe that person is new. One our order was placed, we were quoted a wait time of 10-15 minutes before our pizza was ready. Giving them more of a time cushion, we came in after 20 minutes (12:15). Entering, my coworker and I were not greeted with a hello or welcome, but rather just stared at. Worse yet, when saying that we were there for pick up, our pie wasn't ready and were told to wait another 5 minutes. 5 Minutes? Try waiting another 15 minutes. 

More than anything, it seemed that they had forgotten our order and were making fresh ones when we got in. So what was to point of even calling in?

When asking for paper plates and plastic utensils, we were informed that they were out and not offered an alternative at all. (Thankfully my office had extra plates)

Perhaps the biggest offense today was in the treatment of the customers by the staff. While I know some people have more unique names and may raise an eyebrow, there was absolutely no reason why one of their team members should have snickered and laughed when reading my coworker's name. Who cares what your opinion is, or how funny might be to you? Respect the professional courtesy between business and clients. You don't have to make a side comment to your coworker, especially when we are in ear shot of you. 


Overall, I don't see a way that I'd want to come back here. My office spent over $50 here, for a priceless, terrible experience. The pizza was mediocre, the service was miserable and I'm left with a bad taste in my mouth that isn't marinara. I'd give this place negative stars if I could.

I am not at all surprised by the fact that this place is empty every single time I walk by. It's only fitting with this kind of service and food. 

Your best bet for pizza in this town are definitely Gio's for those delicious NY slices or, if you feel like build your own, Blaze at 5 points.

I found Superior Seafood while in New Orleans thanks to a tip from our Uber driver, we had talked about Oysters and the ones I had the night before when the Uber driver immediately suggested going to Superior for fifty cent raw oysters and three dollar beers/wine for happy hour. 
 Happy hour covers the entire restaurant not just the bar, which is nice. 

My girlfriend and I took the streetcar to Superior from our Air BnB, the restaurant is right across from the tracks.  We arrived around 4:30 and were greeted by our server, I ordered a dozen raw oysters and a glass of house white to start while my girlfriend (doesn't eat seafood) ordered the spinach artichoke dip- not on happy hour menu. 

We were served a loaf of fresh bread with soft butter to start and it was good, however the main reason I came was for the Oysters. Once they arrived and I was already half way through I decided to order a dozen more. These were really good oysters, nice and plump and good taste, plus when served with cocktail, horseradish and crackers hit the spot for me. 

When we return to New Orleans I will definitely hit up Superior for a few dozen more of those plump delicious oysters.
name: Bill

text:
Every time I come here, either in person or to go, I have a lovely experience. The food is fresh and delicious, there are tons of options to suit different dietary preferences, and the servers are charming and engaging. 

Highly recommended: Goat cheese and mushroom omelette; side of bacon; for lunch, I like the turkey avocado tartine and a cup of gazpacho (seasonal). My better half is fond of the tuna nicoise.

We were given a free dessert to write a review, but we come here a lot and I had only not reviewed it because I'm lazy.
name: Lauren

text:
After all of the anticipation, South definitely did not disappoint. I was hooked by the fact the have live Jazz. And usually where the Jazz leads the blues follows.


The service itself was attentive and welcoming. The Manger himself was very much involved in servicing the floor. We had a warm welcoming upon our arrival and were well attended to through out our dining experience. I wanted to make sure our tête-à-tête was perfect, this was our first time in Philadelphia. We started off with the Corn bread; it was the best corn bread I have ever had in my life. Crispy outline and a rich soft texture. My S/O had the wood roasted salmon, unfortunately they were out of cabbage but instead they served it with broccolini . I went with the wood grilled Chicken, and it was great but I do have to admit that my favorite part of the dish were the carrots. Not too soft. We ended up being treated to a complimentary desert, and what better way to end the night then with the Nola style beignets! 

All around it was a culinary experience for the books. My hat is off, this was a bang for my buck. Until next time.
name: Bia

text:
I ate here tonight. Got food to go. Got back to the hotel with no fork or napkins, anything to eat with. The fresh baked garlic bread that I paid extra for was nothing but cold white sliced bread, never even toasted smeared with cold oil and a dash of Italian herbs. They also didn't give me the side of marinara for the "fresh baked garlic bread". It's ok, it wasn't edible. 

Fettuccine alfredo was just okay, needed basic things like salt and pepper. The Greek salad was just ok too. Wouldn't eat there again. Maybe their pizza is better.
name: Misty

text: This restaurant is situated right across from Eastern State Penitentiary. It is a perfect location for you and your friends to grab drinks and dinners while waiting for your Terror Behind the Walls tour. My friends and I ordered a few drinks while we waited. Their hot cider was perfect for the fall weather. Highly recommended!
name: ThùyDung

text:
And by here for lunch and tried the:

1. Deviled eggs
2. Bacon cheeseburger with onion rings added and no bread 

The burger was a good decent burger. The side salad I didn't care for. I asked for ranch with my fries and have to say I really hated the ranch. It tasted like bottled ranch from a store. If the ranch was fresh it would make a huge difference. I don't go to a restaurant to eat things That taste like store products. I also had the deviled eggs which were a little too Smokey flavored and very very cold, but that could be just me personally since people I was with though they were decent . 
The staff and manager are on point and so genuinely friendly which made the not so good meal bearable . 

Overall, I wouldn't come back. The people who work there are great, but the food is definitely lacking .
name: Willow

text:
Appears new owners are in place as we haven't been there in a few years. We sat for dinner and it was very hot and uncomfortable since the ac cannot cool the place because the kitchen and pizza oven is right out front.
My salad was good but my wife's quesadilla was really bad. They initially messed up the order and had to remake. The chicken had some strange spice on it and way too much cheese. Very messy and not enjoyable. 
We had to go orders and the cook who messed up my wife's meal places the cold sandwich on the bottom and the hot meal on top of it, not very bright.
Not rushing to go back.
name: Dave

text:
Don't let the long line scare you away! Yes we waited for an hour to eat here but hear me out. The hype is real. The wait is worth it! 

If you are visiting for the weekend like we were, you have no choice but to wait. But if you are here during the week, I don't think the wait is as long so it really depends and you have to be patient. It was sorta raining that day but the place provides umbrella for the patrons waiting so that was really nice of them. They give you the menus while you are waiting so you can order once you get inside. We got inside and knew what to order. Our ordered were placed then we were seated. A very efficient service I would say.

We ordered sweet tea, bonuts, east nasty, and shrimp and grits. All are very delicious! The bonuts are to die for, you MUST order them especially after waiting that long, girl you deserve it! East nasty was yummy as well, it's chicken thighs deep fried to perfection in between a biscuit with gravy and eggs. Omg it was heaven. A very big portion so beware small stomachs! The shrimp and grits was amazing as well! This place lived up to the hype.

I do not regret waiting an hour in line. The sweet tea was perfect and I'm going to come back here again whenever I find myself in Nashville and get 2 orders of bonuts to myself! Biscuit Love you were amazing to us!
name: Aggie

text: Was excited about eating here and they turned us away. Said they decided to close early tonight.
name: Brooke

text: This was my first time in Philadelphia. This place was recommended to us by a local resident. I'm so glad we came here. The cheesesteak was amazing! It was accompanied by cheese fries. I would highly recommend this place to anyone.
name: Jennifer

text:
So excited to have found a Schlotzsky's in Tucson, fairly close to my home!  The big draw for me is the bread used for The Original...so delicious! 
The  employee at the window was very courteous and friendly, the wait time at the window was acceptable, and the Original sandwich with one exception) was delicious, just like I remember from younger days. The exception is that I asked for no onion, which was confirmed twice by the order taker, but when I got the sandwich it was loaded with onion.  Onions (and other foods) make me very ill, so the single most important thing for me when ordering food is that I get what I ask for. 
I do recommend the food at Schlotzsky's however be aware and check your food if you ask for special consideration.
name: Delores

text: I checked out the Tarpon Tavern Wednesday deal with some friends and we all enjoyed our meals! 39 cent wings + $4 Tito's & Sprite was the perfect combo. My Shrimp Po' Boy was tasty because of the dang dang shrimp...I loved the sauce, but could've done without the sandwich bun. The server great & I wish I could remember his name to give him a shout out because he was accommodating and took a great group photo for us. I'll be back soon for sure!
name: Raven

text: I love this place with my whole heart and have been coming since it opened! Their menu is so accommodating, as they've recently added daiya cheese and cauliflower crust for vegan and gluten free customers (in addition to their gluten free crust). The staff is always so helpful and kind. This place just has such a great atmosphere and that's why I keep coming back!
name: Lauren

text: The Zambia Smokehouse was a hit! The smells coming from this restaurant was luring me in like an invisible hook attached to my nose pulling me in. Now on a busy day expect a line but wait because it's worth it. On the day I went the wait was minimum. I had the All Day Dining Meal which allowed us to have one entree and a side or dessert and a drink every hour at one at the designated restaurants throughout the park. (Get this deal its worth it) I ordered the St. Louis Ribs Platter, French Fries , Apple Cobbler. You got at least 5 rib bones smothered in BBQ sauce, the meat was smokey, moist and tender to the bite. The french fries were hot and crispy but they are those kinda fries you better eat them while they are hot or else. The Apple cobbler was sweet . It was ok to me but just note I got a lite caramel drizzle and it was really sweet. I'll pass next time. The menu is full of delicious items like bbq chicken, smoked sausage and brisket. Yes they did have cole slaw but i passed on it. I got great customer service here, the servers were quick and friendly. I got the best Arnold Palmer made here ( Sweet Tea and Lemonade mixed together). I will be back and I suggest you give them a try. Oh yeah if you don't have the meal plan expect to pay $17 on up for your complete meal.
name: Tesha

text: It was crowded but still moved along. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Outdoor seating looked nicer than the inside honestly. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Will be back. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Worth checking out. The whole meal felt kinda uneven. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text:
La Scala's birra is located on the scenic Cooper River with both indoor and outdoor seating. The restaurant itself is classy but with an open, casual feel. I came for a late lunch on Tuesday with my family after my graduation--everyone in my party was in agreement that La Scala's Birra was the perfect low key spot to celebrate such an occasion. 

Service was excellent, portions were large and prices were good. My family ordered a few drinks as well as the ricotta board. The riccota board had lots of ricotta (seriously, way more than you would expect) mixed with honey in a jar and served with crunchy bread. This helped hold us over before the main course and came with plenty to share between my group of 5. For my entree, I opted for the rigatoni vodka. I loved this as it was served with pancetta and sundries tomatoes which really made it exceptional. For those with dietary restrictions,  I had spotted a few GF/vegan options on the dinner menu but not as much on the lunch menu so be sure to ask about that. All around a great experience-I will definitely be back!
name: Madeleine

text: My Burger was very good like a homemade burger. I enjoyed the band as well. Get there early the band stops playing at 8. Also the staff is very courteous. I would visit again.
name: Leslie

text: Loved the onion rings and the Wallbanger wings. Great food. Fun experience. The fresh food and "farm to table" makes a difference.
name: Jan

text:
What a great hidden Jewel this place is. Louis has made a wonderful environment that's casual but not loose. And decorated but not gaudy.
The food is wonderful. The best Italian in South Tampa.
Don't cheat yourself by missing this experience.
name: Marty

text: Had the gyros and hummus this evening oh my what great flavor! Good size gyros! The guys serving were super nice and helpful.  This will be our new go to spot for sure! Would so recommend for sure!!!! Can't wait to go back and try something different!
name: Tina

text:
I really want to love this place and will be giving it another go because of how much I want to love Habanero Grill.  There is nothing better than a good, local, authentic Mexican restaurant and I'm hoping that Habanero Grill is just working out the kinks still. 
It's not a large place, multiple tables and booths were filled when we arrived and by the time we left every table was full so it's obvious that the community is liking it. 
My friends swear by the Habanero Margarita and my husband loved his Habanero Mojito and as my friends say...a place with good alcohol has the potential for greatness! 
I ordered from the traditional Mexican part of the menu and decided on the chimichangas. They weren't great, the chicken was dry, there were no peppers or other additional items in the fried tortilla, just chicken. Not even cheese. The chicken didn't have a lot of flavor either. I don't really remember how the beans and rice were so that says a lot, they were just ok I guess but not memorable. Everyone else at the table ordered from the grill menu and I was jealous! They had steak and shrimp from the grill and it tasted amazing! So much flavor and not a lot of fluff which is what great food is about! 
We also had a bacon and corn shrimp appetizer which was incredible. Hence the reason I'm willing to give it another try, everyone else had a great experience...mine was just not good that night. 
Also, as we sat there the place began filling with smoke from the grill, perhaps the overhead fan wasn't working that night but smoke was coming out of the kitchen pretty heavily. Not great for someone with breathing issues or asthma. I finally had to go out for some fresh air because my eyes were burning and I couldn't breathe any longer. I'm hoping this was just an off night and I look forward to trying it again and updating my review. 
I really think they need to focus on the grill menu based on our experience, everything that came off of it was incredible...no need for the traditional what everyone expects menu items when you have something simple and good.
name: Amy

text: Excellent choice for home cooked breakfast! You must try the seafood omelet and the gator sausage omelet!
name: Catherine

text:
The service, location, atmosphere, food and coffee are all outstanding. The only thing that wasn't outstanding was the portion size of the biscuits and gravy, $8 for one biscuit was pretty weak, they could probably add another without risking the business going under.
However, the raspberry mocha is , so, take that into consideration.
name: Shayna

text: Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. You can tell they care about customer experience here. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. Would absolutely visit again. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text: Very average experience. Their fried pickles are good and cocktails remain dependable, but their main courses need some work. Turkey burger was a bit dry and their fries were unseasoned... but heck, who really cares, you're at a bar right?!
name: Erik

text:
My first feeling was one of disappointment. While waiting to approach the host, the manager (I assume) walked past me and my party to an older white gentleman and immediately started to make conversation. He explained that they would be sure to accommodate him. Needless to say I was shocked and disappointed. Not one time did he acknowledge our family which was ahead of the white family. Once we were finally seated, we were placed in the corner by the speaker which made it difficult for us to have any conversation or really enjoy the company of our party. 
The food was hot and delivered quickly. The overall taste of our food was average- nothing spectacular but certainly not bad. Our waitress was really sweet. And the band was good. I think we would have enjoyed the band more if we weren't so close to the speaker. 
Throughout my duration there I continued to watch the man who I assumed to be the manager; people appeared to be taking cues from him (a middle aged man with black hair, slim build). 
His inability to acknowledge my presence and consider me and my family worthy of engagement suggests to me that I am not welcome there.
name: Destiny

text: Delicious food. The menu has something for everyone. The owner Martin/Metin is friendly and knowledgeable. I'm excited to go back again and try something new.
name: Manez

text: This place was excellent! I had the El Cerdo hash, it was so good. It was just the right about of spicy, hot, and hearty. The coffee was great too. My wife got bacon and it was delicious and thick cut. I would definitely recommend checking this place out.
name: Anthony

text: Had breakfast here and it was really good! Staff was nice but the were extremely busy so they took a min to come back to my table. I will go back!

text: Visiting here from Seattle. Was extremely pleased by the service and quality of drinks for the amazing price! Great friendly bartender, chill environment

The wine was great as well. We met the owners and truly enjoyed our conversation! Looking froward to heading back there soon!

text: Very good about my orders. Employees so nice and always asking if order is correct.  No problems with this location.

This feels like a place where your order choice matters a lot. Food was fresh and service was quick.

The Maui Maui. Glass of wine and a mixed drink -$110 and worth every last penny. Hands down the best food I have eaten, and service was outstanding

text: Their servers look unhappy, and simply do not care. Our food took over an hour. Food was average. The only reason there are two stars, bc their aesthetic and design are lovely. Bad brunch.

text: Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Food was fresh and service was quick. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Pretty smooth experience from start to finish.
name: User

text:
We got the zucchini sticks, grape leaves and falafels. Everything was delish and ready super quick. The staff was friendly. The zucchini sticks were crisp w a nice texture inside. They came with a yogurt dipping sauce that was thick and rich. The grape leaves were $5 and we got a ton of them. Like 8-10 which is unheard of. My son had the falafel and he said it was one of the best he's had. They have Greek music playing which I enjoyed. The decor is bright, clean and colorful. 

We didn't have any but I appreciated the unusual soda flavors: strawberry, grape and pineapple.

The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Not bad for a quick meal. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. It looked better online than it did in person.

Will definitely be back soon!

text: Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The wait felt longer than it should have. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..

text: Gotta say today's morning adventure was perfect because I ran into one of my favorite local food trucks The Blacktop Grill. If your looking for gourmet Sonora style hot dogs, quesadillas, elote etc. with a specialty twist look up The Blacktop Grill. You won't be disappointed. The food is phenomenal with a nice mix of savoury flavors and a punch of spices all together to make the most simple and classic AZ style hot dog or even quesadilla standout. Go follow them on Facebook or Instagram you spot some drool worthy snapshots of all the great stuff they make. Gabe the owner is a great guy with a passion for his food if your not sure what you want - he'll help find you something to try. You hungry yet? Wanna try it for yourself? Go to their Facebook page and see what events and locations they will be at next. I'm not gonna say I told ya so just you're welcome. Haha. Enjoy!!!

Service was descent for a busy airport, food was good.  I had ribs with 3 sides(green beans, slaw and mac n cheese)my wife had a burger (mushroom/swiss)  both pleased with what we ordered. text:
This is a review for the lunch at District Tavern.  Positives - The view is great with a dog park next door, so there is always something nice to look at outside, as well as numerous TVs inside.  I would say the food is average, maybe slightly above average, but nothing special. 

Negatives -  I have been here multiple times during lunch and there has never been more than 1 server.  The food has taken forever each time.  There is no reason lunch for 2 should take over an hour unless you are trying to stretch it out.  I've got to get back to work so I'm not wasting any time here, but I can never get out in less than an hour.  I went back one more time after I hadn't been in months, and nothing has changed.  Looks like I'm back to Maloney's.
name: Hunter

text: Awesome discovery after scouring Clearwater Beach for a decent cup of local coffee. The two people behind the counter were both very helpful and you could tell that they take great pride in making delicious coffee, breakfast items, and baked goods. We will definitely be returning here before leaving the Clearwater Beach area.
name: Matthew

text: I was there, so you don't have to go. About 90 minutes into my 30 minute commute and still not anywhere near home, having skipped lunch and it was happy hour time, I found myself looking at Chili's while standing on City Ave. "Why not?", I thought, having fond memories of a Chili's I used to frequent somewhere else. There were plenty of service people to show me to a table. On the way I was looking at the floor tiles, all of which seemed laid by an apprentice, and they were a bit spotty which I decided to interpret as "rustic". While waiting for my waitress, I had plenty of time to look around, and after a moment I realized what the noise level reminded me of: A German beer hall. Fortunately, there was no ooompahh music playing, but Abba was telling us about the Dancing Queen. After looking around a bit more, I was wondering whether the peak time of Abba might also have been the last time the establishment had been thoroughly cleaned. Oh well. The crooked floor tiles made my table stand unstable and it was rocking, so, while still waiting for the waitress (is that where the name comes from?) I asked the bus boy if he could put something under the one foot of the table to stabilize it. He could not quite figure out under which leg he should put the few napkins he brought, and at some point, not wanting to embarrass him, I said it was fine. I had wanted to stabilize the table so that the plate would not slip around. Turns out, I did not have to worry: The table surface was sticky enough to keep the plates from sliding. Yes, I had ordered in the meantime. At the beginning, I was surprised they did not bring water, but that came soon after I ordered, only they called it "original margarita". The mango ice tea turned out not to be my thing, but that was not Chili's fault. Maybe it would have tasted better in a mug that was not dull and foggy from going through the dishwasher a hundred times too often. At least I hope that was it. Feeling starved, I ordered the happy-hour-priced boneless chicken wings and the fajita plate. This reminded me why I am not a big fan of what some consider fried food. I would suggest to pass on the boneless wings unless you are a friend of mystery meat in a 1/4inch of breading heated to lukewarm in the microwave, just enough that their sogginess was not wet anymore. I am ashamed to say I ate a few of them because I was so hungry. The fajita plate was nondescript, which is a good thing in this context. Well, maybe if the chicken had been as well done as the steak... Anyway, while eating, I had ordered a beer - what could go wrong with a beer? Nothing, the beer was perfectly fine. And the thing that stuck to the glass was fortunately on the outside, so all was well. As long as you paid attention not to cut your lip on the big chip on the rim of the glass. So, my overall experience? Let me say I did not finish all my food, and people who know me will be in shock now. I finally started the 30-minute process of paying for my food. My waitress tried, but somehow all the service personnel had disappeared around the same time the place was filling, so she really struggled to keep up. Not her fault that the little machine on the table showed someone else's bill. Eventually, she brought another one. Evidently, I was two people who had entrees for two with added shrimp. A little while later, I actually got the right bill. And I left in the safe knowledge that I will never have to go there again. Did I complain about things that were amiss? No, not because I am shy or prefer to bitch instead of talking to the manager. But this place was obviously so run down that nobody really seemed to try anymore, and I doubt my complaining would have done any good. So, why am I writing all this when I normally do not review restaurants? Well, I am a public health professional, and that compels me to point out that having the kitchen next to the bathrooms is not a smart architectural strategy for a restaurant. But what makes it worse was that both seemed to be far away from any acceptable hygiene standard. So, I am not expecting fine dining at a Chili's but I also want to not get sick. I am now at home, drinking a stiff bourbon that will kill any potential pathogens. I hope.
name: Stefan

text: The food is fantastic! We got the Chicken and Waffles-to die for-and the Grilled Cheese with the tomato bisque was absolutely heavenly! Hannah, our waitress was both friendly and attentive-was great experience!

text: If you want fresh Cuban food, Latin Twist Cafe is your place in Wesley Chapel.  We started off with being greeted by friendly staff.  We came right after the rush hour for lunch since the tables were in need of cleaning.  The waitress asked us immediately what table we wanted and she cleaned it.  The Cuban Bread came right after we sat down.  The bread was warm and delicious.  Then we ordered empanadas (beef and chicken) along with papas rellenas (stuffed potatoes with beef).  I personally preferred the beef empanada.  Both empanadas had plenty filling.  The papas rellenas were bite size and had good flavor.  (I would have like more meat.). As for dinner, we shared chicharrón de pollo (chicken rind) with yucca.  Yummy for my tummy!  The chicken was crunchy and juicy.  I would highly recommend!
name: Melissa

text:
This review is more for the Take out section. 
Although it is a small room it is worth the wait for a deliciously made sushi. They serve some unique sushi on their menu not like the traditional sushi people normally see, better than Mikado. Plus they have slushies, smoothies, and tea with lychee and/or tapioca my favourite. Menu is moderately pricey but better than the average sushi like Tokyo Express. Parking is large, staff is friendly, atmosphere is semi-cozy in the lobby for take out. No washrooms for the Take out lobby. I have dined in here before and it appears to not have changed too much and is very chilled but can be busy in this area at times, see photos. They do have specials at certain times and days as well.
Recommended for sushi lovers.
If your looking to take someone on a date, this place would be one of my choices.
name: Edwin

text: Chuchitos were the special appetizer the day we went, and they are so delicious they should be on the permanent menu. text:
Disappointing. We've been here several times and the food is very good, but the service this time left such a bad taste in our mouth that it will be the last time.
We ordered drinks plus a dinner to share plus added on meatball and sausage plus an added side of vegetables. The waitress brought us a basket of bread with three thin pieces of bread in it. The small salad came with only lettuce, croutons and one olive. (The next table had that plus tomatoes).
We asked for a bit more bread and eventually we got a basket with six pieces of bread, which is more likely the right size.
Our entree arrived but we had to wait several minutes for another dish so we could split it between us.
After receiving the tab, we gave the waitress a coupon that we had received at the place where we were staying. It was for 10% off one dinner. She refused to take the coupon, saying we had already gotten a discount by splitting a dinner. She also claimed she gave us a discount by not charging for the extra bread.
We dine out several times a week and always split an entree with added sides, and always tip generously.  I guess they just don't want our business and we'll be happy to oblige.

My Nashville friend said they normally get more than 2 with their meal and that the only time they charge $8 (the menu option) is when you just order drinks and want biscuits WITHOUT ordering an entree. Well, for two more biscuits we still had to pay the $8 although we ordered the entree. $4 a biscuit!! After I tried showing the server the picture of the $8 option on my Yelp app, he just brushed it off. He said, "this price was stated on the menu." Yeah, for a basket, not 2 biscuits! Was this a CMA Fest rip-off? Maybe. The pot pie was small for $20, but for the most part good. If we hadn't been tired from driving 2 hours in downtown traffic, we would have spoken to a manager. Instead, we just left after paying. The lesson learned here: don't go to Nashville during CMA Fest. Period. Never again. This review would have gotten a 1 star review if the biscuits weren't so good.

text:
Underwhelmed

Ulele consistently gets good reviews and is extremely busy.  I finally planned far enough ahead to get a reservation.  And...I don't get the buzz.

We started with a couple of cocktails (Dade City Gin & Tonic and Ulele Sunset).  Neither was anything special.  We moved on to appetizers.  These were the highlight of the meal.  The okra fries and charbroiled oysters were both very good.  From there we shared a beet & pear salad--pleasant but quite small.

For entrees we had the Panamanian Sea Bass which was nice, especially the bed of corn and grain.  We also had the New York Strip Steak which was surprisingly bland.  The glass of red wine with the steak was quite nice.  For dessert we had the chocolate torte on a raspberry coulis base.  Again, the coulis (which should have a nice tang) was only sweet and the torte was bland.

With tax and tip we were out $170 for a mediocre dinner.  I won't be heading back.
name: Keith

text: We are here frequently and can't put into words how much we love this place. The food and bar programs are absolutely top-notch; so is the service and management.
