text: I've actually been treated with respect and very nice by the staff at this establishment. Which is sad to say, is always surprising when it happens that way. When people actually practice decency. It is to be applauded. The Vietnamese Pho is simply delicious here. Was my first time ever trying it. I was recovering from a horrible cold, needed to blow my nose the entire time, so the soup was actually Very soothing and comforting as well. The sprouts are my favorite additive. They are so fresh and add a delicious crunch.  The shrimp is my favorite Pho meat, however. Nice upscale-esq establishment. I will be returning..... A lot!

text: A cozy place for relaxed lunch. Excellent quality pasta and sandwiches; which motivate me to come back.
name: Yasuji

text:
Four stars for taking good care of me and +15 coworkers seated outdoors. We got there at 11am (right when they open) & it made a difference with no crowd. They did a good job getting our drinks & food out in a timely fashion.

I loove a sparkly, an extra fizzy prosecco, which you get a miniaturize bottle and top off yourself, so drink at your leisure. I also decided on a beer with similar taste to Guinness, but crafted locally, so I got Coppertail Stout & always love the deep, coffee-like taste that's quite yummy.

I got their flat iron steak salad 3.5/5 with dressing on the side because I don't like it drenched, which wilts the lettuce. I stole a bite of steak (more tender than my flat iron & secretly envied the whole time) & chicken fajitas 4/5 & would get that instead.

One of my coworker's brought his own set of jenga, which was a fun setup because we had a great time playing while enjoying cool breezes.
name: Joy

text:
I been coming to Àlavita for years! They never disappoint me! The only bad thing is you can't go there the last minute kind of deal since it's a small restaurant and they have limited tables....so plan accordingly!

I love everything they have,..from appetizers, salad, pasta, steak to their desserts! They also have good selections of wine. Their cocktails are yummy also! 

We will be back!
name: Yulia

text: I have never had a bad meal here, but their staff is less than friendly. I've talked to a manager on multiple occasions about the lack of efficient service
name: Tiara

text:
I hate to be the bearer of bad news but i had better Indian food in other restaurants! Maybe it was a bad nite in the kitchen or the Keto Gods wanted to punish me for cheating on a weekday but I was disappointed in the things we got.

Bay leaves is located on North Dale Mabry, across from Saigon Deli. Since it's nestled in a plaza, finding a parking space is quite easy. The restaurant itself looks large, lots of seating available. Their menu covers most popular South and North Indian dishes which was a great surprise. Our server for the nite was amazing, wish i knew her name. 

For starters, we had Samosa Chaat, pieces of samosa topped with chickpea curry and drizzled with yogurt and tamarind sauces. Granted, i only indulged on samosas, It was still my favorite item of the nite. 

For entrees: chicken tikka masala and Lamb Saag. Chicken tikka masala was sweet, i wasn't a fan of it at all. Lamb Saag (my favorite dish), basically creamed spinach with lamb, didn't taste good either. Not impressed. 

My friend ordered Aloo paratha and garlic naan. Aloo paratha (another favorite of mine), basically a potato stuffed flatbread was doused in oil and there was almost no filling. 

Overall, I expected so much more from this place.
name: Robin

text: This food was perfect after we had a rum tour at old New Orleans brewery. I went the special, the fried shrimp and oyster po boy served with fries and it was delicious!! FYI it did have lettuce tomato and pickles and did not disappoint! If only I could pick another side than fries I would be happy but to me the oysters platter was everything. I loved how the seasoning on the platter was perfect, they worked on the natural flavor of the oysters wonderfully! For my 3 days in Nola this was definitely worth my time and I'll be coming back!

text: Hidden gem! My husband and I stopped in here after a massage across the street and were delighted at the food expedience we stumbled into! We both ordered the three sliders sampler: roast beef, chicken and cheeseburger. Each one was better than the last. The chicken slider was a force to be reckoned with; juicy and flavorful. The jalapeños they serve on their food are out of this world. I'm not even a spice fan but I was snacking on them like peanuts! We also got the cheese waffle fries which were to die for. The cheese was such an unusual, delicious treat compared to the stereotypical cheese fries we usually have (with that processed nacho cheese on them... blah...). We were so happy with the food. We got donuts to go: mine was red velvet and my husband's was a slightly more traditional plain glazed but both were incredible. Not too sweet, which is a hard quality to find in a donut! Both were soft and delicious. Highly recommend this food! Also, the people working were the NICEST ever. My husband complimented their music and the young lady behind the register even figured out that we were out-of-towners are recommend some local spots that would totally fit our vibe off of that one compliment! She pulled the place up on Instagram on my phone for us to check out and everything. Over and beyond customer service. Really cool place, really cool people, really killer food. You NEED to find your way there to check it out.
name: Cece

text: Don't be fooled by the Irish bar exterior - this place has THE most amazing Italian food! Make sure to try the Murphs Pasta and the meatball appetizer. And don't sleep on the desserts!
name: Diane

text: It looked better online than it did in person. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. text: Amazing! Delicious food and awesome drinks and wine selection! Will definitely bring people visiting town as it also has a great ambience and New Orleans-vibe.

text: New York...New York! Great place. The NY themed decor here is fun and the restaurant has a cool feel to it. First thing you are greeted with upon entering is their bakery showcase which has an unbelievable selection of items. As well as bagels and coffees. After being seated, it is hard to choose what to eat as the menu has everything !! Service was perfect. My family tried multiple items and all were delicious. From the burger with pastrami, the amazing grilled cheese and tomato bisque soup, to the french dip, and a chicken salad sandwich, nothing disappointed. Bring your appetite or be ready for a to-go box as portions are plentiful. Oh, and they have  a bar area with tv's throughout so you can always catch your favorite game. I will be back for sure!!

text: My hometown has so many good Chinese restaurants and I was looking for one out here in SB. This place is delicious and provides excellent service! Feels just like home!
name: Alex

text: The burgers are unmatchable! Great happy hour and staff! Emily is a fantastic server with great knowledge of the menu and drink specials! The homemade buffalo sauce is to die for! Keep it up!
name: Matt

text: I have tried several items and my absolute favorite is the creamsicle alcoholic drink.
name: Lisette

text: Ordered a to-go waffle with fruit topping and whipped cream from here. I was craving this for lunch. Don't ask me why lol. I had no problems. Easy ordering. Delicious waffle (was not soggy) and the fruit was just the right amoutn of sweet.
name: Ashley

text: I tried three different tacos- pollo, carnitas, and carne asada. I would rank them carne asada, carnitas, pollo. The chicken was okay, but the carnitas and carne asada tacos were so good! I wish I lived closer to this food truck, as I would probably frequent it. They have a large variety of meats, and they were quite popular at the time I came (6:30ish). I had to wait a little while for my tacos, but I'd say they're cooked to order.
name: Danielle

text: Love this place! Easy access to 70. Well worth it, fast and super tasty. Which is saying a lot coming from a KC resident. Haven't had anything we don't like. Sweet potato fries with apple jack sauce are unique and yummy!
name: Beth

text: We were a little nervous to try this place due to the sketchy exterior, but the reviews were outstanding so we ventured in.  Let me just say the reviews weren't wrong!  The burgers are out of this world good and the owner was extremely friendly.  I would definitely recommend stopping in for a bite!
name: Tara

text: Stopped in on vacation and my wife had the lobster roll, my daughter and I basically fish and fries.  We also split a crab rangoon dip.  Fish was perfect and was crispy without being greasy, cole slaw was blahh but I just piled it on my fish coated with tarter sauce.  Wife said her sandwich was full of lobster meat and I better write a good review.  Dip was excellent.  We didn't do the beer or in house vodka so can't speak to the brewing piece but it was a nice stop on our tourist run in the area. Simple but good.  Our waiter was pleasant and attentive, we hit it late afternoon, I'm sure it's more of a bar scene later in the day.
name: Matthew

text: Beautiful place- found randomly while walking in Bywater. The bartender was so friendly and the security guard was also so nice. They both gave us some great recommendations that we had to try. We only had the fried oysters and I'm so glad we did - so good! welcome LGBT best part
name: Kelly

text: I feel like they can do better on the food. At least the dish I had could have been a lot better. I expected the Ora King salmon sandwich would have been pretty hearty and tasty but it was the opposite. I barely had any salmon on my sandwich! And I also upgraded my sandwich to have avocado, which is an extra $2.50. So I paid $20 for a sandwich I could have easily made at home, which is where I suggest you eat if you planned on eating a sandwich here.  The reason they didn't get 1 star is because the server was friendly and the pumpkin bread solid. But for the price, you have to do better on your sandwich. Very disappointed.
name: Brent

text: This place has the best pizza and pasta in the city! The desserts are great as well! Outstanding service! My new favorite spot!
name: Lisa

text: This was a delivery order on a night when I really did not want to cook. Price felt a touch high for what it was. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Would absolutely visit again.
name: User

text: The best Cuban sandwich spot in Tampa to date. The sweetest staff and a home made feeling to the affordable and filling selection of savory sandwiches and delectable sweets. Truly worth my multiple visits and every penny. Become a regular and the La Segunda staff may as well be family to you.
name: Mike,

text: I just got the Carne Asada & Discada burrito here. Nearly brought me to tears.

text:
Came on a Friday night. Settled on this restaurant as it seemed to represent the local area. Decided to sit on the patio. This restaurant was on the second floor. It had a balcony overlooking the Sundial Plaza courtyard. 

Hostess was inexperienced by seating us next to a column that blocked the view. We asked to move, and she hesitated but obliged. The first thing I noticed at my new table was pink lipstick on my water glass.

Apparently this restaurant had 75 varieties of salt, but you only get three for free with your bread, which was picked by the restaurant. Not sure how to sample the other 72, as it was not offered.

Great selection of raw oysters from the north-east. Octopus, branzino, calamari, and crab cakes were just average. Nothing special about these dishes.

Menu was quite overpriced for what you got. Skipped dessert. Every table gets cotton candy at the end.

Overall impression: Pretty place, average food, staff needs improvement.
name: Eugene

text:
Terrible service and food.  Ordered street tacos on corn tortillas. Received BURNT flour tortillas.  When I brought the mistake up to our server Kira her attitude was as if she couldn't believe I am talking to her and said she would be right back.  Lol she returns a few minutes later not with the my order made in corn tortillas rather with 2 cold corn tortillas on a plate laying it on the table and walks away.

 I asked to see the manager who's only option for correcting my meal was an apology and discounted coupon...

Sometimes you have to just shake your head and smile...and of course find another place to eat!!!!!

If your looking for a place...do not look here!

text:
Been coming here since they opened & really like the atmosphere & the beers are great. They just changed the menu & looks like they're going more foodie with higher prices and dropped some favorites, like the Nashville hot chicken, only flatbreads are  duck & veggie and the brisket & pulled pork is an entree not a sandwich. Two wings for $10? Food is good but less choices & higher prices. Disappointed

Updating my review after visiting again tonight. They've revised the menu & brought back the Nashville Hot Chicken & a number of other options; YAY!! The beer is good as ever & I'm a very happy customer! Updated to 5  Thanks!

text: I just had the worst salad ever at this place. The bowl was small and deep and filled to the brim so you couldn't blend the toppings with the lettuce. And it was literally drenched in dressing. I'll never go there for a salad again.
name: Susan

text: My mom and I tried their burgers and were totally disappointed with the food and the service.  I ordered the classic burger well done and it was slightly pink inside.  Both of our fries were cold the moment they were placed on our table.  The impossible burger was dry and flavorless.  This was the worst 45.00 meal ever.  The beverages were the most enjoyable part of our meal(Dr.Pepper and Strawberry Lemonade).  Whenever I decide to come back, I will stick with the Shrimp Pasta.  The server periodically came over to check on us, I'm guessing she was new or struggles to manage multiple tables at one time.  There were long delays in getting drink refills and the check.
name: Ibrahim

text:
Based on taste this is a five star restaurant all day long as the food was so delicious it made me want to slap my mama. That being said the crab clusters were small. 

Located in a strip center this is not a fancy place but they couldn't be nicer or more accommodating. I will definitely visit again..
name: Harry

text: One of THE BEST lunches I have ever eaten! Order the chicken and rice, it was delicious. The chicken is so packed with flavor, the rice so authentic and pillowy and the white sauce just helped bring everything together beautifully! I'm only giving it a 4 star because they forgot to tell me I had to pick up my drink from the fridge - so I walked out without my beverage! But otherwise, absolutely delicious! Will come back again!!
name: Kimberly

text: Get you some!!! Don't pass this by do not sleep on Neyow's! The food is well worth the hour forty five minuets wait on a Friday night! Great atmosphere, welcoming vibe. Family dinner, date night, or just out hanging. My nephew had the chicken pattie melt, the kids had burgers tenders Mac n cheese and fries. My husband and I shared the extravaganza dinner and we chose carrots (taste like yams) and cornbread dressing. Listen..... listen!!! The food was SO good we drank our gumbo juice . The platter was big enough to share with everyone at the table. We are visiting from Cali and we are going back to Neyow's tomorrow! For the 21+ order yourself a BowWow.
name: Mrs

text:
This is the place to be!!!!

You cannot go wrong with arcades, beer, great food and 80-90's music. The atmosphere is great! The beer is priced right and the food is amazing. 

They have pretty much any arcade game you can think of. All of the games are .25 cents. 

You do have to buy a membership to enter but it is priced well. They did this because people were taking advantage of and damaging the games. But I will have to say, I agree with it. It keeps away those kind of people who would do those kind of things. 

They also do birthday packages. I recommend going to their website and looking for yourself.
name: Adam

text: 0 consistency. One day they stay open till 9:30 one day its 8:45 and the next its 9:15. They say they close at 10 but the kitchen closes at whatever time the disgruntled staff finds appropriate for the evening. I woukd reccomend coming at least 2 hours before they close to guarantee a table otherwise who knows when they will stop serving.... changes nightly
name: Enzo

text:
I ordered the food to go and everything was packaged nicely with fresh bread and oil for dipping. When I walked into the restaurant it had great ambiance and would go back to experience the dining there another time as well. 

The said was very fresh and light. Not a fan of the onions on top for that particular type of salad but that's my preference. The bread was crunchy but soft on the inside and great with the oil. The pizza was very tasty and had a balance of ingredients that worked well together.
name: Megan

text:
I absolutely love coming to this bar with my friends. I've been there repeatedly and really find the atmosphere, and the game's engaging. kristoff's it is a board game bar so there are several board games there that I've never played before and they always have fun new ones to try. They have an easy-to-understand difficulty labeling system and all the games are easily visible and well organized (to an extent as I usually go when it's busy on saturdays). The drinks are very novel and fun to get well I'll say I'm having funny of alcohol. The food in my opinion is just bar food so ya, however my friends love it. 

Finally my biggest complaints about this place is that it can feel expensive to pay a $5 library fee for my friends, and on Saturdays it does get very busy. Anyways love this place!
name: Sam

text: The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Service timing was efficient even though it was busy. Overall, a strong experience. Food was fresh and service was quick. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Came here this past weekend twice...don't judge...with my kids. It's kind of tucked away in the Safeway shopping center strip mall. Typical small town style diner with good food and ridiculously friendly service. We had breakfast both days and it's pretty standard American diner style breakfast & lunch choices...with a few local flavor choices. Nothing real over the top about the food, it was good. The service here is unbelievable though...from the minute you walk in, through ordering, and the follow-through. The ladies here are all extremely friendly, prompt, professional and kept the coffee/drink refills coming consistently! Great job here!!
name: Greg

text:
Had lunch here today with my sis in law. We didn't make reservations so we sat at the bar. The servers were all very attentive, knowledgeable , very polite and friendly. 
We started our lunch with a cup of the Lobster/Shrimp Bisque. It was loaded with meat and thick and so damn tasty! There was a very tiny spice after- bite in a very good way! For my main dish I chose the Andulaz Shrimp Po boy. It was such a generous serving I could barely finish one half of it. Fresh shrimp with a light corn meal breading puked high on a crusty baguette bread. Served with a side of homemade Cajun chips.  Dressed with lettuce, tomato and pickles. Side note: it was even delish cold as my dinner later tonight! For dessert I had the enormous portion of chocolate molten cake. It was so good with the creamy ice cream on top and a side of whipped cream. The chocolate just slowly oozed out of the molten hot middle. 
My dining companion had the eggplant Ophelia, a house specialty. Roasted eggplant casserole with whole shrimp loads of crabmeat and mushrooms. Served with a Creole Butter sauce on the side. She said it was the best dish and meal she had eaten in the last 4 months of her visit from Texas! For dessert she had the Creme Brûlée. She also took a loaf of Marsha's fresh baked bread home with her. 
We had a delightful lunch and will definitely visiting again soon!
name: Tatiana

text: I really love this place, I've eaten here many times and just every time is it great. Idk what else to say. The waiters are always awesome. The view rules. I haven't had something I haven't liked yet.
name: Seth

text: I didn't like the meat, it was not good it was really low quality :(... services was really nice though
name: Yessica

text:
This was originally 3 stars but as I started writing this I realized I was getting angry. 
I've never had a meal collapse so thoroughly in a restaurant I actually paid to sit down in. Some of it wasn't their fault. But some problems here are, now that I read the reviews, endemic.  We had reservations but when we arrived we were told there would be a considerable wait because it was raining.  Turns out that about 1/2 of their space is outside with no protection. I don't really understand how that works on a nightly basis (was the night of our reservation the only time it had ever rained in Santa Barbara?) but okay, we waited for an inside table. The beseiged Maitre d' comped us a round of drinks (good on them, and the drinks were great).  When we were seated, we ordered the artichoke "crab" cake, which was excellent, and the white asparagus soup, which was weird -- sweet and tasting like anything but asparagus. Turns out it's sweet potato and quite a few other things with some asparagus -- this wasn't mentioned on the menu.  A weird thing was that at no point were we brought sharing plates, so we had to keep passing stuff back and forth. Which would have been fun on another night. Not this one.
Still, so far everything was fine.  We'd ordered a couple more things and so we waited.  And waited.  When I looked at my watch, it was 8:45 -- we'd been there 1 hour 45 minutes -- and our entrees were nowhere in sight. Our server was scarce. No one was there to check in on us. People who were seated long after us were getting their meals first. And no, not because we'd ordered something complicated. 
Finally our shishito peppers arrived. They were lukewarm and soaked in lemon brine, and they didn't at all go with the dipping sauce. The Impossible Burger was terrrible. I've never had a terrible one before. I didn't know you could screw one of those things up.  It was lukewarm and the green pepper had been, what?, fried or something to the point of sliminess. The cashew cheese was tasteless and cold. You know how it goes when you come to a point where something tiny that makes no difference is actually the last straw? The bun was so firm that biting into it forced the entire burger out onto the table -- not a plate, because they hadn't given me a sharing plate.  Wow, it really was an impossible burger. Petty, I know, but that's when we gave up. 
When we got there, I felt sorry for the folks working there trying to make the best of a rainy night. But by the time we left I felt worse for myself, my girlfriend, and the rest of the diners trying to make do with the inadequacies of this restaurant.
name: George

text: My first meal in Nashville was at Milk and Honey and it truly was a great way to start off my day. I had an omelette with tomatoes and cilantro on top of a piece of toast sided with a bowl of fruit. Although that may not sound that exciting at all, it was! The fruit was so delicious I don't believe I have ever tasted fruit that good in my entire life. The little sandwich in it self was amazing and hit the spot completely. I would definitely rather dine here than wait in the line for biscuit love. Very cute area to dine in and the staff all around was very very sweet.
name: Jennifer

text:
The restaurant itself has a calming, warm, atmosphere. I was greeted upon entry and seated at a corner table for 2 (I went alone). The host then filled my glass with ice water and lit the flame at the table. I had time to review the menu and then order. I chose the Pollo Quattro Formaggio, but substituted angel hair pasta for the rice pilaf. Then, the bread with special olive oil was brought piping hot. Yum! 
The food was ok, but the presentation was surprising. I was shocked to see a plate of white meaty, gooey cheese. The chicken breast was maybe 3oz cooked and the pasta was cooked to perfection. I only wish I had seen more pics of the food beforehand. Good choice though!
name: Alicia

text:
Tonight I decided to have dinner at Bon Appetit to relax and enjoy the striking view of St. Joseph Sound.  I had the lamb which was cooked to perfection.  Decided to order the dessert special - a homemade blueberry cake which is gluten free.  PLEASE keep it on the menu - words can not describe how luscious it was.  Fresh berries within a light cake...like no other.

Another pleasurable dinner at Bon Appetit
name: Kathleen

text: Located on the 3rd block of Bourbon this is a great place to eat. The eggs benedict are really good as are the shrimp and grits. Fresh oysters are just that, huge and great. Grilled oysters are some of the best i'v had. No need to go to acme and stand in line, can't beat this place. We visit nola a lot and always eat here.
name: B V

text: My husband took me here for lunch on my birthday and the experience was amazing. The atmosphere is rustic and they have a brick oven in the back of the restaurant that you can see from your table. It's beautiful in there. The drink menu offers a pretty wide variety of house made cocktails (my thing) and beer selections (for the hubs). Let me just tell you, the garnishes on the drinks were the reason I selected the ones I did. #notsorry :) We ended up splitting the boucherie plate to start and the smoked beef short ribs for our entree. The boucherie was comprised of a fantastic selection of meats from the butcher and the dressings that were paired made the plate so much more savory. My husband and I were blown away with the beef short ribs. It comes topped with a house-made tomato butter that makes the meat melt in your mouth. The only downside to getting this plate is that I loved it so much, it'll probably be the only thing I ever request! I highly recommend this restaurant for a well rounded dining experience. And it's good for larger groups as well!
name: Sarah

text:
"Good evening, Mr. Phelps. Your mission, should you decide to accept it, is to enjoy ONLY ONE SLICE of delicious pizza from Little Italy Pizza. I know you can't eat just one. Your stomach will self destruct in five seconds."

Mission complete. And, no, I didn't stop at one delicious slice. I stunned the crowd and enjoyed...four (count 'em) FOUR SLICES: Two cheese, one white and one mushroom.

And, yes, my stomach did self destruct from over eating. Again. :-/
name: Chris

text: Food was good and came out fast. Also, the whole meal felt kinda uneven. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Honestly, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: Arrived for a 7:30 PM reservation, and were seated in a few minutes.  It took about 20 minutes for our drinks to arrive.  We ordered food hoping to facilitate the service.  It didn't work!  At least another half hour 'til our food arrived.  We really enjoyed the food, but were put off, by the longish wait.  I think the kitchen is understaffed.  I hope they remedy this, as we would like to return.
name: Noe

text: I used to love the place until their entire menu changed. When I first started frequenting WOB, they had a very tasty seared tuna bowl, fish tacos, etc ... now all they can offer are overpriced mundane options such as flatbread, burgers, wings, oh and a $9 pretzel.
name: Kathy

text: I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. No big complaints, just a nice meal. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated bc that happens a lot. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. It felt a little understaffed, especially near the end of the meal. Definitely coming back. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer..
name: User

text:
Weekends in the Gulch can get quite crowded. Bar Louie is an ok fall back if you're looking for a beer and a quick bite. They serve standard restaurant chain food from burgers to pizza to anything fried. Oh and there's salad if that's your thing...

The food is fine, the beer is cold. They have a list of fun martinis, like s'mores and diva, that are $5.50 during happy hour. 

There are many TVs around the bar if you want to watch sports. Only complaint is the inside has had a lingering smell left by someone with too much to drink the night before...There's also a large outdoor area where you can bring dogs or people watch.
name: Michelle

text: Fast, friendly service and great food. We always have a good time here and the salsa is my favorite.
name: Jennifer

text:
11/08/18 - Noticed that our favorite server Terabetha is training to be a bartender. We'll miss her at the tables. Sarah served us today and was very nice. We look forward to seeing her again. 

Terabetha is a joy to have serve us. She is so efficient and sociable. Always gets our order right. If it's not, she makes sure it's taken of. 5 stars for her.
name: Doreen

text: It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Glad we tried it. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.
name: User

text: Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. You can tell they care about customer experience here. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Would absolutely visit again. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. Not bad for a quick meal.
name: User

text:
This place is a joke. I don't understand how it has so many positive ratings. I booked a reservation on OpenTable based on the positive reviews here and there. The band that played was onstage maybe 20 minutes of my dining experience (I arrived at 7 pm, not a tall ask at that time), the service was atrocious, and the portions were laughably small. If your portion size is small, I better at least think it was the best few bites of food I've ever put in my mouth. 

They care more about presentation and aesthetic than the food itself. Save your money, please go somewhere else.
name: Anna

text:
I was disappointed, unfortunately. Great menu selection online, poor execution in person. Everything seemed overly greasy (especially the pretzels), our burgers were undercooked and dripping, and French onion soup was basically just broth. We had a nice waiter, but the table was cluttered with plates and empty glasses for the night's duration. The interior and vibe are nice, but I probably wouldn't recommend, unless you were just using the bar, because of the other factors. 

Please take a review of your food preparation and update accordingly. Thanks!
name: Matt

text: Slow service. At 6:09 pm, the restaurant was moderately busy, but no wait time to get seated. Floors slick walking and front of restaurant smelled like musty water. Tried to not look to closely to determine cleanliness. Meals were on the light side with a white fish dinner and blackened chicken. Tasty. Would get items again if decided to go back.
name: DenEllen

text: By far the most mediocre pizza I've ever had. If you are on campus and perhaps drunk, then it's a great spot. Optimal drunk food. However, if you're sober, prepare for a usually long line, and a super mediocre, slightly stale slice of pizza.
name: Joe

text: Portion size looked small at first but it was actually enough. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The staff seemed tired but still polite. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The food was good and the service was easygoing.
name: User

text: I stopped by here after roaming around the terminal and Reuben seemed to look delicious. I have to say it was very good meat, excellent dressing, and coleslaw was just right. The only bad part for me was that I wanted the sandwich to be pressed and it came out cold. Nevertheless it was great food for the price and I would recommend this place to anyone
name: David

text: Our family stopped by for lunch on Saturday. We enjoyed the food and dining experience here. We were disappointed to find out that the check-in 10% discount applies during the weekday. I don't know if another Yelp review makes note of this already or if I missed this info elsewhere, but just be aware.
name: Grace

text: Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. The food was good and the service was easygoing. Glad we tried it. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Really liked the atmosphere and the portions were decent. Food was fresh and service was quick. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed.
name: User

text:
I went here during restaurant week but wasn't wild about the restaurant week menu so I ended up getting two appetizers as my meal: the pulpo saltado (octopus) and mofongo de cerdo (mashed plantains with your choice of meat, in my case, pork).

They had happy hour going on as well, but the happy hour offers weren't anything crazy special so I didn't get a drink but my friend got a margarita and overall said it was solid.

Presentation wise, both were really lovely plates that I had, but flavor wise it was not quiteee five star.  The mofongo could have used a littleee more seasoning, and the octopus - gosh that was a lot of salt.

So naturally, eating them together though was the best combination because they balanced each other's weaknesses out really well.  I enjoyed it overall, and our server was really great.  When the weather is nice, the restaurant is open air and the outside seating is super cute.  The interior is cozy and Mixto's got a nice refreshing vibe overall.  If you're in the mood for some Latin American/Cuban food, it's a pretty decent option.
name: Grace

text: Atmosphere is very good and reminds me of home. We are from lower Alabama and determined that it reminded us of home. The wine we got was very good and priced really well. I got the grilled fisherman's platter and to be honest it was not worth $40. The blackened grouper that my wife got was really good though. I'm giving this place 4 stars due to how bad their "best" platter was. I would come back for sure but would highly recommend not getting the platter if your hungry.
name: Kenneth

text: 1 hr wait at Brophy Bros. so we settled for this casual place that's a walk around the corner.  This had to work as we were on our way out of SB, but couldn't leave without satisfying a QUICK seafood craving. So as luck has it, turns out On the Alley has a small menu of Brophy Bros food. This joint just basically operates as a to-go shack with a few tables outside. It has a solid menu, simple yet a good selection. They also serve desserts and all day breakfast -unexpected from a small kitchen.  I would definitely recommend the Brophy Bros FISH & CHIPS. Great crunchy batter with white fish that melts in your mouth! The only con to this place is the seating with a sometimes interactive audience of birds.  Wish the stairs inside led to additional dining space instead of storage.
name: Jennifer

text: Great food and quick and friendly service!! Great lunch specials on sushi!! Prices are great, everything was very fresh. Went on a Saturday afternoon & it wasn't crowded at all!
name: Kelly

text: Always a good trip to Show-Me's. It's affordable and has a great atmosphere. The majority of the servers are nice too. We enjoy watching Blues games here. Prices are very reasonable.
name: Gabby

text: Rize is a surprising break from the pizza norm. After being inspired by elpresidente, I thought I'd branch out from my familiar za tree and try something new. I went with the Southern Belle and Pepperoni pizzas with the smaller traditional crust. The pizza itself was delicious. Sauce was tasty and the cheese was not over done or extremely greasy. Not only was the pizza awesome, but the service was fast and friendly with a smile. Can't ask for anything more than that. Will definitely be visiting Rize again in the future!
name: Robert

text: Stopped by after work because I was nearby and hungry. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. I left full, which at least counts for something. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. For the amount of food, I thought the cost was fair. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. I liked the soup more than the entree honestly. We shared dumplings first and those were probably the best thing on the table. Definitely coming back.
name: User

text: When I am looking for consistent, fresh and tasty pizza Jockamo's is first to mind. Went last night to take advantage of Pizza week deals. I got the Tecumseh pizza, some bread sticks, and a Zombie Dust (or 2). First off the  deer meat sausage makes this pizza unique and very delicious, the bread sticks are soft and have a nice subtle garlic taste, and who can turn down a beer menu that features Zombie Dust? If you haven't tried Jockamos yet, it is an Indy must!
name: Josh

text: Simple concept, wings and beer. DO IT RIGHT! Ordered the "loaded" tots and they were missing half of the toppings. Tots with sour cream and bacon are not loaded nor worth the almost $9 they charge. The boneless wings were on special and although they look like chicken nuggets, they tasted okay. I'm always very suspect of boneless chicken that are all the exact same size and shape. Service was just okay, felt like they were closing but it was only 8pm. Not worth the disappointment.
name: Scott

text: Visiting from CA and this is one of the restaurants I have to stop at for my "Tucson food tour." I miss this restaurant and always get the Alfredo's Favorite salad with chicken. It is AMAZING!
name: Cecelia

text: Fall off the bone ribs, great smoky flavor. Perfectly prepared salad, with bite size dicing of lettuce and veggie toppings. Topped mine with pulled pork, added some apple bbq sauce, blended well with ranch dressing. Highly recommend! Will definitely stop in again on our road trips through the area.
name: Sue

text: Great atmosphere, great food, great service. I really enjoyed the escargot! I think the food is carefully paired together with other ingredients- everything tasted amazing! I will definitely be back!
name: kaitlyn

text:
I would give this place a slight edge over Kayne Prime and Jeff Ruby's. We had filets, scallops, Brussel sprouts, tuna tartare, a wedge salad and Mac and cheese. I personally didn't try the Mac and cheese or the wedge because I don't eat dairy or gluten but my friends said it was delicious. Everything was cooked perfectly and tasted great. The service was perfect and our waiter was helpful with what I could order. 

The only thing keeping it from five stars are the drink prices. However, the huge, crystal clear ice cube may have made it worth the $4 extra that they charge over similar establishments.
name: Charlotte

text: Food is above average but it's overshadowed by very slow service, especially when it's not crowded...shame...
name: Scott

text: I came to Jimmy Js with a group of friends after receiving poor service from the front desk at Luke's. I'm glad we ended up here bc Rose (w/o the thorns) was amazing hostess. It's a little hole in the wall restaurant with great good and service. They had THE best hurricanes. It was my first time in New Orleans and Rose set the bar what to expect. You should definitely add Jimmy Js on your list of places to eat.
name: Tamara

text:
Very casual. Everything we got was delish. (And vegan!) loved the very berry smoothy. Loved the salad special of the day! The mocha chocolate cake  was just perfect. 

The decor is fun and full of colorful murals. The seats are surprisingly comfortable for being hard chairs. The outdoor seating is heated and warm even in winter, and lovely. Someone had their puppy  with them on the patio which was adorable.
name: Gin

text:
Food tasted slightly below expected for an average Mexican restaurant. Tortilla chips slightly stale. Street taco pricing confusing as titled as 3 Street tacos but each taco has different price. Cochinita pibil was overly spicy. Portion size generous. 

Service was very slow and mildly discourteous but this was very likely due to being understaffed that day.
name: Aaron

text:
I've been to a few different BJ's locations and this BJ's Brewhouse Lutz location continues the trend with great food and service! I've ordered the bison burger here on many occasions and it is always very lean and tasty. I have been to other restaurants where there bison burgers are really greasy. That is not the case here. The only time I've ever been slightly disappointed in a meal here was when I ordered the salad topped with ahi tuna. It looked nothing like the picture as far as the quantity of tuna. This salad was definitely lacking in that department, but the salad was fresh and tasty otherwise. I'll stick to the bison burger although there are many other options on this large menu!

If you like beer this is the place for you! They have an incredible amount of taps which include their own beers, domestics, imports as well as craft beers of every kind. The back wall of the bar area is a large chalkboard where they list the different beers and they change frequently so that you always have new options most times when you visit.

This location is fairly busy due to it being close to the interstate, in front of the outlet mall and simply in a more congested area of town. It's open for both lunch and dinner. If you have to wait for a table just know that it's worth it!
name: Diana

text: Solid Chipotle but it just opened up so they stuff your bowls/burritos with meat. Let's see if they keep it going but we all know every Chipotle starts being stingy with their portions and force you to ask for "double." Workers are nice and I had a good experience because they comp'd my meal for waiting 5 minutes for chicken.
name: Peter

text: Waffle House is a go to favorite of mine when I have a desire for pork chops, pecan waffle, eggs and scattered and smothered hash browns.  This WH location for some reason isn't crowded but it should be - the service is above norm for most and the food is cooked exactly how I like it everytime. I have ordered the same thing at WH for 30 plus years and this location is one that is better than most and brings me back for more.
name: Glenn

text: I'm giving them a 2 because the food was good even though I couldn't finish it. My frustration took me over and I became so angry I couldn't even eat. We waited about 20 minutes to be seated, all fine and well because it seemed they may have been short staffed. When we were seated, our waitress took our drink and appetizer order. She came back with me and my boyfriends drinks, nothing for my 7 year old daughter so I reminded her that she didn't get her drink. She let out a deep sign and said okay. She came back to the table, no drink! I reminded her again, my boyfriend asked for a refill and I asked for napkins. She came back with his drink, no drink for my daughter and no napkins. I asked her again for her drink and napkins. She brought back napkins! My daughter finished her meal and by this time my boyfriend had given her some of his. Our check and her drink came at the same time! She explained she was overwhelmed because I guess she could sense my frustration, this was only her second day! My boyfriend saw her speaking to the manager, not sure what they were talking about but she was obviously over whelmed and was offered no assistance. As a supervisor at a call center I would never allow my people on the floor drowned like that or allow my customers to be short served. It totally ruined my first experience at chili's!  We saw other people who worked there not doing much so there isn't any reason that this should have happened. Total disappointment!
name: Stacy

text: Drew was our server and was extremely pleasant and attentive. The food was great.  I tried the 5 cheeseburger and was blown away!  Great service and great food.
name: Joshua

text: Simply excellent, after reading a menu, you always get an idea of what a dish would taste like; but this place exceeds my expectations every time!
name: Raquel

text: Loved this place. Food is awesome and authentic. Love their spring rolls and beef and broccoli. Can't go wrong here, all is good.
name: Andrew

text:
Went here before a show at Municipal. Menu looked good and I was excited to dine here.
The place was empty, which didn't bother me at all. It was rainy and nasty out. It was also a Monday.
My wife and I started with the cheese plate. We asked our server for a run-down of these cheeses on our plate, and he sent a member of the kitchen staff to come and tell us what was what. That was great. We both appreciated that gesture.
The majority of the menu were small plates, which is fine. The menu itself was divided up in such a manner that didn't necessarily suggest that fact. Our server made us aware, which was quite helpful. 
I had a couple of rounds of oyster mushrooms, which were grilled and delicious. They came with something forgettable... a Parmesan smear of one type or another. I had something else, but couldn't tell you what it was.
The food here was good. Our server was attentive and did a fine job (he didn't have anything else to do). The 3 star rating is based on price and portion. text: This place was nearly packed when I arrived just before 8pm for dinner on a Thursday night. Granted, the Hall & Oates Show was going on at the Reno Events Center that night, so that may have added to the crowd a bit. Most families and fellow diners didn't look like they were too much in a hurry though. When I walked in I quickly nabbed an empty seat and asked the trio near me if we order at the counter or if it's table service, since there hadn't been anyone to seat me - they said table service - but an employee came by after only a minute or two! I ordered my usual pho preference, the small rare steak (#7 here). I glanced around at what everyone else was eating, as I tend to do more when I dine solo, and everything looked tasty! Next time I'll branch out and try one of the noodle dishes and maybe some spring or egg rolls. This visit I was feeling a bit under the weather, so I was on a mission to get my beloved beef pho. It came out piping hot and delicious as-is, but I piled on all the accoutrements that accompanied it on the side plate: basil, bean sprouts, and a healthy wedge of lime. I skipped the jalapeño this time, just because - but it was there too! I prepped my bowl just the way I like it, making sure to mix everything up really well, before digging in and steaming my face with the beef broth as tried to eat as politely with my chopsticks as I could. It was just what I was craving, and I finished the whole bowl. It's not my absolute FAVORITE pho in Reno, but it's up there!! Hearing fellow diners experiencing pho for the first time was a treat; I'm guessing this spot is more touristy than other pho restaurants in town due to its location. I'm all for people getting out of their comfort zones & trying something new; hopefully it opens their eyes to and encourages positive awareness of other cultures! Parking can be tricky around here, so I parked at Cal-Neva and walked around the corner. Will definitely return, maybe during the lunch hour to see if it's less busy, but either way the food here is worth it!!
name: Stefanie

text: WORST EXPERIENCE EVER DO NOT GO THERE!!! The manager Mark was extremely rude, condescending, and disrespectful - I would NOT recommend anyone go to this location. Lousy deal with this "Coop" that is supposed to be member friendly. I would go to Porterhouse in Eagle to get outstanding quality meat now, even paying just a bit more. They are certified butchers and know their meats and have terrific quality control!! Very friendly and they will make any issue right with you. We took meat back to the Boise Coop and even issues at the other location (actually think the Village can be worse) with sales receipt, as well as being a member and I/we were deemed a frequent complainer, told that I/we can no longer bring any item in for a return anymore, so we ended our membership. Even after, I was still dealing with issues, bought an under T and it did not fit well and asked if it did not fit if it would be a problem returning and it was fine doing so.

Feed up I wanted to let consumers know because it's not just the policy, which mind you they state and told me upon becoming a member, no problem or non member proof of purchase. The fact is that they want you spend money and if there is an issue AT ALL, in ANY form they keep track of who you are and decided like on any given return that they will put your through the ringer and refuse to take care of the matter. 

I have asked on various occasions to talk with the store manager for the Boise location, Matt Fuxan and he is never able to talk, never there and truly what sort of practice is that. Stay clear of this place, go to Natural Grocery, they do coupon events, bonus money for every dollar spent and just a nice clean place. They are getting more local and good Organic produce and fruit, not old hippie fruits that they seem to pride themselves in at both Boise Coop locations. I got sick of their mystery meat, sad looking produce and sloppy workers that look like they rolled out of a two day grunge rock festival (maybe a little deodorant guys...). The ones who have money to spend at the Coop are not liking the unsanitary scene anymore and being punished for speaking up. Also Whole Foods has been another outstanding clean operation. Meat dept is AMAZING and love their selection. 

It's sort of scary looking back that I trusted the Coop that much for so long to not see how bad it was getting... Not that it's all about looks, it's all about sanitation and when the workers don't care enough to have sanitary uniforms on then maybe they are not so good with handling the meats either. Even Fred Meyers health food dept and their organic dept. has really expanded. All those other locations mentioned take care of their customers and present a clean atmosphere. text:
This review is for the lunch buffet they offer Monday-Friday. I think the lunch and dinner experience are much different so I want to make sure people realize the lunch buffet is going to be more basic than the amazing rolls you might normally off of the menu. 

It is my new goal to try one new lunch spot every week. We will see how long I can keep this up. My boyfriend actually suggested Wild Wasabi because he heard about the lunch buffet. It's $12 for all you can eat. I'm not a big seafood fan but I'm getting better. I actually like sushi over other types of seafood so I was down to try. Wild Wasabi is located in Cummins Station close to downtown, or in downtown? I guess I always just picture Broadway and the surrounding area as downtown. For parking: park in the Cummins Station parking lot across the street from Wild Wasabi. Wild Wasabi offers 90 minutes of validated parking for $2. Just make sure to get the card from the server. The interior of Wild Wasabi is pretty typical for a sushi place. It's clean and comfortable enough. The servers are quick to come over and offer you the parking validation and confirm that you would like the lunch buffet. Everyone is very friendly and they are so quick to clean up your buffet plates! The buffet itself has both sushi and other basic Chinese/Japanese food options like egg rolls, noodles, miso, chicken, and rice. I skipped these because they didn't look like anything great. I wanted to save room for the sushi. The sushi is pretty basic but that's what you can expect for a sushi buffet I think. For basic sushi they had red snapper, shrimp, and salmon. The sushi rolls were mostly crab with some salmon and chicken options. I was the loser that goes to a sushi place and eats mostly chicken but I did sample some of the other rolls and really liked a few. The spicy crab roll wasn't too fishy and had a lot of flavor. The salmon roll was also pretty good. It had a nice kick. If I thought it was all delicious then I'm sure people that actually eat sushi on the reg will love it. Of course the fancier rolls are better but for the price and the amount of food you can eat, it's pretty dang good. My boyfriend loves seafood and really enjoyed everything. It was a great lunch overall and we will be back for sure!

text:
Tried the Hall on Franklin for lunch on a rainy afternoon.  Tasty food in a cool hipster setting. 

This food hall is of the variety where you are seated by a host, select from the menus of the seven restaurants and then served at the table - rather than the more typical food-court style where there is no table service.   It is a different food hall experience - and I like it better. 

It's a large, square room, all open space in a re-purposed factory building.  The decor is modern industrial, with exposed brick and cool fixtures.  There is a mixture of low and high top tables, a few booths and several couches around cocktail tables.  Each restaurant has an open kitchen along the sides of the room, with bar stool seating as well. 

There are seven restaurants to choose from, each offering a unique cuisine.  Many, many delicious sounding choices, so it was tough to pick. 

We opted to try avocado bruschetta from Fork & Gallina, coconut lobster salad from North Star Eatery and seared Ahi tuna chirashi from Poke Rose. 

The brushetta is 4 crostini piled high with rough mashed avocado prepared with garlic and a balsamic glaze and topped with diced roma tomatoes.   It's sloppy to eat, but excellence in every bite.  

Coconut lobster salad can be ordered either as banh mi (sandwich), or as a lettuce wrap.  In an illusion of carb consciousness, we tried the lettuce wrap.  Full claw lobster meat, served cold, is dressed with cucumber, cilantro, mint plus pickled vegetables and then sauced with citrus coconut sauce.  The picked veggies add a little heat and the coconut sauce contrasts with a creamy sweetness.   Another sloppy choice, but very very good.    This dish is served with a small basket of designer popcorn - kettle corn (sweet) with bits of nori (salty).  Unique and delicious. 

Ahi tuna chirashi was next.  The best way to describe is like an open-faced sandwich.  All the ingredients of a poke bowl, but artfully served on a plate. The tuna is perfect - fresh, thick, rice-encrusted and seared,   served atop a bed of chirashi rice, pea shoot salad greens and garnished with kanpyo relish. Dollops of coconut-garlic aioli and yuzu vinaigrette accentuate the dish.   This was the best choice of the 3 - it was EXCELLENT. 

Plenty of other options to try across all of the different restaurants.  I'll be back!
name: Mike

text:
This place is 5 stars all across the board and I will explain why! 

Food: My friends and I started out with the "Under the Sea Nachos" and can I just say, wow! Evenly distributed toppings across very thick chips and tasted incredible. Then, we each ordered a bowl. I ordered a bowl with a coconut rice base, tuna poke, and sweet chili aioli sauce along with all of the toppings that come with each bowl. I'm quite a foodie, I eat out often and I so appreciate when a meal is equally as unique as it is tasty and boy was this bowl both!

Drinks: Each of my friends ordered a drink. One ordered the "Pain Killer" and the other ordered "Swimming Pools". They were super sweet but very tasty and refreshing! If you are not into sweet drinks there are plenty of other drink options as well as a variety of beer and wines. 

Ambiance/Service: The entire place was just so unique! I think it was fun and playful and appreciated all the colors outside especially the gorgeous mural. It may not be everyone's taste but it sure was ours! Why not have something so unique and different when bars can get so monotonous sometimes. Additionally, everyone I met was so friendly and welcoming! I'd done a photoshoot there earlier that day and Chad and Theryn were more than happy to just chat before I was even a customer there. The service was fantastic when I dined as well!!!

The owners were really nice and run the place themselves. They were pretty proud of being a mom and pop shop with good fresh food. 

Although they've been open about six months they do still have things to work out. They seemed to forget that they were out of things and kept adding things they were out of as we ordered. text:

Frozen, starving and tired we sat at the table and finally got to order. The food, as posted in the pictures below was marginal at best. The Volcano nachos were mushy and cold in the center. The pic and peel shrimp was actually tasty and plentiful. The lava lava shrimp was tasteless. All in all, the experience was somewhat grueling.

The SiriusXM radio show was fun and the crowd was lively. That made up for a lot of the restaurants shortcomings. This is a restaurant chain, Make no bones about it. They have a business model and a corporate plan and you get what you get. I have rated Margaritaville restaurants in Key West, Atlantic City New Jersey and in Miami Beach Florida. text:
Cobalt is worth the visit! This restaurant recently opened May 1, 2019 and I had the opportunity to visit for lunch. All the new restaurants that I have recently visited, the decor blew me away and Cobalt was one of them! The beautiful decor had me very excited to try the food. Love the menu---the menu had strategically placed photos and the photos they chose were high-quality. I chose the berry Mojito which was not pictured but was very delicious! I will highly recommend this drink!

Service makes or breaks your experience at a restaurant and our server Olivia was outstanding! She was friendly, she was articulate, she gave great recommendations and honest reviews of the dishes that she tried. Even the dishes she had not personally tried she knew how they were prepared and knew the ingredients well. Her table touches were also perfect. She came to the table an appropriate amount of times and we never had to look for her or seek her out. She visited the table just enough to make our service experience extraordinary. I would request her on my next reservation. 

We tried 2 apps, the crab cakes and the mixed grill. Both were phenomenal! Our server suggested the crab cakes and they were an excellent recommendation. The mixed grill was a plank with burnt ends, yogurt marinated chicken skewers and smoked prawns. The prawns were paired with a lemon wedge and garlic ghee.All three were delicious. I would advise the mixed grill for 2 to 3 people max.
Prior to our entrées coming out, our server brought the jalapeño cornbread Madeleine for each of us. She did tell us that there was only one per visit. Considering I recently paid $9 for a bread bowl with 5 distinct housemade breads at Juniper, and that was the best thing I had there, I wouldn't be opposed to seeing a menu option to buy a small plate of these on the menu in the future. 
For my entrée I had to go for the burnt ends. This photo looked phenomenal on the website and I was excited to see smoked burnt ends paired with bok choy and prepared in a pasta dish, which I think is innovative and different. After reading a fellow yelp eliter's review that the dish was salty, I did mention this to Olivia our server prior to ordering. I don't know if the kitchen adjusted the salt based on my comment, but my entree was not salty. 

My fellow yelp elite had the braised short ribs. They were out of the brussels sprouts until the dinner hour so the owner came to the table and offered roasted cauliflower or asparagus. With some hesitation by my lunch partner on which option to choose the owner suggested a little of both and that is what she went for. It was a hearty dinner serving, which made its steep price point warranted, however it was not as flavorful as Cooper's hawk's short ribs, which was the bar my lunch partner set in her mind for braised short ribs so the bar was set high. They were fall off the bone tender, and the mashed potatoes and vegetables were good, just more seasoning (not salt, seasoning that adds flavor)  is my suggestion with the short ribs.

The braised short ribs were not piping hot, as well as the chicken skewers and the burnt ends on the mixed grill. There were not cold by no means, but not piping hot. This was not the case with my burnt ends entree which was steaming, and I was satisfied with the temp of the mixed grill, even though it wasn't piping hot, but thought I would make the mention. Also my burnt ends were not fatty on either the mixed grill or my entree. One of the short ribs were really fatty (more than half of it), the second was about 25% fatty and the the third was meaty with little fat. My assessment was based on the fat my lunch partner pulled off the meat and placed on a side plate. 

Can't end a meal like this without dessert right? We ordered the apple tart which looked divine on the picture and we also ordered the lemon blueberry ricotta cake. Both desserts were plated beautifully! I was not a fan of the lemon blueberry ricotta cake. It was very dense and not very moist. The texture was similar to a dry pound cake, so I wouldn't order that again. The apple tart was good. The apples had a great buttery cinnamon taste that you would expect with apple pie. The crust was crunchy and crispy. It seemed as though they sautéed diced fresh apples with cinnamon, sugar and butter upon order and had housemade prepared tart shells that they filled upon order. Not mad at that, the apples were hot and the crust stayed crispy because of this.

All in all, I enjoyed my experience at Cobalt Smoke and Sea. The environment is beautiful, the customer service was outstanding, and the food was delicious with the exception of a couple of things, which may have been more personal preference than anything. There is still plenty on the menu that I would like to try and I can see coming back to this restaurant within the next 30 days.
