text:
This is a decent service plaza on the southbound New Jersey Turnpike. The parking lot is very spacious, it was clean and free of debris when we visited on our way back to Virginia from Maine.  

There is a large food court inside with plenty of seating if your wish to dine in. On our visit around 6PM on a Friday the area was kind of messy with some dirty tables. The area was mostly empty with only a few tables occupied with diners.  We got some chicken, curly fries and a burger from Roy Rogers then some coffee to go from Starbucks. The chicken wasn't too good, I'm sure it had been sitting under the heat lamps for a good while. The burger was okay but certainly nothing special though I did appreciate the Roy's Fixin's Bar which allowed me to put exactly what I wanted (lettuce, tomato, onions, pickles, mayo, ketchup) on my burger. Service at Roy's was pretty lackluster with the employees seeming mostly disinterested in what they were doing. The gentleman that rang us up was fine with us but I caught him rolling his eyes at the customer ahead of us when the thoughtless patron took her food but left her tray on the counter. Coffee from Starbuck's was good though the service was not great. I stood for a full minute or so before I was acknowledged and had my order taken. I was kind of disappointed when I opened my cup to add sweetener and creamer and discovered my cup was only about 2/3rds full. 

In addition to Roy Rogers and Starbucks there is a Nathan's Famous, Auntie Anne's, Carvel Ice Cream and Cinnabon. There is also a small convenience store/ gift chop where you can pick up a New Jersey souvenir, snacks, beverages, food to go and other basic items you would expect to find in a convenience store. There are vending machines outside and a state lottery vending machine inside. Restrooms were clean and properly stocked on our visit and the number of Sunoco gas pumps outside was adequate for the traffic. Access into and out of the service plaza is easy.
name: Terry

text: I get the appeal, I just don't totally share it. Idk, everything was tasty and the place felt clean. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Honestly, the host got us seated quickly, which i appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. So yeah, the ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but i still finished most of it. maybe I just came on an off day.
name: User

text: My experience could not have got any better here.  The breadsticks with garlic and mozzarella were fresh out of the oven and they didn't skimp on marinara which was greatly appreciated!  Pizza was nice and hot and delicious.  Service was top notch . We went next door and grabbed a beer. They brought our food over when it was ready.  Very pleased with this establishment.  Ignore the subpar reviews and try it yourself! Would love to see what you think.
name: Bryant

text: The place is awesome. Spicy chipotle beef is awesome. Best chips and spicy salsa in Indianapolis. Love this place
name: Martin

text: This place used to be good back in the day, but they just don't care now.  We hadn't ordered from them in a while, so we got it tonight and it was pretty much borderline burnt, flavorless and way overpriced!  If you're in the Beech Grove area/on the southeast side and want a good pizza, order from Wild Card Pizza.
name: Casey

text: Hmmm. Expected more. Haven't been to White Dog anywhere in a long time and the stream of people clamoring for tables would give me some indication that the food is good. That was not the case in our dinner. Over cooked chicken with too much sauce. Stringy bits of beef in the Thai noodles with chopped lettuce as filler. Sad dinner. The best parts were the tuna tartare and the oysters. Hard to screw up raw fish and raw shellfish. I was expecting more, something high quality. I really try to write positive reviews all the time but there wasn't anything here to make me swoon. I doubt we will return to any locations. There are much better options locally.

text: The fries were probably the best part of the meal, honestly. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. I got the chicken bowl and it was filling, though the rice could have used a bit more seasoning. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Idk, the sauces helped more than i thought they would.. text: The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. By the time the food came out I was already annoyed. Probably not coming back. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Would probably stop in again if nearby. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day..
name: User

text: This is our second visit in as many months,  and it's our last. At the first, they served rotten mussels.  I expect to find one bad mussel every few servings.  Every 3rd was bad or rotten! I sent it back. My halibut was edible but undistinguished.  Last night I had "Sashimi". It was really seared tuna, which was ok but not what it was titled. My companion had bang bang shrimp,  which was crisp, fresh, and nicely cooked.  Server was pleasant,  friendly,  but was in a rush to get our order well before drinks were served.  Chop sticks had to be requested for tuna.  Had to hunt down server on first visit to get the check.  The bathroom was discussing!!! One stall had unflushed feces, the other needed cleaning and didn't have toilet paper, just cocktail napkins.  Trash was overflowing.  Even if the wait staff washed after using,  I have concerns for what food they handled.  I will never ever return.

text:
Foods decent for the price, beverage ok for happy hour - a double pour in a tall glass, sporty vibe is good. 

The waitress was awkward  - the chips were fresher than her personality. It would have been quicker to distill our own vodka for our refills. :-(

text: Service was spotty. Falafel appetizer was excellent. Chicken Saffron Curry was bland and served room temperature. Ambience was okay but loud and a bit drafty. It wasn't bad but not memorably good...

text: Love the unexpected customer service. As a national name brand it's easy to miss the little things. This location definitely understands how much the little things mean. Pizza is good. Atmosphere is good.

text: It's really sad but this place has really gone down hill. It was such an amazing place to go food was delicious. It seems like now it's just your regular diner now. No where near impressed anymore

text:
Walk in and presentation is nice, their menu is a little busy and a lot of options. -cool if you like options... however, I'm a firm believer you perfect a smaller menu people won't need that many options. Okay back to the Rush. They have a fresh peanut machine - that's cool. text: Best fried chicken I have ever tasted! They should seriously consider selling that spicey honey. Drove up from Bloomington with a few of my friends who are from Jamaica, Aruba, and Nepal and they all agreed that this place makes the best FC!

text: The food was great, tasty and appropriately seasoned: 2 dz oysters, jalapeno lobster bisque, lobster tail, mahi mahi with crab with mushrooms & fries, rockfish with salad & asparagus, chocolate layered cake and keylime pie. Portions of food were a nice size. Beverages: sparkling wine, LI Ice tea and mojito- mojito was a little on the weakside, Service was good and server was friendly. Nice peaceful sea decor. Can accommodate large groups. Should have made reservations because we had a 45min wait.

text:
We were excited to try this for a Birthday dinner. I noticed it was a little (not a lot, but a little) cheaper than the typical (fogo) brazilian places.. So perhaps I should have lowered my expectations..

We tried Rodizio out after wanting to for a special event for some time. I don't think we will try it again, for the price point we could have enjoyed a great steak dinner at most restaurants. The table has only one green/red indicator so it was pressure on anyone who wanted to try some more meat... once it's green there is a tidal wave of skewers coming at all people in the party, it interrupted any conversations and everyone got super uncomfortable after the first or second wave. I've been to some brazilian places before that you just flipped yours, no pressure and interruption on the table, and the servers would quietly come and offer. We essentially turned it over twice collectively and didn't want to interrupt each other again.... ultimately we didn't eat much of the meat. They give you a tiny sliver each time, so with avoiding the meat barrage we also lost out. As far as the food goes: All of the meat selections tasted exactly the same. Ironically my husband's any my favorite dish was a slow cooked pot roast, so not grilled lol. The salad bar was not very fresh (bagged lettuce that you could tell was old...just cut up some romaine hearts!) and was super small for such a large restaurant full of people. Not an awful experience, but to us, not worth the price point when you think of the nice cut of meat you could have gotten elsewhere for $40. You live you learn :)
name: Nicole

text: Honestly I think I ordered the wrong thing. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. Honestly, the tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than i pictured from the photos. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Their ribs are absolutely amazing and fall right off the bone.  Then when you think it can't possibly get any better you taste their parsley potatoes and think you've died and gone to heaven!  I have been coming to Kojaks for over 10 years and making the drive of 40 minutes each time because it is SO worth it!  You should try it too!  Beware though once you try it nothing else will compare!

text: Nomad is definitely my favorite place to go during SIPS if I'm looking to eat. $6-8 pizzas, $5-6 drinks - what more can you ask for? Their pizzas are absolutely delicious too. Would highly recommend the spicy soppressata (we ordered a spicy sausage instead but glad this one came instead). They were very liberal with the toppings which I appreciate and compared to the sausage, the meat just covers more surface area. I came in two Wednesdays ago and there were 2 large parties that had made reservations :( Luckily, there were 5 spots at the pizza bar and my party of 2 fit cozily there. I didn't even know there was a pizza bar and it was so nice that we got to see how the pizzas were made while enjoying them ourselves! I really liked that aspect and it was farther away from the window where there was hot air coming in the restaurant. The restaurant is a pretty small space, but their service is very quick, waiters and waitresses are very prompt and attentive. Would highly recommend that you try this out for SIPS and maybe I'll even be back to try them when it's not just SIPS :) Keep up the good work Nomad! We love you

text:

Service was a 5 but the food was a 3.

text:
My boyfriend and I had brunch here today and it was great. We wanted to sit outside with our dog and the hostess cleared a table and got us seated right away. We had the breakfast burrito and chicken with waffles, both were delicious. Also our server's name was Evan and he was super friendly/entertaining!

I don't write reviews very often but felt compelled to after our experience today. The restaurant was super busy and they were clearly short staffed which unfortunately happens sometimes. But still they were all super fast and courteous the entire time. The only thing that made this a poor experience was a table of 6 drunk idiots sitting next to us who were hands down the most obnoxious group of people imaginable. They were loud, obscene and spent the entire time harassing the servers. I felt awful for everyone who had to deal with them including us so to any of you working that day who may see this, just know there were people who saw how hard you tried. They just suck.

text: Sushi and service were excellent! The ordering process was a bit confusing for us first timers. Although we had researched the menu prior to arriving for lunch, we thought we could order with ease. However, the menu was written in various formats on different sections on the walls and leaning against the counter. It was hard to follow and decide what we had wanted. Once we did, it wasn't really clear how exactly we were supposed to order. Do we seat ourselves and someone would take our order, or do we place our order at the counter/ cashier. Finally, a very friendly member of the staff directed us to order from the counter. At that point, we paid, and were given a table number so our food could be brought to us when ready. Smooth sailing from then on, as our meals were prepared perfectly and the waiter, who had also taken our order was very attentive. The Sushi was beyond fresh and this will definitively become a frequently visited restaurant now that we're familiar with the menu and ordering process.
name: Gerrianne

text: My boyfriend and I were out in Tucson visiting from out of state, and we were recommended this great burger place for dinner. I can't tell you how impressed I was. Amazing food, and great service. Our waiter was Dylan and he was fantastic! Fast, friendly, and super informative. There are so many different types of burgers to choose from and they come with a large side, enough to feed 3 people. I wish they had restaurants in California!

text: The service was great, food choices for a vegetarian and a vegan were decent and the food was delicious!

text: I don't know what to say on this one, its a different feeling and atmosphere.  Its Saturday and beautiful outside so my friend and i head to the Valenzano winery in Shamong NJ.  While there we here about the Sharrott Winery.  So after finishing up we go there.  When we arrive there are cars parked everywhere and the outdoors are very nice with mumms.  We enter and the place is big.  There is a front greeting test where you are told of the prices and a brief history on what is offered.  There is also a full kitchen with menu and a dining area with a waiting list to sit.  There is also a bar in the middle where you can sit, enjoy wine and eat.  This is what we opted to do.  We had a warm bottle of cider and split the 3 beef taco order.  The wine was good and the taco's were amazing I could have eaten a lot more.  There were at least 100 people there mostly between 25 and 35 years of age.  All in all a nice place however I prefer the old wood winery's with outdoor seating and not that many people.  If you like to hangout drink wine and eat then this place is a must.

text:
Simply delicious.

Accommodated our large group for lunch.  The service was great and the food terrific.  Cool neighborhood, too.

text: We are new to Tampa and came across this place on Yelp! There was no wait and we were seated immediately. It was a really cool vibe inside and the music was awesome. We order the fried chicken app and 2 different ramen bowls for lunch, and it was good! The broth was fine and all the fix-ins were tasty. The service was also super super nice and suggested some other good restaurants in the Seminole Heights area. Would go back!
name: Kimberly

text:
I had bookmarked Saltine because it's really close to my hotel and because the seafood looked really good. I had a larger breakfast, so I didn't want to overeat at lunch. I got the tuna poke bowl with micro greens and 3 raw gulf oysters. The oysters were so good; fresh, briny and went superb with their house cocktail sauce and some Louisiana hot sauce. The tuna poke bowl was also very tasty with ahi tuna, edamame, avocado, pickled veggies, dressing and greens. It was the perfect, not to heavy lunch I was craving! I went at an odd time so don't read into the emptiness of the place in my photos. I'm sure this place gets comfortably busy during peak dining hours. If you're in Nashville and craving seafood, this place is great.

Update: the oysters were so good I had to come back for more at dinner. The gulf oysters are half off for happy hour! So worth it!
name: Adam

text:
Living just down the road from Holler & Dash, I can't believe it's taken me this long to try out this biscuit-house spawn of Cracker Barrel. 

I ordered the "Chicken Holler" biscuit "hot" style. The biscuit itself was good. Maybe not the best I've had, but it was good. The chicken was a little smaller than I expected, but it was still filling. I wasn't a fan of the hot sauce used. It left a slightly bitter aftertaste that I wasn't expecting. I think I'll stick with the plain fried version next time.

While the biscuit was good, the cheese grits were amazing. Tip: take a biscuit half and top it with cheese grits. You'll thank me later.

And as a nitro-brew coffee fanatic, I couldn't leave without trying a glass. While pricey, it was just as delicious as I was hoping it would be: strong and slightly bitter with a layer of froth at the top.

Another highlight of my visit was the staff: everyone was incredibly friendly with employees (manager included) routinely checking on us and asking how we were doing and if we needed anything.

There were several other sandwiches, entrees and sides that caught my eye as I was looking through the menu, so I'll definitely return to Holler & Dash to explore more.
name: John

text: Got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. Honestly, the leftovers held up okay the next day.. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything.. The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. idk I'd try something else next time.
name: User

text: We had a really good time here. They were very accommodating with a group of 16 and we didn't wait at all for our reservation. My only complaint is 6 people in our group ordered their bloody mary and got sick the entire afternoon - I think the mix was bad! Other than that, it was great service and super spicy chicken!
name: Rachel

text:
First time back after it had originally been Flying Fish. Was visiting my sister and we had tickets to the Bill and Hillary Clinton event at the Met and figured we would head here for dinner.

Great place, great ambiance. There were pool tables and couches and a bar on the lower level near the hostess stand. We were seated upstairs in the larger area. It was packed, lots of people there watching the Sixers game and the Masters. Typical for what you would expect for a Saturday night 5:00. We were promptly greeted, our drink orders were taken, and we were given our food. Total time there was about an hour 15 mins.

Good beer selection. Also they have wines on draft which I did not try this time but plan to on my next visit. We ordered the mild wings, tots with bacon, and we split the cheesesteak. The wings were decent. Well sauced and well seasoned. The tots with bacon: life changing. The bacon was perfectly crisp, the cheese was melted and the chipotle aioli added a smoky flavor. I would eat these all day every day. The cheesesteak was uniquely flavored with a teriyaki kind of taste. There were caramelized onions and some mushrooms which added a bit of extra yummy-ness to the steak. I would have preferred a bit more cheese to have been mixed through the steak, but there is always room for improvement.

I immediately messaged my friend from Fishtown about this place and told her it is an absolute yes, that she needs to try it out. My mouth is literally watering as I write all of this thinking about the tots.
name: Christine

text:
To start, our service was really great. Our waitress was attentive and the hostess was nice enough. The atmosphere is cheerful and 'puby.'

The food was a bit of a different ballgame. We came here because I was craving just a quick and average brunch bite.  Drake isn't quite that place as it turns out. If you know that saying that if you keep your expectations low, you won't be disappointed.  This is exactly the attitude you should adopt here. My breakfast burger was a mess. Honestly, I've had better food from fast food joints than that atrocity.  The menu description was clearly not written (or maybe even seen) by the person putting together the sandwich because it was just one giant clash. The menu described a well balanced dish with complementary flavors, the actual thing was blobs of maple syrup and a sorry excuse for a patty slapped together as an afterthought.  Why kid yourself and write a poem in the menu when you're really serving a fist timer's prose.  They also forgot my side of latkas but the waitress was great about checking in on us as soon as the food was dropped and bringing these out in no time (they're from a box btw, nothing to write home about). 
The 2nd and Allegheny burger represented pub fare in a more agreeable manner. Average and easy to choke down with a beer and crispy fries. That's where you should keep your expectations.
name: Kasia

text: Close this location please. Nuggets were burned and cold. Quarter pounder with cheese, bun was dry and hard as a rock, like if it was sitting outside the whole night. I went there at 2pm by the way and the employees looked bothered, didn't want to serve me and not a single greeting. Shut this location down.
name: Sahil

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. No big complaints, just a nice meal. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. A very pleasant experience.
name: User

text: Pretty smooth experience from start to finish. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. Not bad for a quick meal. The menu wasn't huge, which I usually prefer.. For the price I expected more than this. Food was good and came out fast. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price..

text: Dude just go here!  It's awesome. If there's a line, ask if Bob is working, if he is then wait. If he isn't still wait cause the experience is that good.  Order abita purple haze beer and anything on the menu just get a side of rabbit and chicken Jambalaya it was so tender and so good. Mouthwatering. text:
This place was quite the trip, I'll tell ya.  Before coming here, I heard some opinions on the place.  One person told me, "Food is great, service is terrible."  Another person said, "It's red sauce slop and everyone calls you 'hun'."  So I wasn't surprised when we walked into this tiny corner joint on a Saturday night (with an 8:00 reservation, mind you), and weren't seated until after 8:30.  Right off the bat, I should've realized what it was gonna be like when me and my 2 guests entered through the bar and stood, very tightly and awkwardly between the bar and cocktail tables, next to a 4 person party also waiting for a table.  We were then told to go in the back door to the dining room, which we did.  We stood there, very much in the way, for about 2 minutes before the bus boy told us to go back to the bar area.  We spent the next half hour watching both the frazzled bejeweled bartender and the server zip in and out of the back dining room, answering the phone, consulting the ancient reservation notebook, shouting out things like "I'll get you your wine, don't you worry!" and "You're next, I PROMISE!" to, low and behold, the OTHER 3 person party waiting for their table at the other end of the bar who I didn't see prior.

It was a shitshow, to say the least.  Giving them the benefit of the doubt, I chalked it up to them being busier than normal.  Everyone, including the bus boys, was in the weeds.  After trying and failing to hide my hunger and impatience, the bartender told us that the first round of wines we had while waiting were on the house, which was really sweet of her.  We finally were seated after she informed us that the party before us took much longer than expected to leave after finishing their meal.  At this point, I was just happy to have water and bread and oil for dipping.

The meal was also kind of frantic as far as service goes.  She was really nice, just very busy, so we didn't see her much for things like water refills or missing silverware.  We ordered everything up front so we didn't have to wait even longer.  Menu is a good size, not overwhelming, not limited.  Just right, with Italian and BBQ sections.

For starters, we got 2 orders of the bruschetta to split, then a house salad each.  Bruschetta was DOPE, probably my favorite part of the meal.  Salads were better than regular house salads, with a nice helping of freshly shaved parmesan, although the mess hall style plastic plates were meh).  Entrees were BBQ ribs & fries, classic spaghetti & meatballs, and mussels & linguine in a red sauce (LOVE that you can choose between white or red sauce for any of the pasta entrees).  Everything sounded enticing, but my mussels and linguine were a great choice - I'm happy I went with my gut on that one.

"Slop" is kinda right - presentation is definitely lacking (it's more like Sunday at grandma's house) - but my massive soupy bowl of linguine in red fishy broth and second large bowl of delicious steamy mussels made up for the wait.  My cousin loved her half rack of ribs (my BF and I tried them and loved the sauce), but unfortunately, my BF wasn't crazy about his spaghetti & meatballs.  The sauce was almost as watery as my fishy broth (we expected a thicker gravy) and the meatballs were just okay.

For dessert, the waitress said "I have the last apple pie" and I said 'oh that sounds good.'  She brought it right out, which was nice, but I was kinda hoping we would've been able to see a dessert menu first, at the very least.  

Ambiance is very South Philly corner joint and with one less table would feel less cramped (my cousin got stuck in the bad seat literally touching the bathroom door), but prices are more than reasonable for the portion.  I went in with high expectations, thinking perhaps it would be the best hole in the wall Italian food, service aside.  It was good, but not oh my god amazing, which is what I anticipated.  I'd visit back only if I was in the area.
name: Andrea

We all agreed while sitting in Angelo's "It's like being in a nightmare."

It took so long for the waitress to bring the check we had to ask the nonchalant hostess (manager?) for the check. text:
**RACIALLY PROFILED** Before people say, "Oh, he's pulling the race," listen to my story and tell me how you would have felt. On July 30, I decided to go to Datsa Pizza. I had been there once before for a carryout order and had cordial service. I'm a 34 year old black man who was dressed in a light blue, short sleeved, button-down shirt, dark wash blue jeans and wingtip brown dress shoes. The older blonde haired white woman with glasses and her hair in a ponytail, who waited on me the last time, was the server. Initially, she thought I was another patron who was picking up an order and was advertised on a flyer posted on the door. I clarified that she was mistaken and that I was, in fact,  wanting to dine-in. 

She asked me if I was dining-in or getting my order to go. I said that I was dining-in. Instead of escorting me to a table with a menu in hand as most hostesses and waitresses do, she rang my order at the counter and told me to "go ahead and pay now." I thought how odd and that is not how dine-in procedure is done unless at a buffet restaurant. I sat down and waited for me meatball sub sandwich. Two white men were seated and enjoying their meals and each other's company. Soon they got up, I assumed to leave, but no they were paying. She knew his name was Mike and addressed him as such and he paid by credit card. 

As Mike was paying, a white female patron came in and sat down. The same hostess brought over a menu and asked her if she was dining-in. The woman said yes. I'm still eating my sandwich and noticed that she did not ask the woman to pay first or Mike and his friend to pay first. Why was I treated differently than those white patrons? My money is just as green and worthy. I will not be back! I was polite, courteous, well-mannered even said ma'am to her and didn't have to. These microaggressions against people of color have become more noticeable in recent times. She judged me as a black man and, I assume, she felt I would dine and dash or something. I don't truly know her reasoning but I am an American citizen and a person. I have a right to be treated with dignity and respect as she does. In closing, I am not a criminal, a freak, a drug dealer or gang member. I am a man, a 4.0 honor student in college who is on the Dean's List and Honor Roll. Most of all, I am a HUMAN BEING! Love thy neighbor as thyself... I just hope she is a better person to the next black patron or ANY patron than she was to me! #dinewithdignity
name: Adrienne

text:
Wow. WOW. The pedicure at the Atlantis Spa is the best pedicure I've ever had. If at all possible ask for Jamie specifically. She typically does hair, but if your lucky enough to grab her for a pedicure hold on and never let go. She's been doing this for 25 years, and it shows in everything she does with her magic hands. Her treatment of my legs and feet felt borderline godlike. She touched and activated muscles I didn't know I had, and as a result, I floated out of the salon like a finely tuned violin. I turned into an extremely gratified human puddle, I felt liquefied, which I've never been for associated with a pedicure. I came for the spa day pass (which is 100 percent worth it for the brine room), and the pedicure was an afterthought. A ticket to the brine room if you will. No longer! 
This was my first time visiting the Atlantis even though its rated the best spa in the Reno area. I go to Mirage or Soak to relax. The Atlantis is a little pricey for a casual visit and is made to be a full day retreat. The Spa comes equipped with the typical day spa amenities with a few cool add-ons to make the experience feel more intimate to the customers. My group and I found ourselves giggling like children over the tropical shower and the cedarwood sauna (which has a bowl and ladle inside to pour water over the hot coals if your that kind of sadist.) 
Unfortunately, it looked like they were getting work done as the showers and steam sauna weren't working when we were there, but showers were available at our request in another room away from the spa. The snacks were pretty common health spa fair, but they have many beverage options. In almost all the themed rooms there was a choice of flavored water from apple cinnamon to grapefruit, plus tea in a lounge area. My liver was screaming thank you for the mini detox it ended up getting. Overall it was a great day. I spent 10 hours floating around and enjoyed everything that makes this Spa the best in Reno. It's got to be the best Spa Day experience around, and for all that its worth, this is the most couple friendly day spa in reno due to all the facilities people can partake in together.

text: Wow that was some flavorful Mexican! The vegetables quesadillas were AMAZING. chicken fajitas were also really good. Table side guacamole was alright. Very friendly staff. I would definitely recommend this place
name: Swati

text:
Wonderful food. I have been here many times both to eat in and to take out. I'm glad to have a few more options in the neighborhood besides burgers. 

The staff is friendly and warm. They only have 3-4 tables. So it is mostly a Carry our situation but if you are able to dine in you are well taken care of. 

It's a great little oasis under the EL train. 
We will be back soon.
name: nic

text:
I had my special girl's birthday party here last night. Lindsey and her staff were great and I thank them all for making it a wonderful evening.
I certainly would recommend having any event here and it is dog friendly!
name: Donald

text:
I was very surprised by this place. It's not as big as I thought it was going to be, but I actually liked that it was smaller. When we walked in, we were greeted by a friendly hostess and were walked over to our table. I really liked the concept of being served and being able to order from our waitress from all of the restaurants available inside of the ha
I have to admit, a bit overwhelming with all of the selections, but we pounded through the menus and decided on three different types of Stinky Bunz...Chinese bbq pork, Red curry chicken and shrimp. YUM! 
Then we moved onto our entrees. My boyfriend had the Grouper BLT and I had the Poke Rose bowl. Whatever type of seasoning they used to grill the Grouper with, was extremely salty and overpowered the flavor of the fish and sandwich all together. My Poke Rose bowl was delicious. We will definitely be back to try some more of the food. Next time, we will plant ourselves at the bar.
name: Nicole

text: The lunch menu is such a deal! I got the General Tsos Chicken which comes with your choice of rice and your choice of soup. All tasted great and service was decent as well. I would go again for the great prices!
name: Jennifer

text:
I stopped by to pick up some fish spread to take home. The service was very friendly and had a fun relaxed outside atmosphere. 
The fish spread was good but, tasted very sweet and had a lot of relish and onions. I've never had fish spread prepared this way. It tasted more like tuna salad. I wouldn't get it again but, I would go try something else though.
name: Jessica

text: Food was amazing again as I stopped in for lunch for a second time and I was more pleased this time around ! Maybe one of my new regular spots !
name: Fred

text: Absolutely love this place! Great food, great service, great vibe. Intimate, cool, chill - would come here every day if I could - for the good time but also for the food! The pan-fried dumplings are amazeballs - the only thing better are the mussels! I would drink that broth! So good!
name: Kelly

text: Usually have pretty decent service here but today was lacking. After 15 mins of placing my order the staff were having a debate over my order and who was suppose to make it, then blaming each other. It took 18 mins to get my sub which only left me 12 mins to eat ajd get back to work when there were only 6 people in front of me. Quality was on par with what I come to expect. Wait time was the only issue.
name: Ian

text:
So I'll start by saying I did not eat here   
We went to music row happy hour to see buzz brainard (if you don't know how who he is good neither did i, he's the host of a Sirus country radio station). 
So I we waited about an hour around 3:30pm to get upstairs to see the show. We finally got in and it was packed. The energy was pumping.  It reminded me of like a college game day broadcast. People are drinking, dancing and eating. 
We were on a bachelorette party and they picked us to go live on the show.  It was a great experience for the bride!
name: Tiffany

text: One of the best places to get BBQ for sure! There is a reason why you better get your orders in early in the day before dinner because the good stuff(burnt ends, ribs, etc) always sells out fast! That should tell you there just how good the place really is! I definitely recommend giving this place a try if you haven't already! Don't forget to get a side of potato salad too!!
name: Avonlea

text: Came here for a birthday dinner with family. They served us very quick and the food was even better. The rib meat come off the bones and the cornbread is delicious! Good spot for big groups
name: Pedro

text: DO NOT STAY IN THIS FILTHY HOTEL!  I cannot begin to explain how disappointed we are with this hotel.  We came to town for the Essence Festival.  Booked through a travel group and was told we would be in a room with two queen beds.  Arrived to the room to find one bed and one couch.  The room was FILTHY!  Dust everywhere.  Food trays left in the hallway for over 2 days.  Stains in the bathtub.  Extra linens were balled up in the closet.  Dust on the furniture was so bad that the two people with allergies were coughing & sick the entire first night. Microwave & carpet were filthy.  We thought it may have only been our room but when we got back down to the lobby, there were numerous people with the same complaints.  The room was so bad that we decided to leave after only two nights when we were booked for five nights forfeiting over $1000.  It was just that bad!  We were so disappointed!  We are from Dallas and the Embassy Suites in Dallas is a totally different experience!  The Essence Festival happens every year on the same exact weekend!  The management of this hotel knew that these rooms needed to be cleaned well in advance of the arrival of thousands of women, but chose to put people in filthy rooms.  Their reputation will certainly suffer after this weekend!
name: Nikki

text: Best place. Used to go as family as kids in Springfield location. That was a place where my parents as teenagers went on dates.
name: Michele

text:
Went 20m before closing time on Friday 16th, only think I can have was a 
 and a donut, everything else was out of menu because they was "almost closing ".
name: Blas

text: We went to celebrate a birthday and it's was a mistake to come here. I wouldn't come back even if it were free. Service was beYond poor. we waited 25 mins to be seated in an empty restaurant. The hostess did say that the manager would take care of us but that didn't happen. The entire  restaurant was extremely cold it was a bit uncomfortable our waitress brought the wrong wine out and the chef delivers flavorless food and the fried rice  had lots of hard crunchy pieces. This was a big let down  Benihana is the McDonald's of the habitchi grills.

text:
Fallon is a great bartender. I really appreciated her knowledge and expertise on the beer list. 
The brunch menu is pretty great, albeit a bit on the expensive side. $17 for chix and waffles is a bit extra. However, I will say it is probably the best chix and waffles I've ever had. Also, the the poutine with eggs was also bomb.com. 
The space is fantastic! The games are fun!

text: Best poké in the area! I'm a big fan of the Gangnam Spicy Tuna bowl. I've also tried the Truffle Yellowtail and the Smoki Poki, but I always go back to my favorite. They also do custom bowls. Great stuff!
name: Joseph

text: So good! Beautiful view! Food is great highly recommend crab cakes. Reminds me of the one in Hawaii! And Duke's is right next door.
name: Mackenzie

text: The restaurant was very busy, but we got our food relatively quickly. Our attendant had to be reminded a couple of times for water, but no big deal Everything was tasty. What you would expect from a chain restaurant.
name: Jo

text: Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. It was crowded but still moved along. Not cheap exactly, but not ridiculous either. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. Glad we tried it. It looked better in person than in the online photos, weirdly enough.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus..
name: User

text: There food is delicious! Even though I'm not a huge burger fan, they have many other options which are equally as good. The service can be under staffed sometimes though.
name: Taylor

text: While they're still one of the best bakeries in the area, they are skimping on the cupcakes and sticky bun size and icing.  My mom is in the grave right now Flippin mad ( god rest her soul ).  You can't do that to her or my cupcakes or sticky buns.  My word of advice is don't change the product, change the price.
name: Glen

text: Really disappointed.  Service was the worst I have ever experienced.  Came her with a couple of friends and one was a vegetarian.  She ordered the mixed cold appetizers as her entree.  Our entree of kababs and moussaka came out before hers. We were almost done eating our meals when it finally came to the table.  Seriously cannot believe that a plate of cold appetizers would take longer than ours.  I would understand if they were busy but there were only 3 other tables.  Would even give them another chance if the food was good.  Everything we had was bland.  Only decent dish was the lavash bread which is the only reason I gave this place 2 stars instead of 1.
name: Michelle

text: The sandwich was fine, not bad, just not something I'm still thinking about two days later. The food was good and the service was easygoing. The host got us seated quickly, which I appreciated because we didn't have a reservation. It was crowded but still moved along. Price felt a touch high for what it was. Worth checking out. They were out of one thing I originally wanted.. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text:
Serious such a wonderful place, it's a hidden Gem that much people doesn't seem to know about. I love the food court the food is 10x better than the food court at the mall.

I'm honestly not a fan of the regular " stores " that inside just because the prices are ridiculous. We stopped at one of the stores that sold beautiful evening dresses for special occasions and outing and we asked how much for one of the dress & she said $220. Trust me that was NOT worth $220 & it's not even a name brand you know. But anywhooo I just said thanks and kept on walking. 

Now back to the food. Worth it. It was from "Guachos" I think that how it's spelled. In one of the order with the fried steak they brought it and it had a huge slice of ham & I don't eat pork so I went back and told them & they fairly told the chef about it and he said he would change it and make a new one, but honestly I was paranoid that he was going to give me back the same steak and he was only going to take the pork off so I stood and watched and he told me not to be worried that he threw the whole meal away and I didn't believe until he went and get the garbage can to show me & with all this he was smiling and being kind apologizing & I was so happy to be recovering that energy. 
 Well we enjoyed everything and I left a nice tip for them. I will definitely be going back. Also the gyro spot is very affordable & their fried Wings are the Bomb

text: Had brunch here over the weekend and it was kind of a mixed bag. The staff was professional and attentive throughout the meal. Portions were generous and presentation was nice. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. The restaurant was clean, organized, and running smoothly. Food quality was consistent across everything we ordered. A very pleasant experience. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean.
name: User

text: My favorite hotpot in philly! Everything is delicious, and I can't wait to come back each time.
name: Elizabeth

text: The Horse is a great place to get a bite to eat on campus since it is a sit-down restaurant. Great place to go on weeknights (especially Wednesdays) when they have drink specials. Very disappointed they took waffle fries off the menu, though.
name: Sarah

text: Update: In recent months, quality has gone down, as well as fewer options and less turnover while at the buffet. They were going strong for a while, but now all of the saucy dishes are overly sweet and not as fresh as they used to be.  Used to love this place, but I'm finding myself wanting other places nearby (or *gasp* New Jersey) instead.
name: Gloria

text:
Popped in here for a quick and inexpensive breakfast. I opted for the scrambler: scrambled eggs, bacon, tater tots, cheese, and tomatoes in a cup for $4. It took about 10 minutes so it's not the ideal place to grab breakfast when you get off the train and you're on your way to work. The place is in Suburban Station and I found it to be a little grimey - sticky floors, crumbs on counters, etc. The staff however was kind and attentive to customers.

The scrambler was just alright. It was oily and I regretted not asking for salt and pepper because it lacked flavor. The bacon was well cooked and not the soggy kind you can expect from Dunkin. I wouldn't come back here for breakfast. I've had a grilled cheese from here which was solid so it's a 3-star spot.
name: Priscilla

text: Okay,...my first time here. I ordered a double cheeseburger with lettuce tomatoes pickles with regular fries and drink. 10 or 15 minutes later... A server brought over exactly what I ordered to my table. Halfway through my meal a different server stopped by to ask if everything was okay and if I needed anything. My only slight issue was that my fries were not as hot as I would have liked them to be, however my burger was nice and hot. This location was clean with a very nice decor. All in all it was a nice Pit Stop to refuel between my shopping and movie. All the customer service I purposely encountered was both courteous and professional. Good job guys..... I'll be back.

text: Service was excellent however broth lacked complexity. Still, food was fast, hot, and good. Accommodated my picky boyfriend well.

text: I like that instead of the traditional chips and salsa they serve something else out the menu. Food was tasty, inside is pleasant and so is the cook.

My boyfriend and I ate tried individual slices of pepperoni and sausage, and it was Delicious . Make sure you grab some extra napkins, because the slices are huge.
name: Rae

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. Ordering was easy but pickup took about ten extra minutes past the quoted time. The tacos tasted fresh enough, just smaller than I pictured from the photos. The wait wasn't awful, just longer than I expected for the time of day.. Anyway, the sauces helped more than i thought they would.. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. For a busy night they handled it okay. not sure I'd order the same thing again.
name: User

text: A small group of us went for a late lunch and cocktails. The drinks were amazing and the food was even better. We split 5-6 of the small plates between 3 of us, including the burrata, the oysters (so good we re-ordered them), the meatballs, and the tuna. Highly recommend!
name: Emily

text:
CASH ONLY!! Its a great restaurant on the water. Good service and good food. We had a delicious burger and seasoned fries for lunch. 
Its not a fancy place. Its your typical beach bar and grill, which was exactly what we were looking for. 
They don't take credit or debit cards so make sure you have cash.

text: The wait was longer than it should've been for a pretty normal dinner service. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. The fries were hot and crisp but the burger itself was a little messy and kept sliding apart. Inside is casual and a little cramped, but not in a terrible way. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. It landed in that middle zone where you expect a little more but not a lot more.

text: Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. The staff seemed tired but still polite. For a busy night they handled it okay. Worth checking out. Everything came out hot and the staff was friendly. Food was fresh and service was quick. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.
name: User

text: This place is SO good! They have a crazy amount of options on the menu and the prices can't be beat. I paid around $6 for a specialty roll of sushi which is pretty much unheard of in my experience. The wait staff was super attentive and our food was at our  table in a matter of minutes. This is my new go to!
name: Cassidy

text: Great selection of beer to include sours and wine.  Atmosphere and food are outstanding.   Lits of TVs to choose from.
name: Kimberly

text:
Saigon Deli is exactly what it should be - delicious food, served simply. From pho and various other noodle dishes to bubble teas and banh mi, there's something for every appetite and budget. Even meatless options are available, and quite filling as well! Service is prompt and direct and atmosphere is function over form; order your choice of delights from the extensive menu at your table then take your check up to the register, or if you're ordering takeout queue slightly awkwardly to one side of the front while you wait (not too long!) for the magic.

Prices are competitive and the food is simple but delightful, which means Saigon Deli often gets full fast at peak times and the same goes for the parking lot. If you can get there before the lunch rush it's a good idea, but the wait usually isn't substantial and the food, while not trendy or stylishly Pinterest-perfect, is definitely worth it. Many culinary gems are hidden away in otherwise bland strip malls and this is no exception, so don't be put off by looks - here, you can take your palate on a trip without having to deal with the Tampa airport!
name: Julia

text:
Came here on a Saturday night and it wasn't very busy. Clean and nice looking decor. 

The reason I'm giving this a 3 stars is the service was not very good. When we first arrived we saw an older couple that seemed annoyed and waiting on the server and that was our fate as well. drinks were not filled promptly and it took a very long time for us to get our order in and get our check. 

I ordered the Camarones a la Diabla. Not overly spicy but overall pretty solid and had a good size portion. My girlfriend ordered the pork nachos and they came with a TON of very good pork. after sharing both our meals we were stuffed.

This place is worth a look if you're craving Mexican. hopefully you can get better service.
name: Ryan

text:
Returning for another visit remembering how superb it was a year ago when in the area.  I was less than impressed this time and passing along my experience.
We were pleased to encounter free valet parking at this location (didn't forget to tip).  As it turns out, it poured down rain when we left so that worked out great!  We (group of 6) took advantage of the call ahead seating option and upon our arrival at 5:30 p.m. on a Saturday night, we only waited 5 minutes until Chip led us to our table.
Ryan greeted us promptly and got our drink and appetizer order.  We ordered the fried mozzarella and loved it.  
There were 3 teens with us and the menu didn't have exactly what they would eat, so Ryan worked with us to get 2 of them a create your own pasta.  The 3rd ordered the salmon that did not some out with the rest of our table's orders.  It was as if the order had been forgotten because it became awkward for all of us to wait to start our food until it arrived.  It got a thumbs up as it was gobbled down.
We had to ask for our bread which comes with the meal along with an herb paste when added with the olive oil is great dipping.
My go to dish is always the shrimp and sea scallop spiedino (coated with Italian breadcrumbs, wood-grilled and topped with lemon butter sauce) and select fettuccini alfredo as the side.  This time the breadcrumbs were a bit too charred for my taste.  I was also a bit disappointed in the portion size of the side of alfredo.  
Drinks were kept filled and if we had known the cheesecake was going to be such a large slice, we could have ordered 3 and all shared.  It was delicious, creamy and had a nice strawberry sauce on top.
Our checks were a challenge for Ryan and had to be redone 3 times to get all the items on the correct person's bill.  You cannot consider this a budget friendly place but the atmosphere is nice, the food good and there is a little bowl with mints for you to grab a couple on your way out.  :-)
name: Lynn

text: For the price I expected more than this. Our server was nice and checked in enough without hovering. The wait felt longer than it should have. I've paid more for worse meals, so I'm not mad about it. The whole meal felt kind of uneven. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. Solid food, nice staff, and not much of a wait. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. I kept going back and forth while eating it, which probably says everything..
name: User

text: Came here on a Wednesday at 7 PM for my brother-in-law's birthday, we had about 10 guests. Service was timely and the staff were polite and friendly. I tried the tikka-inspired chicken tacos and they were extremely tasty, you can't find good fusion food like that very often in Indiana. I had their American IPA (I forget the exact name of it) and it was a delicious well-balanced beer. It must've been pretty strong because just two pints were enough to get me pretty damn tipsy. I don't really live in the area so I can't see myself returning to this location, but I certainly had a nice experience!

text: This CAN NOT be NOLA's best! Bread harder than Great Depression, Gumbo watered down, like street runoff! Best item : unsweetened tea!

text: I loved my experience here! The servers were so kind, friendly, and helpful, and the sushi was delicious. There are many options for vegans/vegetarians, and you can't go wrong with whatever you get! I would definitely come back here next time I'm in town.
name: Mikaila

text:
REALLY WANTED to fall in love with this place, but I have to admit - I was disappointed. It was good, just NOT AS GOOD AS EXPECTED. To be fair, I had VERY HIGH expectations.  I consider myself to be an ice cream connoisseur & a general sugarholic. I've eaten the forbidden raw cookie dough from the sleeve & from batter I've made with pure joy (& luckily never got sick). B&J cookie dough ice cream was revolutionary & is a solid fave of mine. I got a small which allows you to do 2 scoops of your choice of dough and/or ice cream. I chose 1 scoop of each: 1 scoop of sweet & salty dough topped with 1 scoop of salted caramel pretzel ice cream. The ice cream was high quality, but no the VERY HIGHEST I've had (could have been creamier). The dough was good, but not the WOW I expected. It was too dense, which sounds ridiculous. Now
I think maybe the ratio for me was off. Maybe if I got 2 scoops of ice cream & 1 scoop of dough, making each spoonful the same ratio, I'd have been fully satisfied. I'll go back. Next time, I'm getting 2 scoops of cookie dough ice cream & 1 scoop of chocolate chip cookie dough.  I got lucky on a Thursday afternoon, securing a street parking spot, but it seems parking would be an issue.
name: Nicola

text: Excellent clean food.  Especially great on Saturday and Sunday's for brunch when they have egg bowls.
name: chris

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. The place has that neighborhood spot feel, not fancy at all. The whole meal felt kinda uneven. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Food was good and came out fast. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really.

text:

Stopped in to order to go Gyro sandwich and fries with and order of rice pilaf.
Got hone and was REALLY pleased with portion sizes and flavors.

I'll be back!!!

text:
I've been a few times now both for a sit down meal and for to go orders at Mimi's To Go. I love their meatballs and all the assortments of sauces that you can choose with it! My favorite sauces are the Sriracha Aioli, Spicy Cilantro, and Spicy Bolognese! I've never liked brussel sprouts, but have become a fan of them at Mimi's probably because they are fried! Haha As our waiter puts it, "it's like eating chips!" For a sit down meal, I'd recommend making a reservation though because they have limited seating. 

The only negative I didn't like was the price to portion ratio. For a sit down meal, you can order 4 meatballs for $12 or order individual ones for $3.50. I thought the size of the meatballs did not equate to the price and thought it was expensive.

text:

My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. Honestly, we shared dumplings first and those were prob the best thing on the table. text: Do not recommend.  Karen Stark is very rude and unprofessional.  She apparently doesnt want anyone coming to use the bathroom at her establishment,  so much that she put a hault to her meeting to let us know that it wasnt a public restroom.  We came to browse the store and check out their Thanksgiving meals. My husband just decided to use the bathroom since we were there. Made us feel very unwelcome.

text:
This is a cute, cozy little restaurant where I had dinner with my friend and her family. The restaurant is so sweet, with a real wood fireplace in the center. Now knowing this, the next time I visit this place, will try to reserve a little table near by and enjoy the warmth. 

We ordered a few appetizers and drinks during happy house (4-6pm) and were really blown away by both appetizers: grilled octopus and broccoli (and it's relatively hard to impress me with this vegetable...). I am also delighted to see that this place has a menu to accommodate vegans!  

Also the restaurant was really accommodating to my friend's 1 year old baby, which is super important for any young family! 

Overall - we had a really nice experience!
name: Lauren

text: Rated on a scale of fast food or course. My order is always accurate and the food is occasionally transcendent with everything being perfectly hot, delivered quickly, etc. It is always at least pretty good and 2 times out of 3 you will get everything hot and cooked to order. Note to Sonic: just cook everything to order and synchronize it to be served correctly and hot for any customer that isn't hurrying through the drive through. Don't make the customer ask, just do it right every time. You may waste a small amount of food but you will have better repeat business... don't be unpredictable.
name: Mace

text: My fiancé grandparents recommended this restaurant as being on of the best spots to dine and since they had a vegetarian dish I was excited to go since most steak house restaurants don't usually have that as a option, we were very dissatisfied with our visit. To start once we were sat our waitress took 7 minutes to greet us and when she did she didn't apologize for how long it took her to come over to us. We knew what we wanted so we ordered everything out of fear that we may never see her again because she was being more attentive to her tables that were older and drinking wine. Prior to the food coming she brought our bread and stated she spilled our oil and herbs that it is served with and that she would be right back, she wasn't right back in fact I had to ask another server to bring it to use to we could enjoy the bread. Finally our meal came out and my fiancé's steak was cooked medium well not medium rare. We sent it back and it was made again and brought out by the manager who asked for my fiancé to cut into it and it still was not cooked correctly, but my fiancé was so hungry he didn't care and ate it anyway. Finally once we were finished we waited another 20 min until she came back and I asked for the check which took another 5 minutes once I requested it. Once she brought the check and charged us she proceeded to tell us to drive safe on New Years and that she was rear ended in September and only got a $5,000 settlement and had she known she would have had uninsured motorist, I can't make this up. She did apologize for the steak being cooked wrong which was nice, but the rest of the terrible service can not make up for that apology. Moreover, we are foodies and go everywhere there is to go and for the price point this restaurant has the food should have been much better then it was E&E is nothing more then a glorified Outback Steakhouse. Don't waste your money.
name: Erin

text: I found the food to be overpriced and pretentious. The portions are small and flavors average. It's no way close to the real Asian street food they are named after. Heard good things about it, disappointed.

text:
I decided to pick up something for dinner (take out) while on the north side.  So, I stopped in Yujo to see what they had.

I will state up front that I am not a huge fan of ramen at dine in places.  I struggle with eating noodles with chopsticks and even if given a fork, they often serve large slices of meat (pork in my case) that are too big for one bite.  The broth drips when you lift it and trying to bite through the meat and then returning the remaining part back into the bowl seems awkward if not just odd.

So, I really appreciated that my 'to go' order placed the broth in one bowl and the ramen/meat/other stuff in a separate sealed bowl.  Once home, I was able to place the non-liquid contents on a cutting board, and cut them all to bite sized pieces.  I then divided the pieces between two bowls and added the reheated broth to each.  Ramen bowls are notoriously huge servings for one person.

The flavor of my Yuzu Signature was wonderful!  The broth had a chicken & pork stock base with a bit of lemon zest for brightness of flavor.  The chashu (braised pork belly) was thin, but originally was a large slice (more lean with just a bit of fat).  The rest of the flavors worked really well with the broth and meat for a hearty dish.

I also ordered a half sweet Strawberry Assam (milk tea) but they were out of boba (I wonder if they were going to make any for the evening shift since the place closes at 3 and reopens at 5.)  The flavor was good, but without the boba, was less than expected.

Overall, I found the food quite tasty and the service, though a bit inexperienced due to the newness, was pleasant and helpful.  

If you are a fan of ramen, check the place out.  If you are new to ramen, I recommend getting it to go so you can practice at home.

Been wanting to try this for a while. Love a good barbecue joint and happy to have one in the area. Unfortunately having finally tried it I can't say I'm impressed at all.

I have had brisket all over and in and out of the city and have definitely found a couple stand out places.  This is not a stand out. 

Ordered takeout at 1:30 on this Wednesday afternoon. Absolutely no one in the store when I arrived and things came out quick enough. About 15 minutes from order to ready. The girl at the counter was certainly nice enough.

My order, the $26.99 mixed meat platter. I chose a half lb of brisket, 1/2 rack of ribs, grilled and seasoned carrots, grilled and seasoned asparagus, and it came as standard with a piece of cornbread. Also included were two small containers of bbq sauce. 

First off, the carrots. They were OK. Had a bit of seasoning and if I were to guess they were probably cooked inside a packet or on a bed of aluminum foil after being sliced thinly. Three stars there. Decent.

Second, the asparagus. Five spears of overcooked and untrimmed asparagus. Heavily seasoned. Mushy. Two stars there. 

The ribs were pretty solid but slightly overdone. A slight bit dry but good flavor. These definitely were falling off the bone. In truth, really good ribs should not be completely falling off the bone. They should pull cleanly off the bone but have a slight bit of resistance and a good tender bite. They were decent though and pretty enjoyable. 3 to 4 stars for those.

Now, the half pound of brisket. Quite disappointing. Two thin slices of dried out brisket with very little smoke and an extremely salty rub...overpoweringly salty...There was no smoke ring to be found on the meat at all and despite claims of everything being cooked fresh I'm a little dubious with the dryness I experienced in this brisket. See the picture attached, of a completely brown toned meat with very little "pink". Sorry to say i expected a lot more after reading some very good reviews. 2 stars. 

Finally the cornbread, which was actually pretty darn good. Moist for cornbread and nice and sweet. Four stars there. Sadly/honestly probably the best thing in the platter.

The barbecue sauce, which I guess is their "secret sauce" was very sweet, lacking depth , and completely standard. Could have been out of a jar bought at the supermarket and i wouldn't know the difference. 

I don't know if my experience today was an off day for them or what happened but if what i got was their standard fare, There are much better options for barbecue in both the city, and local suburbs.


In response to the business owners comments below:

Hello Steve. I didn't see you there but really wouldn't have had a chance to address any issues because i did not eat there. 

On the sauce being different for every meat, I got two of the same sauces for the two different meats.

On the meat steaming up in a container and cooking a little more, that wouldn't remove a smoke ring if it was there. Also, if done right moisture can be retained. I've been in plenty of restaurants in the front and back of the house and know this to be the case.

Finally, in response to your comment that a good Yelper always tries more than once and that dining in is better, I have a couple of things to say.

One, of course dining in is better. But take out should still be good. I can tell you of a good few barbecue places where I get take out regularly and have never been disappointed. That is a bit of a cop out. Whether dining in or dining out, that rub on the brisket would've still been overpoweringly salty. And despite dining out, my house is about two minutes from your establishment. The food was cut and placed in the box in front of me and it took about five minutes max to make it from your kitchen to my table. Shouldn't really make much of a difference whether there or taken out, that being the case. The food should be to the same standard. 

Two, With so many restaurants out there, I don't really see the need to go to a place twice in evaluation if i have a totally sub par experience. 

Most importantly, You should be careful with your comment about good Yelpers. In response I would say that good business owners listen to criticism, and look within. They want to be better and instead of lashing back at the people commenting, seek to improve.  I see you respond to every negative review on here with a bit of an attack and as somebody who deals with people every day that's not the way to do it if you're looking to be effective. When one of my clients has a concern about my performance I really want to hear it, because I always want to be better.
name: Adam

text:
We stopped in at the Gramophone for a quick late lunch. I was expecting more of a restaurant setting and less of a bar, so I was a little taken aback.  Even though it was bright and sunny outside, the inside was pretty dimly lit.  High top bar tables lined the front windows and the front room and regular tables were in the back.

The menu is a bit overwhelming at first. They have lots of sandwich options, most are twists on classic sandwiches and many feature Red Hot Riplets.  I had to read through the menu a few times just to make sure I understood everything going on.  I ordered the General Patton, essentially a chicken sandwich with bacon, cheese and Cajun ranch. Hubs got the Delcortivo. We split an order of mac and cheese.  I'm glad I ordered a half sandwich because portions were large! Sandwiches come out wrapped in paper whether you're eating in or carrying out. My sandwich was "okay". Nothing wrong with it, but nothing I would crave. Hubs Delcortivo was huge! The flavors blended well and had me wishing I gotten something different. The mac and cheese was dry and hard on top--but was okay after scraping off the first layer of noodles. 

Gramophone won't be on the top of my list. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone if they were looking for something in the Grove, but I'd go back if someone else was set on heading there.
name: Suzanne

text:
Great local bar, not a bad place to brunch if you want bar food at brunch. 

We needed to find a brunch place that wasn't too crowded. The Blind Goat serves "brunch," and they aren't crowded on Sundays midday.

Sadly, they forgot to put in an order with their grocer earlier that week, so they couldn't serve salads or fresh veggies, but if you wanted pizza, mac and cheese, or wings, you were in luck. Luckily, their bar food is quite excellent, so everyone in our party was happy. The pizzas are very thin crust and not oily at all, so they were great. The wings were very crispy. And the mac and cheese is worth the trip alone (although it does take the longest to come out). Multiple types of cheese, individual serving baked to order so that it comes out crispy/caramelized on top with oozing cheese throughout. 

Despite being a bar, they do have a high chair, and they do have plastic cups and a kid friendly menu, so we felt comfortable bringing our kids here for brunch. I wouldn't bring them later in the day when the bar is fully of drinking patrons. That wouldn't be fair to the drinkers (my kids are toddlers and LOUD). But the outdoors corn hole and giant Jenga are fun distractions for kids as we waited for food to come out.

Service was friendly but understaffed. The location was clean enough. There's plenty of parking. And the music was awesome. It was like a flashback to high school and college for my husband and me, lots of fun.
name: michelle

text:
I was pleasantly surprised on my first visit. Great sushi and very reasonably priced. The restaurant is very clean and the sushi has a very fresh taste. The Vietnamese roll looks delicate but full of flavors. This is my fifth visit and I have yet to be disappointed. On this visit I had the octopus sushi and XXX Hoo roll.  My son had the volcano, rainbow roll and Alaskan roll.  I tried all 3 of his rolls and all tasted very good.  We both enjoyed every sushi piece.

Don't be turned off by the dark appearance while driving by at night. Their windows are tinted. Once you walk in, you will find yourself in a friendly and relaxing atmosphere. 

If you like sushi , give this restaurant a try. 

Note: at this time they do not have a liquor license but they have applied for one, beer and wine. I was told they hope to get it in 2-3 wks from today.

This could be a higher ranking if they know how to manage the restaurant better.

text:
I've lived in the area for 5 years and had never been to Issac Newtons. What a treasure! The beer list is extensive. I'm a cider drinker and they can be rare to  find on tap. Tonight they had Jacks Peach Cider which was a treat! 

When we arrived the outdoor seating was empty but it was full by the time we left. The space is really fantastic on a night like tonight. There were also large tables if you went with a bigger group.

We were seated inside and a very comfy booth. I asked the waitress for food suggestions and she said that the burgers and Caesar salads are what they do best. I took her advice and got the Caesar  salad /calzone combo. It came with pepperoni inside which I don't care for. They were happy to make mine without. The salad was crisp and delicious. The Calzone was good but nothing special. The Caesar salad is something I'll definitely get again. 

My friend opted for the nachos. They were delicious but the portion was way to much. A 1/2 size order option would be ideal. 

Looking forward to my next visit and hoping that they consider adding my favorite cider, Down East, to their offerings! Also, I just tried to see if they have a happy hour but couldn't find any info on that. I did find a great Monday/Tuesday special that I'll go back for!
name: Robyn

text: I know, don't go to a steakhouse for a salad.  I ordered the grilled chicken salad which on the menu was listed as having crisp cold greens.  Well I have never called iceberg lettuce a green and this salad was 95% iceberg  lettuce.  The chicken was delicious, however there were really no greens.  I can get a better salad at Chick-fil-A.

text:
The food we had was great. Ample portions, reasonable prices, friendly but slow service. 

I tried the Shrimp Tikki Marsala and I must say these were the best shrimp I had in a long time. Shrimp are so easily overcooked, leaving them rubbery  and chewy. These were done to perfection, done  but nice and tender juicy shrimp surrounded by a bucket of tikki sauce that went so well over the rice. I highly recommend this dish. 

My friend had a dish with chick peas and spinach (forgot the name of it unfortunately) and it was also delicious. A big bowl of it. I'm not usually into vegetarian dishes, but I snarfed this one up. Very good I must admit. 

The garlic naan was wonderful. Nice flavor, nice and soft with just enough little crunch on the sides to make things interesting. 

Why not 5 stars? Well the service while friendly seems a little unorganized and rather slow. 

And the location just bites. No direct access off Rockville. You have to go to the light to the Target Plaza, turn in as if you are going to Best Buy, but then take an immediate left. Follow that street past the actual building of the restaurant, then turn in left behind the building and follow the road around the building to the front to find a parking spot there. So that's a pain. Also don't forget that whole parking lot is a one way .
name: Sigrid

text: Ordered from here for lunch. My coworker and I were able to share a cheesesteak hoagie. It was nicely seasoned, good amount of beef and the bread was soft. I'm a real estate developer as well as a resident of this up-and-coming neighborhood, and I cannot express enough how happy my wife and I are to have such an outstanding addition to our area!!!

The employees were knowledgeable and eager to please, and the lady we were told is the owner was on site and not afraid to get her hands dirty...as a 20 year veteran of the restaurant/bar/nightclub industry, I know how rare and important this is to the success of an establishment. 

I had a traditional Philly, and my wife had a chicken sandwich of some sort. Both were absolutely top notch! I grew up in St. Louis, where many small establishments such as this compete for business solely relying upon the quality of their sandwich offerings, and this place reminds me of a couple places back home.

I hope the rest of the neighborhood likes this place as much as we do, because we need all we can get in the way of eateries!

text:
Wanted sushi for dinner but figured I didn't need to gorge myself on roll after roll of sushi leading me to hate myself for overeating so I felt a trip to Poke King was in order. 

This place is great and was a perfect choice. The fish tastes wonderful and was of really good quality. It's fun being able to add all the fun flavors and veggies into the poke bowl to make a delicious meal.

My advice would be to talk to the folks behind the counter about the sauces to put on the bowl. They are able to combine two or three sauces based on the flavor profile you like between sweet, spicy, etc and help you make your bowl even better.

You can grab soda, beer or even just enjoy the free jug of water in there to go along with the bowl of your choice.  This is a great place to hit up when you want that sushi fix without the overbearing full feeling you'll get from ordering sushi rolls at a restaurant!
name: Danny

text: Absolutely amazing. I'm incredibly picky about Italian because I usually stay away from pasta (for carb reasons ha!) but-- the Shisedo Peppers, the snapper and all of the pizzas....absolutely outstanding! The cocktails we delicious to match. Can't wait to come back soon!

I usually get the Jumbo shrimp with sweet potatoes and Mac n cheese and you can't forget either lemonade or a lemonade/ fruit punch mix! I suggest going during the week if you aren't the patient type. The food is great!

text:
Noble Crust is new to Wesley Chapel.
After about 4 weeks of breaking in, my wife and I decided to try it.....
They are, sort of, an upscale Italian restaurant and their prices reflect it. 
Their food is good. It should be noted that their soft drinks (coke etc) come in cans so no free refills. Ice tea by glass is available. With refills...
My wife had the scallops, I had salmon, both were excellent although I would like to see them more generous with the salmon.
The deserts looked  as well. They have 4 to choose from, we selected peanutbutter pie, good choice. 
The reason only 4 stars, (3 1/2 if I could), was the service, It was a little slow and not nearly attentive as it should have been. This applies to reception and others as well. Hard to get anyones attention. They should all be trained to help someone at a table even if it's not their station...
Restaurant is somewhat small for the amount of tables they have, so it's a little crowded and more noisy then it should be...
Long waits to get in, probably because the is good and, my guess, people are willing to overlook their shortcomings. I will as well!

Update on a recent visit... they have a singer on Thursday and Friday. I'm not criticizing the singer but he is loud and this means that if you come with a group of people who want to eat, drink and talk as we like to do over dinner it's too noisy to do so onThursday and Friday evening
