text: Price felt a touch high for what it was. Nobody was rude or anything, it just took a while to get water refilled. Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. It was clean enough and the tables were being turned over pretty fast. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. The experience was more frustrating than enjoyable.

text: Absolutely amazing place of musical history!!! Thank goodness they didn't tear this place down. A Southern treasure that should be seen by any music lover of any genre!
name: Anne

text:
I thought the prices were high in 2107, you should see them now. Chicken fingers $22, 8 ounces strip loin $35. High prices and mediocre at best food. Service has also gotten even worse, inattentive, and surly. They still make a great pizza but things like their burgers, chicken patties are all processed frozen stuff from Costco. No flavour and a heck of a lot of money for frozen card board.

I will not be going back any time soon. This is a Pizza joint, not Caesar's
Steak House, which by the way isn't much more expensive than this place has become. This place has completely lost it.

text: Jazz brunch here is overrated. I read up and down reviews, but decided to go for it to experience a jazz brunch in NOLA. The food was disappointing and overpriced. The only good thing was the cute patio and the service. There's so much delicious food in NOLA that I definitely think would have been better than coming here, unfortunately.

text: AMAZING. I didn't think anything could top Fresh Kitchen...wrong. I've only been once so I can't speak for all of their items, but I must say their queso is one of the best I've had.  The tortilla's are the most flavorful I've ever had and I will definitely be back for more very very soon!!

text: It tasted fresh, just not especially memorable. Service was friendly, just kind of slow once the room filled up. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Nothing tasted old or stale, so that's always a plus.. Dessert was weirdly the highlight, which I wasn't expecting at all. For the price I expected more than this. Pretty normal experience, nothing bad really. Service was friendly and everything tasted fresh. The sauces helped more than I thought they would..
name: User

text:
I feel like I'm betraying my other favorite Tampa sandwich shop... but Joyce's....has better subs.

Talk about a delicious Cuban sandwich. It's really one of the best I've had in my life and it's simple.

Standing room, cash only type place. You find parking, walk up to the counter, tell them what you want and then you wait while it's hand made then and there.

The Cuban sandwich is huge. The regular (about $6) is a large to me so the Jumbo has to be out of this world. It's good though, very good.
I wasn't the biggest fan of the deviled crab ($2) they had, but it did fill the urge I had for one.. especially at the price.

To sum up, go to Joyce's. Get a sandwich.

text: Oh man.. what a winner. I had the gator apps then the Gulf fish for entree with a side of Mac and cheese casserole. Super delicious. You cannot go wrong with this eatery. New Orleans is blessed to have a spot like this. I'm sure it's not the only gem  of the bayou. Makes me want to explore more. Thanks for the recommendation my fellow Yelpers. You guys never steer me wrong.

Because it was Good Friday we didn't eat meat, but can't wait to go back to try more of the menu. The atmosphere was nice and our server Dominic was great and helpful.

The only disappointment is a lack of a kids menu other than silver dollar pancakes, however, they did let my 3 children share an item.  Decent and quick service.

name: Luyen

text:
Menu is narrow here, but you understand that going in.  Focus is pig, its that simple.  Ribs are dry rub (they do have sauces available of course) .  Suggestion is go with 1-2 of their starters (their version of nachos is great) and then half rack per person.  Soda's & tea available where you order food, beer at the bar.

Originally gave four starts, but after having the dry rub spare ribs @ Martins on 4th, deducted 1 star.  Dry rub is much better at Martins to be honest...

text: Not a big place, but run extremely well and with charm. Breakfast dishes had novel aspects, and all were really good. Our waiter gets special mention for suggesting a half-order of French Toast, not on the menu as an option, for the almost-three-years-old member of our party. With something for just about everybody, this is a great choice for brunch.
name: Michael

text: Parking was annoying, although that's probably more about the area than the restaurant. They mixed up one side dish and fixed it pretty fast. Nothing about the space really stood out, which is maybe why the food had to do more. Delivery showed up warm, so no complaints there. The ramen broth had good flavor, maybe a little salty, but I still finished most of it. The food was good and the service was easygoing. For the price I expected more than this.
name: User

text: One of those meals where nothing is exactly wrong but you're not excited either. The leftovers held up okay the next day.. Food took a while and didn't really feel worth the wait. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. The food came out looking really good, tasted solid, then kind of leveled off after a few bites. For the price I expected more than this. It was fine, maybe a little overpriced.
name: User

text:
I am a true lover of pizza, and this is my favorite pizza source in Tucson. The crust is near perfect. The manhattanara is killer (especially with added mozzarella), as is the cura. Moreover, the wine is both interesting and affordable, and the salads are simple, fresh, and balanced. 

Beware, hours are limited. It may be worth your while to make a reservation, especially during summer months when the idea of patio seating is hard to swallow.
name: Hannah

text: The sauce carried most of the meal. Nothing was awful but I left disappointed. The sauces helped more than I thought they would.. My pasta was decent and not overcooked, which I appreciated because that happens a lot. My friend liked their dish more than I liked mine.. so yeah kind of mixed on it. Everything was tasty and the place felt clean. Food was good and came out fast. Not terrible, just not something I'd want again soon. Ordered a few things and liked most of it.
name: User

text: Will never eat here and pick up food from here ever again. It took 20 minutes in the drive thru to get my one meal that I ordered, which I was the only one it line for food. The staff was stuck up too.

text: Best onion rings ever. They are actually homemade, not that frozen crap. The burgers were delicious! This place is not like most tourist traps in the French Quarter. The food is amazing. Joe was our server, he was amazing. I will definitely be back!

text: got takeout from here twice now so I feel like I can say a little more. The portion size looked small at first but ended up being enough. Service was friendly, just kinda slow once the room filled up. I've definitely had more memorable meals for the same price.. It was decent, just a little uneven. The service was off and the meal kind of followed that energy. Nice little spot, decent portions too. Would prob stop in again if nearby.

text: Really frustrating... it says they close at 9 o'clock pm so we just walked down there to eat right now, and the gate was closed, even with a giant sign that said "Today's Hours: 10am - 9pm". There were like 15 other people standing there wondering why these young employees closed the store at 7:30pm? We walked around the back where the door was open and got yelled at by a young employee and she said "we are closed!" I mentioned the hours posted outside and she said "we were slow so we closed early". They still had like two whole pizzas there so we said.. ok we will just buy those pizzas and they responded with "well we already started throwing away the pizza so no we aren't going to sell it to you" and they dumped two giant whole pizza la in the trash- what a waste!!! Just because you're slow during specific times doesn't mean you just shut down because you feel like it, when people plan their dinners based off of your posted hours. Not professional.

text: Stopped in on a weekday morning and they surprisingly weren't very busy! Seems like a great local spot for people working or living in the neighborhood. I ordered the egg and sandwich breakfast sandwich, and added avocado. You can choose any bagel you want, and everything on the menu looked pretty customizable. The coffee menu was plentiful too; I opted for a small latte with almond syrup, and it was divine! The ambiance here is cute, and it looks like they feature local artwork, some available for purchase. Perfect little breakfast or lunch date spot off the beaten path; check it out!

text: Lunch date with my sweetie! If you haven't tried Anthonino's on Macklind you need to! The menu has Italian and Greek options and is one of the best in the Lou! So good it was featured on Diners, Drive-ins & Dives!

text: Must stop by...Didn't eat the food but imagine that it has just enough flavor as their drinks do.

text:
This is my new favorite restaurant! The filet was cooked to perfection and the melted cheese and chili's put this over the top. Carlos, our waiter, was excellent and brought out a wonderful tart to help celebrate Damien and Angela's Anniversary. 
Don't forget to try the jalapeno margarita

text:
Parkway Bakery & Tavern was highly suggested on Yelp so we decided to stop on in after walking all around New Orleans on Friday. 
 We arrived around 8:15 pm and there was a nice sized line which gave us time to peruse the menu and decide on what to order. 
 Time was up as we were next at the counter the gentleman took our order. Hers- a small Roast beef Poorboy without Tomato or Mayo and for me a small fried shrimp with all the toppings plus an order of fries for us to split. I mentioned we would also like waters so he gave us two water cups to get from the fountain machine. 

It took about ten-fifteen minutes to get called for our order, however everything is made as soon as you order and was super hot and fresh. 

After a stop to the condiment station which has remoulade, tartar, cocktail, dijon mustard and more for the sandwiches we found a place to eat and dug in. 

 The shrimp sandwich was delicious as it was packed with freshly fried shrimp and the toppings, in fact when eating the sandwich more than a few shrimp fell out onto my platter which then I ate with a fork and covered it with remoulade sauce. 

The fries were hot and fresh and the roast beef sandwich was also hot and fresh and very good. 

I consider this a must stop on our next trip to New Orleans.
name: Bill

text: When parental unit is in town have to head to this spot, that they love.  Completely get why they love this place, I do too!!  For sure their staff is always super friendly, as soon as we step into their patio area, the girl is very welcoming greeting and even opened the door for us.  Late for lunch, hence no line at the register.  The guy there was super friendly and told us about their special of the day, not only was it a special but also a new plate.  We order all went smooth, walked to salsa bar and as soon as we got there the girl was at our table with fresh chips!!! Best!!! Soon our guacamole arrived, and will say it was only second best to my moms guac!  Few minutes later our plates arrived, always delicious and freshly made. And I would have to add with fresh ingredients!! All tasted so good.  Even though it's not full service  restaurant the girl came to check how everything was!! Service, service, service is definitely a priority for them!! Can't wait to come back and enjoy another meal, maybe I'm lucky and will get to try a new dish!!

text: There's literally nothing bad I can say about HCV. Nothing. Every time I go, the staff is friendly, service is good, food is ABSURDLY DELICIOUS and I legit want to go here everyday, sooo that's my review. If you love meat if you don't love meat, this food is incredibly delicious vegan/vegetarian food. If you don't believe veggies can be as good as meat, go here and you will be proved wrong. text:
We were here on a Saturday, slightly before traditional dinner hours. It was easy to get a booth and our server was attentive and pleasant.

I am surprised at the number of 4 and 5-star reviews. At best, this is average food. 

First, I see reference to bread being delivered to the table. If this is so, then we were forgotten. 

We ordered as a start, the Roasted Roma Flatbread. It was good, better than average, and better than the entrees, which were the Carmelized Grilled Sea Scallops, and the Blackened Mahi  Mahi Tacos. Both were okay. 

I would say my partner's tacos were a better "deal" than my scallops. It's a pricey place, so to leave hungry is more than just an annoyance. It's enough to prevent me from going back.

My scallops were okay, all seven of them. I'm not a huge eater--I count calories, track macros and nutrients. The asparagus were the biggest portion, which is good, the risotto was not an average portion (which I'd think is around 1/2 a cup), and the scallops--for over $24--were about $3/piece if I assign $3+ to the asparagus and risotto. They were cooked perfectly, but it's just too pricey and when I pay that, I don't want to leave hungry.

The interior of the restaurant is nice, the server was good, but the food is simply not worth the price if you even just think about how you spend your money.
name: Jackie

text: 3 of us dined here last Friday night at 7, they were only moderately busy due to the off-season.  They were not properly staffed however, wait time at the outdoor bar was an excruciating 15 minutes for a drink.  Dining inside our waiter Rob (?) was super nice but as the night progressed he obviously became deep in the weeds due to a couple large tables with kids in his section.  Entrees were ready way before we were done with our apps.  He held them and kept them hot which was nice but proper timing in the kitchen would've been better.  So, the the food just Ok, some things better than others.  The oysters rockefeller were super good as were the scallop appetizer.  We all had various fish entrees and they were  just Ok.  IMHO the menu needs an overhaul.  Classic case of a menu trying to be all things for all people.  Also, near every dang entree on the menu is served with mashed potatoes, with only a few others served with rice only.  None of the dinner entrees come with a veg side unless you request a veg as an extra side dish. I thought this was very odd. Who the hell eats mashed potatoes with panko crusted snapper?  Even the lobster tail comes with yup, mashed potatoes.  It definitely rates a meh.

text:
We were here recently for a special birthday dinner (we go for special occasions a few times a year).  It's elegant, has live music, and is quiet enough for conversation (a big selling point).  Up until now, I've considered the food and experience worth the out-of-sight prices.

However, this time, the service and quality were lacking:  we waited a very long time for the waiter to come around with the menus, finally had to flag him down to request them; we ordered drinks immediately.  Then they brought rolls, and one basket (we were a group of 8) had the same boring tasteless white-bread rolls, while the other basket had a variety.  As we were passing the baskets of rolls, the busboy came and whisked the charger plates out from in front of us; two people - distracted by having a conversation, had put their rolls on the chargers instead of the bread plates, and the busboy dumped their rolls onto the tablecloth in order to remove the chargers.  The appetizers arrived before the drinks we had ordered, so we had to request specially that the waiter go to the bar and bring the drinks.  One person ordered the salad, but substituting a balsamic dressing (usually comes with blue cheese dressing, and they can't stand blue cheese), and it came with the blue cheese and had to be returned to the kitchen.  

My husband and I always get the prime rib, (the smaller of the two ordered), and indeed it was huge, but surprisingly tasteless and un-seasoned.  The mushrooms were bland.  Everyone else seemed happy with their entrees, except the person who ordered crab imperial; I'm not sure what the issue was with that.

It was a birthday dinner, and at most restaurants, they do something a little special.  Much less expensive and pretentious restaurants will write "happy birthday" in drizzled chocolate on the plate and stick a cookie on the plate.  Normally, at Prime Rib, when dessert comes, the pianist plays "happy birthday", but he was on break (as he seemed to be quite a lot of the time).  We had ordered a couple of desserts to share, and they just stuck a birthday candle into a slice of apple pie (one of our ordered desserts) and plunked it on the table with the others. 

The person choosing the venue seemed OK with everything, but she almost never dines out, and probably doesn't have too much to compare it with; since she picked up the check, I didn't feel comfortable complaining about my meal, but if I had been in charge, I would have sought out the manager on the spot.  The best I can do is to report this here, with the idea that, if you decide to go, to be forewarned that you're going to spend a lot without a comparable experience to go with it.gyWxaz-6ranpe-dyjmem

It seems to me that a restaurant that charges these prices, and everything is a la carte, and also crazily expensive (I mean, if you're going to charge $7 for a baked potato, which requires no baking skill -- it was a large baked potato, but really???), and most entrees are $48 and upwards, that you should have a lovely, attentive experience during which you're being pampered.

text:
I'm surprised there aren't more 5 star reviews. I loved everything about Meril. To start, the decor is fresh and beautiful. The service was exceptional from start to finish. Our waiter was timely and extremely helpful in providing suggestions. The blast from the past 90s music on the night we visited was a bonus, haha. 

My favorite part of this experience was the food and drinks. The cocktails are mixed perfectly! We ordered the crab croquettes, wise guy flatbread, saffron pappardelle, glazed chicken thighs and Mexican style corn. Between two people, this was more than enough food. We were full to the brim. Everything that was supposed to be crispy was crispy. Everything that was supposed to be juicy was juicy. Everything that was supposed to be savory was savory- you get the point. So freakin' good, everything, really. Why not 5 stars?!
